ON THE HARMONY OF THE SOUL'S COMPOSITION. PRACTICE. 273

C H A P. V.

*On the harmony of body and soul with each other.*

Wonderful is the love and fellowship of flesh and soul, that is, of the spirit of life and the dust of the earth, since from these joined together the whole human being is said to be formed. For thus it is written: God made man from the dust of the earth, and breathed into his face the breath of life, giving him sense and intellect; so that through sense he might vivify the clay associated with him, and through intellect he might rule; similarly, so that through intellect he might enter within, and contemplate God's wisdom, and sense might observe His works of wisdom outwardly. God illuminated the intellect within, but adorned the sense outwardly, so that in both the complete human being might find recreation, namely, within for blessedness, outwardly for delight. But because external goods cannot long endure, man was commanded to return from external things to internal things, and from internal things to ascend to higher things, namely from sense to imagination, from imagination to reason, from it to intellect, and from that to mind or intelligence, and thus to God.

Wonderful, I say, and ineffable, indeed truly full of miracle it was, that natures so diverse, divided, and contrary, such as body and soul, could be joined to each other, nor less admirable was it, that in our clay God contracted Himself, so that God and clay might be coupled to each other; such sublimity, namely, and such vileness; for nothing is more sublime than God, nothing viler than clay. Wonderful was the first conjunction, wonderful was the second, nor less wonderful will be the third, when the same human being, Angel, and God will be one spirit, for by the same good is man good, by which an Angel is good, and by the same good is each blessed; if, however, both desire the same thing with the same will and the same spirit: And if God could join such disparate natures, namely of flesh and soul, into one federation and friendship, it will by no means be impossible for Him to exalt the rational spirit, which has been humbled even to the fellowship of an earthly body, with the same glorified body to the fellowship of blessed spirits who persist in their purity, and to elevate it to the participation of His glory. For to this end, by charity alone, and by no necessity, the Most High created him, that He might make him a partaker of His blessedness.

If therefore there is so much joy and so much gladness in this temporal life, which consists of the presence of the spirit in that corruptible body, how much gladness and how much joy will there be in eternal life, which consists of the immediate existence of the Godhead in the rational spirit. Therefore let the body be subjected to the soul, and the soul to God, and there will be one spirit with Him, if only the spirit remains in humility, and acknowledges the grace of its Creator, through whom it is to be glorified and exalted. Therefore man consists of flesh and soul, and each has its own good, in which it rejoices and exults. The good of the soul is God with the abundance of His sweetness. The good of the flesh is the world with the abundance of its delight; but the world is external; God, however, is internal, than whom nothing is more internal, and nothing more present; He is interior to all things, because in Him are all things, and exterior to all things, because He is above all things. Therefore, ascending from this world to God, and as it were striving upwards from the depths, we ought to transcend ourselves. For to ascend to God is to enter into oneself, and not only to enter oneself, but in a certain ineffable way to pass through one's own center. Hence Mercurius Trismegistus [says]: "He who, passing inwardly and penetrating intrinsically, transcends himself, he truly ascends to God." Indeed, in order that this may happen, we must be drawn away from this world...

--- Page 276 ---
174 TRACT. I. SECT. I. LIB. XIII.

distractions, let us gather our heart, and recall it to internal joys. And if we cannot always keep our heart in these, let us at least restrain it from illicit and vain thoughts, so that we may sometimes be able to fix it in the light of divine contemplation. For this is the rest of our heart, when it is fixed in the love of God through desire: This is the life of our heart, when it contemplates its God, and is sweetly refreshed in its very contemplation; And it is always sweet to consider, to love, and to praise; for nothing seems more excellent for a blessed life than for some affection, as if with carnal senses closed, outside the flesh and the world, to be turned within itself, and for an affection estranged from mortal desires to speak to itself alone and to God. Since therefore the soul is incorporeal through a more subtle nature of the body, that is, through fire and air (which are the more excellent bodies in the world itself, and therefore more familiar to the spirit), it administers to the body. These former indeed receive the impulses of the life-giving soul, because they are closer to the incorporeal nature than humors and earth, so that the whole mass may be administered for their immediate service. For there is no identical sense in the body for these two [humors and earth], nor any spontaneous bodily movement in the soul [through them]. Fire and air, because they are light, move earth and water, which are heavy. Wherefore we see bodies are scarcely moved after the departure of the soul, because fire and air, which two by the presence of the soul are held in the earthy and humid body so that a tempering of all may occur, escape to higher regions and free themselves after the departure of the same soul. But as for the composition of the body, it must be understood that the body consists of functional members; which functional members also consist of similar parts, and similar parts likewise consist of humors, but humors consist of foods, and foods consist of elements. Hence we see that none of these is the soul, but the soul acts in these, as in organs naturally destined for it, and through these it cares for the body and for this life, by which man was made into a living soul. If therefore these are temperate and ordered, they are suitable for vivification, and the soul never departs; but if they are distempered and confused, the soul unwillingly departs, drawing with it all things, namely sense, imagination, reason, intellect and intelligence, concupiscence and irascibility; and from these, according to merits, it is affected towards delight or towards pain. Thus therefore then the body, which was formerly whole, as a tempered and disposed instrument so that it might sing a melody and resonate to the touch, lies conversely broken and mutilated; but the soul, with the parts of the elements returning to their homeland, not having where it may exercise its powers, rests from only those movements by which it moved the body through time and place. For although the instrument perishes, yet the melody does not perish, nor that which moved the instrument. From these, therefore, as if with open eyes, we can behold that admirable harmony by which those two extremes, namely the most precious and the most vile, are chained together and harmonize with each other, and that the intermediate spirit of the world, the vehicle of the soul, becomes the bond for retaining them in concordant peace and symphony, and that God is the inspirer of human music, or the player of the monochord's string, or the internal principle, as if from the center of the whole, producing harmonious movements and effects of life in the Microcosm. But the string, by its vibration, dispersing the luminous effects of the inspirer, as accents and sounds of love, through the Macrocosm and Microcosm, is the clear spirit, which naturally according to its site and position participates in both extremes, and connects both extremes to each other, and similarly delineates the degrees or keys of the human system, by which the descent of the soul from the heavens into the body occurs downwards, and conversely also its ascent to higher regions or place

Here we see the whole man drawn, extended in his own image; in the middle of which, along its continuous length, we have drawn a straight line, representing the entire diameter of the Microcosm. Furthermore, the semidiameter A. C. of this chord measures the tones and semitones of the Monochord, and renders musical proportions similar to those found in the harmony of the world. Therefore, in its left part, we have explained the music most similar to that of the world; but in its right part, we have quite properly delineated the harmonious aspect of the soul descending from heaven to earth, and its ascent again from earth or body into heaven or spirit. Therefore, in the left part, we have demonstrated that the proportion between intellect and life in the Monochord is found to be double, in which the spiritual Diapason is contained. Similarly, we have shown that in the same proportion, the interval of the Monochord extended from the sphere of the heart or sun to the earth or genitals sounds a corporal Diapason, uniting life and sense, or the carnal nature, which inhabits the lowest belly. Just as, therefore, in the string of a musical Monochord, if half of it is pressed, one Diapason sounds downwards and another upwards, so also the heart, situated in the middle of the human semidiameter, no differently than the Sun in the middle of the world, by one Diapason consonance looks to the lower parts, namely, the nature of the lowest region, and by the other, to the highest heaven of the Microcosm, in which mind, intellect, and reason hold dominion. Also, on the right side of the Microcosm, we have established a Diapason consonance between intellect and imagination; namely, a Diatessaron between intellect and reason, and a Diapente between reason and imagination; which two, joined together, produce a spiritual and invisible Diapason. Similarly, extending downwards from the sphere of the heart, we find the same proportion between imagination and the body or center of the earth. For the space of movement from imagination to sense is referred to a Diatessaron, but that which is between sense and flesh or body, to a Diapente; which, joined, form a corporal and as it were visible Diapason. The first breath of life, immediately inspired by God into the face of man, administers movement to all these; according to whose voluntary movement, as the prime mover of the Microcosm, the faculties of the lower regions are carried by involuntary movements. For thus we see that the animal action, contained in the highest region, is voluntary; but the others common to the lower regions, namely vital and natural, are called involuntary. We have also explained the day and night of the Microcosm in the aforesaid demonstration, inasmuch as the sources of rational, vital, and natural light always ascend and rise above man's earth, or center, while man lives; but below his earth, nothing is found except its two supports or columns, sustaining and propping up the entire mass as if with Atlantean shoulders. Therefore, in the upper hemisphere of the Microcosm, the light of the first heaven always shines, namely, of the mind, illuminated by divine splendor; in the middle, the heart, filled with solar light; and in the lowest part, the liver, overflowing with the heat of the fiery and airy element. And in this way, I have presented the entire nature of man, both internal and external—although not elegantly enough according to my will, yet diligently, as far as possible, for the observer, and quite clearly, I believe, for a son of light and not of darkness—not without having rendered immense and most grateful thanks to God my Creator, while spurning, neglecting, and disregarding the bitter curses of Momus, the worst slanders of the malevolent, and the impious derisions of the envious, and treating the virulent bites of such viperous tongues with the balm of patience and an unblemished, ancient conscience.

# PROEM.

[Large historiated initial 'I' depicting a figure with a radiant halo, possibly a deity or creator, surrounded by clouds and other figures.]

In the first section of the first Treatise of this second Volume, we have clearly and openly enough explained the nature of the Microcosm, both internal and external: Here, however, in the second section of the aforementioned Treatise, we shall dwell longer still on the disposition of the Microcosm, though not in the same way as above. For in the preceding parts, we were occupied with the creation and generation of man, both internal and external, but in this section, we shall treat of certain sciences pertaining to every region of man or the Microcosm, not straying beyond the bounds of health, which contribute both to the exaltation and explanation of the internal man, or the revelation of hidden nature, and to the symmetrical explanation of his external self. Hence it is, therefore, that we have proposed to treat of divination, because through this, which is most full of divine inspiration and afflatus from the gods, the human mind, as if overwhelmed by darkness, is wonderfully illuminated, and it forbids man to deal with mortals or to be occupied with worldly affairs, inasmuch as it carries the soul's composition upwards with it, and makes it intent on purely divine matters: Similarly, dwelling longer still in the Empyrean heaven of the Microcosm, we shall also speak precisely of Geomancy, and we shall attempt to prove that it is a science of the rational soul, consisting in its just moderation. Finally, we shall discuss the art of memory lightly but effectively, by the exact knowledge of which we shall declare that the memory of a sound man, however strong or weak, can be most easily and most quickly corrected and improved. Then, descending more deeply and further downwards into man, and comparing his nature with the stars, we shall perceive that his complexion, and the disposition of his vital and natural soul, is wonderfully inclined from his very birth towards the influences of the stars, and that the celestial motion, that is, the disposition of the heavens at the point of his genesis, would carry away the whole nature of man with it, unless a portion of the divine mind, whose power, strength, and divinity has exalted it above the stars, governed it more deeply and effectively, communicating to it, if only it wishes to know and obey, that gift, that it may dominate the stars. Concerning Genethlia-

--- Page 287 ---
PROEM. 5

Therefore, in the fourth place, we will speak of Genethlialogia, and similarly concerning physiognomy and chiromancy, which are sciences of the ancient Chaldeans, dependent on the powers and influences of the stars, and are said to explain the nature and inclination of men. And thus, by comparing the threefold degree of the Macrocosm with the three regions of the Microcosm, conferring the power of one upon the other, we will declare both by technical reason in this section, just as in the preceding section we deduced by that physical relation; and by that reason we will amply demonstrate that, according to the model and likeness of the greater world, produced in the first three days of creation, the Daedalian creator graphically and precisely expressed and described this our lesser world, most skillfully formed in number, measure, and weight on the sixth day of creation. Therefore, we attribute prophecy or vaticination to the mind, geomancy and also the science of local memory to the rational soul, Genethlialogia to the vital soul, and Physiognomy and Chiromancy to the faculty partly vital and partly animal; and thus, concerning these things, in the present section, we have decided to treat briefly, but clearly, with divine grace assisting.

B O O K I.

On vaticination or prophecy in general.

C H A P. I.

On the definition of Vaticination or Prophecy, and on the varied opinion
of ancient philosophers concerning its origin and source.

[Decorative initial Q] Although in the preceding Section of this Treatise, we have spoken
clearly, though succinctly, concerning the hidden and mystical virtue of prophecy,
namely concerning its origin, divinity, operation, and effect,
and how the divine spirit, having flowed into man, rules and governs
his soul, yet, according to Iamblichus's opinion, it does not
completely deprive, while it is present, the human soul of the motion naturally
inherent in it; no more, namely, than solar rays extinguish a lit candle
exposed to them (for although the excellence of one may seem to obscure the splendor
and glory of the other, yet the candle does not thereby lose its motion,
flame, or faculty of burning). Here, however, to have and establish a broader
discourse concerning that gift, divinely granted to humans
alone, is not alien to the
subject.

--- Page 289 ---
DE VATICIN. SEU PROPH. IN GEN. 7
a natural inclination to approach its like, inasmuch as by natural instinct likes are observed to delight in likes: So also that highest power in the inner man, which is called mind, since it is from the same source and the same homeland as the divine Spirit sent into the Prophets, by the most intense union of the mind and the middle soul, as if bound and glued to the mind, and with external things gathered to the center of its nature, it can perform wonders and accomplish great things, indeed, it can even draw down from God himself an abundance of Spirit equal to itself, by whose conjunction with the mind the soul is rendered not unlike the nature of Angels, so that it can foretell the future, perform miracles, have familiarity with the Angels themselves, and perform infinite other wonders: But if the soul's powers and rays are drawn away from the center, and occupied with a multitude of matter, the soul's power in its strength will be no less weakened than arrows, which, when joined or bound together and united, are not broken, but when separated are very easily shattered. For so also the soul, the more it contemplates worldly things, the weaker its power becomes in attracting supercelestial gifts. Hence it is necessary that it gather itself to the center and as it were a point.

But, to come to our purpose, we say: *Prophecy is a certain gift or habit, by which men, being moved, discern the causes of things and foresee the future, which indeed, as some would have it, occurs when either the spirit of God or of some Demon descends into their souls, and these descents the Platonists call "illapses of the Gods into the souls of men," to which Platonic opinion the Prophet Isaiah seems to assent with these words: "Declare to us what is to come, and we will say that you are gods."*

However, no small disagreement arises among the ancients concerning this matter, since some would have it that prophecy occurs solely through the inspiration of the Divine will alone, and not of Demons. Hence Cicero, a follower of the Stoics, affirmed that the foreknowledge of future things belonged only to the Gods, and *Ptolemy*, most skilled in Astrology, held that those inspired by divine will alone, and not instigated by the power of Demons, could predict particulars. The Blessed Peter also seems to confirm their assertions, saying: *For prophecy never came by the will of man, but holy men of God spoke as they were moved by the Holy Spirit.*

*Iamblichus says that prophecy is neither from art, nor nature, nor the movements of animals, nor reason, but he wants it to be eternally sent to us divinely, and he relates that the entire power of foretelling is referred to God:* Hence he seems to define prophecy as, *that which is handed down by the Gods, and is perfected by divine works and signs, which has certain divine spectacles, and contemplations endowed with true knowledge.* By these expressed words, he also professes that all authority of oracle, augury, prophecy, and any species of divination whatsoever, consists in the Gods.

Some others, according to the argument of the aforesaid definition, would have Demons sometimes to be the cause of prophecy: Hence *Hermes Trismegistus* confidently and boldly declared that *the influx and illapse of the senses or souls of Demons into the souls of men is the origin of prophecy*, and the ancients called such Demons *Eurideas* and *Pythons*, whom they abundantly left us in the monuments of their histories as accustomed to entering human bodies and using their voices and tongues in divinations of future events.

But we descend into the opinion of both sects, and we believe that the inspiration of prophecy can proceed both immediately from God and from some Demon subjected to divine power, and we shall endeavor to support, defend, and prove this opinion of ours with many reasons, both from historians and from the testimony of sacred writings.

C H A P. II.

*That it is in the power primarily of God, and then also*
*of Demons, to change a common man into a Prophet.*

**N**ot only from many places of the sacred scriptures do we deduce that prophecy flows immediately from God himself, and sometimes also from Demons, both good and evil: but also the ancient Philosophers seem to confess this same thing; for, if we diligently inspect the sacred writings, we will discover that the gift of prophecy has been granted to men of holy life by God immediately and also mediately through Angels. Thus Abraham the Prophet received this inspiration immediately from God, and yet sometimes good Demons or Angels and messengers of God also appeared to him, and warned him of future events; and thus also *Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Moses, Aaron, Balaam, Joshua, Samuel, Saul, David,* and very many others, to whom most holy visions used to appear sometimes immediately from God and sometimes through Angels, both in waking and in dreams. Indeed, this most sacred office was granted to women too, both mediately and immediately; such as to *Miriam* (sister of Aaron) in *Exod. 15*, to *Deborah*, Judge of Israel in *Jud. 4. 4*, to *Huldah* in *2 Reg. 22*, etc. And although a vision sometimes emanates immediately from an Angel, or good Demon, that vision is nevertheless excellent, because it proceeds mediately from God. For Angels are messengers of Jehovah, announcing His commands to His Prophets either openly by vision in waking, or enigmatically, both in waking and in sleep, so that this kind of inspiration is attributed to God. But this kind of inspiration is called mediate, because there is another kind sent immediately by Jehovah Himself into the souls of the saints, of which mention is made in *Num. 11. 2* with these words: *Then Jehovah came down in that cloud and spoke to him, taking some of that spirit which was upon him, he put it upon those seventy elder men; and it was that when that spirit rested, then they prophesied:* similarly, *Moses* received the power of his prophecy immediately from Jehovah appearing to him in the bush, as is found in *Exodus*; so also the Spirit of Jehovah is said to have rushed immediately upon Saul, so that he prophesied with the other Prophets: Thus also the Holy Spirit, sent immediately from God, descended upon the Apostles, and so in many others. From these things it is clear that, however the method of prophesying comes to man, whether immediately from the influx of the Spirit of God, or through the appearance and vision of Angels, all this benefit flows from God and according to God's will, since Angels are messengers of God's will to holy men, just as Prophets or inspired holy men are messengers to other men, as in *Jud. 2. 1*. This also Jamblicus seems to confess among the ancient Philosophers with these words: *The divine power is the origin of prophecy, which is not from the body, nor from the soul added to the body, but from absolutes, that is, from Angels and God, who are everywhere, or at least the power itself, wherever any of the Angels are.* He acknowledges, namely, that divination comes from God Himself, or from other Angels divinely sent by God, whose divinity also comes from God Himself: For, just as the true image of a hidden thing, not to be seen by itself, is sometimes accustomed to be seen in a mirror, so also God's glory, will, kindness, and justice are sometimes seen in Angels, as in a mirror; Whence by Dionysius Angels are called *Agalmata*; that is, most clear mirrors receiving the light of God, in which the glory of the Divine Majesty is discerned, whence it happens that nothing is seen in them, except what God Himself proposes and presents, no more, namely, than a mirror can represent anything to the eye that is not offered to it:

--- Page 291 ---
DE VATICINATIONE SEU PROPHETIA IN GENESI 9

offered: For angels are capable only of divine impressions, nor do they report anything to humans, except what is entrusted to them by the Creator. Among these prophets, who received the power and efficacy of prophecy from God, both immediately and mediately, and who are not cited among the ancients in the sacred Bibles, are named Mercurius Trismegistus, Plato, Orpheus, the Sibyls, the Oracles of the Chaldeans, Cassandra of Troy, Merlin the Englishman, Nostradamus the French seer, etc. For Mercurius Trismegistus, in sermon 1 of Pimander, concerning the word flowing from the mind, which he openly calls the Son of God, prophesied in Asclepius, and concerning the Spirit or God of fire proceeding from both. Augustine, with Porphyry, testifies that the Platonists posited three persons in God, of whom they prophesied the first to be the Father of the universe, the second the Son or the first mind, and the third the Holy Spirit. Orpheus also called the Son Pallas, born from Jove's head, that is, the Father's wisdom and the highest image of God. The Sibyls also in a wonderful way foretold the truth of Christ's mystical advent, and divinely revealed their writings concerning consubstantial matters, and left them to posterity, about which more below. English monuments know and demonstrate the prophecies of Merlin the Englishman and their truth; nor less do the admirable predictions of the Frenchman Nostradamus exist in the world to this very day. For brevity's sake, we will omit here the praises of Apollonius of Tyana and Hiarchus, the wise men of India, who were stirred by the divine spirit in their predictions of future events. But from these, we boldly affirm that men inspired by this divine spirit, or by the gift of Prophecy, not only hide and live secretly among us Christians, but also live in many corners of the earth in a secret and silent way, unknown to the world, and as if under the wings of Jehovah, protected by divine power, according to that [passage] of John, 1st epistle, 3: *The world does not know the children of God, because the children of God did not know the world:* For the children of God have this power and prerogative, to perceive that light which is in the world, and by which the world was made, and which nevertheless the world did not know, according to that [passage] of the Gospel of St. John, chapter 1, and 1st epistle of John, 3: *See what love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God and be so; for this reason the world does not know us, because it did not know Him:* For not all who say they are Christians and know God, are truly Christians, or truly know God. Therefore, very few, in respect to the multitude, are true Christians in the world, and very few true worshippers of Jehovah are sown in the world. Hence St. John, 1st epistle, 3: *He who says he knows God, and does not keep His commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him, etc.* What the commandment of God is, he narrates in the following: *But he who keeps His word, truly in him the love of God is perfected: He who says he abides in Christ, ought to walk as He Himself walked.* Indeed, the Prophet David humbly strove with his melodious prayers to God, that he might be permitted to know this way of God, in which Christ walked. Therefore, it is not easy for anyone, unless exalted by divine inspiration, to tread that path, since it is so difficult to know, that knowledge of it is granted only to the children of God, and not to others: For the way of obtaining the divine Spirit is revealed to men by God alone according to His will and benevolence. Therefore, we cannot sufficiently scorn or rightly refute the foolish assertions of those who say that God removed miracles and prophecies from the world after the advent of Christ, while they are nevertheless compelled to concede that the same God is still here, there, and everywhere, as He was before. Indeed, Christ's strength, power, and life-giving virtue are present everywhere to humans and the creatures of the world, though invisibly: And yet they wish the effects of His benevolence and mercy, which the Sacred Scriptures affirm to be infinite and to endure forever, to be finite, and thus that He has forgotten us. We see the same created and visible Sun in the world perpetually performing its office in the vivification of lower things and

...of superior bodies' illumination; and yet they seem to argue that the Sun and uncreated and invisible light, in its benevolent property, is lacking and deficient for creatures: we annually observe the soul of living things receiving an increase of virtue from the Sun; and yet they attempt to deny that the mind is nourished or illuminated by divine rays, and thus, unknowingly and ignorantly, presume to utterly abolish the power of regeneration. But indeed, let such people know that God is also present to us here on earth, and frequently presents the miraculous gift of prophecy to worldly eyes, which swine reject and avoid out of fear, but the knowing behold and, filled with joy, adore; indeed, it may truly be said that heaven is on earth, and earth in heaven, and in this way, let us not deny that God's gifts and blessings are as much on earth as in heaven, and thus God Himself is finally everywhere, and continually pours out His goodness towards humanity and chooses worthier vessels into which He may infuse His Spirit either more sparingly or more abundantly. But to return to our subject, it must be known that even the Demons adhering to Lucifer, and fallen down with him, and worshipped as God by some, sometimes imbue their priests with the gift of prophecy, as the sacred scriptures themselves also testify: For *Molech and Milcom, Gods of the Ammonites, 1 Kings 11:7, and Chemosh, God or idol of the Moabites, Num 21:29, and Ashtoreth, God of the Sidonians, whom Solomon followed, 1 Kings 11, and Baal-zebub, God of Ekron, 2 Kings 2, and Succoth-benoth, idols of the people of Babylon, and Nergal of the people of Cuth, and Ashima of the people of Hamath, and Nibhaz and Tartak of the Avvites, and Adrammelech and Anammelech, Gods of the Sepharvites,* to whom they burned their sons with fire, *2 Kings 17, and Dagon of the Philistines, Judges 16:23.* These, I say, the inferior Gods of the Gentiles, were evil demons (Cacodaemons), because the prophecies and oracles uttered through them did not originate from God nor from Angels. This is also what *Moses, Deut. 33:17,* seems to admit by uttering these words concerning the Gods of these nations: *They sacrificed to demons and not to God, to gods, that is, whom they did not know, etc.* It is therefore probable that all these Gods of the Gentiles had their priests, to whom they revealed some future events in visions and dreams, and performed wonders: For we read in *1 Kings 18* that the idols of Baal of the Sidonians had many prophets, who were accustomed to divine about future things in their own manner: Hence in the Bibles they are called *Prophets of Baal*: Concerning such prophets, Jehovah also speaks to *Moses, laying down a law against them, Deut. 13: If there arises among you a prophet or a dreamer of dreams, and he gives you a sign or a wonder, (even if the sign or wonder which he foretold to you comes to pass) saying, 'Let us follow other gods,' etc. That prophet or dreamer of dreams shall surely be put to death, because he has advocated apostasy against Jehovah your God.* From which it is clear that even a false prophet serving an evil demon (Cacodaemon) can foretell a true wonder and sign, by that power alone which Lucifer and his Angels furtively and treacherously stole from God out of heaven. Thus *Prometheus* is said to be tormented on Mount Caucasus by the sharp talons of a swift vulture and its hooked beak, because he secretly snatched fire from the heavens, by whose power he attempted miracles on these earths against the Majesty of Jupiter: but such prophecy is for the most part impotent and uncertain because of the weakness of the luminous power which the Devil possesses, so that, where the presence of God offers itself, or the divine spirit is present, there these gods, burdened by impotence, cannot endure even for a moment against God and His invincible Spirit, in respect to divine strength. Hence it therefore happened that the idol or God *Dagon of the Philistines,* placed next to the ark of the mighty God Jehovah, could not stand, but was cast down to the ground face-down before the ark of Jehovah, and thus, with its head and both hands cut off on the threshold, was compelled to worship the supreme God of Gods and venerate Him with forced worship, *1 Kings 5.* Thus also the *Prophets of Baal* undoubtedly could, by divine permission, perform signs and miracles and wonders: But God Jehovah, by His power, the accustomed strengths of Baal...

by His ineffable power restraining and suppressing, so that He might publicly show His people that His power was superior to Baal's, He left those prophets of Baal destitute of all protection of their deity, so indeed, that although they, in their custom, cried out with a loud voice and cut themselves with knives and lances according to their ritual even to copious bleeding, Baal, however, their god, could not move even a foot or a finger to help his prophets; and thus, by the power of one true prophet of Jehovah, namely Elijah, four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and four hundred prophets of the groves were overcome, so that it might be clear to the Israelites and the whole world by how many and how great degrees the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob is to be preferred over the other gods of the nations. Furthermore, among the pagans, the oracles of Apollo, Jupiter, Diana, and all the Chaldean oracles, in a certain way (if Iamblichus is to be believed) confessing the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, received their power from that immense and eternal essence, from whose word and spirit all strength, power, and effect proceeds, so indeed, just as the Devil himself sometimes attempts something of his own accord, and transforms himself into an angel of light, so that by this way he may deceive men, but he does this impiously, and by the power of that primal essence attributed to him by Jehovah, he strives to act even against Jehovah's will; Hence, by divine will, he is hindered and restrained in his actions by the presence of a stronger power and the rock of all strength. It also happens sometimes that God sends a lying spirit into his own prophets, so that he may better ensnare the wicked and lead them to unexpected ruin: Hence *1 Kings 22: Then a certain spirit came forward, and stood before Jehovah, and said: I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all their prophets.* It is clear, therefore, that our definition of prophecy cited above is not to be entirely rejected, but that prophecy is a gift or a certain habit, by which the minds of holy men are stirred either by the spirit of God, who is the source, origin, and strength of all prophecy, or by the inspiration of a good Daemon, or even finally by the inspiration of an evil Daemon, so indeed that even the power of the latter is originally from Jehovah.

C H A P. III.

*In how many ways Prophets perceive future events, &
how they receive the vision of Prophecy.*

**P**rophets or Seers are accustomed to foretell future events in many and various ways, namely, either immediately stirred by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, that is, by the connection and union of the Spirit of God with the mind of the prophesying man. And this kind of prescience is to be preferred above others, since it is infallible, powerful, most divine, and far nobler than all others, or by the connection of a good Daemon with the human soul, by whose power prophets are said to divine about future events: Indeed, angels sometimes used to enter the bodies of irrational animals, to announce the command and will of God to a third person; but also evil spirits, sometimes entering men by divine permission, were able to utter prognostics about future events: similarly, some prophets, imbued with a certain divine or diabolical spirit from dead things, did not hesitate to foreknow and predict what was to happen to the world. But so that we may deal with prophecy more methodically, we will reduce its entirety into a single distinction in this way.

It is also reported that not far from the city of *Epidaurus of Laconia* there was a deep swamp sacred to *Juno*, from which, by throwing into it small cakes made of grain, responses were given, favorable indeed, if the waters calmly retained the thrown cakes; but adverse, if, as if scorned, they rejected them. There are also infinite other examples of this subject, which for the sake of brevity we will pass over in this place. But there are also some things into which the Devil or demon rebellious against God infuses his prophetic spirit, such as the idols of the Gentiles. And perhaps also some of the previously mentioned things received such power both from the inspiration of the Devil and from the Spirit of God, whose original power, however, was from God.

**CONCERNING PROPHECIES OR DIVINATIONS IN GENESIS 15**

**CHAPTER IV.**
In how many ways does God address humans?

First, it must be known that God addresses humans and the world in diverse ways; Then, the persons and things through which or by means of which His words are understood must be considered. As for divine speech, it must be known that God does not speak as a human speaks, but as an invisible God and Spirit, so that, namely, we hear the word, but cannot see the essence: He speaks, however, in a holy tongue, which all humans under heaven understand. He is not formed like a human with a head, ears, eyes, nose, mouth, or other limbs, but as an invisible Spirit, whom no one has ever seen, and to whom no one is similar. Therefore, He also does not speak like a human, or an angelic spirit, but in a sacrosanct manner, as pure and sole God. His word is His will: angels exist by the power of His word; He speaks like lightning and thunder, like fire and a flash: who could withstand His word? However, Scripture denotes the Word of Jehovah to be threefold: One is the Word of God, Jesus Christ our Savior, who is described in this brief and concise saying: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. All things were made through Him, which were made," etc. John 1. Then also, the word of God is that by which He rules and commands, or ordains, heals, performs miracles, and declares all things to humans: Thirdly, this very thing is also called and is the word of God, by which the people are instructed and formed for the kingdom of God: And all these things are comprehended in the Lord Messiah alone, through whom all things were created, and through whom humans are healed, sanctified, and saved.

However, Jehovah speaks words to the world either immediately proceeding from His essence, as when His words were heard on Mount Sinai by the Israelites, not without their ineffable and dreadful astonishment: or mediately, and this in multiple ways: For sometimes He Himself speaks through His Angels and Archangels; sometimes through Urim and Thummim (Exod. 29. 30. Levit. 8. 8. Num. 27. 21. Deut 33. 8. Jud 20. 12 etc.); sometimes through Patriarchs, Kings, Prophets, Apostles, and other upright men, as the entire Holy Bible together with the New Testament testifies; and to those men He speaks, either through visions or through dreams: for through visions God spoke much with humans, and especially with Prophets, in which He showed them very many spiritual things, which they in turn proposed and publicly declared to the people at His divine command: Hence Prophets were called Seers, as if seeing the will of God in a certain vision, as in 1 Kings 9. Similarly, God spoke with Abraham and also with Solomon, Joseph, Samuel, and other Patriarchs and Prophets, indicating future events to them through dreams, and teaching them how they ought to piously order their lives and actions, and to warn others about future prosperity or adversity.

C H A P. V.

That by conversation or speech of God a Seer or Prophet is immediately made:
And concerning the quality, property, and laws of a true Prophet, which he cannot transgress.

Conversation with God is no light matter, because from it a person is illuminated inwardly and outwardly and immediately becomes a Prophet and Seer, since a holy splendor, adhering to the mind of that person, elevates him above his brethren, and seems to exalt him as if to the third heaven, so that he perceives spiritual secrets not to be revealed to mortals. We have a most excellent example of this in Moses, who, from frequent conversation with God, was illuminated in such a way even in his outward face, that the Israelites could not bear or look upon his face shining with exceeding brightness, so much so that when he wished to speak with them, he had to cover his face with a veil. And without doubt Moses received his first prophetic power from that time, when Jehovah appeared to him from the bush in the likeness of fire, and spoke to him: From that, I say, address or conversation with God he received his prophetic power. In the same way, it undoubtedly happened with Adam, Eve, Noah, Abraham, and other Patriarchs, with whom God conversed, so that they were indeed illuminated inwardly and outwardly by that divine conversation, and thus shone before the people above others and prophesied to their children: Hence it is that God himself calls Abraham a Prophet, Genesis 20, and likewise in other places: For this illumination removed all diseases and infirmities from the human body, and inwardly also extinguished, consumed, and removed all sins and transgressions from his soul, since this divine splendor does not dwell in a sinful soul; because that which is holy has no communion with that which is not holy. Therefore, for a Prophet of Jehovah to be truly such, and not a Pseudoprophet, these properties are required in him, namely;

First, that he enjoys the spirit of God, without which he cannot be a Prophet, as is shown in Numbers 11:25. Secondly, that God makes himself known to him by the power of His Spirit, either through visions, or through dreams, or shows him His own likeness, as He revealed Himself to Moses, Numbers 12:6. Hence he is called a Seer in many places of the Holy Scriptures, such as 1 Samuel 9:9 & 19, and 1 Chronicles 19:29, and 2 Chronicles 12:15, and 10:7. Thirdly, that he speaks nothing but what Jehovah has commanded him, Numbers 22:8. For a true Prophet cannot transgress the command of Jehovah by doing anything great or small, as is gathered from Numbers 22:18 and Numbers 23:1. For Jehovah puts the word in the mouth of the Prophet, Numbers 23:9. And hence it was that Balaam could not curse what Jehovah had not cursed, Numbers 23:12. And Balak himself also uttered words of this kind, by which the aforesaid are confirmed: "Behold, I have come to you; can I now by any means speak anything? I will speak that very word which Jehovah has put in my mouth," Numbers 23:1. Fourthly, that he be a man with open and uncovered eyes, or having uncovered eyes, seeing the vision of the Almighty; Hence in Numbers 28:3 it is said of Balaam the son of Beor, "the saying of the man whose eyes are open." Fifthly, that he be a strong hearer of the words of God, and that he knows the knowledge of the Most High, and sees the vision of the Almighty falling down, but with eyes uncovered, according to Numbers 24:16. "The saying of him who hears the words of God, and knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling down, but with eyes uncovered." Sixthly, that his words or prophecies are always true, and never false: For this is the difference between him and

--- Page 299 ---
...and a false prophet, as appears from *Deuteronomy* 18:21. Seventhly, that he not presume to speak in the name of God what He Himself did not command him to speak, and that he not speak in the name of other gods, according to that [passage], *Deuteronomy* 18:21. For he who is truly endowed with the Spirit of God cannot acknowledge foreign gods: so powerful and sublime is Jehovah above other gods, who are creatures and the works of His hands. For all demons and angels were created by Jehovah, the sole creator of all things. Ninthly, that he be a bodily messenger of the commands and will of Jehovah his God, with whose Spirit he is imbued, as we find in *Judges* 21:4. Tenthly, that he may see things future as well as present, for example, 1 *Samuel* 9:9, and 14:18, and 1 *Kings* 20:20. Hence therefore Balaam says, *Numbers* 24:17, "I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near." Eleventhly, that he be anointed, 1 *Kings* 19:16, 1 *Samuel* 10:1. Whence prophets are called "Anointed of God" no less than kings. Twelfthly, that he always stand before God, 2 *Kings* 3. Similarly there are many other laws of the Prophet, all of which to recite in this place would be too long, and perhaps even tedious.

CHAP. I.
*On the various differences of divination according to the ancients.*

[Large decorative woodcut initial P]
Porphyry is said to have touched upon two divine inspirations, one of which
is said to occur mostly or commonly in sleep, the other in wakefulness,
where the inspired and agitated ones prophesy while so awake that they even
use their senses: But indeed Iamblichus, regarding truly prophesying and agitated
souls, maintains that although they seem to sleep, they do not truly
sleep, and also when they seem to be awake, he denies that they are truly
awake, saying furthermore that this happens because the inspired ones do not
act in the manner of men: But we, rather assenting to Porphyry's opinion,
deny that the presence of the divine Spirit entirely removes and takes away the use of human
senses; but rather we say that it so submerges the effect of these (senses) by its divine
movement, that it appears no more, either to the Prophet himself or to those standing by, than a flame
of a candle exposed to solar rays. But, since we have discussed these more fully in previous
sections, we will omit them in this place: nevertheless boldly affirming with Porphyry,
that the states of prophecy come to them, either in sleep or in wakefulness,
as sleep and wakefulness are sincerely estimated by us and without any exception.
*Recent Magi hold that the inspiration of divination occurs in a threefold manner, namely, either in frenzy, or in ecstasy, or in sleep: And this division of prophecy into its species
we do not entirely reject, inasmuch as it closely approaches our opinion: We there-
fore derive our doctrine from these words of the sacred Scriptures. To the Proph-
ets God Jehovah makes Himself known either through vision, or He speaks to them through a dream: But
not so Moses: for Jehovah speaks to him face to face, and shows (Himself) not indeed in riddles,
when he beholds the likeness of Jehovah, Num. 12. 6. For from these words we gather,
that the first kind of Prophecy, more excellent than the others, is that revelation which imme-*

CHAPTER II.
On the first and highest species of prophecy.

It is read in the sacred scriptures, *Genesis 32:30*, that *Jacob* the Patriarch saw *angels face to face*, as if this was something singular and great at that time, that such grace would only be granted to anyone inspired or breathed upon by the inspirer, that he might be permitted to look upon an Angel of God face to face, and so familiarly with

C 2 him

--- Page 302 ---
20	TRACTATE I. SECTION II. PART I. BOOK II.
to converse with him, as *Jacob* did, *Genesis 32:1 & 23*. Similarly it is said, *Judges 6:22, "Gideon saw the Angel of Jehovah face to face"*, so also likewise, the Angel of God appearing to Manoah twice or thrice, and speaking to him, and performing miracles, it is read, *Judges 13:21 & 22, "Then Manoah said to his wife: 'We shall surely die, for we have seen God.'"* From which it is clear that the real appearance of an Angel at that time was almost no less miraculous than the vision of God Himself in His own essence; and therefore it is established from this that the immediate appearance of God, that is, made to a Prophet in His own likeness or image, was held to be a truly most rare and ineffable blessing. And yet we understand from the Holy Scriptures that such and so great grace was granted to Moses especially above other Patriarchs and Prophets: For in *Numbers 12:6* it is said: *"To prophets God makes Himself known either by vision, or speaks to them by dream; But not so Moses: For Jehovah speaks to him mouth to mouth, and shows not indeed in riddles, but he beholds the likeness of Jehovah."* From which it can be gathered that Moses, by this favor of Jehovah, excelled all others, not only the prophets of his own time, but also those of

were led by the sound of music in a frenzied state: This is indeed clearly demonstrated in *1 Samuel 19:20-24. Saul sent messengers to seize David, and each of them saw a company of prophets prophesying, and Samuel standing, who was presiding over them. Therefore, the Spirit of God came upon Saul's messengers, so that they also acted in a prophetic manner. When they reported this to Saul, he sent other messengers, who also acted in a prophetic manner, etc. Then Saul himself went there, etc.* But the Spirit of God also came upon Saul himself, so that, continuing immediately, he acted in a prophetic manner until he reached Naioth in Ramah: where he himself also stripped off his clothes and acted in a prophetic manner before Samuel: thus he lay naked all that day and all that night: Therefore they are accustomed to say; Is Saul also among the prophets? From which it is clear that these Prophets acted in a frenzied manner, and having stripped off all their garments, poured forth prophetic words by leading dances naked; Nor would I have you believe that Seers are seized or possessed by true madness or frenzy (this word being understood, of course, as it is commonly used among men), but we call this species of divination 'frenzy' because the whole prophetic person is rapt by the power of the divine Spirit against the natural movement and sense of the body, so that by common human judgment it is considered as madness, which in reality is nothing other than a movement and state of the body, foreign and alien to the human soul and senses, which is truly called alienation, because the Prophet then becomes, through the presence of the divine Spirit, an alien man, or other than he was before, according to that saying, *1 Samuel 10:6. The Spirit of Jehovah will rush upon you, so that you will prophesy with them, and you will be changed into another man. And ibid. 9. And He changed his heart into another.* The Magi, however, subdivide this frenzied species of divination into four species again, of which, in the first, one skilled in philosophy is accustomed to draw and attract to himself from the heavens the secret power of the celestial spheres, and as it were, the soul of each of them, by the virtue of certain natural things found here on earth and corresponding to them; by binding and uniting that soul of the sphere to his own soul, he illuminates his spirit and renders it prophetic: And since such an attraction of a celestial spirit or soul does not occur from the entire heaven, but from some particular orb or sphere of it, and indeed nine spheres of the ethereal heaven are enumerated, namely the primum mobile, the starry heaven, and the orbs of the seven planets, and consequently also, the souls of these spheres are attributed to the nine Muses, therefore, I say, the name of this species of divine frenzy is dedicated to the Muses; so therefore there are found as many traces or degrees by which the powers of the higher things are enticed to the souls of the lower things, as there are spheres in the heaven, of which indeed the lowest is in the moon, influencing vegetables; Whence it happens that the attraction of such a soul downwards to the earth must be done by the magical virtue of some vegetable, suitable to it by its own nature and disposition, whether it be a root, or a fruit, or a tree, or an herb; Indeed, this sphere also relates to stones and metals, inasmuch as it is in the place of the celestial earth; whence it has the greatest power over the elemental earth. The method of operating through these magical natural things consists in binding or suspending them: Thus they say that among vegetables, the herbs *Verbena and Theangelica* contribute to prophecy; and among stones, *Selenites and Hyænia:* And other such things are explained more fully by Albertus Magnus and other Magi who have written on these matters.
The second degree, ascending upwards, is in the sphere of Mercury, which relates to animals, and considers various mixtures of natural things by which drinks and foods are prepared: Thus professors of Magic teach that if someone devours a mole's heart, fresh and still pulsating, by attracting the soul of this sphere to himself, he acquires divinatory power, so that he can foretell future events, and so in other cases.
The third degree is in the sphere of Venus, which relates to powders, suffumigations, odors, and ointments; whence by their virtue its nature is attracted to lower things. The fourth is in the sphere of the Sun, to which words, voices, and symphonic songs are referred, by whose sweet harmony the discord of darkness is cast out and expelled from the soul, and thus

the soul itself is thus raised, and as it were, strengthened: For they say that Timotheus excited King Alexander to fury with sounds: thus we read in Holy Scripture, 1 Samuel 10: "You will meet a company of prophets coming down from the high hill with lyres and with tambourines, and flutes, and harps before them, who will prophesy." And 2 Kings 3:15: "But now bring me a musician." So it was, when the musician played, that the hand of Jehovah came upon him, etc. From which it is clear that Elisha himself, a man most full of divine inspiration, used harmony as a very necessary instrument for prophecy. Thus also the fury of the evil spirit possessing Saul was mitigated and turned into a milder nature by the melody of David. But now, to turn to other histories, we find it written in Aurelius Augustine that a priest of Calama was accustomed to evoke himself at will from his body into a rapture or ecstasy by a certain plaintive melody, etc., and similarly in other cases. The fifth degree of this species corresponds to the sphere of Mars, in which vehement imaginations and affections, and movements of the soul are comprehended, for experience teaches us how many alterations an irascible affection of the soul can produce in the body. The sixth degree corresponds to Jupiter, in which consist the discourses of reason, deliberations, consultations, purity in morality, justice, and religion, and sometimes induces immense admiration, by whose stupor fantasy seizes man, and leads him beyond natural sense and actions: Whence it happens that then the mind, as if free from its burden, renders itself apt to receive the inspirations of the heavens or of divine powers. The seventh degree is attributed to Saturn, because it holds the more secret intelligences and tranquil contemplations of the mind: Whence the mind, made freer by speculation, entering into the realm of wisdom, remains in it with admiration, as if suspended in equilibrium. The eighth degree is in the eighth or starry heaven, which observes the position, motion, rays, and light of celestial bodies: Here also the artisan works with images and characters constructed according to the rule of the Magi, by which miracles are performed. The ninth and last degree corresponds to the Prime Mover, by whose virtue man is rapt from the consideration of material things to the contemplation of formal and spiritual things, since this degree carries man's free will, as if by wheels, hither and thither, and introduces man to the divine contemplation of God and intelligences, and renders the human soul apt for the society and familiarity of supercelestial Spirits.

The second species of divine fury is that which, by means of expiations and solemn rites, directs and exalts the middle part of man's soul into its supreme part, the mind, and makes it, as it were, a worthy and uncontaminated temple of God, whence it happens that then this soul, partaking of divine wisdom, and as if intoxicated with supercelestial nectar, is filled with the Prophetic Spirit. But we can refer this species to vision and audition, because this fury sometimes happens either through clear vision or through an express voice, as can be gathered everywhere from sacred writings: Such prophets are also said to have existed among the pagans: Bacchus for the Boeotians, Epimenides for the Chians, and the Erythraean Sibyl, etc. And the ancient Magi dedicated this species to Dionysius.

The ancients imagine the third species of divine fury to have proceeded from Apollo, whom they called the mind of the world. This, with preceding vows, mysteries, adorations, and certain other sacred artifices, or arcane concoctions, by which the Prophetic spirit is copiously drawn from on high, causes the soul of the Magus to rise above his own mind, joining it to Angels or good intelligences, or rather, according to our opinion, elevating the soul into the mind, and sublimating and raising both the soul and the mind upwards beyond the sight of the material world into the spiritual world: Thus we read in 2 Esdras 14:38: "And a voice called me, saying: Ezra, open your mouth and drink what I will give you to drink." And I opened my mouth, and behold, a cup

Trustworthy historians also relate (so that we may now wander a little beyond the limits of the sacred Scriptures) that a certain rustic, digging the earth with a plow in the fields, found a certain golden vessel filled with a most noble liquid, which, when he thought it to be dew from heaven, he washed his face with it and also drank; Whereupon it immediately happened that he was renewed and exalted both in goodness of soul and excellence of wisdom, and in beauty of body, so much indeed that he was straightway made and became a porter for the King of Sicily from a herdsman; This indeed occurred in the time of King Ostus, and is moreover confirmed by the testimony of Papal letters. CHAPTER V.
*On the twofold vision in wakefulness.*

We call that a vision which either appears externally to the eyes of the body in wakefulness, or is perceived internally by spiritual eyes, as if in a mirror and in the light of the divine Spirit itself, by which one is inspired, both in sleep and in wakefulness. Indeed, very many examples have been left to us by histories, both sacred and heathen, concerning vision, both of Prophets, and also of those not inspired by any prophetic spirit, appearing externally to open eyes. For to begin with the Prophets, we read that Jehovah appeared to *Moses* in His own likeness and image, as has been said, sometimes in a dark cloud, sometimes also in a pillar of fire, and sometimes in the form of fire in a bush, etc. Thus God wrestled with *Jacob* in the form of a man, whence Jacob said; *I have seen the Lord face to face. Genesis 32:30.* Angels also very often appeared to many Patriarchs and Prophets: Thus an Angel presented himself to *Hagar* and *Manoah* and his wife, and likewise to *Joseph*, husband of *Mary*, and to others, by this kind of manifest apparition or vision. But *Eliphaz*, friend of *Job*, also narrates his vision in this manner, *which occurred to him in wakefulness with open eyes, in the horror of a night vision, when deep sleep usually takes hold of men, fear and trembling seized me, and all my bones were terrified, and when a spirit passed before me, the hair of my flesh stood on end; someone stood, whose face I did not recognize, an image before my eyes, and I heard a voice as of a gentle breeze; Shall mortal man be more just than God? etc. Job 3:13.* From which we gather that this vision can again be understood in a twofold manner: namely, either *by itself* without conversation, or with address and speech; For without address or voice was that vision which appeared to King *Belshazzar*. *Daniel 5:5. In the same hour, fingers like a man's hand appeared writing opposite the lampstand on the surface of the wall of the royal palace, and the King watched the joints of the writing hand, etc.*

There is, however, a certain kind of vision in wakefulness that is more internal and hidden, which is perceived by purely spiritual eyes from the divine spirit, through invisible light and splendor, as if in a most polished mirror. And this kind of vision is either *with ecstasy* or *without ecstasy; with ecstasy* was that vision of *St. Paul*, by which he was caught up into the *third heaven, where he confesses to have seen wonderful and ineffable things:* And likewise that of *St. John* which he explained in his Apocalypse: For these two seem to acknowledge, even with explicit words, that they were caught up and as if seized by ecstasy: Similarly, that vision of *Ezekiel* does not seem to differ much from ecstasy, and was even an ecstasy, *Ezekiel 1.* But a vision without ecstasy presented itself to *Stephen*, as he awaited death and the malice of men, concerning which it is written thus in *Acts 7.* *But when he was full of the Holy Spirit, gazing into heaven, he saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of the power of God, and he said, Behold, I see the heavens opened, etc.* But *St. Peter*, in *Acts 11:15*, also excellently describes the eyes and the medium in which and through which an object of this kind is seen; *I, he said, was in the city of Joppa praying, and I saw a vision in an ecstasy of my mind, a certain vessel descending, like a great sheet, etc.* Where by 'ecstasy of the mind' he understands the spirit illuminating the mind, and consequently they seem to acknowledge that the eyes beholding that vision were spiritual: Thus also *Micaiah* says, 2 *Chronicles 18:18. I saw Jehovah sitting on His throne, and all the host of heaven standing on His right hand and on His left, etc.* Therefore, in spirit, as if in a mirror, with spiritual eyes, the Prophets perceived these visions, and therefore, as it seems to me, they were not entirely free from ecstasy in these visions of theirs: Furthermore, there is still another kind of vision and hearing, by which, as if in a mirror, Prophets were able to see things done in distant places, and explain them by vision, and therefore also

CHAP. I.
*Of the arrangement and division of divine dreams.*

[Large decorative initial 'S' depicting a figure in a landscape] All prophetic and divine things differ from those which arise from natural causes in this, that the latter originate from the fantastic and the rational or intellectual spirit, when these are united, while the former are induced by the illumination of the mind or active intellect, that is, by the union of the divinely inspired Spirit with the soul, by which an illuminated person sees future events in sleep: and indeed, all the more so in sleep, because when a person is awake, the soul, through the allurements of the senses, is drawn away from celestial contemplation to lower and sensible things, that is, from unity to the multitude of material particulars: But truly, when the senses are at rest, the soul applies its entire power to the mind and intellect, and consequently is more intent on truth. These dreams, moreover, arise through mere revelation, either directly from God, or also made by some angel divinely sent: And indeed, the sacred Scriptures make frequent and extensive mention of these apparitions in sleep, concerning which we shall write more copiously below. However, for the sake of a better method, we have digested the entire nature of dreams into the following distinction.

C A P. II.
*Concerning the supernatural and true dream.*

**P**rophet Daniel says *chapter 2:20: "Blessed be the name of the Lord from everlasting to everlasting, for wisdom and might are His; And He changes the times and the seasons, He removes kings and raises up kings; He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those who have understanding: He reveals deep and hidden things, and knows what is in the darkness, and light dwells with Him." And Daniel said to King Nebuchadnezzar: "The mystery which the king has asked, the wise men, the magicians, the soothsayers, and the diviners cannot declare to the king; but there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, and He will make known to you, O king, what will be in the latter days."* From which we gather that it is necessary for the revelation of truth to emanate from Jehovah alone, and not from another, because He Himself is the source and origin of all truth. Hence it follows that true dreams proceed from God alone, and therefore we have not foolishly called them supernatural. From this also comes the fact that Joseph said to Pharaoh's servants, who had dreamed, *"Do not interpretations belong to God? Gen. 40:8."* And to King Pharaoh, asking for the interpretation of a dream, Joseph replied; *"It is not in me: God will declare Pharaoh's prosperity by answering, etc. Gen. 41:16."* Therefore, a dream of this kind is called *true*, because it always remains (like the word of God) infallible and certain; and it is called *supernatural*, because it proceeds either immediately from Jehovah Himself, God Most Good, Most Great, or mediately through His ordination, from His messengers, namely Angels and Archangels: From Jehovah, I say: For thus a vision appeared to Abraham, in which Jehovah, appearing immediately to him, foretold the future, that his descendants would be strangers in a land not their own, *Gen. 15:12.* Likewise, *Gen. 20:2* it is written that God, coming to Abimelech *in a nocturnal dream, said to him: "Behold, you shall surely die, etc."* So also it is read *1 Kings 3:5 at Gibeon*

The parabolic and veiled (things) of King Nabuchodonosor required the help and explanation of Daniel, a man inspired by the divine Spirit, (as seen in) Dan 2 & 4. And similarly Daniel's dream expressed in chapter 7: "I saw in my night vision, and behold, four winds of heaven were fighting on the great sea, and four great beasts were ascending, etc." For this was an enigmatic speech concerning four kingdoms or Monarchies rising up on the earth; which enigma indeed the Angel explained: So also the vision concerning the fight between the ram and the goat, chapter 8, and so in other cases. Moreover, the ancients divide the true dream into four types, of which one is the morning dream, which
                                                                                                                                                           fit

--- Page 313 ---

occurs between sleep and waking: Of this kind was that dream of Samuel, 1 Sam. 3:4, in which he, between sleep and waking, heard Jehovah calling, thinking it was the voice of Eli, and indeed even a third time in succession: Another dream is one that someone sees about another, such as was the dream of Nathan the Prophet about David, 1 Chron. 17:3. Thus also in Roman histories we read that Augustus's physician preserved the life of his lord, who was languishing with illness, by advising him to go out into battle the following day against Mark Antony, because if he had not done so, he would have been slaughtered by the soldiers of Brutus and Cassius, who were invading his tents, along with the others found there, as Valerius Maximus testifies. The third type of dream is that whose interpretation is shown to the dreamer himself through a nocturnal vision: thus Nebuchadnezzar's dream, which neither the wise men, nor the magicians, nor the soothsayers, nor the haruspices could explain, was revealed to Daniel through a vision by night. Dan. 2:19. The fourth type of true dream is that in which the same thing that occurred before in a dream is repeated again: Thus Pharaoh's last dream of seven full and beautiful ears of grain, and of seven others thin and blighted, confirmed the earlier dream of seven beautiful and fat cows, and of seven others ugly and wasted with leanness. For both dreams signified the same thing, Gen. 41. And here concerning the judgment of dreams, we ought to observe that, where a preceding dream is confirmed by another subsequent dream, there exists the best indication of truth.

C A P. III.

On natural, diabolical, and vain dreams, which are not from God, and consequently deviate from the truth.

A dream that occurs naturally happens in two ways, namely, either when the dreamer is in his natural disposition, and then those things usually occur in the dream which have been done or made or said, and thus one sees at night in a dream those things which he did on the preceding day: The reason for this is that the anxious mind offers to the soul things to be thought about, and through a certain imagination, as if really seen, those things which it either saw, or heard, or even proposed to itself on the preceding day: or such a dream occurs when he who sleeps is unnaturally affected by illness, and thus sometimes dreams of things which he vehemently desired, or which he had previously impressed upon his mind. A diabolical dream, although it can be numbered among metaphysical and supernatural things, nevertheless, because it is sometimes contaminated by deceptions, and sometimes mixed with truth, therefore we have placed it here by itself, and in its own nature: Thus therefore the Devil sometimes acts in sleep, so that he excites deceptive and fraudulent dreams, by which he may ensnare the human race and more easily impose upon them: for he is accustomed to delude men in two ways through such dreams: either, namely, by the snares of despair or by the allurements of pleasure. The last kind of dreams is called vain and empty, in which nothing pertaining to the Devil's snares or to the truth of a future event is found. Moreover, this very thing seems to happen to the dreamer from an adventitious illness: for this kind of dream is accustomed to occur either in health or in illness: in health, namely, on account of gluttony from foods and drinks mixed together, and sending vapors upwards into the head, which, forming various kinds of meteors in the imagination, produce vain images: but in illness on account of a strong impression of images in the imagination, and thus in a dream those things occur which neither are, nor ever

--- Page 314 ---

nor ever were, as very often happens to those affected by Melancholy and phrenitis (frenzy):
Similarly, even a dreamer existing within the limits of health, because of the predominance of one of the four natural humors, sees various, but empty and vain things in a dream: for example, a sanguine dreamer is accustomed to dream of red, airy things, of feasts, music, love, festivity, and pleasantness, because such a humor naturally inclines people to those things; Similarly, a bilious person is accustomed to see yellow and fiery things, quarrels, war, weapons, contentions, anger, and fervor in dreams solely from the predominance of such a humor; just as a phlegmatic person perceives white things, and is concerned with waters and things pertaining to water, such as ships, fish, sailors, navigation, and other such things; and thus likewise melancholy perceives blackness in dreams, and sees terrible and horrifying things, and is struck by the horror of dreadful visions, all of which are nothing other than mere imaginations and empty things.

Abdala the Arab says that when someone sees a dream or a vision in a dream, this operation proceeds from the strength of the imagination, which is then said to be stronger when the intellect is more illuminated by its rays and freer from the deceptions of the senses. But indeed he concludes that to understand true dreams comes from the strength of the mind or the active intellect: From which it is clear that if the human intellect and reason are overwhelmed and lulled by excessive commerce with the flesh and senses, or if the imaginative or fantastic spirit is left crude and unpolished; then it cannot receive the empyrean rays of the intellect, and the ideal images of its spirits, or even if it does receive them, it nevertheless becomes utterly useless for retaining and perceiving them. Therefore it is necessary for him who desires to receive and perceive true dreams, to keep his imagination free and pure from the stains of the senses, flesh, and world, and to diligently beware and take care lest it be disturbed—

--- Page 315 ---
D E S O M N I I S. 33

be distracted by perturbations or worldly affairs at the time he wishes to dream: such a spirit, I say, is to be considered most apt for prophecy, because it adheres more to reason and intellect than to sense: Hence it happens that this spirit is the most polished and clearest mirror of all images emanating from things everywhere, receiving the splendor of mind and intellect no differently than it was capable of visible and material light, while it adhered to the senses: **This** spirit, I say, occupied with the senses and external things, can perceive things as far as the sight of matter is concerned, so that it can discern nothing beyond or above the visible object: but truly if it is engaged with spiritual matters, by receiving the essence of the invisible rays of the intellect, it will behold all things, and nothing in the entire world will be hidden from it, if only it consents to the divine will.

Therefore, when someone wishes to prepare himself for true divination through dreams, let him be sound in body and mind, neither burdened by food or drink, nor suffering from want or sadness, and let him be free from vices most hostile to the Holy Spirit, let him seek his bed chastely, and, to say it in one word, let his soul be pure, clean, and free from every harmful thought: these things being prepared, an Angel, through the Spirit, will announce the truth to us, and the human mind will receive into itself sparkling and refulgent rays and images from supercelestial minds, which will effectively impress upon the polished fantastic spirit, as if into a divine mirror, the visions which it discerns in the Divine Spirit, so that this mirror, now rectified and illuminated by divine rays, will present and reveal future things to the wise dreamer far more certainly, clearly, and effectively than any ordinary intellectual inquiry or rational discourse, by the revelation of true dreams from Jehovah.

First of all, therefore, to obtain such grace, it will be necessary for the dreamer to *commend himself to God with prayers and supplications*: For even the Philosophers themselves seem to agree on this, that if someone prepares himself for sleep without fervent prayers, by which he commends himself to God, the dream will be altogether ineffectual for him: because by the power of prayer, the rays of the soul most easily penetrate to the spiritual heaven, without whose spirit and light we cannot spiritually discern future things.

Hence, says *David, Psalm 141:2, "Let my prayer be set forth as incense before thee, the lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice, etc."* And *Proverbs 15:8, "The prayer of the upright is acceptable to God;"* And again, *"Jehovah hears the prayer of the righteous: Ibid. 19."* For prayer is so efficacious that by the magnetic power of the praying spirit, the Divine Spirit is drawn from higher to lower realms and united with the spirit of the one praying; by which union the Divine Spirit carries the human spirit into the empyrean spirit; in the midst of which, as in a most polished mirror, where no fiction or falsehood is found, the truth of every thing is beheld.

By this path, therefore, the soul will be rectified from its sensual and fantastic filth, so that it can be lifted and elevated to the heaven of truth, in which the true ideas of things are discerned, even though it remains radically in the body: Thus also the light of a candle is accustomed by its rays to reach a thing distant by many miles, and just as a candle, the larger its flame, or the larger its wick when lit, is seen to penetrate further through the intervening air, so likewise, if the divine splendor, likened to the flame in a candle, and the spirit of the empyrean heaven, compared to the wick, are joined with the flame and spirit of the soul, it renders the human soul capable of all things, so much so that it can even look out to the periphery of the world, and contemplate and behold God himself.
