BOOK III.
On the inquiry into each native's own Daemon.

BOOK III. PART I.
On each Genius in general.

CHAP. I.
On the various opinions of authors concerning the Genius proper to each.

Porphyry thought that the Daemon or Genius proper to each one came from the Lord of nativity, that is, from the stars, and descended into man: but the opinion of Iamblichus seems to oppose this: for he denies that the Daemon proper to each descends from the figure of generation: but, he says, that it flows from an older principle than are the stars or the leaders of the stars: Therefore, he wishes that each one's proper Daemon should not proceed from some part of heaven or the elements, but rather from the whole world, and from the multiform life and multiform bodies therein, through which the soul passes descending into generation, and acknowledges that that Daemon existed in the archetype before the soul slipped into generation: as soon as the soul receives him as a guide, the Daemon himself, the fulfiller of lives, etc., is present. Maternus, however, a man skilled in Astrology, adhering more to that opinion of Porphyry than to this of Iamblichus, seems to assert that the acquisition and origin of one's proper Daemon comes from heaven and the stars, and yet he seems likewise to disagree with Porphyry in this, that, while the latter seeks the Genius from the star of nativity, as has been said; the former says that it flows either from the Planets having more testimonies of dignities and strength at the point or time of nativity, or from that Planet whose house the Moon entered after that which she occupies when a man is born: Similarly, the Chaldeans, disagreeing with Iamblichus, and partly agreeing with Porphyry and Maternus, namely in place, and partly also differing from them with a varying opinion, say that the Daemon or Genius proper to a native
                                                                                                l 3                does not

--- Page 368 ---
86 TRACT. I. SECT. II. PORT. IV. LIB. III.
...does not arise except from the Sun and Moon: Therefore, they also seek it from them. But others (of whom there are very many among the Hebrews) believe that this (Genius) must be sought from some cardinal point of the heavens, or even from all of them: But indeed, those versed in common or vulgar Astrology are accustomed to seek the good Dæmon from the eleventh house of the celestial figure (whence that house is also called the good Dæmon); just as, conversely, the evil Genius of a nativity is sought, according to some, from the sixth house, inasmuch as it denotes bodily afflictions and illnesses; or rather, according to our opinion, we can deduce the disposition of the Genius from the 12th house, inasmuch as that is the place of the native's enemies: for what is more malicious to the human race, what more adverse, than a Cacodæmon (evil spirit)? Hence it is also, that according to some, this domicile (house) is called Cacodæmon or evil Dæmon. From which it is clear that although there is a certain way and method of knowing one's own Genius through astrological rules and observations, yet that way is so abstruse, and so overwhelmed by the senses and darkness of false opinions, that it is even considered more impossible to investigate the truth of this mystery by the path of the stars, than to make gold by the doctrine and writings of the Alchemists. And just as we see that we act mostly by opinions in the detection and investigation *a posteriori* of God and true nature, so also, without doubt, although the truth of this matter is to be declared by *a posteriori* demonstration, nevertheless, because we only show the thing itself according to our imagination, therefore we cannot truly say or assert that it is so, unless experience itself clearly demonstrates the effect of our concept: This is also what Porphyry seems to imply when he says: _"If anyone knew the figure of the nativity and found the lord of the figure, he would find his Dæmon, and through it would be saved from the fate of the nativity: but it is impossible to know it and to find this (Dæmon), because the rules of Astrology are incomprehensible and uncertain, and many disagreements are inherent in them, and they are assailed by many, etc."_ By these words he seems to confess that although in Astrology there is a certain way of investigating the Dæmon or Genius of a nativity, nevertheless, that way, due to the multitude of rules and their oppositions, is almost impossible: However, we will declare below that there is a certain way of finding one's own Dæmon by astrological reason, which way, however (I will frankly confess), is more supported by opinion than by demonstration or infallible truth: For we confess with Iamblichus and others well-versed in the most sacred inquiry into this matter, that each person's Dæmon and guide originates or is derived from an older, higher, and more metaphysical principle or origin, than from the stars or their rulers: Therefore it will be necessary for us to resort to divine divination, so that we may have the most certain truth concerning the stars: For divination, to use Iamblichus's words, _"can teach the nature and effect of the stars without art."_ Therefore, although the Genius is found with difficulty through Astrology alone, it is found easily through divine Divination: But more on these matters below.

**C A P. II.**
_On the appellation of the Genius, how it descends with the soul of the native, and on its office in the native's life._

The native's own Dæmon is therefore called Genius, because, as it were, the Dæmon of Generation, that is, as if slipping down from the disposition of the world and the circuits of the stars, which are involved in generation, it descends to the genesis (birth) and into the born individual. Iamblichus, however, seems to describe the manner of this descent in this way: "Each person's own Dæmon," he says, "is not distributed from some particular disposition of the heavens or elements"

--- Page 369 ---
CONCERNING THE INQUIRY INTO EACH PERSON'S NATAL DAEMON. 87
...is distributed, but from the whole disposition of the world, when the soul descends, with [that disposition] ruling and accommodating a certain Daemon to it, an executor of life, whom the soul has chosen. But as for its office in the native's disposition, it itself, as Jamblichus testifies, reconciles the soul to the body of the born, and takes care of the life communicated to it, and directs the vivifying power of the soul, continually presents principles to thought, and the native is compelled to do such things as it itself brings to mind; it governs us to that extent, until, consecrated to sacred things, we replace the Daemon with the Lord: For then the Daemon, yielding to God, either ceases from its work, or contributes to the same. But each person's own lot is attributed to the soul, while it descends from the whole body and life of the world, according as it then relates to it, and that lot is led and fulfilled by a certain Daemon. From these things, therefore, Jamblichus concludes that it is impossible to indicate certain events of causes, since we cannot comprehend the concurrence of all causes, except through inspiration.

--- Page 370 ---
88 TRACT. I. SECT. II. PORT. IV. LIB. III.
...are distributed with equal authority or number, in opposition to the good ones. However, more excellent Magi, striving against Jamblicus' Monad, attribute three guardians or Dæmons to each person at their birth: the first of these they call sacred, which, according to the doctrine of the Egyptians, is assigned not by fixed stars, nor by wandering stars, but by the superior heaven, namely from the empyrean, through God, the president of Dæmons himself, to the descending rational soul. And they say that its office is to direct the life of the soul, and always to present good thoughts to the mind, and to act assiduously within us by illuminating, although we do not always perceive it, but when we are purified and live tranquilly, then it is perceived by us, and as if it speaks with us, and strives assiduously to lead us to sacred perfection. The second is called Genius, inasmuch as it is the Dæmon of generation, which descends from the disposition of the world and the circuits of the stars that are involved in generation. The third, however, they wish to preside over the profession and mastery of the born person, which they say is infused by the stars, and provides the soul with customs and a path to worldly dignities and honors. And indeed, they assert that this is found and proven by experience: that if the profession agrees with our nature, similar to us, and the Dæmon of profession is in harmony with the Genius, life becomes more tranquil, happy, and prosperous. But indeed, if we engage in a profession contrary or dissimilar to the nature of the Genius, life is rendered laborious for us and disturbed by discordant actions, etc.

C A P. V.
Is a bad spirit and a Devil given to each person?
And do the souls of the impious become Dæmons after their
separation from the body?

Just as a Genius or good spirit is given to each person, so also a bad and diabolical one is assigned to him; both of which seek union with our spirit and strive with the utmost effort to entice and attract it to themselves, and attempt with every endeavor that it be mixed with them no differently than wine with water. Man, therefore, is in the middle between these two contending forces, and is in the place of free will for himself, so that he usually grants victory to whichever he wishes. For the good spirit or Dæmon makes us similar to itself through good works conforming to it, and transforms us into Angels by uniting us to itself. Hence, in Malachi 4:6, it is said of John the Baptist: "Behold, I send my angel before your face." Concerning which transmutation and union it is written elsewhere: "He who adheres to God becomes one spirit with Him." But also evil Dæmons strive to make us conformable and united to themselves through evil actions. Which we can also deduce from the words of Christ, by which he says of Judas: "Did I not choose you twelve, and one of you is a devil?" And Trismegistus also seems to argue the same: "When a Dæmon flows into a human soul, it sprinkles seeds of its own nature; whence the soul, sprinkled with such seeds, pregnant with fury, then gives birth to wonders, and whatever are the offices of Dæmons." For a good Dæmon, when it flows into a holy soul, elevates it to the light of wisdom; but an evil Dæmon, infused into a wicked soul, incites it to thefts, murders, lusts, and whatever are the offices of evil Dæmons. For good Dæmons, according to Jamblicus, most perfectly purify souls, and being present themselves, they give health to the body, virtue to the soul, security to the mind, they delete what is deadly in us, they foster warmth, they make us more effective for life, and they always infuse light into the mind with intelligible harmony. However, concerning this, there seems to be a great [disagreement] among philoso-

--- Page 371 ---
CONCERNING THE INQUIRY INTO THE NATURE OF EVERY DEMON. 89
a disposition arising among philosophers, whether the souls of men become Demons after their separation
from the body: Indeed, the opinion of the Magi, as Porphyry testifies, is that souls are converted into the nature
of Demons and become pernicious, as they are: Whose opinion, indeed, seems to be confirmed by the words
of Christ concerning Judas Iscariot cited above: And to this, Mercurius Trismegistus also
seems to assent in express words, when he says: *Indeed, a wicked soul, when it becomes a Demon, is commanded to take on a fiery body in obedience to God, thence, infused into a wicked soul, it scourges it with the whips of sins, etc.* But the
souls of the good are transmuted into the nature of Angels by the virtue of the administrations of good Demons.

*BOOK III. PART II.*
Concerning the discovery of the Genius of nativity.
*CHAP. I.*
*Concerning certain principles to be understood before we*
*proceed to practice.*

Before we proceed to the practical part of the generation of a Demon, it will be
necessary first to understand the things conducive to that practice, as without them, it is no
less impossible to attain the perfection of this art than to arrive at a complete
knowledge of Geometry without considering points, lines, surfaces,
and bodies: First, therefore, it must be understood that, just as in Geometry
a point is the origin and principle of that art, so also in this inquiry,
as in every other thing, God is the sole unity and principle
from whom the most worthy, first, and most powerful creatures of all
immediately flowed: which relate to the numbers of the trinity, which are most simple
and, as it were, digits subsisting by themselves; as denarii (tens) relate to digits (ones), inasmuch as they are immediately
derived from digits: Therefore, the creatures of the denary number are more powerful, because
they approach closer to the number of pure formality: And just as the supersubstantial
numbers relate in dominion to the creatures of the denary number by commanding and ordering,
so also the creatures of the denary number are placed before the creatures of the centenary
number in the announcement of the ordination of the first president,
just as these themselves further, in matters ordained by the supreme Lord through his arcane
and abstruse counsel, according to the announcement and admonition of the spirits
or creatures of the denary number, fulfill the will of the King of kings by
further imparting to the inferior spirits, or those of the millenary number,
what is due and necessary to them, and by distributing equally among themselves,
according to each one's dignity, what is established for them by the unique creator, and announced to them
by the creatures closest to him. Therefore, by the creatures of the denary number, we
understand the orders of Angels, one of whom indicates the will of their supersubstantial king
to another downwards, in their own manner of whispering, and finally, Archangels
and Angels of the lower orders announce what they have received from the Seraphim and Cherubim,
and these, in turn, convey the will of the spiritual Emperor to those below,
and the sacred and supercelestial leaders of minds always exist for the constitution of humans
who are descending, as we shall explain more fully below. But by the
creatures of the centenary number, we understand the spirits or Demons ruling over the
celestial spheres: whose role it is to preside over the middle soul of man and the souls of other
things, which pertain to life and the principle of life. From these, therefore, is gathered
the Genius of each individual man, which we were striving to seek with such great effort.

--- Page 372 ---
90 TRACT. I. SECT. II. PORT. IV. LIB. III.
each person's Genius, which *Porphyry* strove with such great effort to seek and desired, without any consideration of a supercelestial Daemon dominating him: Which indeed in a learned man was a very great error, and an indication of extreme ignorance, as *Jamblicus* also seems to acknowledge in very clear words. Finally, by the spirits of the millenary numbers, we denote Daemones presiding over winds, elements, and regions of the world, who have significant dominion over flesh and body, and make and prepare the way by which the mind of the highest heaven, and the soul or spirit of the middle [heaven], may be introduced into the body through the lowest air. What we mean by simple, denary, centenary, and millenary numbers we have most fully shown in the book of this Tractate on divine numbers; where, namely, by simple numbers we described the simplest nature and harmony of the supersubstantial essence, or a point and as it were a unity; by denary numbers, the radical or linear composition of the empyrean heaven, that is, the proportion of light with its spirit; and by the centenary number, the square or superficial mixture of the ethereal heaven in light and spirit; and finally, by the millenary number, we demonstrated the corporeal or cubic disposition of the lowest heaven. Therefore, from the empyrean heaven, these Angels or Daemones are said to look upon the bodies of the seven planets: so that the spirits of the centenary number, who are called Olympic, can do nothing without the nod, command, and consent of those who indicate God's ordinances to the Daemones of the middle region of the world and ensure that they correctly execute, according to the divine will, those things which have been ordained and constituted by God.

*C H A P. II.*
*Angels of the Empyrean Heaven, Leaders of the Mind, and Born Guardians, who*
*Preside over the Planets and their Daemones.*

According to the Hebrew fathers, also more recent Magi, and especially Abbot *Trithemius*, that man endowed with admirable wisdom, seems to attribute to Saturn the Angel called *Orifiel*, who is also named *Zabkiel* by others; to Jupiter, *Zachariel*, or, as others would have it, *Zadkiel*; to Mars, *Samael*, or according to others, *Camael*; to the Sun, *Michael*, although others assign *Raphael* to it, less correctly, as it seems to me: For just as *Michael* is said in the Apocalypse to be, as it were, the leader of spiritual war, who drove the Devil downwards under his command, and freed the empyrean heaven from his strife and contention, and from all impurity, so also the celestial Sun has power of life, purification, multiplication, and of supreme strength and splendor in the visible world, and indeed all the more, because God placed His tabernacle in it. The Angel *Aniel* presides over Venus, *Raphael* over Mercury, and *Gabriel* over the Moon. And this is what Abbot *Trithemius* seems to assert in these words: It is the opinion of many ancients that this lower world is governed by the ordinance of the first intellect, which is God, through secondary intelligences: to whose opinion the conciliator of Physicians assenting says: "*Seven spirits appointed to the seven planets from the beginning of heaven and earth, etc.*" These seven Angels, therefore, are those most powerful ones, under whose dominion not only the wandering stars (planets), but also the Olympic Daemones themselves, to whom it was given to immediately preside over the planets from their creation, have their operation: For just as God, the Monad, looks upon the Angels of the empyrean heaven, so also do they [the Angels of the empyrean heaven] look upon those of the ethereal heaven, and these [of the ethereal heaven] finally upon those of the elemental heaven.

C A P. III.
*Concerning the Olympic spirits, and first concerning those who are subject to the aforesaid Empyrean Angels, from whom the Genius of nativity proceeds.*

Those spirits the Magi call Olympic, who dwell in the firmament and in the stars of the firmament; whose office it is to decree fates and administer fatal events, insofar as God has approved, ordained, and permitted it; For neither a bad Daemon, nor a bad fate can harm beyond or contrary to the ordination of the Most High God. But each of the Olympic spirits will teach and effect that which the star, to which it is assigned, portends: And yet all of them can bring nothing into effect without divine permission: For God alone is He who gives them both the power and the ability to effect: And therefore, when they bring about a bad fate from a superior Angel, in whom there is nothing evil, they are corrected by the divine will: Therefore, all things, both supercelestial and celestial, as well as sublunar and infernal, obey God, the creator of all.

C A P. VII.
Concerning elemental spirits, & those presiding over the regions of the world.

It must also be known that in the lowest region of the world spirits or Demons are found of many offices: since some preside over the 4 winds, and are appointed to the four parts of the world: But because winds are spirits proceeding from God, therefore their dominions are attributed to Angels of the highest region: Wherefore Michael is appointed to the East wind, Raphael to the West, Gabriel to the North, & Nuriel or Uriel to the South: Similarly, Cherub presides over the element of air, Tharsis over water, Ariel over earth, Seraph over fire, or according to Philo, Nathaniel. Each of these spirits, however, is a great prince, & having power of much liberty in the dominion of their planets & signs, and in their times, years, months, days, & hours, & their elements, and parts of the world, & winds, and thus each of them dominates over many legions. These contribute to the disposition of the human body at birth, & of other creatures.

C A P. VIII.
Concerning the Angels, who are attributed to the hours of each day.

To each planet is attributed some supercelestial Prince, as has been declared in the premises, namely Michael to the Sun, Anael to Venus, Raphael to Mercury, Gabriel to the Moon, Orifiel to Saturn, Zachariel to Jupiter, &c. Wherefore when we desire to find the predominant Angel in any hour of any week & day, we must proceed as has been declared in our Astrology regarding the discovery of the predominant Planet in any hour of the day of the week: For example, the Sun claims for itself the first hour of Sunday, beginning from sunrise, Venus the second, Mercury the third, Luna the fourth, Saturn the fifth, & so on for the rest, as has been declared in the previously cited place: Thus we also say, that Michael, who is the spirit of the Sun, will possess the first hour of Sunday, Anael, who is the spirit of Venus, the second, Raphael, who is the spirit or Angel of Mercury, the third, & so on for the rest.

C A P. IX.
How signs and planets & consequently the Demons presiding over them are dedicated more to one place on earth than to another & therefore are seen to exercise & execute their powers there more than elsewhere.

We gather from Cosmographical doctrine that planets claim their own climates: Thus the first climate is attributed to Saturn, the second to Jupiter, &c. We also find from the documents of the Chaldeans that other regions are subject to these or those signs of the Zodiac: For example, Aries presides over Germany, Britain, Gaul, Syria, Palestine, Poland, Burgundy, Sweden & from the cities, Naples, Florence, Capua, Verona, Bergamo, Padua, Marseille, Zaragoza & other similar ones. Taurus presides over Media, Persia, Cyprus, Poland, Russia, Campania, Rhaetia, Switzerland, Lorraine, Britain, Ireland, & from the cities, Bologna, Mantua, Taranto, Pavia, Palermo, Turegia, Breslau, Leipzig, &c. And so concerning the remaining signs according to

according to the order handed down by us in our book on Astrology. Where we have declared which regions and cities each sign of the Zodiac dominates. Therefore, once these things are known, it will be very easy to find the more familiar places of those spirits here on earth; And consequently, we must diligently observe the region, city, town, or place which are under the sign of the house in which the Lord of the place of the good Daemon or Genius of nativity is found.

C A P, X.
**\*For what reason were natural Magi solicitous in inquiring about their own Genius of nativity?\***

Magi versed in Cosmology used to inquire about the Genius, so that by its knowledge, familiarity, and protection they might avert fate, and so that by its will the works of life might be rendered effective, fortunate, and prosperous. Hence Porphyry: *If anyone were to know the figure of nativity and the Lord of the figure, he would find his Daemon, and through it he would be freed from the fate of nativity and would escape fatal things, and would be happy.*

C A P. XI.
**\*Concerning the method of finding one's own Genius.\***

Magi used to first inquire about the name and nature of the Daemon or Genius of the native, and then they endeavored to render the Daemon itself familiar and approachable to the native through convocations, adjurations, prayers, characters, and other ceremonies of that kind: Therefore, when we wish to investigate it, first let us seek the lord of the eleventh house in the hour of nativity; Then let us see what kind of Olympic spirit is attributed to that Planet, and furthermore, what kind of Daemon is given to the sign in which the Lord is found, afterwards it must be seen how these two spirits agree with each other: Moreover, the spirit of the sign of the eleventh house must also be especially considered: Therefore, as the spirit of the Planet agrees or disagrees more with these, so will the native's state of life be, either more constant or inconstant. Some, and indeed not foolishly, choose the spirit of the Lord of the first house for the Genius of nativity, inasmuch as it is chiefly concerned with life: Then also the spirit of that mansion of the Moon, in which the nativity occurs, must be observed; Furthermore, attention must also be paid to which wind blows more powerfully from which region or angle of the world, and which element predominates more than others at the time when the birth occurs, namely whether the time is hot and fiery, or windy or rainy, or prone to freezing and ice: For by these very things we shall perceive the predominant element, and consequently the more powerful spirit, and we shall elicit the one predominant among the elements. Having diligently considered these things, it will not be impossible to gather the aids or impediments of the Genius of nativity, and thus we shall know whose planetary dominion, whose assistance of house and sign, whose blowing of wind, whose elemental rule, whose presence of place, that is, of region or city, can more or less contribute to the Genius of nativity: And by this way and discourse, undoubtedly, by diligently weighing and contemplating those aforesaid things with careful observation, we shall be able to bring forth great things.

C H A P. XII.

*How one can make his Genius familiar and*
*affable to himself, having known its Planet,*
*nature, and name.*

Iamblichus relates that there is a twofold treatise concerning the Demon of each individual: *One sacred or Deific*, which invokes the Demon from supernal causes: and this indeed does not use the exploration of each one's geniture, but more universally cultivates and cares for the Demon above nature: *Another artificial*, which invokes the Demon from the circuits, and this one is concerned with generation, and explores each one's geniture, and more particularly cultivates and cares for the Demon according to nature: That one therefore pertains to the divine and supernatural and principal guide of the mind, and treats of Angels and Archangels, the primary guardians of men; this one indeed deals with the Olympic spirits or the guides of the middle soul, who are subject to Angels and Archangels. And these Olympic spirits are those whom, according to Iamblichus, those who operate artificially concerning nature are accustomed to seek out in an orderly manner from the Decans, that is, from the faces of the signs and from the dispensations of influences, and the images of the sky, and from the stars, and the Sun and Moon, likewise from the poles and all elements and the world, that is, according to what we said above, from the disposition of the degrees of the house of the Genius, the spirit of the same sign, and the Demon, lord of the house of the good Demon, or the eleventh, and the Demon of the stronger region of the world, and the Demon of the element predominant in the world at the time of birth, etc.

Iamblichus, moreover, proposes the method of invoking each Demon in these words: *Through God, the one lord of Demons, the invocation is made, who both from the beginning defined his own Demon for each, and in sacrifices, according to his own will, shows it to each. For always in the order of sacred operations, the lower are called through the higher divinities:* Wherefore indeed among the Demons, one leader of those who hold principality concerning generation, sends his Demon to each individual: Therefore, after his own is present to each, then he reveals the worship suitable to himself, and makes known his own name and the proper method of his invocation: And such Demons are superior, and always benign, inasmuch as their seat is above the region of the Fates: There is, however, another order related to those mentioned, whom we have called Olympic: Who indeed, as executors of fate, bring good or evil to the born, and yet are sometimes hindered in their actions by the divine will through superior leaders, who are powerful messengers of the divine will: For example; the spirit of the Sun and the actions of the solar body itself were hindered by the power of Archangel Michael, God willing it so, such that for the space of one day the Sun seemed to stand still in the time of Joshua: By the power, I say, of Michael, because he himself is the supercelestial prefect and moderator of the celestial spirits dwelling in the Sun, and is always ready to carry out the will of his God, both in exact execution and in the moderation of actions in the solar globe.

But to return to the matter, when we desire to have familiarity with the Genius or Olympic spirit of nativity, we must first observe that time when the lord of the angle of the heaven of nativity has familiarity and a good disposition with the Lord of the eleventh house of the geniture; And let them be so disposed, if indeed it is possible, that they may be found in those houses in which they were at birth; Furthermore, if it can be done, let a time be chosen in which the same wind blows that blew at birth, and let the temperament of the elements also be such as it was in the geniture, similarly also the mansion of the Moon and the disposition of the Sun

--- Page 378 ---
96 TRACT. I. SECT. II. PORT. IV. LIB. III.

...their disposition, as far as possible, may be suitable. This being thus arranged, let the characters of the planets, which were lords of the ascendant and the eleventh house, be sealed and engraved on metal plates according to the nature of the planet; and also, those characters are to be engraved at the times of exaltation and strength of each of the aforesaid planets, at the very hour and day in which these planets predominate. Therefore, let the native hold these plates, and at the adapted time, as before, and indeed on the very day and hour in which the Spirit or Genius predominates, let the invocation be made. And the Magi say that Olympus and its inhabitants in the form of spirits offer themselves spontaneously to men, and render their services to them even unwillingly; how much more then, if you seek them, will they be present? But the wise admonish us not to think that divine invocations of spirits are similar to human ones, or that the ineffable can be compared to the effable, or that those things which surpass every limit and every determined mode can be compared with human commands and mandates, whether these be defined or entirely undefined. Therefore, foolish and trifling are the inventions and contrivances of men for conquering Daemons and subjecting to their command those whom no mortal can compel against their will. Wherefore, this work is to be accomplished only by the permission of God and by His invocation, who alone has power and authority over Daemons:
*Which Bacon also seems to acknowledge in these words: "In this lies the error of those who, neglecting the laws of both Theology and Philosophy, believe that spirits are subjected to them, and that spirits are petitioned by human will: for this is impossible because human power is far inferior to that of spirits, or, because they err more in this, that through certain natural things which they use, they believe that malignant spirits can be invoked or figured, and they still err when men strive to appease and attract them for human utility through invocations, deprecations, and sacrifices: for it would be incomparably easier to obtain from God or from good spirits whatever a man ought to consider useful."*
Therefore, God alone and especially is to be entreated with prayers, so that knowledge and familiarity with one's own Daemon may be granted to the native, because to Him alone, and to no one else besides Him, do the Angels of the first order, or of the empyrean region, obey; and Daemons or spirits of the middle heaven, called Olympians, first render obedience to God, and then to the superior Angels; and finally, the lower orders are subjected first to God, then to Archangels and Angels, and afterwards and in the last place, they obey the Olympian spirits, so that every inferior order of Angels holds the superior in honor. And hence it is said that superiors act upon inferiors, and rule and govern them with a certain distinguished dominion. Therefore, pious Magi prescribe such a prayer to novices, by which they may invoke the help of God, the leader of Daemons, so that they may acquire knowledge and familiarity with their Genius.

*Almighty eternal God, who created all creatures for Your praise and Your honor, and for the service of man, I pray that You send my Spirit and Genius N.N. of the Solar, Mercurial, Jovial, etc. order, who may inform and teach me what I shall ask him with justice and piety, and that he may show me those things necessary for my instruction in the arts and experiments of my ancestors and philosophers, or that he may show me the way to preserve health, and to rightly order my life, or the way to preserve myself from enemies, etc. But let not my will be done, but Yours, through JESUS CHRIST Your only begotten Son, our Lord, Amen.*

Wherefore, having considered the aforesaid things most excellently, you also ought, prepared in this manner, to pour forth this prayer devoutly to God from the deepest affection of your heart, in order to achieve your desires.

CAP. XIII.
*How, having known the figures of two nativities, we may most easily gather,*
*which Genius is more powerful, so that from this, we may discern*
*which of those two in every action prevails over the other.*

Having known two men between whom there is familiarity, or who ought to live
together; a good Artificer, learning the nativity of each, and
eliciting and observing in each nativity the Lord of the eleventh house and its spirit,
can most easily gather which of them has a Lord above the other,
either in play, or in prosperity, or in battle, or in honor: Indeed,
if you find that the Lord of one's eleventh house, and its good Daemon,
is; (and) the other's cacodaemon or spirit of the twelfth (house), and that this cacodaemon of the second (person)
is stronger and more powerful and more fortunate in the heavens than the good Daemon of the first, there will be
between these companions or associates a nature most hostile, most dangerous, and most
inimical to the other, and what is more, this malice of the other will always prevail over the former.
Thus we read that Mark Antony and Octavian Augustus, joined in singular friendship, were
often accustomed to play together; But since Augustus always departed victorious, a certain Magus
admonished Mark Antony in this vein: *What have you to do, O Antony, with*
*that youth? Flee him and avoid (him); For, although you are older by birth, and more outstanding*
*in experience of affairs, also more illustrious in lineage, and as commander of many, you have endured many wars, nevertheless this*
*youth's Genius your Genius fears, and your fortune flatters his fortune;*
*unless you flee far away, it seems that everything will defect to him.* Of this kind, without doubt, were the Genii
of Pompey and Caesar, of Alexander the Great and Darius; And although the armies of Caesar, and likewise of Ale-
xander the Great, were merely like a handful; and not great in respect to
those forces which Pompey and Darius led, nevertheless the Genius of one was
stronger than the Genius of the other, and thus in visible and spiritual battle the armies
or legions of one and the other fought, and consequently the weaker Genius, being conquered, succumbed.
Nor indeed does this opinion of ours disagree with the sacred scriptures: For first it is read
thus in Isaiah; *the Lord of hosts visited the high ones on high, and the kings of the earth*
*on the earth etc.* Concerning which conflict of spirits and rulers we also read in Daniel 10:
namely, concerning the prince of the kingdom of Persia and concerning the prince of the Greeks, concerning the prince
of the people of Israel, and their conflict with each other. And the poet Homer also
seems to acknowledge this same thing in these verses;
*Such a great rumor spread through the heavenly court,*
*When the fierce Gods rushed into alternate battles.*
*Phoebus Apollo fought against Neptune,*
*Pallas Athena contended against Mars,*
*Diana's quiver had opposed Juno in battle,*
*Swift Cyllenius (Mercury) pressed Latona with his darts.*

But it also sometimes happens that the Genii of two nativities are opposed to
each other by nature: and yet one is not more powerful than the other, but the malice
of one equals the malice of the other: indeed it can even happen that the Genius of one is the ca-
codaemon of the other, and vice versa. For we see in Astrology that there is the greatest
friendship and enmity between Planets; for example, between Saturn and Venus,
as we have shown in our Astrology: Of this kind, beyond doubt,
were the Genii of the two brothers Eteocles and Polynices, whose malice as well as
power was equal: Wherefore both exulted in victory, both (met) mutual hands
in death.

died, and what is more, their Genii did not cease to wage war in a spiritual battle after death; indeed, so much so that even the pyre itself, on which they had been burned together in the usual manner, was observed after death to be divided and split and separated as if by mutual hatred.

<p align="center"> *An Apologetic Epilogue.* </p>

Kind Reader, do not therefore believe that I deserve the name of an impious Magus, because I have spoken about the names of spirits and some of their characteristics: For I want you to know that I have spoken only by the mouth of others, and have committed to writing those things which I myself would deny following, or to which I would deny giving certain credence: Nevertheless, I wanted to discuss these things here, partly for the sake of method, and partly for the reason by which Logicians are accustomed to teach fallacies: namely, not that they might deceive men, but that men might beware and be forewarned lest they be deceived: for in this way, in this place, we have also depicted the empty, or rather uncertain, wisdom of the ancients, so that you, instructed in a more certain way, may follow the true, simple, and pious path with better hope and confidence, find the genuine Genius of each person, and recognize the true secret of abstruse Astrology. Therefore, in the preceding part of this book, we have done what painters usually do when they arrange inferior colors on the margin of some distinguished effigy, so that the beauty in the inner part of the delineated image may be more adorned. Pay attention, therefore, Good Reader; And if you have diligently considered things as they are, perhaps you will not reject our labors, these toilsome ones, nor will you waste your own effort or oil. Farewell.

<p align="center"> *BOOK III. PART III.* </p>
<p align="center"> On the True Discovery of the Genius. </p>
<p align="center"> *C H A P. I.* </p>
<p align="center"> *The Author's Opinion on the Discovery of Each Person's Own Genius or Natal Daemon:* </p>
<p align="center"> *And First, Concerning the Angel Proper to the Human Mind.* </p>

Indeed, Iamblichus did not speak ineptly, refuting Porphyry's unsound opinion, *that each person's own Daemon is given from an earlier origin than from the stars or the figure of generation;* For if we have rightly considered the matter, we will clearly perceive with the eyes of the intellect that some Daemon, proper to any of the stars, which we have called Olympic above, is the executor of fate ordained by the divine president, and not its corrector: For whatever God proposes to be accomplished by the stars and His Angels, all of that must necessarily be done by them and be carried out and committed to execution, whether for good or for ill, since all things move at His nod and obey His command. But indeed, the Angels of the higher heaven, inasmuch as they arise and are constituted outside and above the limits of fate from their creation, nothing
<p align="right"> evil </p>

--- Page 381 ---
DE CUJUSQ. NAT. DÆMON. INQUISIT. 99

...evil to man or the world, except insofar as they repay good or evil to each according to their merits; that is, they either assist with their presence him who is pious and good, or also, for his impiety, they leave someone in the power of an avenger. Therefore Porphyry very often opined that man, through the knowledge of his birth figure and the discovery of his Genius, is freed from the fate of his nativity, or through it becomes happy. Indeed, as Jamblicus truly said, the Daemon and guide of the mind and intellect is of an older and higher lineage and origin than those executors of fate, who cannot exceed or depart from God's commands by even a hair or a point. Indeed, there is greater power in the Empyrean Angels for relaxing fates, inasmuch as they are more worthy, more just, nearer to God, and more familiar than those of the middle or lowest order. Hence, greater power is given to them, because of their excellent justice, not only over men, but also over the inferior Angels themselves. For as it has been declared above, that the mind is something divine, not subject to passion, and not subject to fate, and consequently that man adhering to it, by the untouched virtue of his mind, will also rule over fate, so it follows much more from this that Angels of a superior order, who take the most diligent care of it, can achieve much in the ordering and direction of the mind in man, so that like a sailor against the fluctuating dangers of the world, and the bitter and rigid storms of fate, he may safely direct his journey to the desired port of happiness. But so that I may approach more closely to my opinion alleged before, and gird myself to discuss the contention of the ancient Philosophers in this matter, I would first of all wish you to remember (if indeed you have read the preceding with diligent observation) that I have spoken of three regions of the world, which we have called heavens, and of as many portions of the human soul, derived from them; of which I explained the first and supreme, namely the mind in the empyrean or rational and intellectual spirit, as being carried in a vehicle or chariot; the middle, however, namely the middle soul, in the intermediate ethereal or vital spirit with its prince, and its empyrean and supercelestial spirit, is carried downwards into the elemental region, from whose forms, and especially from fire, these kings (namely the supercelestial and celestial) are received, and finally covered by air until they are immersed in the earth and opaque bodies. Therefore, these things being known, it will be right to believe that just as the inner man contains three spiritual portions of the three regions of the world, so also, without doubt, each of these portions possesses its own proper Daemon or Angel, who has his nature and seat according to the dignity of the portion of the spiritual man: Hence it happens that the mind itself, a divine ray of God, immediately breathed forth from the supersubstantial essence, is received by the first and supreme hierarchy, where one of the Seraphim burning with most fervent love, and one of the Cherubim abounding in the fullness of knowledge, and likewise one of the Thrones full of divine justice and most replete with equity—these three, I say, selected from each order of the Epiphany, in honor of the Trinity, from which the mind flowed forth, sustaining the mind with fiery wings, and with burning love, knowledge, and justice, and surrounding it on all sides, lead it down to the second hierarchy of the empyrean heaven, and leave it in the custody of the Angels of that hierarchy, enriched and adorned with their gifts: Here, therefore, that mind is received into the intellectual spirit, as an active vehicle, which is likewise sustained by one Angel from each order of the middle hierarchy or Epiphany: namely, one Angel from the order of Dominions, as a leader in spiritual battles, and another from the order of Principalities, teaching reverence to princes and the way of returning to God; and a third from the order of Powers, indeed having dominion over malignant spirits: Therefore, that spirit, strengthened by their clarity, by a Zephyrean descent, carries the mind in its intellectual chariot

carrying [it] adorned everywhere with the flames of light created on the first day, it is led down into the lowest hierarchy, namely Ephionia; and in this way these Angels adorn that mind with its gleaming chariot with their duties and virtues, before they depart: and so now the mind with the intellect is received by the rational spirit, a spirit most limpid, most pure, and supercelestial, which seems greatly delighted and to exult in their presence: In this hierarchy, therefore, the mind is received with intellectual light by three Angels likewise, each of whom seems to belong separately to one of the three classes of the hierarchy's orders; Thus, one Angel is of the order of Virtues, to whom it was given from the beginning to perform miracles, for in this the virtue of God is said to shine forth: The second is from the order of Archangels, who is one of God's highest messengers or princes of God's messengers, who are like kings, princes, and leaders to the other Angels; The third, however, is from the order of Angels: These, I say, receive the mind in its twofold empyrean vehicle, with love and reverence: To whom one of the seven Archangels, who (according to Job 12:15) stand before the Lord, is assigned as an example of its parents for a guide, God thus commanding. From these things, therefore, it is clear that the mind possesses in itself the supersubstantiality, eternity, immutability, impassibility, and majesty of the divine essence, from which it sprang forth from the origin, and whose act it exists as. From the Seraphim it received the gift of fiery and deiform love, from the Cherubim, the fullness of knowledge and cognition, from the Thrones equity and justice, from the Dominations it has this, that it may emerge victorious in spiritual combat, and that it may dominate over the stars and fate, when it dwells in the fleshy earth, from the Principalities it is taught to revere its God, and to conduct itself modestly towards superiors, from the Powers it has dominion and power over the malignant spirits of the world; from the Virtues the faculty of performing miracles before the world and divine illumination, from the Archangels the gift of prophecy: Indeed, it is capable of all these things by its own nature, inasmuch as it is a deiform ray: Nevertheless, because by itself and in its nature it is above all orders of Angels, and consequently continuous with God, therefore without the covering of the virtues of the lower orders it could not gradually immerse itself into lower things, nor think about worldly or earthly matters. And since this divine essence, adorned with its empyrean covering, and immersed in an opaque body, because of the malignity, gravity, gloom, and manifold obscurity of its dwelling, cannot exercise this virtue of its own, or put it into execution, therefore God assigned to it a good Angel as a leader and guide, by whose assistance its dwelling or palace may be preserved from the malice and rage of the worst spirits, both corporeal and incorporeal, so that the middle soul itself may remain safe and unharmed from the assaults and violence of the Devils: Moreover, an Archangel sometimes enters the mind's dwelling, and joins itself with the soul and mind: For thus we read, Zechariah 2:3: "And behold, the Angel who spoke in me went forth," etc. Indeed, the sacred scriptures are most full of examples of this matter, as will appear more fully from what is said below: Here, therefore, the error of Porphyry becomes manifest, who vainly and frivolously believed that if one knew the figure of nativity and its Dominion, one could very easily find an Angel or Daemon, through whom one would be freed from the fate of nativity and made happy. For it is clear from what has been said that this Daemon, who has power over the operations of the stars, obtains its primary or principal place and dominion outside the region of the stars, and above the firmament in the supercelestial kingdom, so indeed that it is impossible to deduce its nature either from the stars, or from the quality of the figure, or from its Lord, since the power of such a Daemon is exalted infinitely above the nature of the heavens, nay indeed, it itself dominates the stars, and not the stars it, and therefore we cannot investigate its hidden disposition by inquiring into the stars. More correctly, therefore, Iamblichus

--- Page 383 ---
DE CUJUSQ. NAT. DÆMON. INQUISIT. 101

blichus asserted that the origin of the Demon, averting fate, is more ancient than can be known from the stars or from the figure of nativity: and therefore he denies that it would happen that, if the figure of nativity or its Lord or Demon were known, the native would immediately thenceforth be happy; and "*who, he says, would accept this guide to escape the decrees of fate?*" Therefore he concludes that this powerful spirit in man cannot be known except through divination: How this happens, however, we will say below. It is clear, therefore, that *Porphyry* only considered the celestial or Olympic Demon, proper to the middle or vital soul, whom we will declare below to be called Genius, that is, the Demon of the nativity or life of the native, and not that sacred and supercelestial one assigned to the mind, of which the former is concerned with the nature and life of the native, performing its function and duty fatally and by necessity: but the latter presides over both the soul, and the body and life, and therefore also over the middle Demon itself or the Genius of nativity, as its prince, and sometimes also over the stars and fate, dominating by divine will: "*Whence, says Jamblichus, this one reconciles the soul to the body, cares for the life communicated to the body, directs the life proper to the soul, constantly presents principles to thought, and we do such things as this one brings to mind, it governs us to the extent that, being appointed to sacred rites, we exchange the Lord for the Demon.*" And in this way we find that sacred Demon, who according to the doctrine of the *Egyptians* is assigned to the mind not from the stars, nor from the Planets, but from a higher kingdom, that is, from the very president of Demons and Angels (namely God), before it descends into its middle vehicle, which Angel, indeed, we will show below to be from the choir of Archangels.

C A P. II.
*Some examples taken from the sacred Bible and elsewhere concerning*
*Demons of this supreme order, serving pious men.*

[Q] Uoniam because of the fall of Adam, according to that [passage] in Wisdom 9: *For the corruptible body weighs down the soul, and the earthly dwelling depresses the mind that thinks many things, whence we deem difficult those things which are on earth, and what are present before our eyes we find with labor; But who shall search out the things that are in heaven? And who can know the thought of God, unless God gives wisdom, and sends His Holy Spirit from the highest?* therefore the guide of our mind, whom we have declared above and will prove below to be from the number of Archangels, has no commerce or familiarity with our body because of the pollution of the flesh; but is to it as a stranger, nor does it instruct or govern the mind in such a way that its mystery is perceived or understood in the body: it ministers only to the mind, and indeed to it alone, with spiritual teachings, so that if the middle soul adheres to the mind and neglects the sense and formal erudition of the elements, contaminated by the pleasures and concupiscences of the world, then also in some way, the body itself may taste the effects of the mind's wisdom: And although he, the primary Angel, conductor of the mind, may be unknown to the body of such a man, he is nevertheless seen by the eyes of the obedient middle soul (by the virtue and benefit of the mind) and also has some communication with it, by a certain spiritual whispering, even if it is not discerned by the opaque body: But indeed, when the soul, rejecting the Governance of the mind, is prone and inclined to the pleasures of the flesh and sensual appetite, so that the mind seems to be idle in the body, and neglects the body and its middle soul submerged in sensuality, and has fellowship with its good Angel, who n 3 inter

--- Page 384 ---
102 TRACT. I. SECT. II. PORT. IV. LIB. III.
among themselves they hold discourse in their own manner about the things of the supercelestial kingdom, and they forget lower things, unless insofar as they are led around by the corporeal dwelling: And a soul of this kind, I say, deserted by the mind, is then subjected to fate, and has for its supreme guide the fatal spirit which we have called a Genius, so that such a person can no more avoid fate or fatal things than a brute animal itself; For he does not rule the stars, because he cannot be wise, nor can he correct his fate, because he lacks a governor who has dominion over all evil, namely the mind and its guide. Hence therefore, according to that [passage] of *Hermes Trismegistus, Pimander 12*:
*it is decreed by fate that he who has committed something shameful shall suffer, and it is decreed by fate that some will be adulterers, some sacrilegious, etc.*
And although according to him all things are the works of fate, and without it, nothing corporeal exists, no good can do anything without it, no evil can be done without it, nevertheless we say that evil can be averted from the soul, obedient to its superiors, by the virtue of a good Angel and the wise instruction of the mind: For thus Adam lived before the fall by the virtue of his supercelestial guides, so that he never even tasted evil. Who then, according to the passage *Wisdom 9* previously cited, will ever be able to avoid this fatal cup, O Most Holy founder and creator of all things, unless you give wisdom and send your Holy Spirit from the highest heavens? With Him indeed present, we shall be filled and imbued with wisdom, and we shall be most replete with omniscience, so that, immune from the defilement of our parents, and made wise from being foolish, we may rule the stars and subdue the malice of the fates, and be made children of the living God through the grace of adoption. Then indeed, with the body cleansed and the soul rectified, the mind itself, and its Angel, will be familiar, both to the body and to the soul, and the voice and whispering of the sacred Angel itself will be perceived by the ears of the body, and thus he himself will sometimes appear in corporeal sight, as we can deduce from many passages of sacred scriptures, as well as from the authorities of trustworthy ancient writers; from which it is clear that prophetic spirits have shown themselves visible and presented themselves as companions to well-purified souls and prepared bodies: *For example;* in sacred Scripture we read that an Angel appeared to *Abraham, Hagar, Jacob, Gideon, Balaam, Moses, Joshua, Manoah's wife, David, Elijah, Daniel, Tobiah, Joseph, and Mary* the mother of Christ, Peter, John, etc. These Angels were undoubtedly those very ones who were the primary guides to the minds of those to whom they appeared, as if from birth the care of such people had been committed to them as their primary guides. Hence the Magi and ancient wise men attributed to each prophet among the Patriarchs and Prophets his own prophetic spirit: For they wrote that *Adam* had familiar companionship with the Angel *Raziel;* whose name in the Hebrew language seems to denote or signify a secret or mystery, and also the will of God; this certainly had the best relation with Adam, either insofar as he was the first chest, and as it were a sanctuary or a myrothecium, into which God had placed the mystery of humanity, which is His image, or insofar as through this Angel and the revolution of His divine Majesty He first acted. *Shem* also, the son of Noah, had *Jophiel* as his Angel, whose name signifies the beauty of God. To Abraham they attribute *Zabkiel* or *Zabdiel,* that is, the gift or bestowed of God, who is the Archangel having dominion over the Jovian star, whom others call *Zachariel,* that is, the memory of God. And certainly *Zabdiel,* not without reason, signifies the gift of God, and is said to preside over Jupiter himself, that is, the supreme God of the Gentiles, because, where there is the gift of God, there also is His virtue and prosperity: Hence Jehovah Himself and this Angel of His appeared so often to Abraham, made him so rich, endowed him with such great prosperity, and granted him such a complete age, namely one hundred seventy-five years, so that it is found written of him, that he died failing in a good old age, and of advanced years, and

And this is the cause of the change or confirmation of a kingdom into a monarchy, and again of the dissolution of that monarchy and its transfer to the governance of another. But now, to descend from sacred histories to those of the pagans, we find that very many others besides those who are recounted in sacred writings were inspired or breathed upon: Thus we read that Socrates was directed and governed by his Daemon, for he diligently obeyed its admonitions, and often heard its voice, and even frequently saw it in the form of a Daemon: Moreover, by the help of this sacred Daemon, Socrates is said to have avoided the malignity of fate: For when it was indicated by a certain expert in Physiognomy, after first inspecting Socrates' face, that he was most devoted to all vices and every wickedness of depravity, he himself sincerely confessed that he was prone to all those vices indicated by physiognomy, but by the governance of a celestial power he had restrained that fate of his and his evil inclination, and from then on had walked in the paths of justice and probity: Mercury Trisme-

But we deduce from the testimony of the wise that all intelligences, whether they are called created Gods, or Archangels & Angels, or Spirits, Daemons & Heroes, are comprehended under the term "Daemon" no less than various species are accustomed to be subjected to the same genus. And we say that Daemons dwelling above the stars are good Daemons. So also Olympic Daemons and those of the middle region of the world are good in respect to themselves, and indeed by themselves; but nevertheless, in respect to us, in whom they act by fate, sometimes they work good, and sometimes evil, and are called both good and evil. Thus, the Daemons of Saturn are called greater misfortunes, and Saturn itself is called an evil star and a greater misfortune. Similarly, the Daemons of Mars are named lesser misfortunes; while meanwhile the properties of the Daemons of Jupiter and Venus are the opposite. Therefore, the Chaldeans and Egyptians seem to distinguish Daemons into sacred (Daemons), and Daemons of the stars or of birth or nativity or of the natal figure (as) Lords, and elemental (Daemons), who are considered the worst of all.

*They wish Sacred Daemons to be those who are assigned by the very God of Daemons to the descending rational soul, universal and above nature. They say their office is to direct the life of the soul, always to present good thoughts to the mind, to act with continuous illumination within us, however much we do not always perceive that action in the soul. But when we are purified and live tranquilly, then the Daemon itself is perceived by us, and as if it speaks with us, and communicates its voice to us, present before in silence, and it strives constantly to lead us to sacred perfection. They also relate that with the help of this Daemon we can avoid the malignity of fate, which we read Socrates did. And the Platonists believe that men are helped by it in a wonderful way, both by dreams and by signs, averting evils and preserving goods more abundantly. And Iamblichus also seems to confirm those things with these sayings: He reconciles the soul to the body, cares for what has been communicated, directs the soul's own life, constantly presents principles to thought, and we do such things as he brings to mind. He governs us to the extent that, having been appointed to sacred rites, we substitute the Lord as our guide for the Daemon. Then this Daemon, yielding to God, either ceases from its work or contributes to the same. And elsewhere he says: This Daemon existed in the archetype before souls descended into generation. When the soul first received its guide, the Daemon itself stands by, subsequently fulfilling lives, and binds the descending soul to the body. It cares for its common animal (nature), directs the soul's own life, and whatever we reason, it presents the principles of reasoning. And we do such things as it brings to mind, and it governs us until, purified by sacred works, we take God as our leader instead of the Daemon. To whom (God), after this, the Daemon so yields that it either ceases in His presence or contributes to the same.*

Porphyry also says that with the help of this sacred Daemon, the malignity of fate is avoided. But we conclude that this Daemon is the superior of the three Daemons of the body, the guardian, leader, and guide of the mind, subjecting to the mind what is best, and repelling from it what is base, the director of discursive reason in good and virtuous matters, filling the inner intellect with wisdom, and thus having governance and dominion over the whole human being, and consequently also over the Daemons preceding it, no differently than the mind of a wise person over the vital, animal, or sensitive soul. For the mind, inasmuch as it originated from supercelestial parents, requires a supercelestial leader and guide on its journey to lower realms, who places it, with its friends, namely intellect and reason, into the light or soul of the middle heaven and its spirit, and joins all these together with the body, by means of more fluid elements, as we shall discuss more extensively below. From these things, therefore, it is evident that Archangels of this kind, with their leaders serving them, not only have dominion over the Olympic spirits, who

C A P. IV.

*Concerning the seven Angels who stand before God, and that each of them is a leader*
*of many thousands, both of princes and of more common and*
*inferior species of Angels.*

We gather from the instruction of the sacred scriptures, and also from the destined ordering of nature itself, that the supreme Archangelic princes are constituted by God in a septenary number, inasmuch as this alone is that primary and virginal number, from which and in which, and through which the one God, simply formal and super-substantial essence, mixes himself with unformed matter, so that from potentiality he may lead it to the actuality of waters or humid nature. With similar respect, the princes of the Archangels are chosen by the creator in such a number so that in the ternary number they may have a relation to the holy Trinity and their one God and Lord, and in the quaternary they may accomplish and perfect his commands and will in the material mass. Which indeed the Royal Psalmist seems to acknowledge in plain speech: *Psalm 103:20. Bless the Lord, you his angels, most mighty in strength, who perform his word, obeying the voice of his word! Bless the Lord, all his hosts, his ministers, who do his pleasure!* But, so that we may show the septenary number of these principal Angels with more ample testimony from the sacred Scriptures, we read *Tobit 12:15. I am Raphael, one of the seven angels who stand before the Lord,* and *Luke 1:19. I am Gabriel, who stand before God and was sent to speak to you:* And *Daniel 10:13, the Angel Gabriel says to Daniel: Behold, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, etc.* These therefore are three principal Angels from that septenary number of whom Raphael made mention in the place cited before, and each of these has dominion over one of the seven planets, namely, in such a way that they always stand before the Lord, obeying the voice of his word, and yet in the meantime also performing or executing his word both by themselves and through ministers, hosts, and powers placed under them and subject to them, who are constituted in the middle and lowest heaven, as we understand from the aforesaid words of the Psalmist: Hence it happens that, although the aforesaid seven Archangels stand before God, nevertheless they have dominion over the seven Planets and the Dæmons appropriated to them, and likewise over the fixed stars akin to them in nature and disposition: Thus we see, one and the same Emperor remained in Rome, to whom nevertheless Africa, Asia, and Europe obeyed; And again, the Governors of Africa, Asia, and Europe could stand before the Emperor remaining in Rome, while those kings who were accustomed to preside over each region of these parts of the world could accomplish or order nothing, except what was permitted and commanded by the governors, who nevertheless themselves
