DE SPECULATIVE PYRAMIDS OF SCIENCE. 191

Here therefore is the scope of our intention, kind Reader, when we make any mention of a formal or material pyramid; which I therefore wished to explain fully to you and others in this place, because it is the principal key or gate of our doctrine, through which access is open into the area of this Philosophy, indeed truly into all true natural science: But truly since few have been able to attain the secret mystery of the composition of the heavens, due to the lack or difficulty of true knowledge of these pyramids, I therefore wished to treat of them precisely and succinctly in this little book, so that those eager for this science may be able to arrive by so much a readier and more suitable way at the happy end and goal of their honest desire and wish.

Second Volume

SECOND TREATISE,
Concerning
THE PRETERNATURAL
HISTORY OF BOTH
WORLDS:
Divided into three Sections,

In Which }
The First, treats of the causes of meteors, both Macrocosmic and Microcosmic, and their effects in general.
The Second, treats of the particular impressions of meteors, both for good and ill health; and of the signs foretelling them past, present, and future.
The Third, explains precisely the method of averting the worst and harmful future events of meteors; of overcoming their present attacks, and finally, of restoring lost pristine health.

By the Author
ROBERT FLUDD, otherwise de Fluctibus, Esquire,
and Doctor of Medicine of Oxford.

--- Page 489 ---
History of the Preternatural Microcosm

The second treatise of the Microcosm, which is concerned with the art of Medicine, is divided into 3 Sections, of which

{
    The First treats of
    {
        Theosophical,
        Cabalistic,
        Physiological matters,
    }
    {
        the portion of Medicine, concerning which we have copiously treated in this present Volume.
    }

    The Second is divided into three portions; of which
    {
        The First treats of the salutary or curative part of medicine (which is called *hygieinon*), showing the method of preserving health, namely:
        {
            Supercelestial
            {
                By divine influx moving downwards.
                By the prayers of good people penetrating upwards.
                By piety of life resisting the assaults of wicked Demons.
            }

            Celestial
            {
                By the observation of malevolent affections, and by caution in avoiding their effects:
                By the knowledge of repelling the misfortunes of both Planets and fixed stars, and of preventing their malice.
            }

            Elemental
            {
                By the external quality of the elements. In which consists,
                {
                    Temperature of the place.
                    Season:
                    Disposition of time
                    {
                        Hot,
                        Cold,
                        Humid,
                        Dry.
                    }
                }

                With internal regard and peculiar to the body: under which are contained:
                {
                    Diet.
                    Constitution.
                    Age.
                    Motion & Rest.
                    Exercises.
                    Affections of the mind
                }
            }
        }

        The Second is concerned with preternatural, or unhealthy and morbid, meteors. See A.
    }

    The Third describes the skill of discussing and dispelling meteors behaving preternaturally. See B.
}

All of which are brought into a single Section, claiming for itself the capacity of a single volume.

The first treats of the differences of human meteors (phenomena) behaving contrary to nature, of which some are
    Fiery.
    Windy/Gaseous.
    Watery.
    Earthly.

The second deals with the causes of human meteors (phenomena) behaving contrary to nature
    Supercelestial.
    Celestial.
    Elemental.
    Corporeal.

The third has as its subject signs derived either:
    From supercelestial will.
    From celestial position.
    From elemental constitution.
    From artificial ordering of numbers.
    From the present condition of the body behaving unnaturally
        External, and these are either:
            Chiromantic.
            Physiognomic.
        Internal: namely those
            Which are indications of the heart and spirits: consisting in

TO THE BENEVOLENT OBSERVER,
HEALTH OF SOUL AND BODY
IN THE MESSIAH.

[Large decorative initial E] Now behold, Candid Reader, in the most holy and ineffable name of Almighty God, appropriated to Him alone, and in the living and fiery inspiration and divine breath of the symbolic characters of the indivisible Trinity, *namely, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit*, י. ו. and ה., I have happily begun to proclaim to the world some admirable and astounding mysteries of that wondrous name, namely יהוה, derived from them by a supersubstantial reason, and by meditating and reaching the goal without any mental obstacle, I have at last attained the end, completion, and summit of this work with a fortunate and desired degree of perfection. May my glorious God also grant that by the most powerful utterance of His unique, incomparable, and supreme name, and by its ineffable whisper, as well as by fiery arrows drawn from His quiver, stronger than all strength, the worst calumnies of Momus and the malevolent may be plunged into the Stygian waves of oblivion, the foolish babblings of the sons of ignorance may be submerged in the Lethaean lake, and the unhealthy reproaches of the proud and disciples of worldly wisdom may be repelled even to the center of darkness: For the ineffable word of the Lord (in which alone is truth and perfection) will remain forever: while the false deceptions of the Devil, the vain delusions of the world, and the deceitful phantasms of the spirit of darkness will perish, vanish, be reduced to nothing, and be driven into eternal exile from all human memory.

To you, therefore, O brothers of true doctrine and more abstruse philosophy, relying on the wings or pinions of divine mystery, and you, disciples of my order, removed from hateful derision, perverse obstinacy, and the worst malediction, and who desire to penetrate with me into the sanctuary of truth and the monastery of arcane theosophy of mysteries; to you, I say, indeed to you alone I turn the thread of my discourse and prayer.

And although I confess that I have brought this work to light, publicly promulgated it, and revealed it to your eyes by opinion and contemplation alone (with no practice preceding it), according to the limitations of my understanding and talent (which I know to be very small), nevertheless, if with the elevated mind of a true and sincere Christian you explore the matter a little more accurately as it intrinsically stands, you will perceive, with an open gaze and as if with illuminated eyes, that the principles of our sciences are to be derived from the sacred fount and origin of all truth, rather than from the vain and uncertain opinion of the pagans. Indeed, we consider it a kind of idolatry to venerate with such devotion and obstinacy the opinions and inventions of worshippers of foreign gods (neglecting the fount of all wisdom and knowledge), as if no erudition in the method of preserving health, in the diagnosis of diseases, or in the science of preparing and applying medicines for restoring pristine health could be acquired except from pagan spirits, namely, Greek, Arabic, or Latin schools. For by the excellent teaching of the Prophet, we are informed how impious and profane is this imitation of pagan doctrine, by which we are taught that it is not fitting to abandon the fount of all wisdom and to seek art, science, and understanding in foreign lands, as did the *Hagarenes, and those who were in Teman: for they never knew the way of true wisdom. Baruch 3.* To these differ-

--- Page 495 ---
...ference
the Prophet seems to argue a difference between the vain knowledge of the world, born from the uncertain opinion of sinful men and those overwhelmed by ignorance in the womb of darkness, and brought forth into the world by a kind of abortive, rash, and untimely effort, and that unique, sacred, sole, and true knowledge handed down by JEHOVAH God through the Word or Wisdom (which is the Spirit of harmonious discipline) to just men distinguished by piety.

Therefore, repeatedly considering the discrepancy between these sciences, namely divine and human, the Royal Psalmist (as one well-versed in both), exulting in the divine spirit, and as if spurred by the goads of truth, burst forth into these words: *Ps. 119. 125. I have become more intelligent than all my teachers, because the testimonies of God are my meditation: I am wiser than the elders, because I likewise keep your commandments.* This difference between divine and human wisdom the Prophet Daniel also very aptly indicated to King Nebuchadnezzar, *ch. 2. 27.* with such words: *The mystery which the king asks, the wise men, magicians, soothsayers, and astrologers cannot declare to the king; but there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, who will declare to you, O King, what shall be in the latter days.* The magicians and wise men of Egypt also confessed to King Pharaoh, with these expressed words, that the true knowledge of Jehovah surpassed and presided over their own magical arts: *This is the finger of God, etc.*

But I seem to see some already murmuring and smiling, who, plunged deeper into the abyss of unbelief and the mire of ignorance, will object: What do the sacred writings have to do with the art of medicine? Where are the differences, causes, signs, prognoses of diseases, and then the method of healing to be sought in the Scriptures of the divine word? Is it possible that in the sacred text remedies suitable for every disease can be found? To these I respond, as it were, with a single word (if indeed they wish to be considered wise): Read, read thoroughly, but also understand by reading; and I will undoubtedly satisfy your doubts. But if it has not pleased you to grant even a little honor to me and my works, I nevertheless implore you not to despise this Christian admonition of mine, otherwise relying on obstinacy or rather impudence; Flee from creatures, and listen to the voice of the Creator with fear and reverence; Adore Him alone, and His word joined with the Holy Spirit, lest you be considered disciples or followers of King Ahaziah, who, afflicted by a certain disease, commanded his people to consult Baalzebub, the false and filthy god of Ekron, neglecting JEHOVAH, the God of gods, to see if he would recover health from that illness: From which it happened that, the wrath of JEHOVAH being stirred up against him, he died, no help from the false god prevailing. *2 Kings 1:16.*

May JEHOVAH be with me, my refuge and bulwark of salvation, and may He exalt my horn on high, so that, with His benevolence assisting, I may taste and partake of the health-giving draught of His wisdom in this life, by which I may at last happily reach the summit of the true jubilee, and the pinnacle of Sabbath and rest, or the supreme gate of understanding, and closer to the divine presence, by propitious divine will, with a favorable omen, and the benevolent breath of the divine Spirit. Amen.

POSTSCRIPT.

[Large decorative initial N] Lest anyone be deterred in the reading of these our books, we would especially wish the Reader to be admonished that an exact knowledge of the Hebrew language is by no means required for their understanding; but that only a knowledge of Hebrew characters suffices for understanding this our work; since by observing these external or artificial figures, anyone will be able to proceed correctly to the merely formal characters, whether Metaphysical, or Physical and natural, and apply himself usefully to them: For nothing of mystery is found in these merely common and external characters, but in those truly spiritual and fiery ones, which lie hidden beneath these, like treasure in a chest, or a kernel in a shell, so indeed that these hidden characters are, as it were, the soul and life of these manifest ones. Therefore, only the shapes of those common characters should be kept in memory, since, apart from this alone, no Hebrew difficulty is required for this our work. And the letters are these. א.ב.ג.ד.ה. &c.

# Prelude concerning Principle in general.

[Decorative initial H] This word *Principle* exists in the Holy Scripture written in this way בראשית *Bereshiths*; that is, *in the beginning*; And that word descends from the primitive or root ראש; which signifies head, vertex, summit, pinnacle &c. But, if by Cabalistic reasoning we note the characters of this word with diligent observation, we shall investigate from them the order of the entire creation of the world, and we shall perceive all portions of the spherical machine differing from each other in property: For ר or *Resh* denotes in the first place a kind of void and emptiness, and consequently darkness; for *Resh* is a symbol of poverty and indigence: So also ש, on the contrary, is a symbol of repletion; arguing, namely, that that void and emptiness, or that solitude, is now filled with the presence and light of א or Jehovah; although *Shin* signifies fiery spirit, or illuminated waters: א finally is the medium and principle by which the void and the foul and squalid poverty of ר itself or the abyss, upon whose face was darkness, is removed, and the water or י hidden in the belly of ר is illuminated and animated, and י thus clarified and animated by light is converted into ו: which is a hieroglyph of the heavens. Hence, as the word ראש had its origin with ר or poverty, squalor, and defect; so the first principle of all things was void, empty, or darkness, because of the absence and defect of light and grace, called hyle and something in potentiality, inasmuch as it was destitute of all apparent grace and light, and consequently nothing in actuality; because every act is derived from the living presence of divine light. But when Jehovah, a monad lurking in the darkness of ו, and reflecting the ardor of His light into Himself, and consequently called a dark *Aleph* with respect to our capacity, wished to reveal Himself, that is, to shine forth from the darkness, then *Aleph* is called manifest: Hence in Moses the first word of its head was בראש; and then followed the name אלהים as if א appearing from a dark cloud: And thus is verified that [passage] *Job 12:22. He reveals the deep things out of darkness, and brings out to light the shadow of death.* And that manifest and lucid א is the first emanation from the dark *Aleph*, that is, the commingling of the rays of the lucid *Aleph* with the spirit of darkness: Which *Aleph* is now called *Iod*; which is the character and symbol of the number ten; in which, according to the common arithmetic, unity, that is, the dark *Aleph*, or shining only in itself as in a center or point, is joined with a cipher; that is, it is mixed with the spirit of darkness ר *Resh*: Hence the number ten among common people stands thus 10. in a mystical manner יא: inasmuch as where *Aleph* as unity makes the darkness of ר something actually appearing from nothing; that is, it renders what was deformed most beautiful. Hence א after י is a symbol of the first emanation from *Aleph*, hidden in the belly of hyle י, and therefore called dark by the Cabalists: wherefore it is taken for the Messiah or the hidden *Aleph*, which contains יהוה in itself, or by the very virtue of that Tetragrammaton; whose commingling at last with the now revealed spirit of darkness produces ש, which is an indication or exemplar of fire or created light, that is, of the illuminated Spirit. And hence it is that in this word ראש we see, as in a mirror, three images of the properties of the most holy Trinity; since the obscure *Aleph*, signified by ר, is compared to the *Father or unity*, the lucid *Aleph* to the *Son, the Word, or Duality*, and ש to the *Holy Spirit* proceeding from both; since the mother of the mundane spirit was darkness or hyle, and the informing progenitor of the waters or the said spirit was the lucid *Aleph*; so that it is evident that *Shin* proceeds from ר & א; wherefore in the aforesaid word it fills the third and last place: And hence we can consider that the great mystery of the Trinity consists in every Hebrew word, inasmuch as almost all roots, according to the Hebrews, are formed from three characters. But where the root exceeds the ternary number, there also is comprehended the mystery of the supersubstantial and substantial world: For example, that ineffable word יהוה denotes by י: the same as the lucid א looking down from a dark cloud, but nevertheless dwelling in the highest heaven of heavens: But indeed the three following letters are the roots of the created world; since its regions were formed after their exemplar, as we shall clearly demonstrate in the following [sections]. Therefore, as ש & ר are mixed with א, so they denote the act of the created world: For ר & ש are letters of the last alphabetical order, and outside the number of the 10 digits. Hence they denote composition; which indeed is not with God, and in the Archetype: Wherefore א & ש are two of the mothers or secondary principles; inasmuch as א here is taken for the dark *Aleph*: Hence it also denotes the element of earth. But indeed the first universal principle is the wondrous Tetragrammaton; whose characters are primary particular principles; after whose exemplar the world was created. And these characters are of the true simplicity of the digits; inasmuch as י is like a dark א partly hidden in a cloud, and partly shining forth: And ו is the symbol of the number six, just as He ה is the figure of the number five; which are comprehended in the first order of the number ten: Therefore י *Iod* is the same as *Aleph*, both dark and lucid; and ה is the same as the spirit enclosed in darkness, and ו is the same,

# INTRODUCTION

### FIRST PART:

## C H A P. I.

### On the admirable mystery of holy and truly formal letters,
### and the ineffable virtue and power of spherical letters.

[Large decorative woodcut initial Q] ALTHOUGH some perhaps, considering the exteriors of worldly things or creatures with sensible and plainly corporeal eyes, and not contemplating their interiors with spiritual and formal vision, will deem it ridiculous to enclose the essences of things in symbolic types of letters, objecting not without a reason sufficiently probable to men, that letters are mere accidents brought into the world by human invention, by which one person might express their meaning to another through written characters, nevertheless, if they examine the matter a little more accurately, they will perceive that things are far otherwise in Hebrew letters; for these were not invented by man, but were formally inscribed by the mouth of the Tetragrammaton in fiery characters into the womb of *hyle* (prime matter) at the world's beginning, and their powers and virtues were brought forth, breathed out, exhaled, and sounded with an admirable tone through the voice and the word FIAT, from the *hyle* of darkness. Hence, therefore, it was the opinion of the Kabbalists that God inscribed His law in a fiery globe by means of dark fire upon white fire: Whence Rambam Gerundensis says; It appears to us through Kabbalah that there was writing in dark fire upon the back of white fire: And hence that [passage] from Deuteronomy 33: "From His right hand went a fiery law for them" etc. Similarly, Kabbalists argue that the art of transposing letters is necessary, so that בה (bah) may be changed into הו (ho): Whence the meaning is changed because of the confusion of the primary letters, which had appeared in the fiery globe, so that it might be permitted, as it were, to draw them out of Chaos and read them here and there. Hence, therefore, it happened that these letters (as Blaise de Vigenère not unwisely recounts) are called *Elementa* as if *Hylementa*, that is, formal impressions on the dark and shadowy paper of *hyle*: For these letters, as Abraham in *Sefer Yetzirah* (Chapter 1) testifies concerning creation, import the essences of things into a material cloud: Hence also Socrates in *Cratylus* holds that the imitation of essence consists in letters and syllables: And the *Zohar* says that when Adam imposed true and proper appellations on all things, he composed every name of each thing by means of holy letters, which denote the influences of the stars destined for the ministry and service of things: Indeed, these letters in matter are, as it were, parts of the body; and their points and accents are in the place of spirit and life: But nevertheless, this life or this spirit lay hidden and was concealed in the dead letters depicted on paper as images of living things, before the time of the wise Ezra: Whence Reuchlin says; The holy letters were confused and jumbled after the beginning; which the most diligent observers, speculatively intuiting and carefully considering, led by the Holy Spirit, can easily choose, read, collect, and form into any words, here and there, up and down, back and forth, forwards, backwards, signifying a good meaning in good things, and an evil one in evil things: And another says that the law which God gave to Moses on two tablets was written in one continuous tenor and manner without separation of syllables or words, and that it penetrated from one side to the other, so that, according to the opinion of the Rabbis, one could read it in a manifold way and manner, according to the reader's imagination; namely, from right to left, forwards and backwards, from top to bottom and vice versa; But truly, the hidden and secret meaning of these characters concerning the divine mystery or the revelation of divine majesty, according to which God revealed Himself to Himself and to His chosen ones, He reserved for Himself; the secret of which indeed consisted partly in the form of the characters, and partly in the true and proper distinction of the words. This, therefore, is the reason why the Mosaic law used to be read in so many different ways and changed into such diverse meanings. According to this, David said in Psalm 119, verse 29: "Remove from me the way of falsehood, and graciously grant me Your law; the way of truth and Your precepts;"

This is declared all the more evidently by the fact that God concluded each of His actions in creation with the demonstration or particle את Eth; inasmuch as it is taken for a sign, figure, character, letter, or form; and as if all things in creation were comprehended through that limitation or circumscription בראשית ברא אלהים את השמים Bara, Elohim (Eth) hashamaym, (meaning) God created the figure, sign, character, or letter of the heavens, etc. Which letter indeed is Shin ש; inasmuch as it is a symbol of created fire, which consists of spirit, which is the food or nourishment of burning light, and of light itself, which is an act in the spirit or suffering water; And both together are called fire: Whence the highest heaven is called Empyrean, that is, fiery; and the middle is called Ethereal, as if fiery air. And hence, to those well-versed in the Cabalistic art, it appears most certainly and most clearly that the twenty-two formal or fiery letters of the characters were the pigmented foundations in the darkest veil of hyle, both of the world and also of the law: Which indeed also seems to be confirmed by the following assertion of Moses; For God said to Moses; Behold, I come to you in thick

lium Vau with father Iod: Secondary or created and substantial are those things which imitate those primary principles; namely, bright Aleph, compared to the Iod of the Archetype, which signifies created light, and Shin is made in the image of Vau, and Mem, upper and lower, to the He of the supersubstantial world: Whence Aleph denotes created light, Mem above the firmament, thin and subtle waters, and Mem below the firmament, thick and dark waters; and Shin the middle heaven, dividing the upper Mem from the lower Mem; so that the three principles of the substantial and created world are Aleph or light, dark Mem or darkness, and Shin or the intermediate spirit, a vehicle of light participating in all three; Whence it is depicted with three rays ascending and rising upwards from the root, in the manner of fire, in this way [a triangle with three lines rising from the top]. And thus we have those three general elements of the Macrocosm, namely fire, spirit or the element of humidity, and darkness or earth; from which all creatures, both radical, like angels, and quadratic, like stars, and cubic, as composed of the three said elements, are constituted; among which we recognize man to be more excellent and nobler, whose three principles we reduce to a tertiary order: Therefore we call those three principles of the third kind of the Microcosm, namely the luminous soul, compared with Aleph or light, and the body, related to darkness or thick waters and covered with gloom, and its intermediate spirit participating in both extremes, which is attributed to Mercury (☿), in which is the life of things. Whence it is clear that the subordinate kinds of principles are derived from those most general ones: Therefore Mercurius Trismegistus did not foolishly write that the world is the image of God, and man is the world. Therefore the virtue of Jehovah acts in the mothers of the world; and these mothers further transfuse the actions of that Tetragrammaton's virtue into all creatures, but more specially and copiously into man, the Microcosm and noblest creature; although, as it seems to me, there is another Microcosm even more divine than man, and closer to God himself; which is, (as I think) that homunculus of Paracelsus, about whom he sang so many wonders in his works: But, leaving these things aside, we will hasten to approach the subject of this work.

C A P. II.

How, according to the idea of the ineffable name of the Archetype, the created world, both great and small, is disposed?

First of all, it must be known that the world was made according to the exemplar of the living God, that is, in imitation of the characters of His ineffable name, as if His fiery and living characters were to be seen in a mundane mirror: Whence Mercurius Trismegistus called the world the image and exemplar of God; And Moses said that man was formed according to the exemplar of Jehovah: whom the aforesaid Hermes called the image of the world, inasmuch as he contains parts of the world within himself; Which also the wise Ecclesiastes affirms in chapter 3, verse 11: God has put the world or eternity in the heart of man, so that man cannot find out the work that God does from beginning to end: Hence, therefore, it is certain that the concrete world was described in the Archetype by an ideal and supersubstantial delineation before its creation; as also man in both respects, namely before and after creation: Thus we read in Exodus 25:40: See that you make them according to their patterns, which were shown to you on this mountain; Ibid. 26:30: So you shall erect that tabernacle, according to its suitability, which was shown to you on this mountain; And ibid. 25:9: That they may make me a sanctuary, and I will dwell among them entirely, just as I will show you the structure of the tabernacle itself, and the structure of all its furnishings; thus you shall do: Likewise, we read that Noah's ark was previously described by God; And the Royal Prophet boasted that he had received the description of the temple from the hands of God; And the Cabalists refer all these things as having been formed according to the image of the world, both Archetypal and concrete, both greater and lesser. Here, therefore, I have proposed to explain the correspondence of the Archetypal world, or the characters of the ineffable name, with the created world, both greater and likewise lesser, so that it may appear more clearly how the created world, both visible and invisible, is, as it were, the very wax receiving the characters of the ineffable seal יהוה; and from this it will be evidently proven that, just as a seal skillfully made leaves in wax a certain mark similar to itself, which is called the image of the seal, so also the seal of the creator has left its icon in the passive spirit of the world; indeed, it possesses from the origin the real essence, vestiges, and presence of the very Word of the Tetragrammaton, by which such a noble and beautiful thing lives and exists. And since in that great and ineffable seal four characters are found, but only three differing from each other in species, therefore in this place we will open up the nature, disposition, and signification of each of them, by which we may more easily arrive at the doctrine and understanding of what follows; But first, we will adapt the brilliant and fiery-white ineffable name to the parts of the created world, so that from it we may more readily and as if in a mirror perceive how the members of the created world arise from the properties of the figures and icons of the primary elements Iod, He, and Vau. C A P. III.

How is the world numbered by the ineffable name of the Tetragrammaton?

The numerical proportion of the world, by which it is ordered and first distributed into diverse regions, and then subdivided into orbs differing in nature, consists in the numerical respect of the ineffable name Tetragrammaton יהוה: For in the prior place we extract the cube of the ternary number; according to which the root, square, and cube of the world, and consequently its perfection, are produced. Let us consider therefore the ineffable name in its parts or letters, and we will find that Iod denotes 10. The first ה five, and Vau six, and the posterior or last ה, five; to which numbers, added together, will be produced Twenty-six, to which product if again Aleph, which is unity, is added, Twenty-seven will be produced, which is that cube of the ternary number, whose praises Plato so greatly sang in his Timaeus concerning the production of the world: Or, operating differently, we find in this ineffable name three letters differing from each other, namely יהו: Whence, by cubing this ternary number, it will yield 27. But if we wish to proceed further to details, the product of the ternary number יהו multiplied by itself will be 9. Therefore, if three times nine according to the ternary of the aforesaid letters—

C A P. IV.

How the world is weighed in the scales of justice by the power of the ineffable name, and measured by corresponding weights.

If we consider the weights of the mundane spirit, we will perceive them from the letters of the Tetragrammatic name: For since Yod (י) is outside all nature of things (for by that reason we say God is outside all things), therefore God himself

--- Page 508 ---
10 SECT. I. PART. I.

We say that God Ehieh or Iod, the just and benevolent judge of worldly things, holding in his right hand the balance of nature's scales or a plumb line, and weighing all things by the weights of justice, that is, according to the merit of matter: Therefore, he placed light things in one scale, and pressed heavy things into the scale opposite to it; the moderator, however, or the plumb line of justice's balance, or its tongue, is the intermediate spirit.

We see, therefore, that the scale of purity, simplicity, and tenuity is that ה He, which exists closer to Iod, while the other, opposite to it, is the last and lowest ה; into which gross and heavy things, both opaque and diaphanous, namely water and earth, and the other elements, are included: The moderator or tongue of these scales, or the plumb line of judgment and justice, is Vau; which is the moderator, mediator, and true governor of both weights: In which element of the Tetragrammaton, since unity is found above the value of He, through that (I say) unity, the balance Vau is sustained as if by a rope or cord from God Iod, who is the judge; Vau, however, is the mediator, bringing forth truth and sincerity, as if a testimony of truth before the judge.

In a precisely similar way, the Messiah produces testimony of those things which are in the heavens and which are on earth; he himself is the sole truth, wisdom, and justice, through whom any thing is exalted in honor according to its dignity, or cast down into the depths in disgrace according to its merit: Thus, therefore, because of the purity and simplicity of the matter or spirit of the Empyrean heaven, he causes its substance to be raised upwards into the most excellent scale of honor towards the luminous fount; but conversely, he allows the elemental heaven to be pressed down, downwards towards the infernal regions, because of its impurity, grossness, gravity, and dark density; In the middle, however, is Vau, sustained by the right hand of Iod or Jehovah himself; by the virtue and abundance of whose spirit the first ה is exalted, and conversely, by the lack of the same, the last ה is suppressed: For thus we see that Jehovah, by his wisdom, arranged all these things by composing them according to his justice; and yet divine wisdom itself has the root of its essence in the father, since the son is said to proceed from the center of the father: For thus the Messiah, or natural God, or rather God in nature, or the virtue of the Tetragrammaton descending into humid nature and giving it existence, is connected to Iod, the fount of light and the root of the divine tree in nature, in such a way that it can no more be separated and divided from Iod than a solar ray from the Sun.

We see therefore in the composition of the world that, just as Vau is a nexus or bond, and as it were a copulative conjunction, connecting the upper ה with the lower ה, so also the firmament is that which both distinguishes and also joins the Empyrean Spirit with the elemental spirit; that is, it separates the upper waters from the lower waters; and yet it is a nexus and bond through which, and by means of which, the mundane mind is introduced into the lowest region of the world by alluring.

But so that we may produce testimonies supporting this opinion of ours from the sacred writings, we read in Proverbs 3:19 that Jehovah God established the heavens by his wisdom. Here, therefore, the tongue of nature's balance is clearly declared to be Vau, or the wisdom of Jehovah fixedly remaining in its solar tabernacle: Then we find in Job 38:37: "Who made a weight for the winds, and measured out the waters": Here, therefore, the two scales of the balance with the matter contained in them are expressed: For by winds he seems to understand the more subtle spirits, which are weighed in the upper scale ה (since, as declared above, ה is a symbol of spirit, breath, and wind), and by waters he wished to signify the gross spirits contained in the lowest ה, or the more depressed scale.

But that holy Job seems to denote this inequality of natural weights in the same place with these words: "Who can number the heavens in power? And who can make the things that descend from heaven to rest? When the dust hardens into that hardness, and the clods cleave to one another": Similarly, that same wise man says in chapter 26:7, that God "suspended the earth upon nothing, and bound the waters in the thick clouds": Here, therefore, he places Vau, God in nature, as the tongue of the balance indicating truth, the earth as the lowest scale, and the clouds as the upper scale, according to that from Job 25:5: "Behold the heaven, and contemplate the superior clouds, that they are high above you"; all of which he seems to assert are suspended and bound in their proper places. But let us hear, I pray, what the Divine Hermes Trismegistus says in Pimander 3 in this case: "There flourished," he says, "a holy splendor, which drew forth the elements beneath the sand and humid nature; and all the Gods loved the seminal nature; And when they had been indistinct, the light things afterwards flew forth into the exalted region; the heavy things settled beneath the humid sand: When things were distinguished and vibrated, which were carried by the fiery spirit, the heaven shone forth in seven circles." What else, therefore, does that Wise Man mean here, than that the light spirit is carried upwards, but the heavy downwards, and that all things are lifted by the fiery spirit, that is, by the balance Vau ו, or for lack of it, are cast down towards the center of the periphery.

Therefore, the axis of this mundane, or natural, balance is the axis of the world; the supreme part of which is the arctic, or boreal pole, or Aquilo; which is sublimated upwards towards the summit of the heavens. Its opposite end, however, is as it were the antarctic or Austral pole, which is depressed towards the depths of the earth: The south of this axis, however, is Phoebus himself in his exaltation, who is attributed to Vau or the palace of the Messiah. Nor indeed do these things differ from that saying of the man as wise as he was patient, Job 26:7: "God extends the North upwards over the void and emptiness, that is, he made the heaven revolve over the North Pole and suspended the whole earth downwards over nothing."

From which it is evidently clear that the Tetragrammaton, dividing the universal spirit into two parts by the firmament, disposed each of them with various weights in the world. Hence, therefore, it says in Job 28, verse 25: "Waters"

[Large decorative initial 'T' with floral and scrollwork motifs] THE three¹ first enumerations out of those ten divine ones enumerated by the Cabalists, (namely כתר Kether or crown; which refers to the divine essence אהיה Ehieh, and particularly represents patience²; and חכמה Hochma, that is, wisdom, which refers to the most holy name יהוה; and בינה Binah, that is, prudence or intelligence, to which the name of God אלהים is attributed) are called by the Cabalists the three highest and supreme enumerations, which are, as it were, one seat, in which sits the Holy One, the Holy of Holies, the Lord God of Sabaoth; of which three supreme enumerations of the Cabalistic art (which Christians call three persons in the divinity) the infinity and most absolute essence, being withdrawn into the abyss of darkness, and remaining idle without any external action, that is, looking to nothing, (according to that saying of Hermes Trismegistus: "The Monad, before the creation of the world, generated the Monad, and reflected its ardor into itself"; and according to that of Psalm 18:11: "He made darkness his secret place, etc."; because, as M. Indeed, if we examine with diligent attention the parts of the luminous Aleph or the letters of the word Tetragrammaton, we will perceive that it is a most polished mirror, in which the figure and image of the Macrocosm are most exactly delineated with living characters: And hence it is, that the wondrous name יהוה (YHWH) is referred to חכמה Hochma, that is, wisdom, by which Aleph, which is unity, crown, and father, made all things, and Jehova without respect, that is, the Word proceeding from the dark Aleph, by which the heavens were made firm; Which indeed, although it is the second numeration, or emanation, or Sephiroth; yet it is called principle for this reason, because the world was fashioned from it; This is the first procession from the father hidden in the hiding-place of darkness into matter or universal water deformed by darkness, so that it might purify them, and drive all foul impurity to the center by its presence, according to that of the Wise Man; *Prov. 8. v. 22. Jehovah possessed wisdom in the beginning of his way; before his works, before any time, before the age she was anointed; before the beginning, before the first elements of the earth; when there were no depths or abysses, she was brought forth, when there were no springs abundant with waters, before the mountains were founded, and before the hills she was formed; when the earth was not yet, when he fitted the heavens, she was there, when he established the circuit on the surface of the abyss, when he strengthened the upper clouds above, when he made firm the springs of the abyss, when he set for the sea its decree, and for the waters, that they should not transgress the boundary of his mouth, when he established the foundations of the earth, wisdom was with him as a foster-child composing all things, playing before him at all times &c.* And hence St. John calls it the Word of Jehovah; through which all things were made, and without which nothing that was made was made, likewise the principle of things, indeed even Jehovah himself, in whom was the life of created things; which life was the light of men; And that light shines in darkness, both universal and particular, and the darkness did not comprehend it, inasmuch as it is incomprehensible and infinite; It was in the world, and the world was made by it &c. From which indeed it is clearly evident, that the Wisdom of God is His very Word; which is of the same supersubstantial essence with Him, and consequently is comprehended in the ineffable Tetragrammaton, and is as it were the Tetragrammaton itself or Jehovah, who made everything that was made, by the efficacy of His spirit.

Therefore, the idea of the entire Macrocosm can be seen and perceived in this incomprehensible mirror from head to heel, that is, from its circumference to the center of its fabric; indeed, in its exact idea and according to its exemplar, all parts of the world are numbered, measured, and weighed: Hence it is called the Idea of God's Archetype: For as far as the numbering of the world is concerned, we find that the first letter י, namely Yod, denotes ten, and the second ה five, and the third ו Vau six, and the last ה five: When these are aggregated together, 26 will be produced. And if א (Aleph) is added to these, which is the first unity, 27 will be constituted. Or proceeding differently, we find that in the name יהוה there are only three different letters: which number, multiplied by itself, produces 9, or a square, denoting as many simple orders of angels, and as many orbs of mobile celestial spheres, as well as regions in the elementary world: For 9, again multiplied by its root, will produce 27, which are the degrees by which the world is measured; And, if those three numbers 9 are rightly arranged in the Platonic manner in this order 9 9 9, they will show the unique numeration of the world

by an inviolable bond, a nature so divine could not submit to such a vile condition, namely, first to enter a dense spirit subject to changes, and then afterwards to inhabit a body so opaque joined with it. And it is commonly for this reason that Vav (ו) is taken among the Hebrews as a copulative conjunction, and indeed frequently so, connecting the preceding word with the following. Jod (י) is therefore the illuminating father, whose emanation of light, penetrating through He (ה) or pure waters on the first day, made the firmament on the second day by its presence, separating the pure waters or superior spirits from the impure and inferior waters, which are also dense spirits; and finally by its presence, the inferior waters having been purified on the third day, and their dreggy impurity having been driven back to the center, it placed its tabernacle in the Sun. Wherefore it is to be noted that the letters in the Tetragrammaton are so arranged according to the nature and position of the parts of the world, which flowed forth from the ineffable essence of the said formal letters. Hence it comes about that between the Empyrean heaven

who heals all things: Similarly *Job 10:12. You granted me life and showed me kindness; your care preserved*

and thus the humid spirit, or the subtle higher water, namely the first He (ה), is illuminated by the first emanation from Jod (י) itself: *For thus was the Empyrean heaven made; thus first of all was wisdom created, and understanding prudence from eternity; whose source is the Word of God in the highest,* that is, on the supersubstantial throne of Jehovah, as the very words of Ecclesiasticus have it in *chapter 1:4.* And this is the reason why this heaven is called intellectual; whose passive intellect is activated by the rays of God proceeding immediately from the Jod of the Tetragrammaton; This luminous virtue of the intellect is called the active intellect; which is like a golden tree of life emanating from the eternal root Jod, which is Ehieh; whose process in the former is also called Ehieh, because it flows outward: And in this way, Jod in its first procession, joined to matter with He (ה), the supreme portion of spirits or waters, making Jah (יה), denotes the reason by which God, expanding from unity, begins to move from His point and simplicity into a material line for the creation of all things: For, just as two numbers constitute the first number, and two points the smallest line, so also Jod, which is a point proceeding from its unity into the unity of matter, produces a line or duality; And just as before the creation of the world it had no name except one, ineffable, and most simple, namely Jod, called according to its unique essence, or the luminous and apparent Aleph (which is indeed the same as the Tetragrammaton of the ideal world), so also after the projection of its countenance into hyle (matter), all names taken from its works are attributed to it: Hence that unique and hidden name Tetragrammaton, appropriated to it, is called the separated name, in which there is participation: But its other glorious names have meaning with participation, inasmuch as they are taken from the works which are discovered, as the Egyptian Moses testifies: Therefore, its first name, derived from the first work, is Jah (יה), a name of essence, merit, and attribution: Hence it is found in *Psalm 130:3. If you, Jah, should mark iniquities, etc.*

ㅤㅤHence Jod is named, inasmuch as it looks into the darkness: And again *Exodus 15. My strength and my praise is Jah;* inasmuch as through the creation of wisdom, the strength of strength was brought forth into the world, according to that of Hermes Trismegistus in the Emerald Tablet; *This is the strong strength of all strength, for it overcomes every subtle thing, and penetrates every solid thing; Thus the world was created, etc.*

ㅤㅤSimilarly, Jah denotes benevolence towards the whole world and the creatures of the world: Nor is it surprising, because Jod, which is a symbol of the father, denotes clemency and mercy, inasmuch as it is the father's duty to have mercy on his children, according to *Psalm 103.*

ㅤㅤTherefore Jod, which is the progenitor of the spirit He (ה), that is, the producer of its being, by the power of its rays fills it everywhere with its mercy and activates it: And from this benevolence and grace of its infusion into the darkness, the supreme Spirit is prepared, the Spirit of Jod is carried over it, and that thus illuminated is called the light created on the first day; from whose full influence, and by the grace and benevolence of the hidden Jod of the Tetragrammaton, things in potential are brought into actuality, Angels are begotten from the simple fire or light of Jod and the spirit He (ה), Metatron or the soul of the world is placed over nature, and life is communicated to every created thing.

ㅤㅤOh, infinite power of things, and ineffable goodness and mercy of Jod, by which all things overwhelmed by darkness and oblivion are brought from deadly and sad captivity into light and being, and from potential into actuality: Is this not an admirable sign of benevolence and mercy? Indeed, from this fountain of benevolence, from this origin of created wisdom, from this nectar of the superessential Word, and true potable gold, from this divine balm, and from no other, flowed the means of preserving the health of creatures, the remedy for driving away sickness, the method for repelling diabolical injuries, and the reason and medicine for suppressing infernal rage and malice; indeed, and the power to extinguish or eradicate the poison of death itself (which first crept into the world by the malice of the Devil), and to suppress its lethal blow and violence; in which there is neither disease, nor violence, nor death, nor any impediment of nature; for in it there is harmony, unity, life, act, and light, which entirely resists all actions of darkness: Hence *Psalm 80:4. By the light of God's countenance we shall be saved.*

ㅤㅤThis He (ה), therefore

uncreated, is entirely uncreated: And therefore the medium or spirit through which light is diffused throughout the entire world, is said to be created; but the light navigating in it is one and the same emanation from the father and source of lights, Jod, or the luminous Aleph: But the naming of diverse emanations, from which the ten Sephiroth of the Cabalists or divine names originated, proceeds not from an alteration of the light, but from the variety of density or tenuity of the Spirit or medium, in which it is carried: For light is always the same, and the soul, being, and life of creatures themselves, and of all things; since it is nothing other than either the proximate or remote presence of God.

Hence therefore is revealed the error of those who condemned Ethnic Philosophers for this reason, that they called Nature God, and God himself, *nature*: For when they spoke of nature, they understood that which they called invisible fire, from which Zoroaster and Heraclitus taught all things to have been generated.

From which it is clear, that by nature they wished to imply the essential light swimming in universal humid nature; as if they were speaking of the fiery and Holy Spirit Jod, who was carried in and upon the waters, or by the universal Spirit: For such light is of the true and simple essence of Jod itself, or the Tetragrammaton; so that it can no more be separated from its eternal nature than a solar ray, which is indivisible, from the Sun.

And although this divine light extends itself through the entire created Macrocosm, as if proceeding from unity into the multitude of matter, its rays are nevertheless bound to their root no differently than the branches of some tree to its stock and origin.

And this is a reason sufficiently legitimate and not to be despised, on account of which Democritus, and Orpheus, and many of the Pythagoreans believed that a God or a certain soul presided over every thing, and that all things were full of Gods, to whom they established divine honors, and dedicated prayers and sacrifices to them, and pursued them with diverse worship and veneration: But at last they recognized that all these souls or species of light were to be reduced to one world-soul, and all Gods to be referred to one Jupiter.

Hence therefore says Plato; *Speak not of God without light:* And someone in his chemical art explicitly exclaims, *that there is nothing in the very circle of the firmament that bears a greater likeness to God than the soul of the world and light itself:* indeed, he says, *each thing claims God for itself only in so far as it is capable of light.*

And this is the reason that Augustine in his book *On Free Will* says; that light holds the first place in bodies. Does not also, that we may return to the fount of all truth, the Psalmist say, *Psalm 103. 1. & 104. 19. Light is the garment and vestment of God?* Do we not also read in St. John, *that the Word was in the beginning with God, and that all things were made through it, and without it nothing was made that was made? indeed in it was life, and that life was the light of men, and that light shines in darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it: And this was that which was in the world, and the world was made through it, and the world did not know it.*

By these very words the Apostle seems most accurately to confirm that whole doctrine which Moses set forth in the first chapter of *Genesis*; since he clearly teaches us in that place that by the Word of the Lord *LET THERE BE* or *BE,* and by the presence of *that spirit which was carried upon the waters,* proceeding from the father and the son, light, or rather spirit, was wonderfully adorned and created on the first day; For light does not suffer creation, inasmuch as it is a true act of *Jehovah*, immediately sent forth by Him from the Holy heavens to create spiritual things, or waters hidden in the womb of hyle; that is, to bring them forth from darkness and as it were from nothing into light and actuality.

Here therefore with an attentive mind we discover how nature itself is called God, namely, inasmuch as the light of Jehovah, which is His essential emanation, is present in universal humid nature; which also from then on the Ethnics called God, wrongly taking created matter for the divine essence and form or the most holy creating light. And in this way God is considered in the concrete, receiving various cognomens according to His works, and not according to His being: But indeed, inasmuch as God, the dark Aleph, is considered in the abstract, to that extent He exists without any regard to created things, that is, by His simple and infinite essence in His supersubstantial kingdom, and on the sublime throne of eternity, triumphantly seated above the highest summit or apex of His spherical machine, and outside all limits of the waters. From which it is clearly evident how God is truly said to be within and outside all things, and how He exists everywhere and nowhere inclusively, and how He is also infinite and comprehended by no limit. We have therefore in this way an intellectual vision of Jah itself, or the first emanation of Jod itself; which is the symbol of the ineffable Tetragrammaton, filling the entire space of the three primary numbers 9 9 9. In which interval, indeed, brought forth into light on the first day, consists, according to Cabalists and Platonists, the simplest portion of the Spirit. But we, for reasons alleged in divine numbers, attribute that first mundane space, named the Empyrean heaven, to the denary numbers; because that part of creation consists of the composition of two, namely, light and Spirit, from which angels were created: Whence, as denary numbers are composed of two, namely, either of a digit and a cipher,

Since an Angel is otherness, as consisting of two, namely the spirit He (ה); and light emanating from Jod (י) (for in Jah, by this reasoning, the most noble nature of Angels shines forth) and God, Jod (י), or Aleph (א) is identity, but the first otherness is the binary, we rightly believe that the number of Angels arises from the multiplication of the binary: For thus, twice two, twice makes eight, which is the first cube; but as for the octads of angels, if you distribute them into nine choirs, there will be 72. For so many are nine times eight. Return therefore, if you wish, through the choirs to the cube, through the cubes to the Tetractys or Tetragrammaton, and from that to the binary, signifying the angelic nature, and thence to the unity of Jod, or God, the Best and Greatest. And you will experience that by that way, if we apply ourselves to this study, through the angels we are joined to God, to the ineffable Tetragrammaton Jod, He, Vau, He, in which first the most noble nature of these angels shines forth. But let us return directly to our purpose: Conclusively therefore we say that Jah, which is the first emanation from Jod, namely by the addition of He (ה) with Jod (י), or the conjunction of the most holy light with the formless spirit of the supreme heaven, that spirit is created, changed into a luminous substance, which is called the light created on the first day. Hence therefore it is clear that the goodness and mercy of God Jod, (which is symbolically denoted by Jah according to the Cabalists) is exalted above the heavens: Whence also the Royal Prophet says in Psalm 36; "The mercy and goodness of Jehovah is from the heavens, His faithfulness reaches to the upper clouds &c." that is, up to Yah (יה) immediately flowing from Jod (י); For by the upper clouds he seems to designate the clear spirit and the luminous waters placed above the firmament; from which, that is, from the highest heavens, the goodness of Jah descends to earth to vivify the waters that are under the firmament, and to infuse life into the creatures created therein, according to that of the Psalmist, Psalm 33: "The earth is full of mercy and goodness": For "by the word of Jehovah the heavens were made, and by the spirit of His mouth all their host." But conversely, goodness and salvation are produced for the world from one extreme, namely from the luminous source; and from on high it flows into the lower regions, namely from Yah (יה); immediately proceeding from the luminous Jod (י) or Aleph (א), and transmitted and infused to the ultimate, or the waters existing under the firmament; where the reason for diseases, alterations, and discord abounds because of the proximity of the lowest waters around the other extreme, which darkness inhabits; whose prince is the Devil; concerning whom it is said in Wisdom 3: "By the envy of the Devil, death entered into the world &c." And Wisdom 1:14: "For God did not make death, nor does He rejoice in the destruction of the living; For He created all things that they might exist, and He made the nations of the earth curable; and there is no medicine of destruction in them, nor the kingdom of the underworld on earth &c." From these things therefore it is clear that the mercy of God in repelling diseases, both of the soul and of the body, is more powerful than the malice of the Devil in infecting them with his pestiferous and deadly poison; since it is

SO now that we come to the second production of God, and the creation of the firmament itself, it must be understood that the firmamented heavens are nothing other than the firmament itself: But *by the word of the Lord were the heavens established*, as the Psalmist testifies; Therefore also by the Word of the Lord was the firmament made, intersecting and dividing the waters above from the waters below: The firmament, I say, was made; that is, that middle spirit, which is called ethereal, was brought into being, through the presence and action of the most holy light; for it mixed itself with it, and clarified and informed it; And so by the uncreated power of Jehovah was created an intermediate spirit between the waters or more subtle spirits, and those grosser and denser ones, both luminous and opaque. Does not Mercurius Trismegistus confirm all these things with the clearest words in Pimander 1, where he speaks these words: *Pimander, the mind of divine power changed its form, and suddenly revealed all things: For I beheld a certain immense spectacle; all things, namely, converted into a light exceedingly sweet and pleasant.* This is the obscure Aleph itself, or the mind of divine power, going forth into the act of the world, but where, shining back upon itself, it suddenly becomes a luminous Aleph or, in the number ten, duplicates itself in the form of Jod, its luminous emanation having now entered into formless hyle, and made all hidden things and those covered by shadows appear; that is, He (ה) is converted into light, or pleasant light, and thus that illuminated light created on the first day is called. But now, so that we may observe that this first emanation is the Word in shadow and illuminating, I would like you to attend to the following discourse of the Sage, which is as follows: *A little later a certain horrible shadow, with an oblique revolution, glided underneath, and migrated into humid nature, agitated by an ineffable countenance; thence a certain great smoke burst forth into a sound; from the sound a voice emerged, which I considered to be the voice of light: From this voice of light the Word made its appearance: But standing by this humid nature, it cherished it,* etc.

By these things the Philosopher seems to indicate that the light first emanated from Jod (י), the unity of the Tetragrammaton, as from a fount of light into the first He (ה), expelling darkness from it, manifesting the hidden; and that the Spirit, enclosed in the darkness gliding underneath with an oblique revolution, and eagerly embracing the most beautiful and God-begotten and superessential light, emitted by the first emanation from the eternal mind Jod, by divine power thus enclosed within it, there is an eruption from the darkness, and in the eruption a voice is produced and with the voice the Word, which is the virtue of the first emanation, sounding from Jod, or Jehovah; and it is produced not in vain, but with such effective strength that it sounds and speaks with sound; and the word thus enunciated, and the sense of the discourse, imprints fiery and formal characters upon the surface of dark Chaos in such a way that it is impossible for the effect not to follow, according to that sacred saying: *Not one jot or tittle of his words shall fall to the ground; that is, it will perish, or be uttered in vain;* And elsewhere: *The Word of Jehovah shall remain forever.*

It is, he says, the voice of light, or the voice of Jod itself, or of the father's light first produced in He (ה); whence the Empyrean heaven, from whose pure elements intelligences of every kind are procreated, was made; Then into the middle He (ה), which is comprehended in Vau (ו); and the firmament was made; and finally into the last He (ה) of Jehovah; and the lowest heaven was made: Indeed, these three heavens are formed from water, more gross or subtle, and differ from each other according to the greater or lesser dominion of divine emanation: For the more that most simple God-like essence predominates in the world, the purer, cleaner, more transparent, and more subtle is that part of the world or humid spirit, or water. Hence therefore St. John ch. 1: *In the beginning was the Word, that is, infinite shadow or hyle, And the Word was with God; and the Word was God: The same was in the beginning with God: All things were made by him; and without him was not anything made that was made: In him was life; and the life was the light of men: And the light shineth in darkness (that is, in horrible shadow); and the darkness comprehended it not;* (that is, it burst forth from the darkness, and produced a sound) etc. He was in the world, *and the world was made by him* etc.

Therefore, just as God, the dark Aleph, was the first unity outside the created world, and before its creation, so also its first emanation of light, through which the Word, the Messiah, or the Virtue of the Tetragrammaton entered the world, indeed which is the Word itself, being of the same essence as Aleph Jod, Jah, Ehieh & the Tetragrammaton; it speaks: Thus, just as Aleph was the first unity in the Archetypal & ideal world, delineating the ideal figure of the world to be made; so its Word, expressed by Vau (ו), is the unity & principle of the ideal world, reducing it into a real disposition and sensible form: And hence it is written in Zechariah, that God the Tetragrammaton will be YHWH (יהוה), that is, one

born medium; whose role it is to penetrate confusedly through all elements, since it participates with each of the said
natures, and treats them gently & courteously, & thus makes & conciliates peace among enemies.

But that the Word is always present to this cornerstone, whose house it indeed is, since the divine Word is, as it were, its soul (whence Vau with an angle is thus described ו), we can confirm from many places in the sacred scriptures: For first it is written, *Psalm 118:22: “The stone which the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone; this is from Jehovah, and it is marvelous in our eyes:”* And concerning this Jesus said, *Matthew 21:42, Mark 11:10, Luke 20:17, Acts 4:11: “Have you never read in the Scriptures: ‘The stone which the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone,’ etc.”* And it is written: *“Behold, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, and whoever believes in Him will not be put to shame.” Romans 9:33.* Or, as it is in *1 Peter 2:6: “Behold, I lay in Zion a chief cornerstone, chosen, precious; and he who believes in Him will not be put to shame:”* And in *Isaiah 28:16* we find it thus written: *“Behold, I am laying in Zion a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation; whoever believes will not be in a hurry:”* And we can adduce many other passages by which it is proven that the cornerstone of Jehovah, and the spirit of His omnipotent wisdom, is the base, by whose admirable power not only is the earth suspended in the air by the scales of admirable justice, but also every dense celestial body, and, because of its thickness, ponderous, is sustained in the ether by the wonderful spirit of divinity, as a column and support: This base of things, proceeding from eternity, is nothing other than the Word of Jehovah, symbolically signified by Vau, confirming and establishing all things by its power and strength: Whose nobler palace is the Sun; for it, with its angular Carbuncle, vivifies all things with light and life, no differently than the spiritual Word dwelling within it heals the souls of men laboring under despair, sadness, and other mental disturbances, and wounded by the poison of the Devil and the darkness, with the balm of its grace and mercy; And hence

multiplicity they are more immersed in: So also is the supreme He, or the region attributed to the Father, simpler, purer, more subtle than the others, and consequently more similar to, more conjoined with, and more contiguous to the divine nature. And thus God the Father descends into the world; then from He into He the Word is emitted, and obtains the middle place between the first Yod and the last He: Whence the firmament, by Vau, to which the Word is symbolically referred, is dedicated to the Word, or the Son, or the second person proceeding from the first: Thus it is said; that by the Word the heavens were made firm; And thus was produced the seal of all truth, which Ehieh used for the creation of the world, and for manifesting the benevolence and mercy of Jehovah to the world and its creatures. But now at last we shall arrive at the ultimate He, and in its cruder and denser spirit, navigating with a willing mind, we shall diligently inquire into its disposition.

CH. VI.
*On the nature of the last letter of the Tetragrammaton itself, and how it relates to the lowest heaven of the world.*

The last He of the name Tetragrammaton, which is also the end and limit of that ineffable name, denotes the ultimate and lowest region of the world; And thus this wondrous name extends itself from the eternal world even to the center of the created world: Whence it is said that God is in all things, and outside all things: For in the measure of a spherical figure we see that nothing in it is omitted or left unmeasured, if any semi-diameter, circularly encompassing, is occupied from the circumference to the center: So also the virtue of the Tetragrammaton in Yod is eternal in the world; in the first He is the divine mind; in Vau is the celestial Sun, and the nature of the stars; in the last He is the elemental virtue; from whose center or middle region of the air in this heaven it shines forth, like the Sun from the center and middle of the ethereal region. And this virtue of the Tetragrammaton, as witnessed by St. Paul and St. John, is that life-giving Spirit, who is called Messiah, and the light of the world; who, as stated above, is the ineffable virtue of the Tetragrammaton, and operates in its power: And to this leads me this word משיח (Mashiach); whose letters, if transposed Cabalistically, will be מישיה (Mishiyah), that is, Messiah; who is also called the Word, which is God himself, and of the same essence with God; by whom all things were made, and without whom nothing was made, etc. And this eternal virtue is in the eternal world with the Father and the uncreated Spirit, and operates in them and with them; since it itself proceeds from the center of the Father, and the Spirit from the center of both: Therefore the Spirit and the Son are in the Father; inasmuch as He, after their procession from Him, reflected the ardor back into Himself; so that now the Father is in the Son, and the Son in the Father, and both in the same Spirit; And all three are one and the same in essence, and are signified in this world without emanation indeed by Aleph, which denotes unity, simplicity, and as it were a point; but with emanation or irradiation by Yod; which is assimilated to a line, as the first and simplest progression of divine virtue from its eternal source, Yod. And then this virtue is called the uncreated Mind, or the ray of the one God Yod; and being disposed in the center of the Empyrean heaven, from that place it first illuminates the spirit He; and then, by procreating its angelic creatures, it gives them virtue, and perpetually nourishes them with its essence by its rays; no differently than in the middle heaven or palace of the Sun it is accustomed to nourish, vivify, and illuminate innumerable stars with its surrounding rays: Nor does it do anything without the counsel of its father and source Yod, to whom it has always been obedient, according to that of the Wise Man, Proverbs 8. *When he prepared the heavens above, when he strengthened the fountains of the deep, when he set a bound to the sea, etc. when he established the foundations of the earth, I was Wisdom with him as a foster child, or arranging all things, when I was with him bringing up, and I was daily delighting, rejoicing, and playing before him at all times.*

From which it is clear that the Word or Messiah operates in the virtue of Yod, in whatever heaven, for its creation and establishment: that is, it observes the will of the Father, and obediently perfects it so precisely and carefully that it cannot deviate or err even a hair's breadth from it; indeed, it has performed or accomplished its father's will, both on earth and in the heavens, by its wondrous action, both in the creation of the world and in its preservation, and will perform it eternally. But now on the third day of creation, that is, the third eruption of light from darkness, an immediate emanation from Vau (which is situated in the middle between the double Heh, that is, between the spiritual or higher waters, and the gross or lower ones), which is indeed called the third emanation, or tertiary light from Yod, with respect to the diversity of the triple medium through which it passed, immersed itself into the darkness of the lowest heaven (which darkness is now truly called Chaos, because it contains confused and ill-disposed elements, contending with each other in its depths), and there it brought forth into light that He, or dense and crude spirit, devoid of light and form; which had been delineated in the idea of the wondrous name Tetragrammaton before the age, and from eternity: For God, the Archetype of the Macrocosm and Microcosm and of the disposition of every creature, first ordered the measure, number, and weight in the ideal world, before He actually produced them through His Word: Whence Wisdom 11. *But thou hast ordered all things in measure, and number, and weight:* And this was an excellent sign or argument, in the created light, or the Word, or the virtue and power, or the emanation and flow of the omnipotent Jehovah, of benevolence, and mercy, and of salvation, and peace;

--- Page 527 ---
Dᴇ Pʀɪɴᴄɪᴘɪɪs Sᴜᴘᴇʀsᴜʙsᴛᴀɴᴛɪᴀʟ. 29

argument; which evidently descended from the middle heaven or firmament into the crude mass of Chaos, to repel and drive away the contentious darknesses of this region or the ultimate He, and to reconcile among enemies; waging a horrible and continuous war against each other, eternal peace and concord: Was it not also for this reason, namely on account of Adam's fall, and the ruin of his succession, and on account of the dark sin's assaults in the human body and soul, and the strife and discord of the elements in human composition, inducing death to the body and captivity to the soul, that this holy virtue descended into human Chaos, dispelling its darkness with its light; repelling the sicknesses of bodies in this world, repressing the rage of the Devil, overcoming death and destruction, and demonstrating by infallible example and argument that it becomes the anchor of all faith, announcing to us the liberation of the soul from darkness and captivity? This, I say, the essence of divinity, this symphony of eternal concord, this reconciler of peace, this inviolable bond of union, with the darknesses dispelled to the center and around the center, and fixed and secured in the lowest place with a strong chain, by its harmony so disposed every element of that lower heaven, that peace and friendship may be preserved everywhere through the lowest He in the real world (which refers to the ultimate He of the ineffable name, which was the idea of the eternal and created world simultaneously, and consequently infinite and ineffable). This therefore is that honorable medium, whose nature is so sweet, so uniform, so strong and predominant, so essentially efficacious, so harmonious and symphonic, that, when it is joined with anything whatsoever, it immediately converts it into its own composition, and changes it into its own nature, as it were, and renders obedient to itself everything that it touches with its spirit: And this Holy Spirit, or Deiform virtue, is that, which, as if by a certain magical whisper, is accustomed to render all created spirits immediately obedient to itself, even in the blink of an eye, according to that saying of Hermes Trismegistus in the Emerald Tablet; *Thus you will have the glory of the whole world and all obscurity will flee from you; This is the strong strength of all strength; for it will overcome every subtle thing, and will penetrate every solid thing; Thus the world was created.* This therefore is that strongest bond, by which the elements, constituted in their places by God Yod, that is, in the region proper to each element, are suspended in the lowest He in such a way, that concord and peace may be had among all things: Hence he placed air between fire and water, so that it might be a mediator to both, namely, that by uniting its humidity with water, it might float above it, and by being contiguous to fire, it might soothe and cherish it with its warm humidity; and that finally in this way it might interpose itself between the cold nature of water on one side, and the hot nature of fire on the other; so that one cannot contend with the other by contrary motion and adverse effort: Similarly, the element of water performs this similar office, and becomes a mediator of peace between earth and air, so that the humidity of the air cannot inflict violence upon the dryness of the earth; And indeed, so that this moderation may be obtained so much more easily and better, water has been made such that it agrees with air by its humidity; for its consanguinity or kinship with air is so great, that by means of heat, it is even converted into air through rarefaction; and on the opposite side, it has a similar familiarity and consanguinity with earth because of its coldness; The bond of all these in such concord is the virtue of the Tetragrammaton, interceding first between fire and ether, then between air and fire, then afterwards between air and water, and finally between water and earth; with all of which it also commonly mixes itself to produce their essential forms: Hence God is said to be in all things, and all things in Him, and through Him, according to that of Job 28. *Who made a weight for the winds, and weighed the waters by measure, when he set a law for the rains, and a path for the sounding storms, then he saw wisdom, and declared it, and prepared it, and investigated it for man, and said; Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, etc.*
This Vau is that formal medium, dominating in the middle heaven or firmament, and in it, as in a place destined for the second person
