From which it is clear that this portion of the Spirit He in heaven is double: Whence these letters, which are symbols of the Planets, are called double, and are always pronounced with aspiration; from which it is argued that they have in themselves the superior virtues of He, or of the Empyrean heaven: And this is the reason, as it seems to me, why an Angelic Intelligence is said to preside over each Planet; according to whose disposition that Planet moves and acts, both in the firmament itself and in the elemental realm; and thus by the virtue of Vau in the ineffable name, the virtues of the superior He are infused into the inferior He: Whence we can certainly gather how glorious is the Vau connection between He and He, between which it is placed; by which indeed the superior things communicate with the inferior, and in turn the inferior, embracing the superior, rejoice in them and are vivified: This, I say, is the bond between the sublime soul and the lowest body; and this again is that powerful and noble bond by which the elements are brought into composition and are peacefully preserved therein: If indeed this bond fails in any part of the composition, a most certain disease and imbalance follows therefrom; because the elements, being contrary in composition, by the defect of this most powerful virtue, immediately begin to quarrel and contend among themselves, and to rebel in the human economy: But if this primordial virtue should fail entirely, inevitable death will follow therefrom; so much so that if this ethereal nature were to neglect and not regard the inferior things, and not daily cherish them, all things would immediately sicken, or languish, and forthwith by swift or sudden death would suddenly be reduced to nothing.

But perhaps some scrupulous person will say; if this virtue is an emanation of the Tetragrammaton itself, why can it not accomplish the same for inferior things from its own middle heaven, without Empyrean influences descending from above, or without the aid of intelligences sent from the superior He into the region of Vau; since the virtue of both the Empyrean heaven and the firmament is the same essential emanation of light: To this objection, indeed, we respond, as before, that the emanation of one and the other is of the same essence, no less than the properties of the most holy Trinity are of the same fount, nature, and origin; but when we speak of these emanations or the efflux of divine virtue in physical creation, that is, in the mixture of divinely infused light, we are not dealing with the nature of uncreated and simply formal light, but with the created spirit in which that light predominates, and which it moves and governs in every action, whether metaphysical or physical: And hence it is that, according to the greater or lesser presence or measure of this light, the spirit is usually more subtle or more gross; because the act of that simple virtue is always to purify spirits and to remove their rebellious grossness and density: And hence it is that there are diverse spirits in the world, which, according to their diversity, produce various effects: This, therefore, is the reason why, although there is unity in the divine efflux or the virtue of the Tetragrammaton, yet multitude is said to exist in the world from the variation of matter: Hence the Empyrean spirit is said to be more worthy than the Ethereal, and this latter again nobler than the elemental; although the uncreated light and virtue, by which those spirits are such as they are found in the aforesaid regions of the world, is always the same, and is never and in no way subject to mutations and alterations; because wisdom is *a holy, unique, simple, subtle, undefiled, harmless, or passion-free, stable, certain, all-virt

But also, if it were said to be absolutely created, we would likewise stray from the truth; because the virtue informing it, and reducing it from nothing into act, is uncreated: But indeed, insofar as the Spirit itself has a denomination, by which it is called either Empyrean Spirit, or aethereal spirit, or aether, or intellect, or reason, or air, or water, etc., to that extent, because the denomination arises from the material part, it is a creature: And this very thing is perceived through the nature of Vau ו; which, since in an arithmetical respect it is composed of five and one, it follows that א and ה adequately represent that number; from which the composition of this heaven is manifested, consisting namely of light, or the emanation of God, or the luminous Aleph, and the spirit ה: Hence therefore Vau ו is symbolically taken for the firmament; and the firmament for the aethereal spirit, that is, fiery air, that is, consisting of the luminous Aleph and ה; which are the same as ש, the hieroglyph of the fiery spirit itself, and aether is the same; which is the fifth essence, and the fifth essence is the same as the vital soul, and the vital soul is the same as the receptacle of the mind in the Empyrean or intellectual spirit, and finally the bond and connection and coupling between the Empyrean spirit and the gross spirit, both of simple things, namely in the elements themselves, and of composite things, as in bodies or elementals: And this is the reason why Vau ו is often taken by the Hebrews for the copulative conjunction, (And); as by it is indicated that in natural things it ought to couple two extremes; and indeed all the more so, since in the great name of the Tetragrammaton, Vau ו is interposed between ה & ה; by which those (He's) seem to be joined together as if by the conjunction (And): And hence it is said that no one can know the father except through the son; whence also the Word is called Mediator between man and God, and between the superior spirit or spiritual or linear heaven, and the inferior spirit, or elemental and corporeal heaven; For, just as from a line to a body there is no progression except through a surface, nor from a root to a cube, except through a square, and vice versa; so also there is no transition from the Empyrean heaven to the elemental, except through the firmament; just as not from unity to the ternary number, except through the interposition of the binary, which by a bond of justice joins the two extremes.

Hence therefore the fabric of the world is made for the representation of the properties of the Trinity; For unless its composition were in number, which distinguishes the highest from the lowest, the subtle from the dense, the luminous from the dark, good from evil, it could not have measure and weight; and unless the number of its different parts were ternary, the whole work would be imperfect, inasmuch as in the binary number there is indeed a beginning and an end, but no middle, because the end is lacking to it; or no end, inasmuch as the middle is lacking to it; Hence in the disposition of the world through that number, the world would be imperfect: Similarly, if the world were one, then it would only be the beginning of the world and of creatures; and consequently no created thing would exist, but all would be one beginning; and for this reason, the four elements would not be created, but only a single one: Wherefore it was necessary that the world be constituted from a non-imperfect number; which indeed, if it had happened, the world, that most excellent and beautiful creature of Jehovah, would be imperfect; which to say or believe would certainly be utterly profane: Whence it follows that the world is a most noble, most perfect, and most complete creature, fashioned after the exemplar of the Trinity; whose number is ternary, in which there is a beginning, a middle, and an end: For, even in the ineffable name יהוה of the most holy essence of the individual Trinity, number is found, namely י Jod, related to the father, to the son, and ה to the holy spirit. For although there is a double He there, nevertheless the first is the conjunction of the second person with the first Jod; and the last He again is the bond and agglutination of He after Vau with Jod; so that from the circular letters of the wondrous Tetragrammaton in the Archetypal world, a circulation of divine properties may occur; For, just as in the delineation of a circle three terms are observed; namely the term from which, and the middle and the end; which end in a circle is always the same as the beginning, inasmuch as all terms become unity there; so also the matter stands in the production of the persons of the most holy Trinity. And to this matter, Mercurius Trismegistus seems to assent with very few words: 'The Monad generates the monad, and reflects its ardor back into itself,' as if to say; God, a unity, spoke through the spirit; through which spirit the Word emanating from His mouth is coupled to Him, and again that Word through its same spirit reduced itself to the point of its unity, so that three distinct persons are nothing but unity in essence. But God did this when He first thought about creating the world; that is, He first delineated its image within Himself, namely in the ineffable name; after whose image the entire world was exactly created; whence it is also said to have been made in the image of God. Thus also the Prophet David boasted that he had received the description of the temple from the hand of Jehovah; which itself is indeed also said to contain the mystery of the created world.

From these things therefore we see that the fabric of the entire world is contained in the wondrous name of the Tetragrammaton; in which the image of the ideal or Archetypal world is symbolically explained, after whose exemplar the created world is said to have been made; For, just as in the ineffable name Jod precedes ה: so in the creation of the world, the emanation from Ehieh, which is the Word with the spirit, the prior portion of the spirit was revealed and stripped of darkness; And it is said; 'The Spirit of the Lord (which always accompanies the Word) moved upon the waters,' that is, upon the superior spirits already then revealed and informed by the light of the spirit through the Word, and created by that informing: We do not, however, wish that this spirit was the first He of the name Tetragrammaton, which was uncreated, and a symbol of the Holy Spirit, by which the first and second persons, i.e., Jod and Vau, are joined to each other as glu-

CHAPTER I.

*Concerning the primordial cause of health; how manifold health is; And that all good,*
*both corporal and spiritual, comes to us from Jah, through the Word;*
*Concerning the three principles of health of one essence;*
*which is the Tetragrammaton itself operating*
*through its wisdom.*

[Decorative initial P] THE material and created world having been produced in the preceding manner, according to the exemplar of the uncreated Archetypal and formal world, we now deem it necessary to inquire further with diligent attention, first, how good, and then afterwards, by what reason evil, its contrary, entered the world; since from good all that which is good is accustomed to proceed; in which especially and among all things, Salvation, health, and the happiness of life hold the supreme place. Since therefore God Jah, that is, the first emanation of God into He, or the Empyrean Spirit, is the benignity, life, and being of every life and every creature, we conclude that, without doubt, this emanation, mingling itself with the stream of life, is the author of life both spiritual and corporal, and its preserver in health, and the restorer to pristine health from health that has fallen and been precipitated into ill harmony; Which indeed we can most easily prove by numerous collected citations from the sacred scriptures. But if with the keenest eyes we look into the general nature of soundness or health, we shall immediately perceive with the greatest admiration that three species are subject to it, corresponding to the dispositions of the three spirits of the world; of which the first is salvation or redemption, which pertains to the soul and body together, or rather to the whole human being, as to life and the tabernacle of life simultaneously; which redemption is indeed to be expected by faith in the second life; The second species is properly called salvation or health, which pertains either to the internal disposition of the soul alone, or to the sound and good temperament of the body alone, along with the good state and condition of both joined together, which ought to occur in this life; The third species, however, is the liberation of the whole human being from external tribulations. The cause of all these species is the benignity and mercy of Jah himself; Which appellation of God indeed imports benignity, inasmuch as it is the fire of all purity in an obedient, gentle, and soft spirit; by whose flexibility and humility God acts according to His own and eternal goodness; while conversely, in a hard, dense, and rebellious spirit, which partakes of darkness, He is said to act harshly and through His wrath: And this is the reason why the eyes of mortals are said not to be able to behold God in His nature; for before whose face mountains and stones

--- Page 533 ---
DE PRINCIPIIS SUPERSUBSTANTIAL. 35

...mountains and stones melt and are dissolved; and a foul, muddy, dark, and hard body is changed at His sight, as it were, in the twinkling of an eye. Do we not see that in the very sheath, the iron of the sword, because of its rebellious nature, is shattered or consumed by the force of lightning, the sheath meanwhile remaining unharmed, inasmuch as its material is obedient to the impressions of lightning and not so rebellious? How much more then will the inexplicable and omnipotent face of Jehovah act in dense things, and in those partaking of darkness? Furthermore, He often also hardens the spirit or heart of men, so that by their own spirit they may act more vehemently against Him. Therefore, Jod in י (Yod) is the same as Jah; which is a symbol of clemency and benignity, inasmuch as it exists in an obedient, gentle, and humble spirit; For we see that the same fire varies its effects according to the effects of the medium in which it exists: Yet fire never changes its action; but the variety of the spirit or matter upon which it acts is the cause of the variety of its effects.

But, since all these properties are unique to the one essence of God, therefore we call Jehovah the general source of all health, who in himself, and in his ineffable essence, contains the three aforesaid properties of the Godhead: For God, and his power, and the Spirit of both are one God, no differently than the Sun; and the light of the Sun, and its heat are called a single Sun; because God without his power and holy Spirit can no more be called God, than the Sun, deprived of its light and heat, would thereafter deserve to be called the Sun: Hence Moses said; *Jehovah your God is your life, and the length of your days. Deuteronomy 30.* And Solomon; *God gave the number of life and days. Ecclesiastes 5:17.* But nevertheless, these properties are also attributed to the world, on account of the diverse operations of the emanation of rays or light flowing from Jod, arising from the diverse resistance of diverse matter. We say therefore that God is the general principle of life and health; We also say with St. John, *that the Word was with God, and the Word was God, and the Word was in the beginning with God, and that all things were made through him, and without him was nothing made that was made.* From which it is clear, that this was that Wisdom, of which the Wise Man *in Proverbs 3.* says, *that by her Jehovah founded the earth, and established the heavens, and broke open the deep, etc.* But let us proceed further with the words of St. John; *In him was life, and the life was the light of men, and the light shines in darkness; but the darkness did not comprehend it, etc.* This Word therefore is the light of the world, or that Wisdom, *which Jehovah possessed in the beginning of his way, before his works, before that time, which was with him as a master craftsman arranging all things. Proverbs 8.* Or, as John means, *the Word, which was in the beginning with God,* this was that unique and simple Spirit of Wisdom; which the Wise Man *in Wisdom 7.* called *a vapor of the power and might of God and a certain pure emanation, or a stream of the clarity of almighty God, or the brightness and splendor of eternal light, or an unspotted mirror of the majesty of God, and an image of his goodness; which is more beautiful than the Sun, and above every arrangement of the stars; compared to light, it is found to be prior;* This, I say, is that light, the fountain of life; and all lives of things are said to flow from it; Hence it is said, that the word of God is like a refined fire, which is a shield to those who take refuge in it *Proverbs 30.* that is, who preserves life and health for those who place themselves under the shadow of his wings, according to that *Psalm 35: You preserve men and beasts, Jehovah; how precious is your loving-kindness and mercy; when the children of men take refuge under the shadow of your wings, etc.* This wisdom therefore is the light of men; and that light is the life of things; Therefore life, being, and light are from the Word or Messiah, who is the power of the Tetragrammaton, inasmuch as in him, and through him, all things that exist were made, and without him nothing, as John testifies: This, I say, is that tree of life situated in the midst of paradise, *Genesis 3:24.* of which the Wise Man *in Proverbs 3.* says that it is a tree of life to those who lay hold of it. In this wisdom, therefore, we Christians believe with certain and infallible faith that we are to be saved in soul and body through a complete resurrection, and that we shall enjoy that second and eternal life, subject to no disturbances, through death, and that it was necessary for this wisdom of the Godhead, or the Word, to humble itself in the spirit of Jah, and to put on human flesh, so that it, finally made man or the second Adam, after having won victory over death and the Devil, might abolish the sins of the first Adam by its righteousness, wipe away the deadly stain of the human race, and by its life-giving spirit bring it about that what is sown in corruption and dishonor may rise in glory, and that what is natural and mortal may become supernatural and immortal, and thus also, that what was formerly dark and corporeal may, by the power of that divine man, be made luminous and purely spiritual. Moreover, that such a man, with a God-like spirit, would be exalted beyond and above human reason, and that he would thus be of the lineage of the Gods, who would be the true *savior* or creator of the human race, the very Gentiles themselves held for certain and believed; while, however, various people, holding various opinions about his person, wrote not without hesitation and uncertainty, as will appear in the following.

CHAPTER II.
*Concerning the diverse opinion of the Gentiles about the Savior &*
Redeemer.

The Gentile philosophers also perceived that a certain Redeemer would come into the world, who would cleanse all men, submerged in the darkness of death and the shadows of ignorance, with his divine and salutary rays, and wash them with the water of eternal life; and they recognized that he would arise from a divine and glorious lineage and ancestry; but who, or what kind of person he would be, or whose, or whose mother's son he would be, was not well established among them; since one named this one, another that one, and finally a third named a third. Some wished him to be Aesculapius, the son of Jupiter, whom they said would come into this world through transmutation; among whom Emperor Julian in book 2 *against the Galileans* writes thus: *Jupiter, in his intelligibles, begot Aesculapius from himself, and destined him to earth through the life of the generative sun: He, making progress from heaven to earth, appeared uniformly indeed in the form of a man around Epidaurus: Therefore, having increased in successes there, he extended his salutary right hand over the whole earth, to restore ill-disposed souls and bodies in poor health:* Similarly, in Plato's *Phaedo* it is held that the wisest Socrates, condemned to death, vowed that a rooster should be offered to Aesculapius; inasmuch as the rooster is sacred to Apollo Phoebus, who is called the Sun, because he is the joyful messenger of the hours and the day. The reason for this, however, is that Aesculapius was named by the ancients

--- Page 535 ---

jubilation, victory, and triumph of Apollo, which is called Paean. Therefore, he offered that rooster to him in sacrifice, so that to Apollo, that is, to the first and incorporeal Sun, the dispenser of eternal life, he might render the soul of one dying peacefully with the jubilation and Paean of joy; For Paean denotes a brief cessation and rest after liberation. That divine Orpheus also seems to assent to the opinion of these, who sang in his hymns: ἰητὴρ πάντων Ἀσκληπιὲ δέσποτα παιάν ἐλθὲ μάκαρ σωτὴρ βιοτῆς τέλος ἐσθλὸν ὁ παύων, that is, Healer of all, Aesculapius; Lord Paean, come, blessed savior, providing a good end to life. And these opinions of theirs pertain only to the salvation of the soul. But as for what pertains to the cures of the body, the aforesaid Julian, invoking Jupiter as witness, asserts that he knew many who were helped in the greatest dangers; indeed, he confesses that he himself, suffering grievously, often escaped safe by his remedies. Others, Hercules himself, son of Alcmene

CAP. III.

*Concerning the action of the Word, or the virtue of the Tetragrammaton, in the first and principal kind of health, which is called Sal-*
*vation.*

The Word, the Wisdom of Jehovah, and its first emanation in the production and creation of light, introduced Jah as the first cognomen of God from its operation in the world; in which it exercises benevolence towards the creatures of the first He (ה) or heaven, which is joined with Jod (י): And hence David the Prophet says; *If you, Jah, O Lord, should mark iniquities, who could stand? With you there is forgiveness, that you may be reverently worshipped: He has redeemed Israel from all its iniquities: With Jehovah there is benevolence and abundant redemption with him* Psalm 130. Hence also wisdom is called a sweet, humane, and benevolent Spirit, inasmuch as it acts in a subtle, flexible, sweet, tender spirit, and one most obedient to its actions: From which, and in that heaven and its simplest and purest elements, it made living creatures, subject to no sickness or passion of contrariety; namely, angelic intelligences always rejoicing in God, and eternally obedient to Him: In this heaven, therefore, wisdom rejoices and is affected with inexplicable joy: Hence *Proverbs 9. I, wisdom, stood by him as a foster-child, arranging all things, while I was with him in upbringing and was in joys daily, gladdening and playing before him, at all times:* Hence also it began to have the will, that likewise with the sons of men, who most closely approach angelic nature, it might have delights and pleasures, and might gladden and play similarly in the habitable world, as is found in the same chapter: And this is the reason why the Prophet says *Psalm 33:5. The earth is full of the benevolence of Jehovah.*

Then this most sacred emanation of the Tetragrammaton, extending itself more deeply, namely to the region of Vau (ו), and immersing itself in the darkness of that region, namely the Firmament, produces Jeho (יהו); which is a seal situated in the center of the world; by which the Word marked permanent forms of life in a more hard and rebellious spirit. And in this heaven the virtue of the Tetragrammaton, or the emanation of omnipotent clarity, acts not so sweetly as in the Empyrean spirit; inasmuch as it resists its actions and the impressions of Jehovah's seal more: And yet, since this Spirit is of a middle nature between subtle and dense waters, therefore with minimal resistance it is rendered obedient to receive the vital rays of eternal light: Hence also, because of its obedience, divine light acts mercifully with it, and by imbuing it with immortality and incorruptibility, established it as an ethereal and vital tabernacle of the soul of the world, moving in the sphere of equality; so that divine virtue satisfied the appetite of that Spirit; Thus, therefore, by a remarkable mediocrity, as a medium between the term from which and to which, it separated one extremity from another, namely the upper He (ה) from the lower He (ה), that is, waters from waters, namely the subtle from the dense.

Finally, this virtue and power of Jehovah, penetrating from the region of Vau (ו) even to the center of the earth, delineates the lowest region of the world, symbolically described by the last He (ה) of the Tetragrammaton: But, since this region includes all dark spirits, repelled from the superior heavens, therefore the spirits of this region are rebellious, hard, cold, and of great resistance; From which it happens that divine strength, stronger than all strength, whose task it is to subject to its dominion even hard and perverse power, breaks up the ranks of darkness, and with a great and thundering voice repels them into the center of the abyss, so that they cannot rise again to this very day. Thus, therefore, the warring elements are distinguished, and are separated from each other by the bonds of peace and harmony: Thus the earth was founded, and thus the heavens were made, And indeed all these things were accomplished by Wisdom, according to that saying of Solomon *Proverbs 3. Jehovah by Wisdom founded the earth, established the heavens by understanding, by which the abysses were broken open, etc.*

But here it must be observed, that these lowest spirits, because of their density and rebellious nature against the disposition of the active light, and because of their participation with the darkness from which they emerged, by which they are more opposed to the Deiform light, are always prone to rebellion; Hence also, because of their resistance and rebellion against the actions of the Word, simple elements are subjected to mutations and alterations, and their compounds to sickness and death: And yet the endeavor of the spirit of wisdom is also in this corruptible region of the world, through purification, subtilization, separation of darkness, and illumination of opaque things, to save things subject to death, and to cure those that are sick, to restore those wasting away, and even to raise up men extinguished by disease and lifeless by a double resurrection: For Jod (י) through the highest He (ה) produced Vau (ו) the Word; and the lowest He (ה) through Vau (ו), or the virtue of the Tetragrammaton, or the Messiah, will be led back in the circuit of time into Jod (י), or the term from which; when, namely, according to *Daniel 6. The Ancient of Days, coming in majesty, will give power, and honor, and kingdom to the son of man;* For

--- Page 537 ---
**DE PRINCIPIIS SUPERSUBSTANTIAL. 39**

For it will be necessary, since the letters of the Tetragrammaton are all circular, that the last letter He, of the name Jehovah, return from the nature of a dense and rebellious spirit into the disposition of the higher He, namely, mild, humble, benevolent, subtle, and immortal, according to that [passage] in Revelation 21, *I saw the new city Jerusalem descending from heaven, etc.*
For the eternal Virtue is always the same; but the difference of actions occurs by reason of the matter and the subject upon which it acts. And in this way, heaven and earth, constituting the world, are produced by a wondrous creation, by the power of the Word and the Wisdom of the Creator, according to that hieroglyphic and symbolic exemplar of the ineffable name Jehovah; in whose dimension is found the origin of both health and salvation, and of sickness and death: But so great is the benevolence of the Tetragrammaton, that it far exceeds its indignation: Hence its first He, or the Empyrean heaven, is full of divine grace, and therefore is the sanctuary of salvation, redemption, resurrection, and eternal life. Furthermore, also from its Vau, or the ethereal heaven, in which the fount of life and the tree dwell in their solar sanctuary, a benevolent and universal medicine descends, which is called the quintessence itself; by whose presence rebellious elements, freed from their native ethereal bond and now beginning to contend, are rendered obedient, and by the power of that common bond and wondrous glue, are perceived to agree with each other in perfect harmony; so that we perceive the greater portion of the mundane spirit to be filled with grace, life, and the benevolent spirit of the Almighty; but we observe the smaller, and especially the lowest and elemental portion, to be subject to change, morbid intemperance, and death itself, as we shall show below. It now remains for us to declare what that virtue of the Tetragrammaton is, by which so many and so great kinds of benevolence towards creatures, both lower and higher, are exercised.

**CAP. IV.**

*Concerning the author's Cabalistic invention, by which he seems to prove, with numbers, the mixture of divinity with the natural spirit; Likewise concerning the greatest divinity of the number five, both in numbers and in Hebrew letters.*

Most difficult is the dispute and discussion, both among common theologians and scholastic ones, concerning the essence of the Deity immersing and expanding itself into the material world: For theologians entirely deny that *God is Nature itself*: Hence they usually impose the name of heretics upon those who confuse God and nature, saying that Naturalists so venerate nature that, ignorant of God himself, they take Nature for God: But (with their leave, I would say) those are entangled in a more difficult labyrinth of ignorance who, having ignored nature, think they will arrive at the true knowledge of God; since it is impossible to reach from one extreme to the other without a middle, or to ascend Jacob's ladder without steps, or to contemplate and meditate on the highest pinnacle of the fifty gates of the sages' intelligence, unless we begin from effects and, according to the order of creation, gradually tend towards higher things by speculation. How, I ask, is it possible for us to reach from earth to the third heaven, where Ehieh or Jah is found, unless through the steps of the elements we gradually and increasingly refine our sense according to the disposition of the higher degrees, and then ascend through the orbs of the ethereal heaven, full of the quintessence, in whose region the marrow of all nature, and God himself, is clothed in the garment of the moist nature of the firmament, so that we may at last arrive at the Empyrean place, where God Jehovah or Jah is adorned with the simple garment of the intellectual Spirit, to whose knowledge Moses arrived, although he could not see Him as He was, a simple Jod, stripped of all material garment? Hence therefore it was the opinion of the Cabalists that God in nature is clothed in many garments: And I indeed, also by a speculation not to be scorned or rejected, have found this multiplicity of those garments in this way.

In the Archetypal world, through the progression of one property of the most holy Trinity to another, we have observed a threefold order from the digits of a simple number, namely three times three into nine; of which the first was 1, 2, 3, which is the radical order, and the simplest of all; hence it denotes how unity has flowed into a radical line, which is formed from points of the first order; and so this order designates the linear and simple nature of the emanation of the first mundane heaven; whose unity is Jod: And the first hierarchy is attributed to 1, the second to 2, and the third to 3. Here therefore it denotes that Jod in this heaven puts on a simple garment of lines, namely He (ה): as if 1 were to put on 2 and 3, which make five; which is the number of He, according to the disposition of the first order in the Archetypal world. The second order of emanation, proceeding from the first in a ternary number, is 4, 5, 6, denoting an imperfect surface, namely three times two, or twice three: Hence the last number 6 signifies Vau; and five in the middle declares He hidden in the belly or center of Vau: From which it is clear that this second [order] in the formal world, from the first order

emanation is the type of the middle heaven or firmament: And since the odd number (five) is found in the middle between 4 and 6, it therefore denotes that the perfection of that heaven is clothed with a double portion of matter: For an even number denotes matter, and an odd number denotes form: And 4 similarly denotes the square of duality, or the surface of a line; and thus the number 5 establishes its tabernacle in the middle, between 4 (that is, the upper part of the ether or firmament) and 6 (which are the lower and coarser part of the middle heaven); namely in the Sun, which is called the heart of heaven: And hence it can be said that this heaven, on account of the position of the formal number five in its center, is the Fifth essence: Therefore, in this second order of the Archetype 4, 5, 6, the starry heaven and the sphere of Saturn, and the sphere of Jupiter are given to 4. But the sphere of Mars, the sphere of the soul or equality passing through the center of the Sun, and the solar sphere itself are assigned to 5. And the sphere of Venus, Mercury, and the Moon are assigned to the number 6: And certainly, the reason is at hand why the two extremes are even and imperfect, the former being of a lesser order, and the latter of a greater; because, namely, the upper, that is 4, is the spirit of that connection with He (ה) or the Empyrean spirit, which is the more subtle part of matter; Hence, a lesser parity is continued with it by the fact that it approaches more closely to a simple odd number; But the lower, namely 6, is joined with the gross and lowest spirit of He: Hence it exceeds the upper even number by two, denoting by this very fact that the more the emanation of Jod tends downwards, the more it immerses itself in imperfect matter, and progresses deeper into multitude.

And although we attribute to the divine majesty, dwelling in the sea of the world, only three vestments for the diversity of the matter of the three heavens, which are manifest, nevertheless, God puts on in the world as many and as varied garments as there are units in the multitude of matter; And hence arises in all things the distinction of genera, and in genera of species, and in species of individuals from one another.

But, to proceed to the ultimate typical order of the formal world, which is 7, 8, 9, just as in the supreme He or first emanation 1, 2, 3, we found an even number between two imperfect and odd characters; namely 2. So also in the lowest, where matter is multiplied, or in the ultimate progression of the divine numbers 7, 8, 9, we find 8, an even number, between two perfect odd numbers: The number 2, therefore, the center of the supreme order, as a root multiplied by itself, produces 4, the square in the second heaven; and that again produces 8 in the lowest, which is the cube of the whole. Thus, therefore, we see how God is clothed with matter in the world: For every odd figure of these divine digits or numbers is a symbol of divinity: And hence it is written that **God delights in an odd number**; namely, because of its perfe

In Abraham's *Yetzirah* we read these things; Ten Sephiroth beyond the ineffable number of 10 digits, namely five against five; and the superlative covenant of one intended in the middle; in the interpretation of the tongue and circumcision, ten Sephiroth without the ineffable. Therefore we have studied to arrange or dispose these 10 digits by Hebrew letters in such a way that five would be against five; so that the superlative covenant of one might be established in the middle. Therefore, in the first preceding demonstration, I placed five, namely א י ו ה ה, against ה ה ו י ב; yet in such a way that the covenant of unity might be found in the middle. I therefore arranged, as described previously, namely Aleph (א) and Yod (י) as if in a hidden world endowed with eternity, thereby denoting how God was Alpha and Omega before creation. Hence Aleph (א), as Unity looking towards Nothing, is called Nothing or Non-Being, and not an end; as far as we are concerned; although All in itself: And thus it existed with respect to our understanding, before it decided to shine forth into the potential world, and by another name; as the Cabalists wish, it is called the dark Aleph (א): But when it wished to change its form, and to behold the world submerged in darkness with its splendid and luminous face, it was called the lucid Aleph (א): Whence it is written of it; "As is the darkness, so is its light." This also Hermes Trismegistus left to us, handed down in open words, saying; "When he had said these things, he changed his form, and suddenly revealed all things; for I beheld a certain immense spectacle; namely, all things converted into light, etc. And a little later; A horrendous shadow glided underneath with an oblique revolution, etc." Then, in alphabetical order, I placed Beth (ב) after Aleph (א), inasmuch as it is a sign of Wisdom; and it also denotes grammatically a house or habitation; symbolically it also designates He (ה) as the son, inasmuch as it is the first emanation from Aleph (א), and so in other cases. Similarly, we placed Yod (י) in the same way in the center of the numbers, or in the place of the quinarius (number five); however, since we did not find that grammatical and common arrangement so suitable for finding the mystery of the name of the Tetragrammaton, we therefore arranged those letters in this manner, so that Aleph (א) in the center, on the right side, looks upon He (ה) with its light; furthermore, Yod (י) looks out from the left from a single center, which we said was above the quinarius number; since this number is a double center, as has been demonstrated before; namely, either of the formal digits 1, 3, (5), 7, 9, or of the material digits 2, 4, (5), 6, 8. Now indeed it has been said above, that the dark Aleph (א) is taken for God and for the principle and formal unity without respect to matter; And Yod (י) is unity, or the lucid Aleph (א), and it respects matter; Whence Yod (י), always existing as unity, is joined with the cipher for its existence; just as in Jehovah it is joined with He (ה), which denotes the first entry into matter; Or the lucid Aleph (א) illuminates the spirit He (ה) next to it: And, as Aleph (א) is the first letter, which is the principle of the divine essence Ehieh (אהיה), who is the father, and the first origin of all, or as it were a point in the body, so to it the first heaven is dedicated, namely He (ה); into which, looking with its shining face, it is called the lucid Aleph (א); which is the same as Yod (י) in the Tetragrammaton: Whence Aleph (א) is called the principal, namely unity, and one, or the final, namely for the end of the denarii (tens). Therefore the lucid Aleph (א) claims for itself the first heaven through He (ה), signified on the right side of the order, which properly denotes spirit and respiration; And because it is simpler than all the spirits of the letters, and stronger in its simplicity, it denotes the North wind; and from the lucidity which it first received from

of the word YHWH, in which much divinity is comprehended, namely Aleph, the first power of light, and Yod, the act of light in He, and Resh, denoting objects which are seen by the eye as if of God: For Resh signifies things born of the earth, and the four elements, and all lower things, which are vivified by divine sight, and multiplied by creation; whence it denotes the fruitfulness and grace of offspring. We could institute an infinite discourse about this mystery; but for the sake of brevity we deem it to be omitted in this place, so that we may proceed more quickly to other things. Therefore, just as on the right side the entry of the rays of Aleph into He produced the first heaven; so also on the left side the entry of Yod into Vau produced the second or middle heaven: For, as Aleph is to Yod, of which one is different from the other in position, and yet they are the same in essence; so also is He to Vau; since of these He is prior, and Vau is posterior; and yet both are of the nature of a humid spirit. And this is the name of divine majesty, revealed through the ineffable Tetragrammaton in a fiery vision from the dark center of Chaos, or from the dense mist of waters and clouds, namely, YHWH: Where the two interior letters denote the supersubstantial form, but the two extreme letters denote matter: Which letters, if arranged thus, הויה (Ho-yah), will represent the ineffable name of God; For He has the property of He itself at the end, both inasmuch as one or the other is not pronounced, and because Aleph denotes aura, as He denotes spirit: Indeed, according to Abraham in Yetzirah, Aleph in its grammatical signification denotes spirit itself and respiration: Furthermore, it is also a guttural letter, like Chet. The cloud or Chaos surrounding this appearing divinity will be on the right side Daleth, which signifies a door, a gate; Therefore, it is as it were the door of divine apparition, through which wisdom goes forth into the world: And hence it is that, according to the Cabalists, Daleth is an indication of wisdom, as Reuchlin attests. Afterwards, Gimel and Beth make up the more sloping part of the cloud or shadow: Where also Gimel in the last place argues for life, produced into the world through wisdom. So also on the left side, Zain denotes arms; Whence Psalm 18:31: The word of God is most pure, and a shield to all who take refuge in Him: And Kaph, Pe, Ayin represent the remaining portion of Chaos or darkness, from which again, as from purified elements, creatures are composed. Therefore, on one side we have 5 letters, and on the other 5, but in the center of the quinaries remains the ineffable mystery of the Tetragrammaton. This quinary number, therefore, is the center of the denary number; which is also a spherical number: Whence, by multiplying Yod or 10 by He (five) (which two letters make Yah), the product will be 50, which is the number of the gates of intelligence; Or by multiplying 5 by 5 (for a double quinary is found in the same center) the product will be 25, which, multiplied by the number of quinaries, which is two, will make 50. Indeed, the field of this mystery is so vast and ample that we could fill an immense volume with it; but, since the main subject of this book calls us elsewhere, having left that Cabalistic doctrine, we will approach a plainer path.

CAP. V.

*A still clearer demonstration of divinity, existing everywhere in the mundane spirit; Where it is also proven that the Messiah is the virtue or act of the Tetragrammaton, for the universal salvation of things, and their liberation and redemption from darkness and the stigmata of death, and for the healing of bodies and souls that are beyond the limits of health, and their restoration to pristine health.*

What that virtue of the Tetragrammaton is, which we, with the Cabalists, not disagreeing with the sacred scriptures, call the Messiah, although in the preceding chapter we have openly declared it in the manner of the Cabalists, here, however, we will explain it with a demonstration more familiar to the common people. The Cabalists seem to distribute the world into as many virtues of God as there are worlds or heavens: Therefore they wish that the animated world be illuminated by that mind which they call Metatron; And they assert that the supreme or angelic world is ruled by the soul of the Messiah (which they call the ideated idea of all lives), and that the eternal world is governed by the light of the soul of the Messiah, which is Elhai, that is, the living God: And this light of Adonai is Ensoph, that is, infinity, as it were the highest, incomprehensible, and ineffable thing. Therefore they make Metatron, whom they call the active intellect of the primum mobile, communicate with the Messiah, that is, the soul of the world with the soul of the Messiah, or the nature of the Empyrean Spirit with that of the ethereal. They also hand down that the soul of the Messiah and the light of Elhai do not differ from each other: But they call Elhai the fountain of living waters, and the soul of the Messiah the spring or river of life; and they assert that this supreme world, Ensoph, is that of the Deity, whom the Seraphim celebrated by saying, Holy, Holy, Holy, Tetragrammaton, that is, God Himself naked in His purest essence without any respect to matter. These therefore wish that the soul of Metatron be distinguished from the soul of the Messiah, and that the latter finally from the light of Elhai, whom

--- Page 543 ---

whom we have called the luminous Aleph. But, as it seems to me (with their kind permission), they have spoken of the variety of the operation of the one God in the multitude, or of the indivisible and uncreated form in the created mundane spirit: For, as we said before, the act is always the same, but the difference in spiritual matter in obedience and obstinacy, that is, in thinness and density, entirely creates and brings about the difference in mundane acts: For the act is always according to the nature of resistance; because the act, which is divine virtue and power, overcomes all things; Hence, with the gentle, kind, humble, and obedient, it acts kindly, softly, and sweetly; but with the hard, proud, obstinate, and perverse, it proceeds gravely and violently: And from this it happens that, although God is always good, and His virtue tends towards goodness, nevertheless, the resistance opposing this goodness of action is the cause of the denomination of evil; so indeed, that divine action is always good, even if, especially with respect to the effect of rebellion and resistance in that suffering subject upon which it acts, it is called evil by men; since evil is not found before God, but before men: And from this arises that the act of God towards men, is understood by men to be the same as justice and benevolence, or punishment and reward and joy; and yet justice and benevolence are one and the same before God: Thus we also see in fire both benefit and harm; namely, it is observed to warm cold limbs with its heat; and yet the same unchanged nature of fire burns and destroys. Therefore, the rebellion of the subject causes or is the reason why the action of God is called wrath; and likewise, conversely, the obedience of the same causes it to be called grace, and salvation, and life. But more on these things below. From these things, therefore, we conclude that the virtue of the Tetragrammaton is the same throughout the entire mundane spirit, although the effect differs according to its thinness and density: For thus we see that the heat of this virtue, looking down from the Solar body, is hotter and more effective in the air during summer due to its density, inasmuch as it is thickened by vapors rising from springs, rivers, and stagnant waters. Therefore we also see that the Cabalists, in distinguishing the action of each heaven, have dedicated the lower and visible parts of the world to Metattron, but the higher, invisible, and angelic parts to the soul of the Messiah, and the eternal world of Ensoph or the Deity or Trinity to the light of Elhai or the Tetragrammaton: For they seem to confess that the fountain of living waters, that is, of uncreated fiery spirits, is the kingdom of the Tetragrammaton Ensoph, from which Jod looks down, and that the soul of the Messiah is a stream gushing forth from that fountain; whose sea, into which that stream or emanation discharges itself or flows, they make the angelic or Empyrean heaven, or He (ה), the second letter of the Tetragrammaton: And yet elsewhere they acknowledge that this soul is the ideated idea of all lives, to which all vitality, both individual, specific, and general, is referred: We also confess that this virtue of the Tetragrammaton, inhabiting the Empyrean heaven in this world, is the highest source and genus of all lives among created things, emanating from the most general genus, that is, from the Transcendent Being. But indeed, that a genus exists without its species, or a species without its individuals, we utterly deny. Therefore, the virtue of the Tetragrammaton of the Messiah in the Empyrean heaven is, as it were, the genus of vivification, and is compared by the Cabalists themselves to the trunk of the root, whose roots are in Ensoph: Then this genus divides itself into species in the ethereal heaven, or the trunk there spreads its branches, which are the stars: Finally, those species transmit other subordinate species downwards into the elements, like the branches of a tree transmit their tips and leaves; and at last the fruits of the subordinate species in the elements communicate the fruits of life to individuals, namely, animals, vegetables, and minerals.

From these things, therefore, we see that, just as the effect of the root in a tree is the trunk; which retains in itself all the virtue of life that it received from the root, and then diffuses the same vital force into a multitude of branches, and the branches again into other subdivided twigs, and these finally into a multitude of fruits; or as a genus is divided into its species, and those species are subdivided into subordinate species, and these themselves finally into individuals, so also the matter stands in the emanation of the glittering river of life from the fountain of living waters, existing in the supercelestial paradise; which river, flowing into the Empyrean sea, as a genus, divides itself into branches, through which it fills all the luminous fountains of the ethereal heaven; from whose fullness other streams gush forth, each downwards into individuals destined and

...ral? Is it indeed the Messiah God, or the angel Metatron, or nature itself? Certainly, it is the Messiah, Angel, & universal nature; but accepted in different ways. The Messiah Christ is called, both by sacred scriptures and Cabalistic doctrine, the beginning, middle, and end of all creatures, and consequently the beginning, middle, and end of divine fluxes communicated to created beings: Indeed, St. John teaches that it is the very beginning, and that it is God himself, and that this beginning was with God, denoting that it proceeded from the palace or kingdom of Ensoph into this world: Therefore, inasmuch as it is the beginning in the world, the more worthy place in the world, and the first created by it, is attributed to it. That it is the middle is attested by the beauty of the Sun, in which it placed its tabernacle; whence the Sun is also called the dispenser of life and light, because from the Word, in which was light, which was the life of all, it received its life-giving power: Hence it is also called the tree of life placed in the midst of the garden of Paradise, Genesis 2:9. For its seat was in the midst of the universal created Paradise, namely in the heart of the world or heaven, or in the center of the universal dark cloud: Hence it is written in Ecclesiastes 24: "I, Wisdom, like a ditch drawn from a river, and like an aqueduct, proceeded into Paradise, and I said, I will water my garden most excellently." But that river or fountain, from which this virtue, or holy and shining wisdom, proceeded, was the Tetragrammaton itself, according to that in Psalm 87: "My fountains of life are from God." And Ecclesiastes 9:17: "God gave the number of life and days." And certainly, first from the composition of the Macrocosm, from whose midst Phoebus, the origin of life, is said to flow into the lower regions, and then afterwards through the fabric of the Microcosm; in whose center or middle region the heart, the fountain of life, is found, denoting that the process of spiritual life, and the fountain of lives, is that middle through which all things are vivified: But it also similarly exists as a mediator between the most miserable condition of the region of darkness, and that excellent and splendid palace of the lucid fountain, in which Jah, full of clemency and benignity, reigns for ever and ever; so that by its mediation, salvation is conferred from holy heaven upon the sick and languid, and salvation and redemption are sent from the highest heavens to things condemned to eternal death. Finally, it is called the end, because, as the small א (Aleph) was its lucid beginning, so the great Aleph was its end; indeed, from which it returns to the point from which it came; and so on to infinity. Hence by St. John in Revelation 1, it is called Alpha & Omega. The Messiah is therefore the beginning from which all things proceed, and into which they return.

And this virtue, indeed, inasmuch as it is considered in itself and by itself simply, without any matter in whose fluid it floats, is the true and absolute essence of God, and consequently God himself: Hence St. John says; "And this Word was with God, and that was God himself." But indeed, inasmuch as it is regarded in mundane mixture, that is, inasmuch as this virtue is mixed with the humid nature of the world; to that extent it is called an angel: For thus the denomination comes not from simplicity and identity, that is, from Divinity, but from simple composition and alterity; since an angel is created from a most pure created spirit, and uncreated light, creating that spirit: Hence the denomination comes from the created and informed part, but not from the uncreated light. Hence, understanding it of the Messiah, Jacob said to his sons in his last testament. Genesis 48:16: "The God before whose sight my fathers continually walked, the God who feeds me to this day, the Angel who delivers me from all evil, bless these boys, and let my name be invoked upon them, and also the names of my fathers Abraham and Isaac, and let them grow into a multitude upon the earth." Since therefore in this place Jacob asks the same things from the angel that he asked from God himself, and since he deems him worthy of equal honor, this angel certainly cannot be taken for anyone other than the Messiah, and for God clothed in a created spiritual garment. Hence also, he who is called Jehovah in Exodus 13:21, in those words: "Jehovah going before them by day in a pillar of cloud, etc." of him it is said in chapter 14:19: "Then the angel of God himself, who went before the camp, etc." To them it was a cloud and darkness, but to these it illuminated the night itself. From which it is clear that Jehovah is here called an angel, inasmuch as his power was joined with humid nature, or clothed in the garb of a cloud: Hence, because here there was a composition of the first kind or alterity, namely from fire, which is the simple essence of God, and from water, which was the covering of that essence (for a cloud and fire appeared), therefore here in one place the angel has his denomination from the fiery form or essence, which is the power of Jehovah, and thus is called Jehovah; but in another place Jehovah is denominated from created matter, namely from water or a cloud, and is called an angel: And again, that angel is called Jehovah, ibid. chapter 24, in those words; "When Jehovah looked down upon the camp of the Egyptians in the pillar of fire and cloud, etc." From which it can also be known that, when Jehovah is called an angel, the denomination of the cloud is preferred to the denomination of fire, arguing that according to the disposition of created matter, the discourse is about a creature, namely an angel; so indeed, that from this the word cloud and its order precede the denomination of fire: But where in the last discourse Jehovah is taken or placed for an angel, there the name of the formal essence, namely fire, is preferred to the material or cloud word: Hence by "Angel" in this place (as interpreters have not inappropriately hinted) the Messiah and Christ are understood: By which form of speech he is also mentioned in Exodus 23:25, in these words, "Behold, I send an angel before you; Take heed of his face, etc." because my name is in him. From these things, therefore, we conclude; that in the Messiah the complete name Tetragrammaton, J. H. U. H., is found, inasmuch as he himself operates by its power: For the Messiah is the very power of the Tetragrammaton.

My reason is, because משיח (Mashiach), by Cabalistic transposition, becomes ישמח (Yishmaḥ), that is, Messiah. There are, however, Cabalists who say that this angel was Michael, because in his name מיכאל (Michael) is found: But the same can also be said of Raphael, Gabriel, Zabkiel,

kiel, Uriel, and others; In whom we can observe that in the otherness of Angels, God Himself appears in a certain way, or His essential power; whence they are called mirrors, in which God is seen: Yet, inasmuch as they are composed, they are called creatures; and, because they are creatures, they are therefore inferior to the creator, and subject to Him and His ministers. Others believe that this angel is Metatron, who was the angel ministering to Moses: For the Cabalists made him the soul of the world, and handed down that he was the first created thing, and contained in himself the perfection of all things: Indeed, they held this soul of the world to be that most holy wisdom, which *Sirach 1* narrated was created first of all things, and was the understanding of prudence from eternity, whose source it wrote was the word of God in the highest: This they said was that angel, in whom the name of God is found; indeed, in whom the name Shaddai, enclosed by a number equal to both words, is found. However, these opinions of theirs do not please me, because, according to our discovery, established by secure contemplation and certain foundations, we have found that that angel was the Messiah himself, or the power of the Tetragrammaton, containing in himself the complete name of the Tetragrammaton: Hence, not without a singular reason, this angel is sometimes called Jehovah, namely with respect to the power and the name itself placed in him, and sometimes an angel, namely with respect to the angelic nature, in which those living and eternal characters of the Tetragrammaton itself are expressed. The ineffable name of the Tetragrammaton is the Most High God Himself, universally dispersing the being of this His name through the mundane spirit: But where this spiritual angelic nature is, there also this fiery, complete name of the Tetragrammaton is found: And yet the name of the Tetragrammaton extends everywhere and in all places; Therefore, likewise, this angel, who is the spirit of wisdom, filling all things, and leaving nothing empty, mixes himself throughout the universal mundane spirit, and informs all things through the name and power of the Tetragrammaton, and preserves them once informed. But how this created spirit received in itself all the characters of the letters of the Tetragrammaton, by which it, and with it the whole universe, was informed, we have demonstrated in the preceding [sections]; namely, Jod (י), the root at the summit of the machine, through its spirit He (ה) illuminated the upper waters, or the Empyrean spirit: and Vau (ו) illuminated and informed the ethereal kingdom of the stars, and from the power of the final He (ה), the elemental heaven acquired its being; so that in the head of that angel is Jod (י); in the breast and middle, where its heart is, Vau (ו) resides in the Sun; and the final He (ה), carrying with it the spirit of divinity, prepared the lower world, and informed it, making it beautiful and cleansed from darkness, and distinguished the elements. Hence the universal spirit is called *Mundus* (World/Clean) from its cleansing and washing from unclean darkness; which indeed was done by the power and presence of the name of Jehovah. Nor will anyone say that if the universal spirit is a material part of one angel, no other angels can exist, because one angel would have filled the entire world. For we respond that, just as God Tetragrammaton is outside all things, and yet contains all things in Himself, so also His power, which is of the same essence as Himself, contains all other angels, and indeed every other creature, as an infinite king subjecting all things to His will. Therefore, this power is inherent in all composite things, by whose beneficent property they live; it is also present in the elements outside all composite things; and the entire spirit receives soul and action in it and through it: Hence the spirit, in which it dwells, is its garment; and this very divine power informs its garment in diverse ways according to greater or lesser subtlety or density, and imposes a name upon it according to the condition of the body or matter thus created. This, then, is that Wisdom (*Sirach 1*) created before all things with respect to its garment; but truly uncreated, if we consider that its power is of the nature and essence of Jehovah Himself; Of which the Wise Man speaks in *Proverbs 3*: *Jehovah by wisdom founded the earth, and established the heavens by understanding: And Proverbs 8:22: Jehovah possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works, before any time, before the age I was anointed etc.* Here then we see that wisdom, the greatest angel, and prince of angels, the soul of the entire world, the power of the Tetragrammaton, inasmuch as the name and power of Jehovah are inscribed upon it, is called created with respect to matter: But, all consideration of matter removed, there remains only the most formal and ineffable name of the Tetragrammaton, from whom, in whom, and through whom all things were made. And this, if I am not mistaken, Saint John understands in chapter 1 by saying; *The true light was in the world, and the world was made through it etc.* namely, by the true light he signifies the true essence of God, and the power of the Tetragrammaton, and by the world he denotes the garment of that light or the universal spirit, which was made and created by the said light according to the will of the creator. Finally, of this angel Malachi speaks in chapter 3:1 by saying; *Behold, I send my angel, and he shall prepare the way before my face etc.* Finally, this power (inasmuch as it is held to be the essential form of the elements, by which some things are affixed to others in their spheres and places, destined by creation, as if by a divine glue, and by which all things are simultaneously coupled and connected in peace and obedience) is accepted and held by Philosophers as the very nature of things. And in this way you see, Readers, perhaps eager for novelty, how the same divine power in diverse composite forms is accustomed to have various cognomens; namely, with respect to the purest and divine light in the abstract, it is taken for God alone, and the Messiah, and Christ, that is, for identity and charity, which is the life-giving spirit of the Almighty; but in the concrete of the first composition, namely from two, for an angel, who is the otherness or creature of the first order, and in the concrete of the third composition, as in the elements themselves and the things composed of elements, for the very nature of things.

C A P. VI.

*On the reason for the benevolent action of the virtue of the Tetragrammaton towards life and health: And*
*how this same virtue, conducive to life and health, acquires various denominations in*
*the world according to the diversity of its garments.*

Through the preceding (discussions), it is explained more clearly than noonday light (as I indeed believe) to anyone, even one overwhelmed by significant foolishness and the darkness of ignorance, why the name of God Jehovah is used in natural things, since He Himself is by Himself outside and beyond all things, and is said to reign in His secret and hidden heaven without any regard for matter: Namely, His name is used there where the power and virtue of that name, clothed in Spirit, is understood, inasmuch as it dominates in all things; and again it is called Angel, inasmuch as the spiritual matter of the angel, which the name of Jehovah produced by its presence, is denoted; and so it is also called Messenger, according to that (passage) in Malachi 3: "Behold, I send my angel," etc., that is, the virtue of my name, which is in the angelic spirit, and moves it to perform the will of its creator; where by "angel" His word is understood, according to that (passage) in Psalm 40:9: "Behold, I come; in the volume of the book it is written of me, that I should do Your will." For every action is from God; but passivity is from the created spirit. And hence it happens that the denomination of an angel comes from the passive and created part, when the word 'cloud' is placed before the word 'fire'. And for this reason David in Psalm 104:4 called angels 'winds,' or 'spirits,' respecting their created nature; But joining the created part with the uncreated denotes action in the passive; Hence in the same place he calls them ministers, and a flaming fire; that is, luminous creatures created from the Spirit, illuminated on the first day.

Now the Messiah is the luminous virtue of the ineffable name's very letter, inasmuch as it is considered in nature clothed with the life-giving Spirit of the first letter ה in the name Jehovah, after whose pattern the Empyrean Spirit was created. Therefore, the being of the Word is in the Tetragrammaton and its spirit ה: The being of the Angel is in the Word, or the virtue emanating from Jod, which the Tetragrammaton implies; And the being of nature is in the soul of the angel Metatron, and in the twofold lower spirit; But the being of all composite things is in the soul of nature. And all these differences are understood with respect to the diversity of matter in which the virtue of the Tetragrammaton operates; inasmuch as all multitude is in matter; while conversely the power and virtue of the Tetragrammaton, which is the Messiah Himself, is one and the same through all things: But the diversity of matter resisting in various ways makes the acts of active virtue diverse as far as we are concerned, though not likewise with respect to divinity; inasmuch as all acts are the same there, and weighed in the same scales by supreme justice. Therefore, this virtue, bearing the presence of God Jehovah, when it immersed itself in the first created spirit, received its denomination from the nature of the Spirit: Hence it is called an angel; descending into the lower world, where it puts on a manifold garment, it is called Nature; entering into any thing, both simple and composite, it is called life. And hence arose the opinions of the Gentile Philosophers, affirming that all things are full of Gods: Hence also Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Apollo, Venus, Mercury, and Diana were affected with divine worship, as Gods, because of the copious reception of this virtue. God is stripped of all substance (א), the root of all created things is Jod; whose virtue, emanating from the Holy, Holy, Holy heavens into He, is the Messiah; Hence Jah is referred to benevolence, and benevolence is attributed to the son. And this virtue in the first created Spirit is mind or intelligence; but intelligence is an angel, which, putting on the middle spirit, is called Metatron, and the virtue of the Messiah in its center is called the soul of the world; and then the angel, putting on the elementary garment, is called Nature, which retains all superior things within itself.

Therefore, the benevolent presence of this divine virtue brings life and health; but its particular absence is followed by sickness, and its total absence by death; Thus, in the higher spirit, the Messiah gives invisibly luminous life without any obscurity; Hence angels are said to always stand before the face of Jehovah: In the middle (spirit) He gives life partly visibly and partly invisibly luminous, moderately participating in darkness; Hence the spirit is said to participate in both extremes: Therefore, in this heaven, because of the augmentation of matter, free will begins; since its nature is to adhere sometimes to the higher, sometimes to the lower: Here, therefore, matter equally mixes itself with divine nature: And this is the reason why fate is said to dwell in this place: However, in the last and lowest spirit, it encloses luminous life emanating from both higher (spirits) into a cubic and opaque body; where, because of the narrowness of the enclosed light, unless the virtue of Jehovah constantly assists it, it is oppressed, not indeed with respect to itself, as it does not suffer; but with respect to the passible and created spirit, with which it is clothed as with various garments and is said to be covered as far as human comprehension is concerned. And hence it is that the supercelestial life is that immortal (life), by whose virtue man will be free from the death of the lower spirit according to divine promise, and believes with certain and undoubted faith that he will rise again: Hence, therefore, will arise that salvation and redemption which the human
race

humanity awaits by the advent and descent of that virtue from the third heaven of St. Paul. But the celestial life is that which usually serves man during his days on earth; Which indeed is afflicted in many ways by the disquiet of the soul's virtue, Metatron, due to its defect: For this Spirit is subject as much to the evil dispositions of darkness as to the harsh or gentle actions of the light of the world. Furthermore, the outer garment of the soul, which is air, suffers as many impressions as the airy mantle of the world-soul, as will be declared below. Therefore, the elementary life conduces to a good disposition of the body, and especially resides in the faculty or natural virtue existing therein according to the laws of nature: Whose primary office is to nourish by apposition, union, and assimilation, to augment in length, breadth, and depth, to generate by the transformative virtue which draws forth the seed, and the formative virtue which shapes the drawn seed, while the secondary is to attract through straight fibers, to retain and digest through oblique fibers, and to expel through transverse fibers: Indeed, by the defect of these offices, diseases of the body or of the external man are generated and induced; but its perfection is the cause of health and the obedience of the elements: These two extremes usually occur either because the Deiform virtue, turning away its face, leaves rebellious elements the freedom to fight each other, or because, turning its face towards some hard, crude, rebellious, and preternatural humor dwelling in the body, it excites, through its preternatural resistance, an intemperance of natural action, and consequently changes it into putrefaction; hence fevers and putrid diseases: But if it gradually turns away its face of life, darkness usually creeps in little by little, and cold, stupid, crude, and frigid diseases are induced, as we shall demonstrate below.

**CHAPTER VII.**

*On the nature of the second life and its eternity; likewise on salva-*
*tion and redemption.*

**J**UST as in the name of the Tetragrammaton we find a double ה, namely one near and conjoined to the divinity of Yod, but the other more remote, and more immersed in the multitude of matter, inasmuch as the lowest waters are as far as possible from the throne of Alpha or Jah, and as close as possible to the center of darkness; But the first He is found in the waters above the firmament, where the characters of Jah are mystically delineated: thus also we see the first waters adorned with greater grace and essential light of Yod: Hence in those is found the fount and origin of eternal life; but in these, only the sustenance and succession of temporal life, descending from that supreme fount. Wherefore, due to the defect of the waters of life, and the multitude of matter, that matter always desires a new form, and the former being removed, it suffers corruption and death, so that it may put on a new form succeeding it. Hence we read; that *God has set before men two cups; one, namely, of ruin and destruction, assigned to the wicked; but the other of salvation and health, prepared for the just: For in Psalm 11:5-6 we find it thus written; Jehovah examines the righteous, but the wicked and him who loves violence his soul hates: He will rain upon the wicked coals, fire, and brimstone; and a stormy wind joined together will be the portion of their cup: And in Psalm 23:5, He sets before the righteous a saving cup; You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies; you anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows; Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of Jehovah for length of days: Likewise in Psalm 116:13, I will take the cup of salvation, and call upon the name of Jehovah.* Furthermore, that the fount of life is from God, we are taught in many places of the sacred scriptures; For thus in *Psalm 36:9 are these words; They are abundantly satisfied with the fatness of your house, and you give them to drink from the river of your pleasures. For with you is the fountain of life, and in your light we shall see light.* All life, therefore, flows from God, who sits in the highest heavens; And this life was with the Father, and this life was in the light of the Father, which is the Word of the Father, His first emanation, and Jah, or God in the benevolent Empyrean spirit, or the son of the dark Alpha, and the luminous Alpha itself; Which emanation is eternal life, or Christ and the Messiah, from whom is the life of all things, according to that in 1st Epistle of St. John 1, *Life was with the Father, and appeared to us:* Eternal life is promised to us *Ibid. chapter 2.* Life is from Christ: *Ibid. chapter 4:* God has given us eternal life, and this life is in His Son. From this life or eternal light, inasmuch as its nature and power are considered in the supreme He, where it is covered by a single, most subtle, most delicate, and most benevolent garment, proceeds that most powerful and ineffable act of rising from the dead; The effect of which is called the second life: Concerning which *Revelation 21. In the second life there will be no more death, nor sorrow, nor any more pain; In this second life they will neither thirst anymore, nor hunger, nor will the sun fall upon them, nor any heat, for the Lamb in the midst of the throne is, and will rule them, and will lead them to living fountains of waters; and God will wipe away every tear from their eyes. as it is found in Revelation 7:16:* And these things agree with that passage in *Isaiah 30:26. And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days;* By which it is signified that the uncreated light of the world will descend into the midst of the throne, that is, into the place of the sun, and will take upon itself the office of the Sun, and will cause the new Jerusalem to descend to earth, etc. For that light is that Wisdom, which is *the splendor of eternal light and the emanation of the clarity of the Almighty* F Sun
