C H A P. IX.

On the composition of the life of creatures, and on its nature, both
passive and active.

By the reasons previously alleged, it is declared that the virtue or ray of the Tetragrammaton is the unity and root
of created things, and God himself: Thus, the otherness, made from Jod and He (ה), is an angelic composition or
duality, which, joined with a third nature, namely mingling itself with the coarser spirit of the firmament, produces a
superior and simple nature, from which the vital soul usually springs. We see therefore, that
the life of the intellectual heaven (ה) becomes the supersubstantial act of Jod, which is of divinity, and in composition
the root, and becomes Jah (יה): And the life of the ethereal spirit is Jod and He (ה), that is, uncreated light in the first created spirit, and
becomes Jod, He, and Vau (יהו), that is, uncreated light, the first created spirit, and the second created spirit, this
is a double He (ה) and Jod (י) or unity; And this is the seal, by whose impressions all elemental
creatures are marked with the impressions of life; which seal is indeed called nature itself. Then the fourth
nature, namely the last He (ה), joined with those three, that is, the aerial or elemental spirit, brings
forth a dense elemental spirit, which we call the lowest and less simple Nature; by whose
action the composite body or palace, both mineral and vegetable as well as animal, is built; and
in this way the world is completed in the image of the Tetragrammaton. Therefore, Mind or Messiah is the
soul and life of angels; Sun or Jah in the ethereal spirit is the soul and life of the stars distributed
into three kinds of composition: and the fiery element (in whose womb the Messiah, covered externally by a dense cloud and a
dark veil, sometimes appears both in creation itself and after it) is the restorer of the body and of the elemental,
provided it is capable of the higher appearances of the Messiah in simple or intricate garments.
Wherefore we see that the uncreated virtue or fiery Spirit of Jehovah becomes the general life or soul of all things,
but operating in the world in diverse ways according to the diversity of its covering or garment:
Hence that self-existent Word is called, in the Empyrean spirit, Mind or active intellect, and the spirit is called
passive intellect or reason, in the ethereal spirit, soul, and its spirit is called vital spirit, in the elemental spirit,
elemental form, in the creature itself, life. Hence, therefore, Hermes Trismegistus did not speak amiss: "The Word in the mind, the mind in reason, reason in the soul, and
the soul in the spirit, and finally the spirit with all these in the body." From which it is manifest that for the life
of superior creatures both a humid and a fiery nature are required, namely divine light in an
obedient and subtle spirit: But since the spiritual part of life in this heaven is very obedient to the uncreated
light, which superabundantly flows in it, therefore this life is immortal and will never perish. Again,
looking towards the middle region, we find that its life also consists of a middle spirit, and an
Empyrean spirit adorned and animated by light: Hence it is clear that, just as the form of the Empyrean heaven is
the purest divinity, and a mere ray of Jod, so the form informing the middle spirit is composite,
namely informed Empyrean nature: Hence its form is not as efficacious as the superior one, because it has within itself
a spirit with a soul enclosed in the spirit; And consequently, it is declared that the species of middle life is
subject to alterations due to the multitude of spiritual matter that contributes to its composition:
And hence it follows that this species of life, by which the body is vivified, is not durable;
according to Psalm 9:4: "A thousand years, if they pass, are in your eyes as yesterday's day." And Psalm 39:6: "Behold, you have made my days as handbreadths, and my time is as nothing before you." And Job 7:1: "Is not the time of a mortal on earth predetermined? As the days of a hired man, so are his days."
Similarly, this same thing is signified in many places; where the cause of such brevity of life also seems to be
explained; namely, the multitude of spirit joined with the Empyrean ray: Hence it is
said in Psalm 109:23: "Like a shadow when it lengthens, I am forced to depart;" And again Job 7:7: "My life is a breath," etc. And Job 14:2:
"Man born of woman is short-lived and full of trouble; he comes forth like a flower and is cut down; he flees like a shadow and does
not"

nor does it endure. Furthermore, also in Wisdom 2:4: "Our transitory life is like the traces of a cloud, and is dispersed like a mist, assailed by the sun's rays, and more heavily driven by its heat; for our time is a passage like a shadow." By these things it is declared, first, that this middle life in man and other animal creatures is not eternal, like that supercelestial life; then the reason for this seems to be connected by comparing life with wind, shadow, cloud, and mist; since all these are compacted from a multitude of spirits; as if it were implied by this very fact, that the shadowy, dense, windy, or airy, and misty matter of life, due to its thickness, performs the same function in the animal body as a shadow, wind, cloud, or mist; that is, that it now appears, and now again vanishes; because the supercelestial bond is not sufficient to perpetually retain and join so many parts of the dense radical moisture: For through the multitude of matter we are alienated from God, and the further we are from His face, the further we are from the length of life, because Jehovah Himself is life: Whence it is written in 1 Chron. 19:15: "We are strangers before You, our days on earth are like a shadow that does not endure." Therefore, for a long life, divine benevolence is required, or the multiplication of a portion of the Empyrean substance, in which the fount of kindness, wisdom, and life, and its tree, is found: Which the Psalmist also seems to prove, Psalm 90:14: "The prolongation of life is the kindness of God;" and ibid. 17: "May the pleasantness of Jehovah be with us;" Likewise in the same Psalm, and 10: "The span of human life is miserable without God's kindness:" Whence we see that the increase of the vital soul is the kindness of God and Wisdom: For in Proverbs 9:12 it is found that through Wisdom days are multiplied, and years of life are added to man: And Proverbs 3: "Length of days is in Wisdom's right hand:" Furthermore also Psalm 18:29: "If You illuminate my lamp, O Jehovah my God, You make my darkness shine

CHAPTER I.

*A brief recapitulation of the preceding: Likewise concerning the last letter He (ה), or the idea of the elemental region, and how it is the cause of transmutations, diseases, and corruption.*

[Large decorative initial I]
IN the preceding [sections] we have clearly treated of the ineffable root of the world and all its creatures, Jod, the first member of the Tetragrammaton; and then likewise of Jah (יה), the second, or the first degree of the Tetragrammaton into this world, whether emanation or aspect, by which the simplest and purest composition is made from two, namely from uncreated light, and a spirit most pure and most obedient; Whence Jah signifies benevolence, since from it we receive eternal life; Afterwards Jeho (יהו), the third, immersing itself in the darkness of the firmament's region in the second degree, produced a middle composition in the world, namely from the spirit Vau (ו) and with the emanation of Jod with He descending into Vau. And the essential emanation of the creator, donning the double created garment יהו, is therefore called by the Cabalists the seal of God, because by its eternal impression, as by the character of the uncreated Word, all corporeal things, both celestial and elemental, are marked with the life by which they live and exist. But since the material covering of this seal flows into the multitude from the luminous fount, therefore that life, especially in elemental things, is not eternal, but transitory: For just as life is produced through Jod into He and Vau to the ultimate He, so also, progressing circularly (for all the letters of יהוה are circular, as has been related), the ultimate He, through a putative or imaginary death, by the power of Jod itself (which is the power of the Tetragrammaton, or the Messiah, or Jesus, or Christ) will return from the ultimate degree of multitude, or dense and obscure cube, into Vau, and afterwards again from Vau, shedding its ethereal garment, into Jah, namely into the angelic nature, and finally, for those to whom the divine mind was given, there will be a transition from alterity into the very identity of Jod in Christ, through Christ, and with Christ; as it is certain that eternal life is from Christ descending into the first He; while temporal life, by which we are nourished here, is from Christ with his first vehicle in Vau: Both of these lives are conferred upon man through Christ; and with the former, indeed, he possesses a mind, while with the latter, he lives like other animals. Whence it is clear that man alone among other animals is found to live a double life; namely, immortal and mortal: But other animals receive the nourishment of life from Vau alone, and have received their animal reason from the spirit of the first heaven enclosed in darkness. And this is the reason, if I am not mistaken, why the name of the Tetragrammaton is called ineffable; namely, because

By these things, therefore, it is explained why all these things in the lowest region of ה, although they are impure, submerged in darkness, subject to density and hardness, and prone to rebellion, nevertheless, before the face of Jehovah, who chastises all impurity, subjects rebellion to Himself, and separates all dross from pure silver through ineffable examination, are able to persist; namely, that this happens through the mercy and benignity of Jehovah; who, although He can destroy and deform everything in the blink of an eye, yet, moved by clemency, He partly restrains the ardor of His face and reflects it into His Paradise, and partly, by the spirit of wisdom, He bends hard spirits and renders them moderately obedient to His actions. Therefore, the abundance of the benign spirit of life is the reason for maintaining health; but its defect or diminution is the occasion of illness, and its total loss is the introduction of death. This, I say, is the cause of changes and alterations in generation and corruption in this lower region of the world; this is the infallible origin of life, sickness, and death. How, moreover, Jehovah is also called the author and procurer of good and evil, health, life, and death, we will declare in the following chapter.

**CHAPTER III.**

*How, according to the opinion of the Cabalists, the ineffable name of the Tetragrammaton, and the surnames of God, which are used with respect to the works produced by Him, denote both severity and punishment in Jehovah, as well as benignity and clemency.*

Cabalists called the ten Sephirot or divine numerations and measures, the garments of divinity. Hence the Psalmist says, Psalm 104: *Clothed with light as with a garment;* that is; the first ה being illuminated, which is called Light. To each of these Sephirot, they attribute one of the divine names, of which one seems to denote the benignity, and another the severity of God: Those which signify mercy are אהיה Ehieh, which is ascribed to the first numeration, namely כתר Keter or crown: And Jehovah יהוה or Jod י & Jah יה to the second, which is called חכמה Hochma or wisdom: To the third numeration, namely בינה Binah or Prudence and intellect, אלהים Elohim is referred: To the fourth, חסד Chesed, that is, clemency, the name אל El is appropriated: To the fifth, תפארת Tipheret, that is, grace and beauty, the name אלוה Eloah is given: To the sixth, יסוד Yesod, the basis and foundation, אלחי Elchai, or שדי Shaddai is attributed. Of these names attributed to the aforesaid Sephirot, the first denotes paternal mercy, namely, His mercy, inasmuch as He is the father, the unity, basis, and foundation of the whole; indeed, it is called the crown of benignity: We see here, therefore, י Jod and ה from the letters of the Tetragrammaton, denoting Jah, who is the father of mercy: The second is Jehovah Himself יהוה, where Jod sounds the same as the entire Tetragrammaton; because Jod, denoting 10, contains 1, 2, 3, 4 within itself; which are an image of the four letters of the Tetragrammaton. In this name, moreover, the Messiah is contained, by whose benignity all things are to be saved; He is also the distributor of life and being for everything: The third, Elohim, inasmuch as its numeration flows through the orders of thrones into the sphere of Saturn, denotes, according to the opinion of the Cabalists, repentance and the remission of sins: The fourth, El, through the signification of its numeration, argues for clemency, goodness, grace, and mercy: The fifth, Eloah, inasmuch as its garment is grace, beauty, decor, and delights, is not far from benignity: Similarly, the sixth, Shaddai or Elchai, by reason of its Sephiroth, declares redemption and rest. From these things, therefore, we see that the greater property of God revolves around clemency and benignity: Thus we also see that the two upper heavens abound in the richness of clemency; For the upper gives eternal life and resurrection from the dead, while the middle gives temporal life and health. Likewise, the names of God which signify severity are Elohim; whose Sephiroth גבורה Gevurah denotes power, strength,

--- Page 560 ---
62 SECT. I. PORT. I. PART. I. LIB. III.

strength, severity, judgment, punishment; And אדני Adonai, the Lord, whose numeration is Malchut, kingdom, empire, etc. And according to the Cabalists, under this numeration is denoted the truncation of the kingdom, and the removal of the tree of life because of Adam's sin: From which it is clear that few are Jehovah's properties for punishment; but very many for mercy; It also denotes the mystery of the law given by mouth; whence it also implies severity. they called that again, which had been torn and cut off, composing. By these things they seem to imply,
that from the even number, namely 4, to which material spirit is referred, and the odd number, namely 3, to which light and form are attributed, as the patient and agent, or female and male, that is, in the septenary number all things are generated and composed, and again by the same reason are corrupted and dissolved; But generation is from heaven, and is life, that is, supercelestial light, and a life-giving force as if from Apollo; but corruption is from darkness and the underworld, that is, from the tearing night: And this is the reason, that for night they appointed Dionysius, tearing apart, as if an introducer of evils; but for day, Apollo, harmonious, as if a repeller of evils: Therefore the Athenians called Apollo Alexiacon, that is, a banisher of evil, and Homer, Ulios, that is, the author of health: For he makes all things harmonious, perfect, and consonant.

But we will show how these things usually happen through the septenary number previously mentioned:
Indeed, this number is formed from 3 and 4, of which the former is an odd number, and the origin of all perfect numbers, inasmuch as it contains in itself a beginning, a middle, and an end; Therefore it presents the simplest form, and a specimen of the divine essence, which is the acting act, and the actor of all things, or the virtue of the Tetragrammaton itself: And just as the number three is the origin of all perfect or odd numbers; so also the number four is the principle of imperfect and even numbers; inasmuch as according to the Pythagorean doctrine, two is not called a number, but a confusion of units.

The number four, therefore, signifies matter to be formed; which, finally formed, that is, united with form and the number three, constitutes the creation of the entire world; and thus this is, as it were, the septenary number, which is formed from 3 and 4. Where 3 is a symbol of the properties in the most holy Trinity, and 4 is an indication of matter or spirit, appearing from vast darkness. Here, therefore, we see that Jehovah God, who is all in all, in respect to the number three and the luminous, is called that supercelestial Apollo, who is the life of all, the father of generation, the restorer of health, and the gatherer of parts separated in corruption; But in respect to the number four, the offspring of darkness, he is called Dionysius, corrupting all things according to his good pleasure, and destroying composites, and dividing and tearing them into their similar parts: Whence we see that God, in respect to His supersubstantial essence, is always kind, benevolent, and merciful to creatures; but in respect to the created garment, drawn from the blackness of Chaos, He is said to tear apart and corrupt composition into parts: For matter, whose being is God Himself, never content, constantly desiring new forms, is the cause of destruction, corruption, death, and diseases, and all disturbances; but on the contrary, light or form vivifies, nourishes, restores, and produces all good: Whence it is truly said that nothing besides God alone is good: since other creatures are called good only by participation, namely inasmuch as they participate in divine goodness, according to that which is found in Gen. 1; And He saw that it was good, etc.

From which it is manifest that malice and corruption are not in God the agent, who in property is a perfect ternary, but in the patient, which is always found apt to participate in the malice of darkness, from which it arose: Dionysius, therefore, or God clothed in darkness, is he who is accustomed to tear apart the darkness in which he is, and with which he is mixed, inasmuch as he tears apart things that are in every way contrary to his nature. Thus we also see that Jod in the upper י is said to be clothed in light, according to Psalm 104:2. Light is the garment or clothing of God; but in the lower, in darkness: Therefore, in the upper is the Spiritual Apollo and Mind; in the middle, the visible Apollo; in the lowest (although in himself he is always the same in clemency and goodness) Dionysius, inasmuch as appearing in a dense cloud and thick night, he is accustomed to tear apart mountains, to set rocks ablaze with the fire of his countenance, and to inflict those infinite things in infinite ways upon creatures, which we call evils; Which things, although produced by the action of God, are nevertheless the effects of rebellious, impure, and dark matter; inasmuch as, being poorly disposed to receive divine actions, it produces bad and very bad outcomes, as far as our senses are concerned; however much those things, considered in themselves and intellectually, are constituted by God for the best end; so indeed, that just as that which seems good to men often displeases God, so also that which appears evil to them is always held for good by the actor, namely God.

And in this way we see how God is called the Lord of clemency and benevolence, and how of severity and punishment; likewise why He Himself is the author of good and evil, health and sickness, life and death. Moreover, that Jehovah is the God of mercy and severity, the following testimony drawn from the sacred scriptures concludes, Exod. 34. v. 6. And Jehovah passed before him and proclaimed; Jehovah, Jehovah, strong, merciful, gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in mercy and truth, keeping mercy for thousands, and forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and and who by absolving does not absolve, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children's children, and upon the third and fourth generation. Here therefore it is clearly taught that Jehovah in His prior and principal progression is gracious and merciful, but in the latter severe and punishing even to the third or fourth generation: Furthermore, we see the way by which He extends His mercy, namely through the splendor of His face, remo-

Jehovah, incline your heavens, and descend; touch these mountains, and let them smoke: Although here, and with at least a small word, I would diligently remind everyone of this, that the difference of the heavens is not always to be considered in the distance, or height or depression of places, in in terms of space, but in the sublimation of dignity, and the exaltation of goodness and purity: Thus it is said that God or the Holy Spirit is not accustomed to dwell in an impure or unclean heart; and yet truly, where God dwells, there is paradise; and where paradise, there we say heaven is; For heaven is on earth, and conversely, earth is in the heavens, according to that saying of Hermes in his Emerald Tablet: 'That which is above is like that which is below, and vice versa; that is, the subtle is the dense, and the dense is the subtle:' For water is thin earth, and air is thin water, and fire is thin air; therefore by the condensation of fire, air is made, and by the same reason air is made water, and water is made earth; Conversely, by the subtilization of earth, water is made, and water is made air, and this air is called heaven: Whence it is said in Deut. 11:17, 'Jehovah will shut up the heavens, so that there will be no rain,' etc. And Gen. 1:30, 'the birds

From which it is clear that the power of Yod itself (which is a symbol of the entire Jehovah), namely, of the Messiah or God's wisdom (which exists in the name of Jehovah as the light of the Sun in the Sun), is in every heaven in the same nature and being, although with respect to the variety of garment (for in every heaven it puts on a new and different garment) its uniform action produces various and different effects: Thus in the supersubstantial heaven, the Godhead, the Messiah, the power of Jehovah, or the divine essence, is naked, and to be seen in its simplest form, stripped of all garment; Which vision God utterly denied to Moses himself, indicating that no mortal could behold it in that supreme state with their eyes without sudden death: Then, immersing itself in the waters of dark hyle (primordial matter) in the first degree, namely, descending into He (ה), *Psalm 104. it is said to be clothed with light or radiance as with a garment;* With respect to this clothing, Jehovah is said in *Psalm 93. to reign clothed with majesty and loftiness:* Afterwards, with it descending into Vau (which is the ethereal Paradise) it is said in *Psalm 104:2. that heaven is, as it were, the curtain of God's house;* that is, the ethereal spirit is like the garment of the house of Vau, or He, in which unity dwells; or it is a thin covering and veil, through which the Messiah, clothed in the former garment of light, is covered; by whose thickness and condensation the light, as the garment of Jehovah or the Messiah, has become visible; and thus it is said that he has placed his tabernacle in the Sun. But it must also be noted here in passing that the luminous garment of God is nothing other than the appearance of invisible light in the mundane spirit; which spirit, thus illuminated, is called light; and; since it receives the power of Yod in its spirit or the prior uncreated throne He (ה), it is therefore called the house or garment of God in its throne, although the light itself, considered in itself without spirit, is nothing other than the very essence or emanation of God the sitting He (ה), whose garment, or vehicle, is the prior created spirit.

Finally, the same divine essence, with the first and second garments, descending into its lowest kingdom He (ה), and putting on there an elementary covering, or entering an aerial hiding place, or an aqueous and transparent tabernacle, is said according to *Job 26:9. to 'constrain the face of his throne, and spread his cloud upon it;'* And *Job 22:12. Thick clouds are a hiding place for him;* that is, upon his throne He (ה); with respect to which the aerial heaven was made on the third day of creation. by which (says the Wise Man ibid. 12.) your days are multiplied, and years of life will be added to you. And Ecclesiasticus 24. 3. I,

I say that salvation and length of days proceed from the beneficent fount of life and health, from the throne of the Omnipotent,
through the virtue of Wisdom, like blessed dew, that is, distilling from the life-giving stream of Paradise's delight,
and that this Wisdom, whose delights are with the children of men (Proverbs 8), is the director, governor, doctor of medicine,
and mediator for the just man between Jehovah the Father and man, who is subject to changes,
gently removing the blemish and morbid spots of the body, washing and wiping away the spirit of the soul defiled by sin
with the balm of its benignity, and then afterwards, finally, causing his whole being to be sublimated on high
and transfigured into a celestial and spiritual nature, with true resurrection and complete preparation or purification preceding.

Therefore, for the creation of the world and its creatures in the beginning, the Creator Jehovah God acted through wisdom, that is, through Messiah or His own virtue; and thus from nothing, that is, from a dark and unformed mass, He produced something; which indeed was the first testimony of His benignity: Whence He was first called Jod, or a point, or a center without any dimension, that is, without respect to the work; then, after the beginning of the work, Jah יה, which is a name of benignity and power; afterwards יהו, which denotes the seal of the existence of all things, by which, as it were, letters patent of the life of all creatures are sealed or secured from the term F I A T, to the ultimate PEREAT, and finally יהוה, which completed the whole marvelous work, and is the beginning and end of all things, God within and outside all things, nature; and God beyond nature, the circumference and yet the center of things, the archetype and also the created world, all in all, and outside all that exists, the sole act, king and emperor, effector, dominator, bond, harmony, heaven and earth, substance, quantity and quality; yet none of these, because He is a transcendent Being, and nevertheless any of these: He, I say, is called all things, as they are garments for Him, existing as something by His presence; and yet none of these, inasmuch as He is the simplest and supersubstantial essence: He is created light, or the Empyrean, ethereal, and elemental spirit, which He puts on; and yet He is none of these, since they are created; He is an angel, He is nature, He is the sun; He is man; whose bodies are to Him as a temple and sanctuary; and He gives them that being by which they exist as they are: Thus He is called the angel in the bush, and the Sun giving grace and glory, Christ man God; while He Himself, as unity, is neither an angel, which is otherness, nor the Sun, which is composed of three, nor man, who is composed of many: He is therefore the life and center of all things, by which they exist, and the form, and the first act, giving name and being: Thus a creature, solely in respect to the uncreated light which it receives and by which it lives, is sometimes called Jehovah; but in respect to created, passible matter, it assumes a name according to the condition of its substance, namely, creature. Oh, how ineffable and inexplicable are these things! how admirable, and found to be placed beyond the grasp of human intellect, to investigate the reason for this stupendous matter by any inquiry: For if one is all things, it necessarily follows, conversely, that all things are one; Thus therefore the marvelous name יהוה expanded itself from the center Jod into the circumference in the beginning, and thus made the material world in its own image: For it extended itself from a point to a line, and from a line to a surface, and from a surface to a solid body; or, speaking arithmetically, from unity to the root, from the root to the square, and from that finally to the cube: So also in the end, it will again reduce all this peripheral or round work by constricting it to its center; And what is impure in the world, and defiled by sin, will be devoured and absorbed by the eternal oblivion of hyle, deformity, and perpetual darkness, devoid of all grace and light: But what remains of the pure, simple, and undefiled spirit, that will be for ages of ages the unique palace and tabernacle of uncreated unity; where there will be no death, no sorrow, no hunger, no contention, or suffering, since the one cannot die or suffer, as it has no contraries within itself.

This holy unity, therefore, relying on its marvelous characters as on the wings of uncreated winds, and descending into the world, dividing it according to the number of its characters into regions or stations, and because of the simplicity and sincerity of its essence, unwilling to tolerate and put on the crude garment of the world, from each of its characters (surrounded on all sides by its said characters, and as if looking forth from its uncreated throne) it shone upon each region of the world, and brought into being things submerged in darkness, utterly lifeless, and formless, and plainly existing as nothing; in which act it indeed began to inhabit the diverse dwellings of the world.

How, moreover, this unity Jod is naked on its throne, and then afterwards puts on a different garment in each heaven, we have depicted here with a living demonstration.

CHAP. I.
*Concerning the three natural characters, which are symbols of the three Physical principles.*

**A**S the Metaphysical characters, comprehended in the wondrous name, namely YHV, are the Fathers, producing all things into being; so their last two are referred, with respect to the divine properties, to the Son begotten by the Father, and to the Holy Spirit proceeding from both; But indeed, inasmuch as all these properties, namely Unity, Father, Wisdom, or the Word, Son, and Holy Spirit or fiery, are co-workers in the macrocosmic work; (for *By the Word of Jehovah the heavens were established, and by the spirit of His mouth all their host*) to that extent, with respect to created things, we call them fathers or primary ministers, according to that of *Proverbs 8: I, Wisdom, was with Him as a nursling, or arranging all things:* But, since the supernatural properties or Fathers YHV require portions to be created for the creation of the world, into which, according to the respect of each of their properties, they act as fathers into mothers, or males into females for procreation, therefore the wiser ones of the Hebrew nation, among whom I especially name Abraham in *Ietzera* h, named three mothers at the instant of creation; which by the action of three

of the three uncreated Fathers into light and being, first of all in the world were produced, namely Dark-
ness, Waters, & Light: For Moses made mention of Darkness and Waters, before he came to Light:
And darkness was upon the face of the deep; and the spirit of the Lord moved upon the waters: And he said, Let there be Light.
From these things, therefore, it is clear that first there was Darkness, and then Waters; which, by the power of the fiery spirit ema-
nating from the luminous Aleph, or Yod, now rising and revealing itself in the center of the dark abyss (inasmuch
as it previously lay hidden and was called dark), were created into the form of waters; and
finally the first composite creature, namely from the commixture of the rays of uncreated light with the created spirit or
waters; which, with respect to the created spiritual body it informed, is called created light; although it is
nothing other than the mixture of uncreated light with the created spirit, by which that spirit is informed, and animated
with eternal life. Moreover, the Cabalists and Abraham the Jew, in the previously cited book, assigned these characters to these mothers;
namely, א for Darkness, מ for Waters, & ש for created light: Now, the significations of these mothers
according to Cabalistic doctrine are as follows.

א Aleph, when it is withdrawn and immanent in the abyss of darkness, and idle, or, as they say, looking to
nothing, is therefore called אין, or; non-Being, and no end; because we, afflicted with such
poverty of intellect in divine matters, judge concerning those things which do not appear, no differently than concerning those things which do not exist: But
when it thus shows itself to be something, and truly subsists, then the dark Aleph is converted into a luminous Aleph;
And it is then indeed called the Great Aleph, when it desires to emerge from darkness, and appears as the cause of
all things through ב, which is the symbol of the son, and of Wisdom: Whence אב is called the father of all
generation: It is clear, therefore, that with Aleph contracted and hidden in the womb of the abyss of darkness, dark-
ness appears in its state: Whence מ is that mother which is ascribed to darkness; and consequently also de-
notes the element of earth, which is a mass of darkness driven back to the center of the machine: It also
signifies the West, which is why it is given to night; furthermore, also to Autumn; whence it denotes melancholy, which
is the most foul humor: Therefore, just as א, being most simple, and in itself without any respect to creation, was the
first principle of the Archetypal world, so also here, by its occultation, it makes darkness the first principle
in creation; from whose womb the second principle is drawn, namely מ.

מ is the second mother, corresponding to waters and spirit, born from the womb of the first mother; And it is, according to
Cabalistic doctrine, the hieroglyph of Waters: Whence water is written in Hebrew with a double מ, thus
מים: And just as א made darkness as a father, so מ made מ manifest as a son: Whence מ is attributed by the Caba-
lists to the son, or the Word proceeding from the voice of the luminous א, or י. And here we must note that
a double character of Mem is reckoned among the Hebrews; of which the former is called מ common, &
the second is ם final: The first מ signifies illuminated and open waters, while Jehovah spoke from
the cloud; whence it is opened at its base; The other denotes closed waters, and signifies darkness, and is a symbol
of silence. But this mystery is not hidden from the wise: It suffices for us to testify in this place that מ is
the character of Waters, and the second mother in creation.

ש is the last mother, which refers to fire and created light; Whence fire in the Hebrew language is called אש;
where all are testimonies of light; namely, the presence of the father of light, that is, the luminous א, and ש itself,
which is a symbol of created light, and refers to the Holy Spirit in its property, whence it has three points in
its crown, thereby arguing the properties of the Trinity gathered into one. Here, therefore, it must be
noted that, just as the dark Aleph, through the divine spirit, gave being to the Waters, or מ, so on the con-
trary, the luminous Aleph, through its rays, gave being to ש itself; which is the fullness of things and contrary to emptiness, or
inanity.

As for the less significant Elements, understand them thus;
ב is a symbol of house or dwelling, life, son, wisdom, the beginning of the Law.
ג signifies retribution, peace, strong angels, etc.
ד denotes a door, gates or entrance, third intelligences, wisdom.
ה signifies alma, spirits of the blessed, scent, etc.
ז is a character of terror, speech, also denoting angels of the seventh order.
ח is a sign of inclination, Cherubim.
ט imports the palm, the primum mobile, fixed stars, riches.
כ denotes doctrine, the sphere of Saturn, business.
ל signifies son, grandson, sun, passages.
נ is a sign of apposition: it denotes spirit, that is, רוח.
ע signifies the left eye, Moon, laughter.
פ is a character of the mouth, the intellectual soul, & the animal spirit.
צ imports the matter of the heavens & elements, & suspicion; & ץ final imports the
forms of the elements.
ק signifies revolution, circuit; and is a symbol of inanimate things, & minerals, and those
things which are called mixed elements; it signifies slumber.
ר is a sign of poverty & indigence; & in creatures it signifies all vegetables & fruits; simi-
larly it signifies grace, fecundity, & inheritance.

CHAPTER II.

*Cabalistic explanation of the three secondary Physical Principles,
immediately proceeding from those three Theosophical ones.*

Now that the treatise concerning the three supernatural and all-primary principles has at last been completed, namely concerning the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, that is, concerning the three properties of the one Godhead, symbolically and hieroglyphically signified by the Cabalists under the great and ineffable name of the Tetragrammaton, and concerning these characters alone endowed among others with spherical perfection, namely יהוה in the composition and ordering of the world and heavens, through the divine and unique wisdom of Jehovah, the Messiah, or virtue, residing in them as in three distinct thrones of property; it remains that in this small book we briefly discuss the created principles, and those immediately flowing from those primary ones, in a manner both Cabalistic and open and common, yet Theologico-philosophical.
Therefore, as we have perceived through our speculation and observation, according to the doctrine of the Cabalists, the three spherical letters of the name יהו were the characters and symbols of the uncreated principles, namely the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit (which indeed we call the primary Fathers in creation); so also, according to the opinions of the other Cabalists, those three mothers alleged by Abraham in Yetzirah are secondary principles, into which, as females, the father characters are said to act for the creation of the world. The three mothers are named by Abraham א Aleph, מ Mem, and ש Shin: And although א is an indication of the uncreated God, and of His sacred unity in the Trinity, yet here it is necessarily expressed among the secondary principles, inasmuch as nothing could exist without its presence: And, as has been declared in the preceding, that in the second place the cipher, which we compared to the unformed spirit, usually denotes nothing without the presence of unity; so also that spirit or water could not be denominated, unless its mother, from whose womb or depths it was drawn, was first denominated: Hence Moses in Gen. 1. first makes mention of Darkness before Waters; Nor indeed could Darkness have its denomination, unless Aleph had shone forth from them: Whence, with respect to their opposition to light, they are called Darkness. It must therefore be noted from these things, that, just as Yod follows Aleph, and is as it were the conversion of the dark Aleph into light, that is, the flowing of the luminous form from its hidden center to the manifest mundane circumference, so also darkness preceded the luminous spirit; which, being pregnant and impregnated by the spirit, by the hand of Demogorgon, that is, by the now manifested light of Aleph; brought forth Bread or the entire humid nature, or water, or the mundane spirit; Whence, as the mother precedes the son, so also Darkness precedes Waters; and consequently Aleph, which was dark, is taken for the darkness itself, to which it gave denomination: So also Yod, which is the second progression from unity (for unity receives itself into the denary number), gave denomination to the superior waters; Whence they were called light created on the first day. Hence therefore, according to Abraham, Aleph in natural things denotes the element of earth; which was made from the collection and conglomeration of darkness into a single place or the center of the universe. Furthermore, we will perceive that this word 'earth' was also taken by Moses for universal darkness, before they were reflected to the center; if we diligently consider his words, which are these in Gen. 1. *Now the earth was without form and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep.* Therefore, the Prelate does not seem to speak of the earth created on the third day, because that was not void and without form, inasmuch as it was fruitful and fertile, adorned with herbs producing seed, as is explained in the same chapter, but of darkness universally dispersed; which were in potentiality to the earth resting in its destined place on the third day; To which indeed we are all the more led, because the waters were not yet named at that time, extracted from the depths of the formless earth, or any spark of light revealed: But since the fulfillment of all things comes from God א, and indeed that א was still dark, that is, contracting the rays of its light within itself, the earth or darkness was called void and without form, from whose conglomeration into the center of the machine the earth was made; For the cause of fullness is fertility; and again the cause of fecundity are the multiplying rays of light, which flowed forth from the revealed face of Aleph, or Yod, which is Aleph with a cipher, or unformed spirit. But this can also be confirmed by these words of Job 26. 7.; *He stretches out the north over the empty space and the void,* (that is, he made the heaven revolve, where the earth was empty and void) *and hangs the whole earth upon nothing;* (that is, he conglomerated and gathered that empty and void space, whose space heaven now filled in creation, into one mass, which is called earth, and is suspended upon nothing.
Hence therefore it is, that the ancients feigned Saturn to be the father of the Gods, that is, the dark Aleph, clothed in Saturnine garb; by the expansion of whose splendor Jupiter, that is, Jehovah, and from Jupiter Apol-

daughter of Darkness, & created light, about which we will treat copiously in this place.

CHAP. I.

*Are (as some wrongly think) my opinions and the foundations of my doctrine*
*recent, and as it were, new?*

[Decorative woodcut initial Q]UITE a significant error has arisen among men, since some believe my opinions to be recent, and the foundations of my philosophy new and by no means ancient. I have therefore deemed it worthwhile to demonstrate to the eyes of justice, that if my foundations are ancient, and my opinions supported both by philosophical reasons and by living demonstration, then without doubt they are not new, and consequently also not so dangerous, inasmuch as the argument of the adversaries is formed only thus: that my opinions are dangerous because they are new. Moreover, that my Macrocosmic principles or foundations are drawn from the deepest recesses of antiquity, we can prove and confirm not only by the authority of ancient philosophers, but also by the testimony of the sacred scriptures; since from those very principles the world and all things that are in the world had their origin. If this doctrine of mine had been founded upon Aristotelian bases or principles, namely upon Matter, Form, and Privation, it would certainly, without any hesitation, be considered ancient by those men agitated by excessive curiosity, and would be divulged publicly without any contradiction from them: But these new principles (as they say), namely Darkness, Water, and Light, are not to be admitted, inasmuch as they are recent, and as it were, newly invented and unheard of before this time. Does it not seem, however, to be a gross and palpable argument of ignorance in Christian men, to embrace so eagerly the assertions of the pagan Aristotle, and to defend them with the most vehement arguments of insult, and even for their sake to repudiate, neglect, and hold in derision the most true principles of the leader Moses; on whose authority, nevertheless, we place the foundations of our faith? Does not our Moses seem to assert that darkness was an impediment to form and essence, by saying that the earth was void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep? Does he not himself make darkness the receptacle of the formless earth, and as it were, a deformed veil; which matter, indeed, he calls the scarcely imaginable abyss? Did not the Spirit of the Lord, by the power of His uncreated light, inform that almost nothing, or the deformity of darkness and hyle, so that He reduced the abyss into the form and being of waters? Whence Moses says:

--- Page 583 ---
DE PRIMAR. NATUR. ELEMENT. 85

ses: "And the Spirit of the Lord was carried upon the waters," from which, as Saint Peter testifies, the world, and all things in it, were made. Was not finally light created on the first day as that formal principle and first act, by means of which, as an immediate emanation of the entire fount of light into the purest Spirit of water, all things thereafter were founded? Do we not therefore here from Mosaic doctrine discover those three principles or foundations, by which heaven and earth were established through creation? But if the faculty and freedom of following the sole and truest Theosophy as well as Philosophy of the Holy Bible is denied to us, so that, with the clearest light of sacred literature forbidden, we are compelled to wander like blind men in the filthy and muddy obscurity of heathens and infidels, indeed, against that unjust (if such it be) opinion of men, we can not unsuitably allege that argument of the Prophet Baruch 3, which ought by no means to be rejected by a just man, in our defense and excuse: *It is not fitting to abandon the fount of all wisdom, and to seek art, science, and understanding in foreign lands, as the Agarenes did, and those who were in Theman, who indeed never recognized the way of true wisdom.* By these words we are clearly taught to embrace sacred scripture as the fount of all wisdom, but to abandon heathen and foreign doctrine or scripture, inasmuch as no true science or divine wisdom is found therein. But what will these Censors of mine say, if I prove with solid and irrefutable arguments that even ancient and famous philosophers of the heathens, by traversing Egypt, Arabia, Assyria, and especially Judea, secretly stole the foundations and principles of all their philosophical doctrine from the sacred fount of mysteries, and from the Biblical, or Word of God's, treasury, and unjustly attributed them to themselves? Indeed, setting aside all further dispute and proof, we shall perceive this same thing even clearly with our own eyes, if we have thoroughly read the mystical writings of Plato, Mercury Trismegistus, Orpheus, Hesiod, Ovid, and other divine philosophers, both poets and others. But if not even all these things suffice for the most accurate admirers of Aristotle, let us descend to an inquiry into Aristotle's own principles, for thus we shall most easily at last perceive him to be a disciple and imitator of the High Priest Moses, or rather a plunderer of Mosaic principles, falsely attributing them to himself. For what else (I ask) is that primary matter of Aristotle, which he plainly says is nothing in act, but a mere quasi-imagination, or, as his teacher Plato would have it, an apparition appearing in a dream? Hence Aristotle called this something in potentiality; And yet nothing is said of that which is formless, since form alone gives name and Being. Is not this scarcely imaginable matter the darkness of Moses, which was upon the face of the abyss, which Synesius and others, along with Aristotle himself, called Hyle? Then what is that second matter of Aristotle except hyle or primary matter brought into act, or the dark and formless abyss of Moses now informed by the presence of uncreated light and act, and designated by the name of Waters, which were the universal matter of all things in creation; so that now that Void of Moses, or this quasi-Nothing of Aristotle, is brought into act by the splendor of uncreated light, that is, it is created: Hence Moses said, "The Spirit of the Lord was carried upon the waters," that is, by the presence of the informing Spirit, the Waters are now named and actually produced, which before were not, or were not named. What then was that essential form of Aristotle by the aspect of which this matter in potentiality was reduced to act? Was it not that light created on the first day, which was the first and immediate emanation from the living God into humid matter? Did he not therefore call this essential form the first act, or the first informing principle of material things? Finally, what did Aristotle understand by Privation if not darkness and formlessness, which matter in potentiality shed at the very point of information or creation? Which darkness, nevertheless, before the creation of things, was not privation, inasmuch as no position of matter preceded it; a fact which Aristotle seemed to ignore, because he, differing from his teacher Plato in this, considered the world eternal and uncreated. But this darkness, with creation preceding, can be called privation, inasmuch as they are said to possess matter at that instant which is between the point of corruption and generation. What then do you now think of these new opinions? Are they so recent and new, when their foundations are found to be so ancient and old? Or, because I, a Christian, perhaps more powerful in the use of Mosaic doctrine than Aristotle, attribute to my teacher Moses what is his due, in just measure, and in this I seem to differ from Aristotle, who, hiding the marrow and sense of Mosaic discipline with a foreign veil of words, arrogantly and falsely ascribed these principles of creation to himself, which Moses himself received from the mouth, by the inspiration, and as it were by the hand of the living God Jehovah the creator, and converted them to his own heathen sense; because (I say) I acknowledge the divine doctrine and true philosophy of my divine Master, am I therefore to be blamed? Are not the Holy Scriptures the fount and origin of all wisdom and knowledge? And shall we abandon or desert them, so that we may follow the inconstant doctrine of the Agarenes and those in Theman, that is, of infidels and heathens, who never knew true wisdom or certain knowledge, but constructed a philosophy for others, relying on vain opinion and fragile imagination, upon those foundations which were secretly stolen from Jewish mysteries, and thus, by abandoning life and the true knowledge of the soul, we shall knowingly and willingly bring death upon ourselves.

                                   CAP. II.
                      *Concerning Darkness, & its species.*

THAT darkness existed before all things, into which the Tetragrammaton acted for the creation of the world, so that He might lead them into His luminous nature or act, that most wise Solomon teaches us, Wisdom 11:18. Whose words are as follows: *God made the world out of unformed matter;* Or, as Jerome interprets, *out of invisible matter;* that is, out of a spirit or waters empty and void, i.e., filled with no luminous form or grace, or brought into being in any way: Whence it happens that, since light is in every way opposed to darkness, it necessarily follows that darkness and gloom succeed there where light is absent: Hence it is said in Wisdom 7:22: *Wisdom is clearer and more luminous than the Sun or Stars, to which night succeeds;* that is, to the absence or defect of the divine spirit's presence, darkness and gloom succeed: These words of Solomon Job 12:22 seems to confirm excellently. Indeed, from whose express words we can excellently deduce three species of darkness: *He reveals* (he says) *the foundations out of darkness, and brings forth into light the shadow of death:* Therefore, by the word (Darkness) he understands the mother of all darkness, namely the most obscure hyle, in which there is no trace of light: And although Aleph is hidden in it from eternity before the world was brought forth into light; nevertheless, that (hyle) is called entirely dark relatively, although in itself it is absolutely luminous; but it did not wish to emit rays to the circumference, that is, into the multitude, but contracted them in its own center and unity: Hence Mercury Trismegistus says: *The Monad generates the Monad, and reflected its ardor into itself:* And this was the reason why the universal humid spirit, devoid of all divine grace, was covered and veiled by immense darkness and absolute gloom, so that not even a spark of light was present to it: Whence it was plainly held for nothing, and nothing seemed to exist; but all that which was, if anything at all was, this was called nothing; inasmuch as it was nothing other than darkness, which utterly resists form, name, and being-giver, and strongly opposes divine action; indeed, in whose nature and disposition it is never to move, but on the contrary to rest eternally in its connatural place. These, then, are those general darknesses, or hyle, from whose matrix or depths, finally, with Aleph operating, the deep (that is, the abyss of waters) is revealed from the center towards the circumference: And the lethal shadow (which Mercury Trismegistus calls horrendous), which was still everywhere upon the face of the abyss, was that obscure Chaos, in which holy splendor was present, but in a confused and irregular manner; from whose congregation, finally, into the center of the created machine, the earth or dry dust was produced. Therefore, we will discuss each of these in this booklet in a methodical order; before we descend into their public field, we will institute a brief and succinct discourse on the consideration of holy characters, by which the natures and dispositions of each of the aforesaid species are explained as if by living hieroglyphs.

                                   CAP. III.
*Concerning the examination of holy characters, by which the aforesaid species are explained in the holy language*
          *according to their exact nature and condition.*

IN the preceding, we have clearly enough declared that every thing has its own denomination according to the property of its disposition, so that the characters of a name are like symbols and hieroglyphs of the condition of the thing named; For in this respect God brought to Adam all the beasts of the earth and all the birds of the sky, that he might give them names suitable to their natures, that is, that he might assign to each name characters which would best declare the proportion of their life in heat and humidity, that is, their internal nature, by formal and essential letters, and explain the measure and number of the body in the mass of elemental composition by more material and opaque letters: Whence it happened that to each creature he attributed a name composed of living letters, in all respects agreeable and suitable to its disposition; Nor certainly (as I think) is there anything in the nature of things expressed by the golden characters of the Word of God, whose nature and being are not explained in them clearly, but in a mystical way; so that, if the mysteries of the sacred letters or living characters were fully revealed to humans, I would indeed not believe it impossible that they would behold the exact form of any thing, and also the composition of its body, as if in a mirror; since even in a crude manner, and by mere external consideration, we are accustomed to reveal not insignificant things, and to render judgments not absurd, though not so absolute; For example, in our present subject (for we shall now gird ourselves for our matter); when general darkness is mentioned, according to Genesis 1, there is placed first תהו (Tohu), i.e., solitude, emptiness, shapelessness, or lacking all form, and vastness; so that Moses says, *the earth was such before creation;* And by earth he understood those empty darknesses, from which, finally, the earth, filled with light and enriched with fertility, was made after the repercussion of darkness to the center: And the earth was emptiness or solitude; i.e., the substance of the earth visible and sensible to us was at that time vast and empty darkness without any form or spark of light; inasmuch as its matter before creation was the substance of hyle, in which there was no light infor-

All these things seem to be best demonstrated by the Rabbis of the Jews writing in the Cabalistic manner, saying: that Aleph (this they call the principle), withdrawn into the abyss of darkness, and immanent, and idle; or (as they say) looking towards nothing, is therefore called [Hebrew: אין], that is, *Nothing or Non-Being, and no end*, because we, afflicted with such poverty of intellect in divine matters, judge concerning those things which do not appear, no differently than concerning those things which do not exist. But when it shows itself in such a way that it is something and truly subsists, there the dark Aleph is converted into a luminous Aleph. Whence it is explained to us that, since Wisdom (which they call Aleph and the Principle) is considered by our meager understanding as Nothing, because, hidden in the abyss of darkness, it seems to be as nothing or non-Being, inasmuch as it does not appear in actual existence, it follows thence (I say), as from conceded premises, that darkness itself is much more to be held as nothing, since by its deformity and privative aspect something becomes nothing. But if these assertions of mine do not yet suffice for you, I certainly do not doubt that I shall satisfy your curiosity by the following reasoning, so that I may at last reconcile and unite your ambiguous spirits with my mind in mutual consent. I believe that no one of sound mind is unaware that our God Jehovah decreed to fashion the world from nothing by weight, measure, and number, through His secret wisdom and inscrutable counsel, and first delineated its type of creation, matter, and form in His eternal and supersubstantial idea or Archetype, before it was brought into actual existence by true creation for human perception. Hence it follows, however, that mere and absolute nothing was so prepared by this secret decree of the creator that, although that matter may appear to the weakness and poverty of our apprehension and intellect as formless, that is, scarcely imaginable, nevertheless, being destined by the arcane counsel of God to exist as the matter for creating the world, it was then suddenly prepared from plain nothing in such a way that something existed in potentiality. This potentiality or preparation was, for the decreer himself, already then as it were the most absolute creation, though most hidden and least apparent, inasmuch as it was not yet brought into sensible act. But, to conclude this clause of this declaration briefly and as it were in a single word, by that which in scholastic doctrine is in no way considered to dissent from the substance of divinity, we say that, inasmuch as God is present at all times, to that extent all things which had their beginning and actual existence in the concept and intellect of men, have always been in objective potentiality in the eyes of God; which potentiality, although it may seem nothing to human consideration, yet with respect to the preceding decree of the creator, it is in a certain way and as it were already then a creature actually made before God. We conclude, therefore, in order to strengthen this opinion of ours, that we may produce an even clearer passage, that it is probable from the very context of the sacred scriptures that the world, and those things which exist in the world, are formed and produced from matter by no means created, that is, destitute of actuality, and consequently formless, because concerning this, the express words of Solomon himself, most complete in Cosmological Magic, are found in *Wisdom chapter 11, verse 28*; which according to Pagnini's translation read thus: "*The hand of the Almighty made the world from formless matter*", or according to Tremellius's exposition, "*Your hand created the world from formless matter*", or, as Jerome renders it, "*Your hand created the orb of the earth from invisible matter*"; from which it evidently appears that my aforesaid opinion does not in any way depart from the object of truth itself.

                                        CHAPTER VI.
        *Concerning the second kingdom of darkness, namely the Abyss, and its species.*

Abyss, or ἄβυσσος among the Greeks, sounds the same as [Hebrew: תהום] among the Hebrews, and *profundum* (deep) among the Latins: Its holy characters, by which the living nature of the abyss is signified, do not differ from the characters of hyla or empty darkness; except that in the final letter [Hebrew: מ] it is changed to [Hebrew: ם] (closed Mem): He (ה) however denotes a more hidden and concealed spirit; Mem (מ) on the other hand, a more open spirit and one almost brought into act; Whence it denotes that the waters began to appear from the womb of hyla, but in an obscure manner; so that the dark Aleph (א), previously quiescent, now by moving intrinsically from the midst of infinite darkness, caused the face of humid nature, not yet formed, to leap forth outside the universal hyla; but in such a way that Mem (which is a symbol of the same obscure aspect) was closed, and not open; for light had not yet erupted from the womb of hyla: Whence it is said in *Genesis 1*, that *darkness was upon the face of the abyss*: And these abysses were those depths, *which Jehovah revealed from the darkness, and the deadly shadows which He brought forth into light*, according to that previously cited from *Job 12:22*. These are those shadows and darkness, by ineffable light-

The species of abyss is properly called Chaos; inasmuch as in its center fiery nature with watery, and watery with earthy, are contained with no order observed; which will also be very easy to discern from a Cabalistic inspection of the characters of its word; concerning which we will discuss more broadly in the following chapter. Under this species of darkness can also be understood those Egyptian darknesses, about which it is written, Exod. 10. 23. *The darkness of the Egyptians was so great that one could not see another, nor could anyone rise from his place for three days:* Furthermore, these darknesses were also sensible or palpable upon the land of Egypt, so that anyone could feel them: But such also were those darknesses which occurred from the sixth hour until the ninth in the passion of the Savior, Matth. 27. 47. The reason for this is readily available; because, namely, God, who is the unique light of the world, turning away His splendor first from the region of Egypt, and then from the kingdom of the Jews universally, for a space of three days in one place, and three hours in another, permitted the true darknesses of the abyss to creep into the air or lower waters in the manner in which they existed in the beginning, before light had fully shone upon the world; And thus, from חֹשֶׁךְ (choshek), deprived of all light, He rendered the darkness of the Egyptians palpable; In the other place, however, the darknesses were not so palpable, but very wondrous, and arose in a supernatural manner; Concerning these, Saint Lucian of Antioch, a Martyr, being established in the torment of his passion and death, exclaimed to the judges standing by him; *Search in your annals, and you will find that in the times of Pilate, when Christ suffered, the day was interrupted by darkness, even with the sun put to flight.* Nor certainly was this eclipse without a significant finger of God, or a manifest turning away of His face from the iniquity of the deed, as if He had been unwilling to behold such a crime; because three miracles accompanied it; inasmuch as it (which is wondrous to say) was primarily made against the natural order of common eclipses; inasmuch as they never usually occur at full moon, that is, in the opposition of the Moon to the Sun; and indeed this happened immediately after the opposition of the Sun: Secondly, the part of the Sun towards the East was first overshadowed, and the same later recovered its light even earlier; which likewise is certain to happen contrary to the common disposition of nature; Finally, (which can be considered the most prodigious of all, and almost incredible) at the hour of the eclipse, the Moon moved against its natural course, namely from East to West, whereas its natural motion is contrary to this; and then afterwards, immediately after the eclipse ended, it hastened again by its natural motion towards its usual goal, from West, I say, to East: Furthermore, this eclipse was also universal, whereas common experience teaches us that other eclipses, on the contrary, are merely particular. Wherefore it is manifest that God Jehovah, in a wondrous and ineffable manner, turned away the saving light of His countenance for the space of three hours from the lower region of the world, inasmuch as in it those darknesses persisted throughout the entire interval of that space, namely between the sixth and ninth hour, in the lowest heaven, like the first abyss. Under this species also was that darkness, about which Joshua 24. 7. speaks. *He put darkness between you and the Egyptians;* however much this species of darkness can also be most aptly referred to the disposition of Chaos.

CAP. VII.

*Concerning the third kingdom of darkness, which is called Chaos.*

That Chaos is the third degree of darkness, distinct from the two preceding ones, we can deduce and observe from the living characters of its word; namely; חֹשֶׁךְ (choshek), that is, darkness or Chaos: And these darknesses are not so empty and void as the preceding ones, in which no character of light was present; but are filled with the treasures of divinity itself: For in its center they have Shin (ש), which is a hieroglyph of fire and light, and a symbol of the indivisible Trinity; whence it is marked by three upward-tending protuberances: But this Shin (ש) is covered on all sides by the dark and terrible veil of the ח (chet) itself from the front part; which is a sign of terror and speech, because through it Jehovah sometimes penetrates with His rays and speaks to the world: Thus also, the dense and obscure letter on the other side, namely ך (final Kaph), which is an index of the palm (for thus Jehovah hid the essence of His face from the countenance of Moses with the palm of His hand), is covered and concealed: Hence it is found fertile in a kind of quasi-abyss; where the true agent or male of the world, and its true female or patient, are simultaneously contained in the same dense and obscure vehicle; And consequently, this species of darkness is closer to creation than the other two, inasmuch as it contains within itself the act of all perfection; Indeed, this is sometimes called the hiding place of Jehovah, whose alone it is to bring lethal shadow into light; according to that passage from Job. 12. 22. previously cited: And this is that darkness, under which Jehovah Himself asserted that He dwells: Concerning these also is understood this saying of the Royal Psalmist, Psalm. 139. 11. *Even darkness cannot so obscure that God does not foresee, but His night illuminates like the day, and darkness is to Him as light itself.* Chaos, therefore, is matter which is not as remote as hyle and abyss, but is in proximate potency to receive form and a regular position. And so it is said in Psalm 104:5, that God covered the earth with the abyss, as with a garment; And in Exodus 15:5, "The abysses covered them," that is, they were submerged in the deep of the waters; And ibid. 8, "The abysses congealed in the innermost part of the sea by the blast of your nostrils" &c. From which it is clearly evident that the matter of the earth is like a "caput mortuum" and terrestrial dregs, left behind in that great and stupendous work of true and primary Alchemy, in the mundane Philosophical Egg; which egg of universal nature is contained in a furnace made of empty or void earth or mud, that is, in the womb and matrix of hyle itself, and by the virtue of the light and heat of the fiery Spirit brooding over the waters, is concocted for so long towards the goal of perfection, until it emerges in the form of a living Spirit, entirely invisible, and quasi-Deiform; and flees and vanishes from mortal eyes; since this spirit is a portion of the sixth essence, from which the Empyrean heaven consists. And these are those most subtle waters or spirits who are always present before Yod, or before the throne of Jehovah; concerning whom David thus speaks in Psalm 148:4, "Waters above the heaven praise God"; Or Psalm 104:3, "The upper heavens are covered with waters by God." From this portion of the Spirit, therefore, Jehovah made the heavens of heavens; concerning which Nehemiah 9:6 [speaks]. These, therefore, are those subtle waters concerning which it is said in Genesis 1, that God separated the firmament from the lower waters. Then from wine we can extract the fifth essence; And also from the universal watery mass, God extracted in the second place the nature of the firmament; by the mediation of which pure and spiritual waters are separated from the gross and material ones; And this firmament He also called heaven, in which afterwards He placed the two greater lights and the remaining stars: Finally, in the third place and order, He extracted the fourth essence, in which was the smallest portion of divine act and essence: For thus this relates to the upper heavens, as the phlegm of wine relates to its various degrees of spirits; For the more a spirit is mixed with phlegmatic water, the weaker, less worthy, and worse it is: A similar reasoning is also held in the production of the three heavens; since the purer of them is produced from the first circulation of

imbued, and elevated to the highest dignity of the terrestrial kingdom. The reason for these three species, if we are not mistaken (for who among mortals, in such an uncertain doubt, will consider himself entirely free from all error?), proceeds from a threefold diversity of darkness, which were gradually reflected on the three days of creation, each with a similar spirit enclosed within them, in a divided order: For first, the darkness from the supreme face of the abyss was driven downwards with a large portion of the spirit of the same heaven or subtle waters; which, being viscous and tenacious, and avid for divine and virgin light by which they might be informed, seized infinite sparks of that light pursuing the dark shadow, and claimed them for themselves: Hence the dignity of the darkness or dark spirit of this heaven is no more eminent above the two lower portions of darkness than the honor of its spirit, permanently residing in the Empyrean heaven, is elevated in place and essence above the middle and lowest spirit: For thus we see that the spirit of wine by natural instinct floats above its oil, and again, that (oil floats above) its so-called phlegm. The reason, however, why the dignity of the supreme darkness is above the others, is because it participates in the immediate ray and emanation proceeding from God Jod: But since the spirit of the middle darkness seizes for itself the rays of secondary light, which light is from a portion of created light, therefore its light is not so noble; indeed, since that (first light) is a ray of God, this (second light) is of nature. Finally, the third light, whose sparks the spirit of the lower darkness seizes and appropriates for itself, is composed of a twofold light, namely of God and of nature; which is immersed in a twofold spirit: Hence the matter of these darknesses is rebellious against this composite light. From this, therefore, it follows that, since among the spirits of each heaven one is found more worthy and higher in place than another, according to the greater or lesser proximity of its light to the divine nature, it is therefore also necessary that the darknesses likewise obtain this same dignity and exaltation in their dark world or terrestrial globe: For through this divine light comprehended in the darkness of the earth, God is said to be as much in the earth as in heaven, wisdom is said to be on earth, and the earth is said to be the footstool of Jehovah, just as heaven is traditionally said to be His throne in sacred scripture: Indeed, in every respect, this opaque terrestrial globe behaves like that celestial and transparent globe: Yet we find three regions in the diaphanous world, of which the middle one, according to the opinion of the sacred text, separates the lowest from the highest; Therefore, also in the obscure machine of the earth there are undoubtedly three regions; of which the middle one, from which the vegetative force emerges, distinguishes the highest from the lowest. It follows, therefore, that it is probable that the mineral nature is from that region of the earth which is the lowest, both because it occupies a deeper place and has a denser and harder substance, and also because it has its soul from a weaker light: Hence it is more given to rest, and is enveloped in foul darkness in the center of the whole; and therefore also, because of its immense gravity, it strives more downwards and towards the lowest abyss: From which it is clearly evident that this species of creatures belongs to the dark kingdom of the lowest darknesses; where the efficacy of light is found to be lesser and less worthy, due to the abundance of rebellious matter; and therefore it is recognized that earth and water abound more in minerals. In a similar proportion, the opaque vegetable composition is referred to the kingdom of the middle darknesses, since vegetables are perceived to be born and arise from the middle part or region of the earth, which is, namely, closer to its upper and superficial part or region; Do we not also, comparing the aether with that region, see that the Sun, Emperor of the ethereal kingdom, and at the same time the other stars, are the cause of vegetation and multiplication? As for the animal kingdom of the opaque creature; we find that it is formed from mud and earth, namely from the supreme region of the earth: Hence it is perceived to be hotter and stronger than the others in fire and air; and therefore it also happens that it not only has local motion, but also sense: Moreover, and what is greater, Adam himself with his kind, a distinguished animal, formed from the mud and clay of this kingdom as to its external part, participates in reason and intellect: And indeed, the reason for this is readily apparent, because, namely, the element of fire was made from the superfluous spirit emerging from the first darkness, and adorned with the dignity of supreme light; Hence, due to the dominance of light, it is called hot and dry: Thus the element of air draws its origin from the superfluous spirit of the middle heaven; hence it is hot and humid, due to the equal temperament of spirit and light: The element of water, however, proceeds from the superfluous spirit and weak light of the lowest darknesses; and this is the reason why waters and springs are so frequent in the innermost bowels of the earth; Hence waters are called cold and humid, due to the scarcity of heat in that kingdom; namely, due to the humid nature of its thinner part. But more clearly on these matters below in their proper place.

We see therefore that the mineral kingdom, as it is the lowest portion of darkness, consists of water and the lowest darknesses; the vegetable kingdom, however, of air and the middle darknesses; and the animal kingdom of fire and the supreme darknesses. Consider, I ask, that the mineral is composed of an opaque body and a conforming spirit; similarly, that vegetables cover an opaque body with a lighter spirit; and finally, that animals possess their opaque covering with a most free spirit: Hence these bodies differ from each other only by the varied nature of the earth, since you yourselves confess that the reason for diverse spirits proceeds from the diversity of elements, one of which is exalted in dignity above another.

Furthermore, if an animal body is burned by fire, it exhibits a more violent and more vivid flame than a vegetable, because of its closer kinship and disposition with fire, mixed with air; since in a vegetable, fire predominates less, and water more. Similarly, also, a vegetable is more easily ignited and conceives flame more quickly than a mineral; because it resists the violence of fire due to the stubbornness of its compact substance. And so also, an animal leaves fewer dregs or ashes after its combustion than a vegetable, and a vegetable likewise leaves fewer or less than a mineral. Since, therefore, every sublunary creature is composed of body and spirit, it is necessary that the body itself corresponds to the spirit in the proportions of darkness; and this is the reason why there is so great a difference between species and species, and between genera and genera. But concerning these kingdoms we shall discourse more fully in the following chapter.

CHAP. I.

Concerning water, or the universal spirit without any regard to light or information.

[Large decorative initial S]
The substance of the waters enclosed in the womb of hyle was nothing, or rather something between Being and Nothing; and therefore Non-being, but in potentiality to being; since every Entity has its existence from the presence of informing light: Whence these waters in potentiality, and covered by the veil of primary darkness, were called by the Peripatetics the first and most remote matter; which they named something in potentiality, but nothing in actuality: Nor indeed could their darkness be called privation by them, inasmuch as no form, which would cause them to exist, had preceded; but from the origin in the vast abyss of hyle, formless, uncultivated, empty, and void, Jehovah or Aleph not yet illuminating them, nor looking forth from His center into their deformity, they existed. And in this way the waters are to be considered nothing, indeed scarcely anything imaginable, but a substance in potentiality constituting empty hyle, or a void and Phantastic earth. But truly, when א Aleph looked forth from His center into the deformity of things, then the spirit of His mouth, and the rays of His countenance, were carried upon the dark face of the Abyss; on whose exterior face the deformed waters, previously hidden, now appeared outwardly with the form and perceptible appearance of waters (whence the abyss is thus written תהום, inasmuch as by the presence or first appearance of the uncreated spirit ה it is enclosed): For although by a sudden intuition of light the first face of the waters was revealed, yet its rays had not yet penetrated into their depth: Whence it was said that the Spirit of the Lord was carried upon the waters, and not, that it was yet in the waters: Therefore, after the manifestation of the upper waters, the first creature, namely light, was created; that is, the supreme portion of the waters was illuminated; which most noble creature of all is composed of the eternal rays of the uncreated spirit, and of the most subtle water, as will be explained below in its proper place: By the virtue therefore
