108          SECT. I. PORT. I. PART. II. LIB. II.

that divine [thing] or Word, of which the wise man speaks, is the cause of their illumination through its entry into the entire
mass of water: For Wisdom encompassed the roundness of the heavens, walked in the depth of the abysses, in the wave of the sea, & in all the earth. Ecclesiastes 1:4. From which it is also clear that that axiom of St. Peter
is most true (2 Peter 3:6), that the heavens & the earth itself were first from water, & through water, consisting by the word of God:
Which waters God indeed, through the same Word, weighed in diverse regions by measure,
and placed a law for them throughout the universe. Therefore, we do not take water here for mere cloud or sea water,
which is visible, but for all humid nature, counting from the supersubstantial heaven down to the lowest

is in them, God constantly preserves forever. Wherefore, in many places of our work, we have called these waters the universal

than gross water, & gross water, which is nothing other than the substance of the abyss, or subtle earth:
We call subtle all that invisible which is called heaven; And so it is said that Jeho-

the subtle, nor the subtle other than the gross, because what is gross will be the same as
what is subtle by attenuation, as we see in the burning of wood; And what is subtle is rendered gross by inspissation,

Trismegistus found in the Emerald Tablet, where it says: "That which is above is like that which is below," etc. We conclude,
therefore, that this material element is signified by Abraham's second mother in the Yetzirah: For Mem (מ)
is that Hebrew hieroglyph which signifies waters brought forth into light, just as Tav (ת) was the
character or symbol of darkness: And hence it is that the Hebrew word for water is formed from the
gemination of that character; in the middle of which characters the letter Yod (י), formal or luminous, is found,
as it were the Sun illuminating the waters, both upper, as well as lower; in this way: מים Maym, that is, Water;
where the preceding Mem (מ), which is open at the base, denotes the luminous waters; through whose open base Yod (י)
flows into nature: And the final & closed Mem (ם) indicates the lower waters, which terminate with the darkness of the earth:
And Yod (י) in the middle is in the place of the Sun, in the middle of the firmament dividing the waters from the waters:
Thus, therefore, you have a brief exposition, according to the reasoning of the Cabalists, of the living & primary word for waters, מים:
in which, by living letters or characters, both the substance of the waters and the symbol of God Jehovah,
who informs them, lying hidden in their center, & illuminating & informing them from all around the center, is explained.

CHAPTER II.

That water is the mother of all things.

JUST as Abraham in his Yetzirah made Aleph (א) obscure, or darkness, the one & first deformed
mother or prime matter; so also, not inappropriately, he established Mem (מ), which is the symbol of water gushing forth from the belly
of the dark Aleph, as the second mother, or the second matter of things, from which the
substance of heaven & earth, and all things found in them, are derived: For in the beginning, not heaven, but water
was created, and then afterwards heaven & earth were made from water; as it were, from whose multitude
God at last created all things, & separated them from each other, such as heaven, earth, fire, air, & water,
of immense height, depth, & breadth; all of which were reduced & compacted into such
harmony & unity, that even in each of these separated bodies those four essential matters
are found; namely, Air, hot & humid, containing in itself water & fire and also earth;
Water, cold & humid, containing in itself air & earth, whose shadow appears, whence it is also called Abyss;
Earth, embracing in itself water, fire, air; But also water comprehends in itself earth, from which it also has its form,
and by the same reason fire, which lies hidden in the earth, & air, from which it has its softness & mobility:
And these, I say, are all from water, through water, & in that immense water, which is the first mother,
whose character or hieroglyph is Mem (מ); in which so many regions or species, as it were diverse of one kind, are found because
of the greater or lesser presence of uncreated light in them.
We see, therefore, that water itself is the first unactualized matter of all things, & consequently

--- Page 607 ---
**On the Primary Nature of the Elements.** 109

which is the first mother of all things, and as it were a storehouse, from which all things, both visible and invisible, were taken and separated: Nor, however, is this to be understood or heard as if God made all things from one mother, which existed from eternity, for example, from water; and that for that reason, water is the first being of all things; For, as has been said copiously elsewhere, the first mother and storehouse, from which God created water, was Nothing; that is, Darkness and hyle signified by מ [Mem] as the first mother; From whose matrix, by means of and emanating divine light, מ [Mem] Mein water, came forth: But this is to be understood in a human way, that God created water from Nothing; And it is rightly said; since in the beginning or hyle there was nothing visible, nothing formed, but mere formlessness, from which, as from nothing into being and consequently unimaginable, and from nothing invisible, and therefore also insensible, God Elohim created and brought forth waters into light: Moreover, if we truly and beyond human understanding wish to consider whence water has its true origin, it cannot be denied that in the creation of water there was a certain formless matter (as I said) in the highest mystery or hyle, which was in the divine will, From which storehouse, as a mystery, they flowed forth in the creation of water; which seems too obscure, indeed even incredible, to human understanding: For we, who are born of flesh, both feel and speak carnally about such matters; but if once, divine grace leading the way, we are reborn of the spirit, we shall understand such mysteries to satiety, and shall know the origin and first beginning of water; which from the highest invisible and formless mystery was made visible; from which then afterwards the other principles arose: And so this water can now rightly be called the matter of all things; namely, invisible water of invisible things, such as the heavens and their intelligences; and visible water of visible things, namely, of the earth and sea, of fresh waters; and of those things which dwell in them: Whence it is reasonably to be concluded that water is the second mother, or secondary matter of all things, both celestial and terrestrial; and consequently, that the entire universe, including heaven and earth, is nothing other than water altered and changed in diverse ways, according to the diverse manner of the luminous act operating differently upon it: For thus we see that one part of the same river can be dyed with ink, another with blood, another with saffron, and the extremity of the same with milk or lime, while nevertheless in the meantime it is one and the same water in species, and of the same continuity. Finally, we have sufficient testimony for this matter from the Apostle in the previously cited passage, namely 2 Peter 3, that the heaven in the first times also was, just as the earth, consisting of water by the Word of God. Therefore, that water Mem, which is the first mother of things, is simple and mixed with no other thing, appears from what has been said above; That it also embraces the principles of the other three elements within itself, and contains within itself the seed of all things, both visible and invisible, is quite clearly established; inasmuch as from it, and in it, God founded heaven, earth, and all their things, both visible and invisible, and consequently also the four elements, and placed their seeds in it: Wherefore it is also certain that the elements themselves were made from water, as will be demonstrated in the following chapter.

**C H A P. III.**

*How water is the mother of the heavens, and of all elements, and*
*the glue, by means of which, through divine act, they are connected*
*in composition?*

**IN** the preceding [chapters] it has been declared that the substance of formless darknesses were waters or spirits, and that hence it follows that one species of darkness is preferred to another; namely, that which belongs to the superior heaven, to that which belongs to the middle heaven, and again that to this which belongs to the lowest; namely, with respect to the mobility of the place of that light, whose sparks these dark spirits seized for themselves, while, as light pursued darkness as something opposed to itself, the superfluous spirits of each heaven were gradually driven downwards towards the center with their dark veil: For although that scarcely imaginable matter in hyle, which now appears and is called water through the revelation of the fiery spirit, was equally dispersed throughout the vast and infinite abyss or chasm of hyle (since all inequality was made by a diverse act, which did not manifest itself before the beginning in hyle, inasmuch as its source א [Aleph] Aleph had not yet revealed itself) nevertheless it is now to be understood that this equality is turned into inequality by the appearance of uncreated light: For, where the presence and effect of light is more clear and copious, there, because of its attenuating and subtilizing nature, those spirits, in which that clear light dwells, become more subtle and rare; Whence, the Empyrean heaven having been purged of its superfluous dark spirits, that superfluity, like a horrible shadow, was forced to flow downwards by the gaze of Jehovah; Indeed, this whole mass was greatly disturbed, according to that [passage] in Psalm 77:17: "The depths trembled at the presence of Jehovah, and were troubled;" And, Hermes Trismegistus, Pimander 1: "At the presence of the immense revealed light of Pimander, a horrible shadow flowed downwards in an oblique revolution;" that is, the shadow, that is, the denser part of the unformed spirits, inclined itself towards the center at the presence of the uncreated light, and the thinner portion of the same, purified from darkness, [became] a vehicle for the uncreated light of the place—

**CHAP. IV.**

*On the manifold division of waters, and especially into visible and*
*invisible:*

Now henceforth we shall briefly say a few words concerning the division of universal water into its particles. In *Gen. 1.* we read, *that the waters were divided into the expanse, which indeed is part of the firmament or heaven, and into the collected, which is called the sea:* For this is the exact division of clear waters; which seems to imply the same thing as the distinction of water into visible and invisible; concerning which below: Again, water is divided into an upper and a lower part; Thus it is said that the firmament distinguished the upper, subtle, and spiritual waters from the lower, gross, and material ones; And the firmament itself or the middle heaven participates in both, and its waters are moderately thin and moderately thick; Hence the sphere of equality is said to pass through the center of the middle heaven: Again, in *Proverbs 8.* it is divided into the upper clouds above, into the fountains of the deep, and into the sea; These are the words; *When Jehovah strengthened the upper clouds above, when he made firm the fountains of the deep, when he imposed his decree upon the sea, and upon the waters, that they should not transgress the boundary of his mouth, when he established the foundations of the earth; I, Wisdom, was with him.* Therefore, by the upper clouds above, he understood the heavens themselves, according to *Psalm 104. 3. The upper heavens are covered with waters by God;* And *Job 25. 5. Look at heaven, and contemplate the upper clouds, that they may be high above you;* Similarly *Psalm 89. 7. Heaven is called the upper clouds;* And *Psalm 89. 9. To God Jehovah, who is considered equal in the upper cloud?* By the fountains of the deep, he meant fresh water, and by the sea, salt water, and by the earth, opaque water, which was the dregs in the creation of universal clear waters. But elsewhere he seems to include all visible waters under the name of the sea; namely *Psalm 146. Heaven, earth, sea, and whatever is in them, God constantly preserves forever;* And *Gen. 7. 24:* Clear water is distinguished into the fountains of the deep, and the cataracts of heaven: And *Deut. 4. 18.* visible waters are divided into waters under the earth and above the earth; Likewise, visible and sensible upper waters are divided into cloud, mist, vapor and exhalation or wind; of which mention is made in *Psalm 104. & 105. 39. Psalm 135. 7. Ecclesiasticus 1. 3.* and in countless other places; Likewise, the same waters are divided into liquid and condensed; such as snow, hail, ice, manna, and so forth in others: Similarly, visible lower waters are distinguished into sweet, and salt, acidic, bitter, sulphurous, and hot, and actually cold; Furthermore, waters are either living, *which Christ himself said remove thirst forever in John 4. 13.* or common waters, which do not perpetually extinguish thirst. But among all other divisions of water, this one is preferred by us, which is into spiritual and invisible, and into material or visible, and by which again spiritual waters are distinguished into natural and supernatural, and again natural into ethereal and elemental, and similarly material or visible into limpid, namely the element of water, and opaque or earth. Therefore, we shall discuss this kind of division of water in this place. Therefore it must be known that water was invisible in the beginning; But, so that humans and other animals could see it, God clothed it as it were with some transparent garment; just as all visible things were invisible from the beginning, and afterwards at last clothed in a visible form, as if with a garment, so that they could be seen and perceived by bodily eyes: And so water will persist in this visible essence, until its fixed term, when it will again return to a clear, invisible, and plainly spiritual essence: Concerning which that greatest Psalmist of Israel sings in *Psalm 102.* But that God created visible things from invisible things is testified by sacred scripture in *Epistle to the Hebrews 11. By faith we acknowledge, that it has always been so done with the world through the Word of God, that from those things which could not be seen, those things which can be seen were made.* Therefore, in the beginning, water was invisible, from which all visible things were created; Which noble creature also, so that it can be seen, is accustomed to put on a garment or a shell: Thus indeed we see invisible air put on the garment of a dense and visible cloud; and also sometimes heaven, containing the best treasure of Jehovah, is made visible to man according to *Deut. 28. 12:* But if anyone knows the method and art of capturing and collecting true invisible water, then, the Sages say, he possesses the most excellent balsam, healing all kinds of infirmities; concerning which I will explain more clearly below in its proper time, what I have received from trustworthy authors.

CHAPTER V.
*Concerning the measure of waters; And whether water was created sweet or salty.*

[Large initial Q] Although the body of created water is of such magnitude as no mortal can grasp by reason; nevertheless, God measured it with His hand, *Isaiah 40,* as He who assigned to each thing its measure, *number, and weight, Wisdom 11.* Indeed, this craftsman also measured the created water in such a way that He holds its measure by number, namely, how many thousands of its bundles exist: Moreover, the weight of water has also been explored by God's most exact balance, and thus a most certain number of pounds or weights has been recorded. This measure, number, and weight of water are joined with such harmony and equality, that that whole body cannot move either upwards, downwards, or even sideways without the Creator's permission; but it so constantly perseveres in its measure, number, and weight, that not even a drop of it perishes: For in whatever way we use water, by washing or pouring it on the ground, nothing of it is lost, but it returns either to the water of the earth, or even into the air; since water is likewise there; so indeed, that nothing at all perishes, but it is always preserved in its measure, number, and weight without any diminution: Nor indeed is this to be said only of common water, but also of the earth; the same is to be understood of visible water, of air, of cloud, of fire, of aether, and of the Empyrean spirit; which indeed are diverse species of the most general water: For concerning the measure of the earth (which is the dregs of water, or opaque water) it is thus written *Psalm 95:4. The deep places of the earth are in the hand of God, in whose possession are the heights of the mountains etc. And Psalm 104:5. God founded the earth upon its bases, that it should not be moved forever: Likewise Job 26:7. God hangs the earth upon nothing; And Proverbs 3:19. God founded the earth by wisdom; And Job 38:37. Who made the things that descend from the heavens to rest? When the dust descended into that hardness, and the clods adhered to each other?* Concerning the measure of visible water also we find it thus written, *Job 26:10. He has set a boundary for the waters, or by decree has encircled the surface of the waters; And ibid. 28:5. God weighs the waters by measure.* Likewise, speaking of the proportion of the cloud, it says *Job 28:25. He appointed for the rain its law, and a way for the sounding storms; And Proverbs 8. When Jehovah strengthened the upper clouds above etc.* Concerning the number of the heavens also it is said *Job 38:37. Who numbered the heavens in wisdom? And ibid. 26:7. God stretches out the north over the void; And Proverbs 3:19. God established the heavens by understanding etc.* From which it can be seen, that God from the beginning ordered every species of universal water with just balances and due measure, and has perpetually observed such perfection of disposition.

But as for the sweet and salty quality of water, no small doubt can arise from this, whether universal water, indeed whether the sea, from the origin of its creation, was salty or sweet: To which, to answer in a single word, we say that universal water, and consequently all its particles, were sweet from the beginning, and also of such pleasant sweetness and odor, that nothing similar can be found in the whole world: Indeed, this best water, as a wonderful, holy, and unique creature of God, was equally of such pleasant, sweet, and wholesome odor and taste, that human language cannot express these things. But since God clothed this very work of His with a certain transparent shell, or garment, or husk, and enclosed in it its sweetness and taste, and that most pleasant and wholesome odor, it will certainly not be a light art to remove that husk from it, as from other things in which noble balsams lie hidden, and to extract from it a uniform and invisible essence: But this is the labor, this is the task: I know indeed that it must be done, yet I cannot accomplish it; But, to return to the reason for the saltiness of water, we say that on the second day, the waters having been separated from the waters by the interposition of the firmament, all water comprehended under the firmament was gathered into one place and called "sea"; Which indeed immediately, and at that very hour, became salty, nor was anything left in it without salt: Whence it was called *Salty Gen. 14 & Num. 34.* On this occasion, it is also worth noting that salt is found in all fruits of the earth, trees, herbs, animals, minerals, and indeed in all visible things that exist in the whole world, as can be demonstrated by the daily example of the Chemists. The reason, however, is readily available, why salt is found in every composite creature; because, namely, every composite body is made from the dregs or ashes of dark water: Hence, when gross water concurs in the composition of a creature with the ashes of darkness, it follows that that creature contains salt in its composition; because the water of its composition is assimilated to sea water: Hence, therefore, we perceive urine in animals to be infected with salt; and lye from wood, and tartar from wine are very easily made. Wherefore we see that in the beginning universal water was sweet and of pleasant taste; but after its separation and conjunction with the earth, as common water with ashes, that water began to extract the salty nature of the terrestrial ashes, and thus immediately became salty: But indeed the waters of springs and rivers behave differently; For although their origin is from the sea and they return again to the sea according to

CAP. VI.

*Whether water has sense in itself or not?*

BUT here arises a question, not insignificant; namely, whether that universal creature is endowed and gifted with sense and intellect by God? To which we, responding affirmatively, say that first in water, and then in all other creatures formed from it, there is as much sense and intelligence as suffices them to listen and hear the voice of God, so that they tremble at it and obey it: For the Spirit of the Lord, who moved over the waters, so mixed His fiery and intellectual nature with them, that, with the uncreated Spirit moving and hinting, as the agent, the created spirits or waters, as the passive, understood the sense and will of God, and always showed themselves obedient to Him: For because of the presence of the luminous Spirit, the universal waters had life, which were called the Messiah or the power of the Tetragrammaton, and in the regions of nature, Metatron: Hence was that water of Paradise and mystical, which is, as it were, the vital spirit of the whole mass, and is called living water in many places of the sacred scriptures; For God commands that they pour living water upon the ashes. *Deuteronomy 19.* By which reason also David speaks, that the water saw Jehovah, and feared, and the deep was moved. *Psalm 77:7.* And at Christ's command, the waters obeyed, so that its tumultuous or raging waves suddenly submitted to His voice. *Matthew 8:26.* In which places it is confirmed that there is some sense and intellect in water, so that it sees, hears, and fears: Furthermore, it is also said in *Psalm 148:4* that the waters above the heavens praise God: And elsewhere; Heaven, and earth, and sea, and whatever dwells in them, shall praise God: Moreover, water also hears and sees the malice of men, and patiently endures it: Indeed, the waters are said to speak; whence it is said that the heavens declare the praise and glory of God, and that the firmament of the heavens announces His works, which He has made with His hands: Yet men cannot obtain or achieve this, as a punishment for their sins, that the waters obey them, as they obeyed Moses, Joshua, Elijah, Elisha, and Christ, when they passed through the Red Sea with dry feet *Exodus 14:21,* through the Jordan. *Joshua 3:16 & 2 Kings 2.* and walked on the sea, as in the place cited before; notwithstanding that God subjected all His visible creatures to men, so that these might command them, and those, on the contrary, obey them with fear and trembling. *Genesis 1:9.* But this hearing, seeing, fearing, and speaking, which we have said to be in water, rises above all the physical writings of the Gentiles; nor is anything about this very thing found in their books; since they knew neither the true God nor His creatures, but ridiculously fabricated for themselves a certain god and world of their own; Whence they fell into those blind errors, in which even now the world, and this age of ours judging the world, are stuck: And indeed, I myself in a way submit to their opinions, though with a certain constrained will, lest, if I depart too much from the common error right at the very beginning, they call me a critic, an introducer of new opinions, a vain person, and an opponent of old doctrine: For would not this seem foolish and ridiculous to some overwhelmed by ignorance, if it were asserted among them that the Empyrean, ethereal heaven, and the seat of God is both in the elementary world and in the highest; and that heaven is on earth, and earth in heaven, likewise that God is in man, and man in God, and that the Sun, Moon, and Planets descend: And yet we boldly affirm that all these things can be proven and confirmed by the clearest testimonies of sacred scripture, however much they lose credibility when related to the ignorant: Therefore, I desire to lead and attract you through the ancient way and human and fictitious wisdom to the divine and true gate of wisdom, that is, from Aristotelian foundations to the Elysian field of the Word of God or the paths of the sacred Bibles through similar principles, in which is the unique and sole truth, and outside of which there is none: For it is not fitting to abandon the source of all Wisdom, and to seek art, science, and intellect in foreign regions, as the Hagarites and those who were in Teman did; since they never recognized the way of true wisdom *Baruch 3.* For this source alone possesses the key of David, which opens and no one shuts, and which shuts and no one opens. *Isaiah 22.*

CAP. VII.

*Concerning the greatest mysteries that are in water.*

INDEED, Jehovah placed very great mysteries in this general water of His; nay, truly, He enclosed the hidden property, power, operation, and motion of water, though in an invisible manner, within every one of His creatures, both visible and invisible; so indeed that in it lies hidden the seed of all things; And consequently, according to our preceding doctrine, this is the universal mother of all things; since in its womb are contained the seeds of things; namely, of heavens, stars, animals, vegetables, gems, and metals; about which extensively in the Section On Medicines; **There is also**

...[continuing from previous page: "Est etiam..."] also the food and nourishment of all living things of every kingdom, and likewise the glue and connection of all elements and palpable elementals; The most experienced Sages also said that it is the most excellent medicine that can be found anywhere under the Sun between heaven and earth; And finally, it is the greatest mystery of all, that God made all the stars, and indeed the Sun, and the Moon, with the other Planets, and the entire air, and the angels and spirits dwelling therein, and finally the terrestrial globe itself with all existing things in it, out of water, and enclosed them in water in a wonderful way, and firmly sealed them in it by His living and omnipotent word; and that each one of them constantly perseveres in the order originally instituted, and executes its function without interruption for the praise and honor of God, and the utility of the human race.
We see therefore that heaven is, as it were, pure water, and that all the stars, as it were, swim in it, no differently than wood in water; And yet that wood

moving, and there resting, we suddenly perceive it to be corrupted, and rendered most foul; which also does not happen from a simple condition of water, but from its mixture with some hidden heterogeneity; which indeed heterogeneous nature, thus hidden by its long immobile station in the same water, is corrupted, nor can the water prevent the marks of corruption, inasmuch as its action and motion are removed, and thus, because of the corruption of the terrestrial matter adhering to it, the water itself is said to be corrupted: So also can that water, which is imbued with some foul thing, be said to be corrupted or to corrupt, although it itself truly in itself and by itself remains incorruptible and pure and healthy forever: This also is the reason for corruption in man; who nevertheless by himself, both with respect to his spirit or water, and to the vivifying light, is incorruptible and eternal.

C A P. IX.
*Concerning that portion of the lower water, which is called the sphere, or element of humidity; And concerning the most proper quality of water.*

ILLA portion of the lower waters, which is situated between two extremes, namely between fire and earth, is called the sphere of humidity; which is nothing other than those two elements, which they called Philosophical water and fire, that is, visible water, and invisible water, or dense and subtle: For this sphere is distinguished into two parts differing from each other in nature and place, because of the proximity of the two extremes approaching each of them, so that the lowest portion of the sphere of humidity is rendered visible and dense because of the dominion of the earth's coldness in it; whose property it is to condense: The upper part, however, is invisible and rare, because of the companionship of the neighboring fire's heat, whose property it is to attenuate, and by attenuating, to render invisible. Therefore, earth is the lowest extremity of universal water, and the opaque tabernacle of cold; fire, however, is the supreme summit and apex of the lower waters; water and air, which are called the single sphere of humidity, are suspended between these two. Their origin, as has been said in the preceding [parts], is derived from the lowest darkness and the middle of the sky: For by the compression of these darknesses around the center of the universe, certain superfluous spirits of the soul and wings of sparks enclosed within them are either exalted more sublimely or submerged more deeply according to the dignity of the light which is carried in them: But indeed, sparks of secondary light, or of nature, immersed in the spirit of the middle darknesses reflected downwards, are more dignified and more vivacious than those tertiary ones which are infused into the spirit of the lowest darknesses: Therefore, the latter fills the place of the sea and visible water, the former the vast capacity of the air; and both together constitute the entire sphere of equality: But here a great doubt can arise; namely, why, since both the element earth and the element fire are portions of water, these two are not called humid, but on the contrary dry, although humidity usually accompanies the condition and nature of fire in its origin.
To which we respond, in the first place, that although earth is called arid; because of the condensing and constricting presence of immense cold, nevertheless it has within itself a hidden humidity of water, as can be seen in the nature of salt, found in the middle of any portion of earth, that by means of actual humidity with heat it is reduced to water: Whence it is clear that the earth itself, in a hidden way, and as it were in potential, has humidity within itself; but because of the congelative action of the dry cold itself, the effect of that humidity is removed; which humidity nevertheless lies hidden in the earth in the meantime, and exists in potential. Hence therefore it is that humidity, as far as we are concerned, is said to be absent from the earth, so that it is called dry and arid, not indeed because it is truly and centrally so; but because, as far as human sense is concerned, humidity does not seem to have dominion in the earth, inasmuch as all its mass appears dry in the midst of the waters, as is held in *Gen. 1*; And yet, if we look into the matter as it is with the eyes of understanding, we find humidity centrally here; but, inasmuch as it is congealed by the force of cold, it is called not humidity but aridity, and humidity is said to be absent for this reason; which absence of humidity in the earth is for this cause called dryness. For a reason not dissimilar, humidity is also found in the element of fire; for it is, as it were, the vehicle of essential light; Nevertheless, this, because of the attenuating nature of fire, is so attenuated, namely, the spirit receiving igneous force, that no sign of humidity appears in it; and consequently this member of water is called dry, inasmuch as, because of the concealment and imperceptibility of humidity, its contrary seems to be present, namely aridity, as we will more fully declare in the description of the ultimate principle, namely light: Therefore, the cone of the material pyramid is packed and suffused with imperceptible spirit; and consequently, humidity, as far as sense is concerned, is thought to be absent in that place, and dryness is said to predominate; In the base, however, of the same, aqueous spirit is found in abundance, but it is congealed into a hard and dry mass by cold, and the act of humidity is removed, and it is transformed into aridity. But, to return to the matter, we say that the intermediate sphere, which contains water and air, is formed from the proportional conflict of the opposite qualities of the two extremes, namely Earth and Fire; namely, from the action of heat on the cold of the earth, and a similar and corresponding passion, reaction, and resistance of terrestrial cold against the pursuing nature of fire: Therefore, the diameter of the igneous pyramid passes and descends from its base, located in the element of fire, to its cone, which ends in the earth; and conversely, the diameter of the terrestrial pyramid ascends from its terrestrial base to its cone

--- Page 615 ---
DE PRIMAR. NATUR. ELEMENT. 117

its cone ending in the belly of the element of fire; Whence it is demonstrated that the proportion of the material pyramid, elevated from earth to fire, is equal to the proportion of the formal [pyramid], of the element of fire, which descends from fire to earth; and consequently, action is proportionate to the resistance of passion, and the place of intersection made by those two pyramids is that true place, or sphere of elemental equality, in which Jehovah is accustomed to manifest Himself to us wonderfully in His glory; just as also in the middle intersection, made by two universal pyramids, transcending through the entire mass of created water, the sphere of the soul and of mundane equality is said to be encompassed, in which Jehovah placed His tabernacle. We say therefore, that the cause of humidity in its proper sphere lying between earth and fire is of this kind: The entire disposition or mass of the earth is divided into three regions, namely into three spheres of the darkness of the three heavens; each of which excels the dignity of any other, and has a different respect for resisting the actions of the element of fire: For its upper region (from whose coldness the element of fire, manifested by compression, fled upwards) penetrates even to fire; but since the spirit of this dark cold (which is animal) exists from the dignity of the Empyrean Spirit, therefore the nature of fire easily disperses and dissipates it; and it appears almost entirely fiery from there: But, because the portion of the middle darknesses penetrates only to the convex surface of fire, and, because its coldness is stronger, since the vegetative heat is less, therefore it is accustomed to freeze in the air; but that dryness in coagulation is resolved by the action of the fiery pyramid, and is converted into an intermediate temperature between heat and cold: But if the action of fire is weak, then in the middle region of the air hail, ice, and snow are generated; which again, urged by heat, are reduced into humidity and vapor, or rain and dew. Moreover, the humidity of these two elements varies and differs so much in respect of thinness and density, in as much as they are nearer either to the lower or to the upper limit: For in the lower place the humidity is denser and thicker because of the power and dominion of terrestrial cold in that aqueous medium; but in the upper [place] it is thinner and more subtle because of the property of fiery heat in the disposition of the humid: Furthermore, water is also such a gross humidity; seeing that it is extracted from the dense darknesses of the visible and mineral world's region. From these things therefore we see that the region or sphere of humidity is all that which fills that entire space between fire and earth; and that the essential quality of enlightened water itself is nothing other than humidity; which is therefore called a passive quality, because it is made by the action of hot nature upon cold nature, reducing all that into actual humidity which, by the presence and dominion of freezing and astringent cold, was in potentiality for such an act: Therefore the frozen spirit, and made dry by cold, suffers the action of heat; by whose dissolving power the dry is removed, and the ice is reduced into moisture; and thus finally the quality of humidity, or a nature intermediate between heat and cold, is begotten; which is the true and natural disposition of revealed water; whose absence, as far as we are concerned, is called dryness; although, as it seems to me, dryness, absolutely speaking, is not found in the nature of things; but only comparatively or relatively, as will be clearly declared in the following book. These words of Job 24:19 seem to confirm the elevation of this pyramid of humidity from the earth: "Vapors ascend from the extremity of the earth, etc." Indeed, we could write a book of immense magnitude concerning the ineffable mystery of waters; and their condition, both hidden and manifest, but, since that does not pertain to the purpose already committed to our hands, therefore we shall omit it in this place, so that we may finally advance and arrive at the third and nobler luminous principle, both of supernatural and natural things.

CHAP. I.

*Concerning the ultimate mother* ש *Shin, and how it proceeds from the first mother, illuminated, namely*
א *, and from the second mother, not illuminated.*

[Large decorative initial Q] Uemadmodum in the wondrous name, or the supersubstantial elements of יהוה, the emanation of the most essential character Yod, as a second person, and a son from the father, passes into the first spirit Heh; So also in the three substantial elements, which are called mothers, we see that the immediate principles of the world and natural things are derived from it: For the dark א, by looking forth from the darkness of prime matter, becomes luminous, and thus denotes darkness by its silence and concealment; but by its manifestation, it denotes the point, center, and origin of illumination; And since its immense ray מ illuminated the waters, and reduced them from the nothingness of the abyss into actuality, therefore מ is said to proceed from א, as a son from a father; and therefore it is compared to a line, which is the first progression in Geometry from a point: And hence it is taken by the Cabalists for the divine Word, as the informed for the informer: And ם, Mem final and closed, denotes the word FIAT not uttered, but still enclosed in the womb of the Abyss; Hence ם closed is a symbol of silence. But indeed, מ, open Mem, signifies an open and uttered word or discourse; And it is a symbol of the sphere of Jupiter; thereby arguing that, with the abyss of waters opened, the glory of Jehovah is revealed to men. We see therefore, that Mem, the second mother, signifies the son, the second person, or the Word; because by the presence of the Word, the waters appear as they are; And from them the heavens were created, according to that Psalm: *By the word of the Lord were the heavens made &c.* But now at last let us come to the ultimate mother of natural things (concerning which I have proposed to treat in this little book), which the Sages have called ש: Which indeed relates to the two preceding ones as a surface to a line and a point; For, as a surface proceeds from a point, as a primary principle, and a line as a medium; so also Shin ש flows forth from א and מ: Therefore, as מ proceeded from א, as a son from the Father, or the second mother from the first, so also ש proceeds from א and מ as a certain third thing, derived as it were from the Father and the Son, and is assimilated by the Cabalists to the Holy Spirit: And hence it is that its character is formed as having the shape of a crown with three eminences; so that it is thereby argued to be a symbol of the Holy Trinity: Furthermore, grammatically we say that ש is that which suffices, or is enough, as if it were sufficient, inasmuch as it is a symbol of the Trinity, and the completion of the whole machine, according to that aforesaid saying; *By the word of the Lord were the heavens established, and by the spirit from His mouth all their power;* Where the Lord is א the speaker; and the Word is Fiat מ actualized; and the spirit from His mouth is ש Shin, from which, as from a fiery form, all action and power proceeds: For א is in Mem, and the power of both is in ש Shin: For these three mothers are nothing but one spirit, which is one God, to whom *Abraham* also assents in *Ietzirah*: One God

Living God, & Blessed Himself, & blessed be His name, who lives forever, voice, & Spirit, & Word; & this is

CAP. II.

Concerning Shin hidden in darkness, & revealed; And how, according to the
position of its character, the property of the word is observed to differ?

IN the preceding it has been declared, that Shin ש, which is the symbol of fire & created light, or of the fiery spirit, of the un-
created א mixed with the created מ spirit, is either enclosed & hidden in the dark waters of the abyss,
or not hidden; In the former case it denotes the penultimate species of darkness, which signifies Chaos,
& is thus enclosed by dark characters חשך: and thus the divine fire came forth from the dark
cloud on Mount Sinai before the Israelites: But if it is not hidden, it appears to be that terrible
& consuming fire, passing before the face of Jehovah, of which the Israelites, speaking to Moses, said.
Deut. 5. 31. We have heard the voice of Jehovah from the midst of the fire; If God were to continue to speak with man, would he live? Now therefore
why should we die? would not that great fire consume us? &c. And in this case it is not hidden among dark characters,
but is thus depicted אש signifying fire; where Aleph denotes Jehovah, of whom it is a
symbol; & therefore that mixed with ש argues that Jehovah appears from the center of fire or created light.
Hence it is said in Psalm. 104. 2. God is clothed with light, stretching out the heavens like a curtain, or a veil: Furthermore,
the essence of the Sun is also explained by such living characters שמש, that is, Sun, so called from ministering
light; Where מ Mem, or water, or the clear spirit & pure substance of the Sun itself is seen in the center,
and the two characters of Shin, include it on both sides, arguing that light is seen only
in the Sun, & the substantial spirit, which by Philosophers is called the denser part of its orb, is covered
on all sides with light & fire. By which we are clearly taught, that this most efficacious mother is the cause
of visible light, & that its virtue emanates from the living parts or characters of the ineffable name;
according to whose exemplar the mothers of nature are produced, and the parts of the world are delineated:
And hence it is, that the primary & spiritual light, which flowed immediately from the face of Jod, or the lucid Aleph,
emanated from the characters or formal elements of the Tetragrammaton itself: Hence that most sacred word FIAT,
surrounded on all sides by fiery spirit, is thus expressed in Holy letters יהי. Where, as in the Sun שמש it is held by a single mother
with a double embrace, which is the tabernacle of the Word in the world; So also ה the central spirit
of the most efficacious Word FIAT is likewise contained by a double embrace from the single Jod, father of light: where
in place of the entire wonderful name יהוה, Jehovah we have יה, Jah, & ה which equals a double ה;
so that from this it is denoted, that י Jod fills the triple יהה, that is, the three heavens of the entire world, &
consequently, that the Messiah, or the virtue of יהוה is everywhere in the world, & through the world; that indeed,
which was Wisdom itself, & existed, before anything was created, with Jod; as is found in the sacred text:
Light therefore, shining immediately from its spirit, retains in itself the characters of divinity: Hence it is called
in the holy tongue אור: where ר as was said before, is a sign of poverty, emptiness, & void, & consequently
can denote the darkness of hyle; from which א shining forth, renders the middle ו, as Jod in He, or
lucid Aleph in ה; which constitute six; The hieroglyph of which number is Vau ו. Therefore it denotes
the illuminated divine spirit: For, as Mem or illuminated water is called Light, & is denoted by
Shin ש; in which מ is hidden, as in the Sun שמש; so also ה the Holy Spirit is hidden in Vau;
for this argues uncreated light, while that argues created light; And in אור, that is, light, Vau, being a spherical
letter, argues that between א God & ר darkness, the spherical world ו was placed illuminated.
Hence it also denotes, that God is outside &
inside all things.

C A P. III.

*An exposition of the word 'Heavens' from the consideration*
*of its living characters.*

[Large initial U]ST as three substantial mothers of nature are derived from three supersubstantial and most primary fathers, who are explained through the three characters of the stupendous name, namely יהו, as through hieroglyphs, that is, through ו ה י (for י is a symbol, and as it were the soul of mother א, and ה of mother מ, and ו of mother ש), so also from these natural, or primary substantial, and most simple principles, secondary, or more composite principles arise: For from מ and ש, the substance of the heavens themselves is composed, namely from מ as the material part, and ש as the formal part: Whence the highest heaven is, as it were, entirely Shin, or fiery; whence the Empyrean is called from *pyr* (πῦρ), that is, fire; And the middle heaven is ethereal, as it were *aether*, that is, fiery air: For, just as in the first ordination, ש proceeded from luminous Aleph, and מ from spirit or water; by the mixture of which, subsequently, אויר (avir), air, light, was created, whose hieroglyph

sacred scripture made mention of the pillar of fire, *Exod. 13. 12.* It also speaks of the fire of Jehovah descending and consuming the burnt offering and the stones and the wood, and licking up all the water in the trench, *1. Reg. 18. 38.* By which spirit also the captain of fifty with his fifty was struck dead, *2. About these, however, we will briefly discuss in order in the following chapter.

CAP. V.

*Concerning uncreated invisible light, and how it is compared to the nature of visible fire:*
*Furthermore, it is also proven that visible light is a certain reflection of uncreated*
*and invisible light in the garments which it puts on.*

**L**IGHT, that invisible and uncreated light, from which heaven and earth, and all things both visible and invisible, were formed, is that unique, sacred, ineffable, and eternal Word of God, or Messiah, and the true power of the Tetragrammaton; And this Word was in the beginning with God, and the Word was God; All things were made through this Word, and without Him was not anything made that was made; in Him was life: This is that Word, in which all things firmly subsist, and through which God powerfully and gloriously manifested Himself to creatures: This is that Word, through which God spoke from the mouth of Prophets and angels, and announced salvation to the human race; This is that Word, which powerfully took upon itself the sins of the world, and reconciled the human race with God: This is that Word, which in the most holy divinity constituted the third person: For God created heaven and earth; by which indeed the first person itself is noted for us; And the second in that God spoke this Word יהוה FIAT; and the third in the spirit of His mouth; All these things God Himself explained through those brief words already mentioned, that in His divine majesty He is three in uniform essence, namely, God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit; and thus indeed three in persons, but only one God: This, I say, the Word FIAT, is eternal and divine; the splendor of divine glory, and the image of the invisible divine essence, and the light of this world, which illuminates every man in this world; He who with a humbled heart and true desire apprehends this light, it shines before him into eternal life. This light is not perceived by human eyes; But it is seen by the Spirit, which is implanted in man by God, in this and the future life: For, since the human body, given by God, is obscured by flesh and blood, so that its eyes are blind, it is impossible for it to behold this light; nor can a mortal body, before clarification, see that which is immortal: Scripture also testifies that man has neither seen God, nor will he ever see Him in this carnal body, until it is purified, and after this life, made conformable to the body of Christ through clarification, and as it were, divine; For then he will see God, as He is. This is that eternal light, which first illuminated the formless waters in the identity of the Spirit with the Father; This is that divine Wisdom, which by its power distinguished the three heavens from each other, and by whose gaze light things, flying upwards, and heavy things, descending downwards, were established: This is that peaceful knot, by which, with the discord and strife of humid matter removed, harmony was made throughout the regions of the entire world, and perpetual peace was reconciled among the contentious and litigious elements: This invisible light is the intellectual mind of the superior heaven's spirit, the essence of the ethereal heaven, the form of the elements, the life of composite creatures, and the soul of the universal world; The soul, I say, is of the universal waters, and the center or point of life in all seeds enclosed in water; and consequently the first, true, and unique act of all creatures: Through it the earth is suspended in the vast center of the world upon nothing by the scales of justice; Through it the mass of the earth rests, and the seeds contained therein grow and multiply: Through it minerals daily but slowly grow rich in form, and vegetables decay,

decay, so that in a multitude of perfection they may rise from the earth in a better and more dignified state; animals produce offspring through mutual coitus and are carried hither and thither by local motion; through it, elemental fire lies hidden in every creature, animal, vegetable, and mineral; from which it is also extracted by art; and through it, visible fire burns, and is accustomed to examine and purify impure things, and likewise to reduce contaminated compounds into their pure elements by a wonderful act; indeed, the Word acts in the center of every fire most evidently: through it, the seas flow and ebb again, are tempestuously stirred, and again are calmed and composed; but also, at first, through this most clear and active Wisdom, visible water was reduced within its limits into this mass; by the presence of this Spirit, winds are perceived to gush forth from every corner of the world, like rushing rivers, clouds are sustained in the equilibrium of the air by admirable balances, waters are converted into snow, hail, and rain, and, what is more miraculous, fire is hidden in the center of dense and frozen clouds, and is seen to burn in them despite the power of the waters: finally, the fiery element is exalted above the air through it, and the air above the water; and the earth also, by the same law of the Word, is subject to and lies beneath the water.

Therefore, the divine Word is the eternal light, the sacred Wisdom, the Messiah or virtue of the Tetragrammaton, that central principle, uncreated and eternal in itself, but created with respect to the thing into which it acts and moves, as far as men are concerned: for God exists imperceptible to us who are led by sense, and is known only by effect; so that men, observing things with sensible eyes and not spiritual ones, wrongly take the internal actor for the Spirit in which it dwells, and likewise the internal Spirit, which in men is the temple of God, for the body: thus, they wrongly regard the creature, neglecting the creator, and so are ignorant of the divine act in creatures, and value it cheaply due to lack of faith: and yet, what is visible was made from the invisible through the Word, as chapter 11 of the Epistle to the Hebrews teaches us; *“By faith,” it says, “we understand that the world has always been so acted upon by the Word of God, that from things which could not be seen, those things which can be seen came into being:”* from this it is clear that what is visible is made from spirit or subtle and invisible water through condensation, by means of the Spirit of Wisdom; who dwells in the center and operates all things: by a similar reason, through this virtue of Jehovah, the ethereal fires glow and, with constant motion, like visible watchful ministers of God, circle the entire machine, while their intrinsic principle impelling them is this secret and invisible virtue of Jehovah, without which nothing exists: for His fiery spirit lies hidden secretly; which, by contracting the invisible Spirit, renders such a visible appearance as is seen: indeed, this visible composition would suddenly vanish like smoke, unless that divine act, by its mysterious presence, bound its parts as if by a bond of nature; for if this seal of Jehovah were to withdraw from the world, it would be necessary for all things to be reduced again to formless hyle; inasmuch as the form and essence of everything depends on the presence of this virtue. Oh, how glorious is that solar globe, in which the presence of this sacred virtue reigns in abundance; indeed, into which Jehovah has placed His tabernacle! Yet that light which is emitted from the Sun is not from the immediate presence of the sacred light; but is a certain reflection of it, which appears colored and visible due to the density of the body, although in itself it cannot be seen by bodily eyes without death and the destruction of a part: therefore, it is the colored aspect of the body that is seen, and by no means that eternal light of God, which is the secret and hidden virtue of the Tetragrammaton existing in every visible thing, by which it subsists: indeed, the angels of the superior heaven, who stand before the face of Jehovah, possess this virtue as the divine mind of their bodies; so that this uncreated light is to them as a soul; but the pure spirit, in which it floats and is carried, is their body: hence, just as God is called identity, so an angel is alterity, inasmuch as it is formed from a created spirit, as a body, and a luminous and uncreated spirit: and hence it is that an angel is called a creature with respect to its body, and by reason of the divine virtue abounding in it, is called God and Jehovah; whence an angel is also called Elohim (אלהים): indeed, it is even used for Christ or the Messiah in some places of the sacred page, as has been clearly explained in the preceding (parts). From this, therefore, we see the reason how this Holy Spirit, the Word of Jehovah the Father, by immersing itself into a greater or lesser multitude of matter, produced all things previously uncreated and existing only in potential, into something in actuality, and that without it nothing can persist or remain in actuality. We conclude, therefore, that where there is something visible, it becomes such through the invisible presence of divine virtue; which is inherent in the thing seen, and without which nothing exists, but all things vanish into the substance of hyle; and consequently, whatever we see, that indeed can be called God. And hence it is that both worlds are called the image of God; inasmuch as both are such as they are seen to be, because of the presence of God; who, as the Psalmist testifies, is seen and perceived in His watery works, like the face of the creator in a created mirror, polished with uncreated light. The reason, however, why the mundane regions and their things differ from one another, lies in the diversity of the watery garments, which differ from one another; in the mass of which the virtue of Jehovah has operated in diverse ways, both in creation and after creation: for this virtue or uncreated light, entering into the Empyrean spirit, puts on created light as a garment; Hence *Psalm 103 (or 104), 2: God is clothed with light...*

according to that [passage in] Wisdom 11: *You have mercy on all, because you can do all things, and you overlook the sins of men, that they may repent, etc.* But would anything have remained, had you not willed it? Indeed, some for this very reason made the Sun, and Moon, and stars into Gods for themselves; among whom I will also count the unhappy multitude of the Jews, who impiously and profanely rejecting and miserably despising their true and central, and precise and unique God, wanted to venerate and adore a superficial and non-essential fire, something originated and made rather than the origin and cause, and thus a creature rather than the creator; For in 2 Kings 21:3, he built altars to all the host of heaven; and *ibid.* 23:5, likewise those who adored Baal, and the Sun, and the Moon, and the Planets, finally the entire host of heaven: And so, led by an evil plague, they accepted the passive and unformed instead of the first active and supersubstantial form, a colored, visible, and created body instead of the invisible, eternal, and uncreated spirit, not paying attention to that command of Jehovah published through Moses in *Deuteronomy 4. a. 16. You shall not look upon the Sun, the Moon, or the stars, or any thing of the heavenly host, so as to bow down to them and worship them.* And certainly among other iniquities of idolatry, the abomination of the Gentiles, who passed their sons through fire, came closer to the truth; arguing by this very act that they recognized that the God whom they ought to adore dwells in the marrow and hidden depths of fire. But what need is there for them to adore a ray of God in fire, or the Sun, or any other created thing, when God, the fount of all things, and the Sun, giving grace, splendor, and glory both to spirit and to body, is in his entire essence in his super-essential kingdom, from which he pours forth the rays of life of all things through the Word into worldly creatures, by which they exist. Let us therefore venerate Jehovah in himself, and through himself, existing outside all things, and in all things; but let us consider visible creatures, in which life exists as it were, to be viler than ourselves, inasmuch as we are made in the exact image of our creator: Let us worship, I say, God, or the Word hidden in humid nature and its compositions, and commanding all things outside all things, and let us contemplate and admire nature itself, as the effect of that adorable Word, to whom be praise, honor, and glory forever.

C H A P. VII.

*How the entire mass of created waters is distinguished into three heavens by means of the Word.*

[Large initial N]UMBER to the number of spiritual days, namely between the creation of light and earth (in which God worked in the world to divide it into distinct regions), the very number of those heavens, or regions, corresponds: But in three days, or three apparitions of the Spirit, the entire humid spirit was created; Therefore, that entire spirit is divided into three heavens; among which the work of the first day is more worthy than the work of the second; and finally, that work of the second day is more worthy than the work of the third day. Saint Paul makes mention of this number and dignity, when he confesses that *he was caught up in the spirit to the third heaven, where he saw wondrous and inexpressible things.*

--- Page 625 ---
DE PRIMAR. NATUR. ELEMENT. 127

These heavens indeed, we have said, were created according to the pattern of the character of the name Tetragrammaton; in which name we have proved that He (ה), being closer to Jod (י), as the fount of perfection, is the type or image of the supreme and more dignified heaven due to its proximity to unity: So also we see that the more an object approaches fire, the more effectively fire acts upon it; and consequently, it more freely bestows its gift of perfection upon it; Jod therefore, beyond all things, wonderfully illuminated and blessed the Empyrean heaven with its glory on the first day; in which a simple composition was made, constituting Jah (יה): Afterwards, on the second day or illumination, the middle or ethereal heaven was formed after the example of Vau (ו), in which there is a middle composition, namely from Jah (יה) and Vau (ו); which is YHV (יהו) or the seal of natural life, and is called the composition of the middle order; because there is a double He (ה) there, namely He (ה) in Jah (יה), and another He (ה) or spirit hidden under the rays of the unity of Vau (ו); since He (ה) is five and Vau (ו) is six: Hence, just as Jah (יה), the first composition, is in the number ten (for it behaves as 10), so YHV (יהו) is in the number one hundred; indeed, where a double He (ה) stands for a double cipher, and the unity above He (ה) five in Vau (ו) for Jod (י); in this way 100. Hence this composition is square, inasmuch as its root is 10, or superficial, because its line is Jah (יה).

Furthermore, the last He (ה) is the icon of the lowest heaven, which is the ultimate mundane composition compacted from material elements, so that YHVH (יהוה) with Jod (י) make the number one thousand, as 1000, which is the cube of the square 100, or the body of the surface YHV (יהו); this is the complete perfection of the world in the likeness of the complete name Jehovah (יהוה).

Hence it is manifest that there are three heavens, and that the supreme heaven is more dignified than the lower, inasmuch as it is called the seat and place of Jehovah due to its dignity: Indeed, wherever Jehovah is, whether in heaven as far as we are concerned, or in the free air, or in the waters, or on earth, there also are all these heavens, and He Himself usually dwells in the more dignified one; Although this may seem ridiculous to some, it is nevertheless demonstrated by the sacred scriptures that the matter is so: For in Proverbs 8:28, Heaven and the upper clouds are said to be strengthened from above; And in Psalm 89:7, Who among the sons of God is compared to Jehovah in the upper cloud; Hence it is clear that, wherever Jehovah appears to men, He speaks from the midst of such a heaven; as can also be seen from the vision of Ezekiel chapter 1; Likewise Isaiah 6:a.1 and elsewhere: Moses also speaks of the multitude of heavens in Deuteronomy 10:4, The heavens of heavens are the God of gods; Where he understands that Empyrean, from whose center the glory of Jehovah usually shines forth, and the Word is poured out: And this is that house of God, of which words are made in Psalm 104:3, whose curtain, as it were, is the second heaven, or the firmament. Nehemiah 9:6 speaks of these supreme heavens in these words; Jehovah made the heavens of heavens, and all their host: Furthermore, the Psalmist also says; God sits upon the heaven of ancient heavens; that is, His place is that first and most ancient region of the heavens, which was manifested in the world on the first day, with the appearance of Jod, and in which God placed His first dwelling in this world: The second heaven is that transparent one, which is called the firmament, or expanse, or stretched-out air, separating the supreme from the dark cloud, or the lowest, as Moses testifies; where also in the solar center the divine Word established its more than royal palace: For by this Word also the heavens were established, Psalm 33:6, inasmuch as, under the name of wisdom, it was present at the structure of the heavens, as a foster-child arranging all things, Proverbs 8:27. That also that elemental space existing below the Moon is called heaven, the sacred scripture teaches us; as in Genesis 1:30, The birds of the heaven etc. And Deuteronomy 11:27, Jehovah will shut up the heavens, so that there be no rain etc. where heaven is taken for the air, and the whole transparent space. By these things we are taught that the diversity of the heavens consists in the diversity of the cloud, and that individual heavens are as it were clouds, differing from each other in density or subtlety, which are suspended in this world in a higher or lower place by the admirable power of the Word: For admirable is the bond of things from the divine Word, by which each of them, according to its dignity or merit, is elevated or suppressed in a higher or lower place.

That each heaven is a cloud, moved hither and thither by the breath of the fiery Spirit at the divine will, we are taught by these passages of the holy Bible: Proverbs 8:28, Heaven strengthened from above by the upper clouds. And Psalm 89:7, Heaven is called the upper cloud; And Psalm 104:3, The upper heavens are covered with waters by God: But subtle waters are nothing other than vapor or cloud; and subtle clouds are nothing other than spirit: Indeed, clouds are that curtain of the house of God alleged before; according to that also Psalm 105:39, God spread a cloud for a covering; And Exodus 40:34, The cloud covered the tent of meeting; And dense clouds are the vehicle of God or His chariot, who rides upon the wings of the wind, Psalm 104.

It must therefore be understood that, just as there are certain dense and perceptible clouds, so there are also subtle and imperceptible clouds, most full of the invisible light of eternity; indeed, the subtle is dense, and again the dense is subtle; and this by the Word contracting or expanding those things, or by the power of uncreated light which acts both in the visible and invisible spirit.

We therefore see here the reason how the waters, by emanation from Jod, are distinguished and divided into different regions, which are called heavens; It also appears that these heavens are nothing other than gross or subtle clouds, sustained in the vast world by the wings of winds emanating from the treasures of Jehovah. We can also observe that a greater or lesser act of light is the cause both of imperfection and perfection, both of density and tenuity, both of visible things, than

CHAP. I.

*That the primary principles of the Microcosm are the same as those of the Macrocosm: Concerning the spherical*
*letters constituting the ineffable Tetragrammaton; And that they are not common*
*and dead; but fiery and living. What the influences of the hidden*
*world are like.*

[Large decorative initial 'V' containing a landscape with a figure and a building]
JUST as in the description of the origin of the Macrocosm (brought forth by us above) we explained
in very few, but clear words, that its primary principles were round or spherical letters (which we called
perfect on account of their perfection); so also the same are the supersubstantial foundations of the
essence and existence of the Microcosm; since it is an image of the world, just as the world itself is
called an icon or exemplar of the Archetype itself; inasmuch as it is a most polished mirror, in which
the most beautiful and most sacred image of the Tetragrammaton is beheld. Hence it comes to pass,
therefore, that both these structures are called sons of the Tetragrammaton; inasmuch as they not only
derive their paternal origin from it, but also bear its truest likeness; inasmuch as by the virtue of His Word,
or the uncreated seal, in which the Divine Majesty is imprinted, they receive the impression of life and being,
and exist as myrothecia or sanctuaries, in which that supersubstantial treasure is hidden as in a most prepared ark,
and is secluded and separated from the abyss of darkness or hyle,
and finally the universal created mass is illuminated, actualized, vivified by the splendor of His presence,
and preserved to its ultimate end. These letters, therefore, containing within themselves the infinite virtue of the Tetragrammaton,
constitute that unique and true ineffable name of God, by which all things, both of the Macrocosm and the Microcosm,
were delineated in the ideal or Archetypal world before creation. Nor indeed is it to be believed
that these letters are of the same essence or nature as those common Hebrew letters depicted by ink
or human sculpture (which are indeed truly dead and fictitious:) but those letters were the same as those
brought forth in the beginning from the dark hyle, and expressed by golden characters, or compacted from the purest
fire, by whose presence, effect, and motion the word immediately emanated from the Archetype into the spherical
structure; by whose act, as the Psalmist testifies, the heavens were established, and the spirit full of fiery love
was carried over the waters, by whose influence all virtues and especially souls were first infused into the world, and then
into its creatures: Of such great importance, I say, and of such great efficacy were these formal or fiery
and spherical letters of the first order, י Jod ה He ו Vau, as being of a nature remote from those
common and accidental letters produced by human invention for public use; in which no force,
no virtue is inherent, except inasmuch as they are, as it were, marks or characters of art, by which the intention
of one person may be understood by another. And yet nevertheless, so great is the ignorance of common men,
so extreme their blindness, that they are willing to admit no letters other than these fictitious and dead ones alone,
being entirely ignorant that spiritual letters (as the Apostle testifies) are written in the interior and more central
parts of the creature itself, by whose impressions the Word comes forth, in which, according to St. John, is the life
of every

...nature. Therefore, that divine name was not trivial or accidental, concerning which, when Moses asked what it was, God himself responded, i. h. u. h., that is, YHWH, "this is my name forever, and this is my memorial from generation to generation." Therefore, the Tetragrammaton is the name of eternity: and consequently, the letters constituting it are living, perpetual, and not fictitious or accidental, which possess neither life nor duration in themselves; since the Word consists in these primordial and purely fiery letters, not even a single jot of which will ever fall to the earth, but will remain forever. These letters, therefore, are principles, solely spherical, original, and as it were the true Fathers of both worlds, applied to the most holy Trinity; with י Jod rightly attributed to the Father, ה to the Son, and ו to the Holy Spirit, that is, by nature and property. Indeed, these persons, existing before the existence of the world, inasmuch as each of them moved according to its peculiar office for the completion of its mechanism, I have not ineptly called Fathers in the preceding [text]; inasmuch as they acted upon the Mothers א Aleph, מ Mem, ש Shin for the production of Darkness or earth, Water, and Light: so that it is not impertinent to consider that, just as we see in the world Angels acting upon stars, and stars upon elements, and these upon creatures, so also the Fathers act upon the mothers, and the mothers upon their elements, and the elements upon meteors, by whose aid composite natural bodies are moved both to generation and led to corruption. And this was the intention of the more occult philosophers, who supposed a certain invisible Zodiac, which made its influences upon the visible Zodiac, and this again upon the Planets, by which they asserted fate was dispensed to inferiors, and all things governed. This was also the intention of the Cabalists in their inverted tree of 10 Sephiroth, whose root was Eheieh presiding, Cheter or the crown, and the summit tending downwards, Adonai, beneath which is Malchath or the kingdom. And by these, the degrees, numerations, and dimensions by which God variously operates in this world seem to become known; concerning which we will speak clearly below.

**C A P. II.**

**On the number and measure of the Tetragrammaton, by which both the Macrocosm and Microcosm are numbered and measured.**

In our book on divine numbers, we explained the reason why the world is divided into 27 parts; namely, for the production of the Cube from the most exact and perfect root of the number 3, embracing the most holy Trinity; whose square was 9, and consequently makes a Cube of 27, that is, three times 9. Or, as the Platonists explain, 9 9 9, in which they include so many mysteries: An exact demonstration of which can be seen in Treatise 1, Section 1, Book 1, and Chapter 12 of the Microcosmic History. Therefore, we will here elucidate the mystery of this number, and in this way deduce its reason from primordial foundations. We see, namely, first of all, that the ineffable name consists of three fiery and formal letters; inasmuch as they include the source of all light, 1, 2, 3, which are only spherical, and therefore superexcellent, most eminent, and constitute the primary and simplest number of perfection, namely 3. And hence it is that the Cabalists wish this to be that unique name revolving the universe and connecting all things; namely, the highest with the highest and the lowest with the lowest, and the highest with the lowest and the lowest with the highest: so much so that from this we find that the aforesaid cubic number 27 is the numeration of that dimension to which the world's semidiameter, measured from the circumference to the center, is adapted. For, if we look at the Hebrew numbers, which are explained solely by letters, we will perceive that cubic number to result from the value of the letters of the Tetragrammaton name. For ה He (5), and ה (5), and י Jod (10), and ו Vau (6) constitute 26. And א Aleph, which is always the root of the number ten, or unity, and is never separated from God, constitutes 27. Hence, therefore, it is that God is called Alpha and Omega, the Beginning and the End: for He who is the beginning of the world is also its end: Wherefore it is also right to observe that God began His work with the small א or unity, and finished it with the great א, which signifies the number a thousand. And this is the reason why, in the sublunar region, the number a thousand is found in our pyramidal demonstration; and this not ineptly, inasmuch as it is the cube of the number ten. From these things, therefore, it is quite clear that the entire name Tetragrammaton is nothing other than א Aleph; and everything that exists is included by Aleph or God, who is YHWH; Which name is again Aleph, or the measure between the principal and final Aleph. Whence it is evidently proven that everything that exists, and every Being, is God Aleph Himself; who is light and darkness; namely, darkness when hidden in prime matter, and light when manifesting Himself: And this is the reason why Aleph is called by the Cabalists dark and luminous, as is clearly explained in the preceding [text]. By these things it is also clearly declared that God is whole through whole, and only that which is from the circumference of the machine to the point of the center; that is, within and without everything that is created: Whence in Deut. 10: "Behold, O Lord, yours is heaven, and the heaven of heavens." And in Isaiah 66: "Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool." But that He is in every-

But this is demonstrated even more clearly by this definition of Hermes Trismegistus, by which he declares the infinite and omnipotent existence of God: God, he says, is a circle whose center exists everywhere, and whose circumference nowhere. Which indeed is best represented by these two arithmetical notes 10, signifying ten, explained among the Hebrews by the letter י Jod, which is a hieroglyph of Jehovah itself, signifying the same in the denary number, or first article, as א Aleph is explained in unity: Of which notes, the former, signifying unity, is as it were an indivisible point, through whose whole the center is found: For there is no number in which unity is not found, inasmuch as all numbers originate from it, nor is number anything else than a connection or congregation of unities. Furthermore, also the cipher (which is the second note of the denary number) circumfer-

that the Sephirot are divine measures and numerations in the dimension of the world, which the Cabalists call the garments of divinity. Hence it is said in Psalm 104: *Clothed with light as with a garment.* These numerations are therefore diverse lights descending from one root, by whose favor all things are created and, once created, are nourished: Hence also by some they are taken for the days of creation, and are sometimes called by the Cabalists the Days of Bereshit, by whose diversity diverse works were made in creation, and these are continued and preserved from creation to the ultimate destruction.
