Of these ten numerations, three are called supreme by excellence; inasmuch as their seats are the highest, where sits *Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God of Sabaoth;* and they represent persons in the Trinity, and consequently are more principal; just as the remaining seven are less exalted in essence. And although a peculiar name of God is attributed to each Sephirot or numeration, yet it must be seriously understood that among those ten names, only one is truly appropriated to God: The other names, however, are taken from His works: That one unique name, namely the ineffable Tetragrammaton, primarily attributed to God, signifies the substance of the Creator with a pure meaning, in which there is no participation; but His other glorious names denote a thing with participation, inasmuch as they are derived from actions, or works, which have been found: Thus, for example, the surname of God, Adonai, is taken from this name Adon, which is Lord: Thus it is said; the man, the Lord of the earth, spoke.

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Adonai, however, is said (as Rabbi Moses Aegyptius relates) for the sake of glory and honor: And thus Abraham spoke to the angel; *Adonai, if I have found favor, etc.* Adonai, therefore, is an epithet of the Creator: but all other names, such as Judge, Just, Gracious, Pious, Eloi, etc., proceed from His works. Of the three principal ones, the first is, as it were, the root of the entire Sephirotic tree, and is called by the Cabalists כתר, Cheter, which among Latins is called Corona (Crown): This Crown is hieroglyphically signified by the letter ש Shin; inasmuch as it is crowned with three eminences, and is a symbol of the Trinity. Furthermore, the crown is also indicated by the character of the cipher 0, which we compared above with the circumference of God, which is nowhere; inasmuch as it is infinite, and consequently outside all things; and whose center is 1, found throughout; so that when these are joined together, they form the number ten, comprehending all things: And certainly, if we contemplate the order of the world's creation, we will find the cipher 0 to be a type of the universal formless and infinite matter, which Hyle was, the dwelling of God not appearing to the world: but truly, when through 1 He appeared in the world, 0 from nothing became something of moment: For the appearance of the central unity reduced the darkness, filling the concavity of the already created world into the form of waters: Hence it was said, *And the Spirit of the Lord moved upon the waters:* which before were darkness, or the abyss, whose face darkness had covered. And thus this crown of God is eternally lucid; for to it, as the Psalmist testifies, *darkness is as light, and night as day:* but truly, what was formless and overwhelmed by darkness to creatures is now adorned with sensible beauty, and from nothing, as far as human sense is concerned, is brought into being by the appearance of unity, reducing that nothing into a quantity or denary dimension: And from this infinite crown flowed the first emanation into the formless shadows, by which they were reformed: Thus the Messiah or the virtue of the Tetragrammaton was produced into the formless world, by whose presence the heavens were established: Thus the fiery Spirit flowed into the bosom of the mass of darkness, by whose virtue the waters are now revealed, and the divine Majesty of humid nature is unveiled: Thus the royal Psalmist rightly said; *By the word of the Lord,* that is, by the virtue of the Tetragrammaton, *the heavens were established, and by the breath of His mouth all their host.*

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;This Cheter or Crown, therefore, is called by the Cabalists the root of the entire Sephirotic tree, which consists of the number ten, denoting the effect of the character י Yod, which is 10, in which the name Tetragrammaton consists; so that this single letter Yod sounds the same as the Tetragrammaton. Therefore the Crown, or Cheter, or the root of the divine tree in the world is the same as Yod; and again Yod is the same as 10; and finally 10 denotes unity or the fount of light looking forth from its dark dwelling into the formless world 0, by whose presence 0 from nothing becomes a whole in full actuality. And hence it is that to this first Sephirot, Cheter or Crown, that name of God is attributed which has the closest relation to the divine essence, and denotes the Father among the persons of the most holy Trinity, from whom the Son and the Holy Spirit are derived: Wherefore it also seems to denote the three times of eternity, and the plurality of persons with the unity of nature, inasmuch as, where the Father is, there the Son is presupposed to be; and w-

For Ehieh is the future tense of the verb Hajah, 'to be' (Sum), denoting according to the interpretations of the Talmudists the eternity of God; for through the future tense it argues the present and the past: Indeed, these three differences of times are reduced to the divinity, which is not comprehended, Psalm. 90. Therefore, the office of this part of the Sephirotic tree is to flow through the orders of the Seraphim into the primum mobile, and from that to all things, to which it gives being: For in this place it must be observed that just as in creation three heavens were made or fabricated, one after another, so also there is a threefold reception of influences before they can operate an effect in the lower realms; namely from the Sephiroth of divine unity, and from those to the spheres of the middle heaven, and then afterwards from the elements, which immediately rain down or infuse them into bodies adapted to them: Although, as it seems to me (against the opinions of some Cabalists who place the influences of this radical Sephiroth into the primum mobile), Ehieh, having pre-eminence in the numeration of Cheter, inasmuch as it refers to the divine essence, gives powers and authority from its own office to the trunk and branches of its tree, so that from them influences may finally be sent down and infused into the lower realms, as God's will and the necessity of his creatures require; no less than the virtue of the root of some tree communicates virtue to the trunk, and the trunk to its branches, and the branches to the fruit and leaves: which afterwards usually nourish creatures: Yet the immediate reason for nourishment is not attributed to the root of the tree, but to the fruit or leaves, although it is certain that the same nutritive virtue proceeds originally from the root, inasmuch as without it the tree and its fruit cannot subsist. And indeed, if we inspect a little more accurately the nature of the name Ehieh, which presides over the root of the tree, we will find that it differs in no way in essence from the ineffable name יהוה Jehovah, to which the trunk of the Sephirotic tree is attributed: For, just as God before any creation was א Aleph or unity, so also at the point of creation, he moved from א to י Jod or the pure denary, where unity is joined with a cipher. Whence, just as Jod 10 proceeded from א Aleph unity, so also the divine essence moved from the root, over which Ehieh presides, to the trunk, over which Jehovah predominates. Therefore, in the Tetragrammaton name Jehovah is the universal power of the Crown Ehieh, no differently than in the trunk of a tree is the virtue of the root: And the efficacy of Jehovah also passes into the lower names, just as the nourishment of the trunk penetrates into the branches and leaves, by which animals are finally nourished and refreshed: From Ehieh, therefore, all intelligences in the hierarchies rejoice, the father, namely, moving them: Which intelligences, being moved, also move the spheres and celestial bodies over which they preside: And this is the reason why God is called by Hermes Trismegistus a circle, whose center was everywhere, and circumference nowhere, as was said above. From these things, unless I am mistaken, it is clear that the proper office of Ehieh is universal, and by no means so particular as some have wished to make it; for if it were, then the lowest Numeration Malchuth would not flow into the Moon, which is the common receptacle of all superior influences, but would have a lower place for its receptacle; which indeed, as it seems to me, would be irregular.

Moreover, since all things were made by wisdom, which was present with Ehieh as a helper, composing all things with its right hand (as Solomon says), and since that Word and virtue of the Tetragrammaton Ehieh, or the Messiah, and the universal emanation flowed from that luminous source, in which was life alone and light, by whose virtue the heavens were established, so that he himself existed as the soul or Metatron for the whole world, it seems probable that the immediate influx into the primum mobile is from him who holds the name of Jehovah impressed in himself, so that from him afterwards it may rain down into the lower world to all things to which it gives being. This therefore is that ineffable and sacrosanct name presiding over the second Sephiroth, which is assimilated to the trunk of the tree: And this Sephiroth or numeration of the second order is called חכמה Hochma, that is, Wisdom; to which indeed the first generation is referred, inasmuch as it immediately succeeds Cheter, over which Ehieh presides, related to the Father: Similarly, the primitive law, inasmuch as wisdom was first with the father, and was sent forth, as a primary and constant law, by which the world was fabricated from the beginning according to that of the Royal Prophet, Psalm. 136. The fabric of the heavens by the Word, or as the Wise Man wills, Proverb. 3. 19. God established the heavens with Wisdom. To this also is attributed Being, inasmuch as, according to the witness of Ecclesiasticus 1, wisdom was created first of all Beings, and was the Being of Beings, inasmuch as all things were made by it, and without it nothing, according to St. John 1. Whence it is also written, that nothing is the most ancient principle except wisdom alone. For Ehieh by itself was infinity, when it was withdrawn into the abyss of darkness, and as it were idle, or (as they say) looking to nothing: and therefore it is called among the Hebrews אין Ein, that is, Nothing, or non-Being and no end; because we, afflicted with such slender poverty of intellect in divine matters, judge concerning those things which do not appear no differently than concerning those things which do not exist.

The Messiah, or the Virtue of the Tetragrammaton; which is diffused everywhere from the mouth of Jehovah through the world, by which the world is animated, and its creatures enjoy life, namely by the virtue of the name of Jehovah: For (as Archangel rightly says in the Cabalistic dogma) this name is unique, encompassing the universe and connecting all things, namely the highest with the highest, and the lowest with the lowest, and the lowest with the highest. But now we shall descend to the third Sephiroth, whose name in Hebrew is Binah (בינה); which in Latin signifies Prudence or understanding, and is the lowest Sephiroth of the three superior or Principal ones; wherefore it is attributed to the Holy Spirit. And this is the reason why the name Elohim (אלהים) is attributed to this numeration, which is most properly assigned to the Holy Spirit among the holy persons. Hence, inasmuch as it is here the common bond of the preceding persons to unity, by some Elohim is rendered by interpretation as "Gods," making a

Whereby, through the imposition of names upon the stars, the attribution of virtues is understood; because each of them received a name according to its nature and property: For by this sign Adam gave names to the beasts of the field and to the birds of the sky, etc., as is read in Genesis. And this is the last of the three Sephiroth of the higher degree, which show the traces of the Trinity; by which indeed all virtues are finally infused abundantly and liberally, first from the Zodiac to the Planets, and then from them to all inferior things. This is therefore the reason why the Planets have the power of the signs of the Zodiac and of the other fixed stars situated outside the Zodiac. Thus we say that Saturn has the nature of Capricorn within the Zodiac; but of the belly and tail of Cetus, and of the beak of Corvus outside; Jupiter, the nature of Pisces within the Zodiac, and outside, of the bright Hydra, and so for the rest. The seventh Sephiroth is called Netzach (נצח), Triumph, Victory; And the name ruling this is Jehovah Sabaoth, God of hosts. This numeration projects and pours out its influences through the orders of Virtues into the sphere of the Sun: From which it is filled and abundantly overflows with vital power, which it liberally pours down into the lower things: And its angel Michael or Metatron is the leader of the army of God, who triumphed and had victory in spiritual battle over the prince of darkness. The eighth numeration is called Hod (הוד), that is, Honor, Beauty. Its divine name is Elohim Sabaoth (צבאות אלהים), God of hosts, not for war and vigor, but for piety and concord: Its influence indeed occurs through the order of Principalities into the sphere of Venus. The ninth is called Yesod (יסוד), that is, basis, foundation, redemption, rest; Its name is El Chai (אל חי), Living God, or Shaddai (שדי), Omnipotent, or rather, He who is sufficient unto Himself, without any external thing. Its influence, moreover, is through the Order of Archangels into the sphere of Mercury: For through a messenger or Archangel, peace was announced to the earth. The tenth and last Sephiroth is called Malkuth (מלכות), Kingdom, dominion, Temple of God. Its name is Adonai (אדני), Lord; and it sends its influences through the order of Angels into the sphere of the Moon. And this, in that part, is our opinion, namely that I defend the opinion of the Cabalist Archangel in his Commentary on the Dogmas of the Cabalists, who absolutely posited the influences of Malkuth through the order of Angels into the region of the Moon; although Reuchlin himself, and some others, say that the influences of Malkuth pass through the order of blessed souls into rational creatures. Nor certainly can we entirely repudiate their opinions, who make 10 spheres or orders of the Empyrean heaven. But we have only made progress in the number nine, and according to its measure, we have treated of the Sephiroth. According to their opinion, therefore, Keter, or the first Sephiroth, flows through the orders of Seraphim into the primum mobile, and from that to all lower things, to which it gives being. Indeed, I will by no means contradict this opinion of theirs, considering that, just as the divine name Ehieh, related to the divine essence, represents the first person of the Trinity, namely the Father, and consequently claims for itself the first act in the superior and supernatural world; so also the primum mobile behaves in the natural world, inasmuch as it is, as it were, the father and immediate origin of the motion of all lower spheres. But indeed, because the Word or Wisdom, namely Chokhmah, was the first mover in the world, therefore I said that its influences were adapted to the primum mobile: But both are granted, and neither will be denied by me. Chokhmah, the second Numeration, they say, flows through the Cherubim into the eighth or starry sphere. Nor will this also be entirely denied by me, inasmuch as the Zodiac of this starry heaven is said to derive from Zoon, that is, animal. But in the Word was life, which it pours into that girdle of life, so that from there, by means of the Planets, it may be carried down and showered upon lower things. Nevertheless, our opinion does not seem to differ much from the truth, wishing that Binah, or the Sephiroth attributed to the Holy Spirit, may pour its influences into this sphere. They also say that the third Sephiroth, Binah, flows through the order of Thrones into the sphere of Saturn: Whence they call Binah the supramundane Saturn of the intelligible world, thereby noting repentance and the remission of sins, which occurred at the end of the multiplication of the square of the number seven: Thus also will the great Jubilee be drawn forth from the Jubilees of the future age. Afterwards, in the fourth place, they wish that the numeration Chesed may shower down through the order of Dominations into the sphere of Jupiter; And inasmuch as he is a friend of the human race and of the life of things, we willingly admit that he has his influences from Chesed or the supercelestial Jupiter, or Chesed (חסד), always denoting Clemency, grace, and mercy for the life of things. They also say that Geburah, the fifth Sephiroth, flows through the order of Powers into the sphere of Mars: Nor indeed do I say that I entirely deny this; inasmuch as Geburah, the superior and spiritual Mars, is power, severity, judgment, and punishment; of which condition likewise is the celestial Mars, inasmuch as he threatens wars, desolations, and plundering. They make the influences of Tiphereth, the sixth numeration, penetrate through the order of Virtues into the sphere of the Sun, attributing to it clarity, light, and life, which descend from the sphere of the Sun to produce all minerals, among which gold is the head, and as the Sun among celestial bodies, bread and wine among vegetables, and man among animals. Nor indeed do I think this deviates much from the truth, inasmuch as Tiphereth denotes grace, beauty, and adornment; all of which are observed to exist in the Sun in abundance. In the seventh order, it can be that Netzach flows through the order of Principalities into the sphere of Venus: And those influences descending from Venus produce the love of justice, and finally bring forth in the elemental world trees, plants, herbs, and other vegetables: In the eighth place, that Hod sends its influences through Archangels to the sphere of Mercury, which afterwards descending produces animals: Afterwards, that Yesod of the ninth series pours out its flows through the sieve of the order of Angels into the sphere of the Moon; from whose region thereafter the increase and decrease of things descends: And in the last disposition of the Sephiroth, that Malkuth flows through the order of blessed souls into rational creatures, bestowing the knowledge of things, science, and industry: Let it be supposed, I say, that all these things are granted as certain, if only the sphere of blessed souls (as some Theologians assert) is included in the Empyrean heaven; nevertheless, if our reasoning is well considered, which is concerning the measure of the number nine, you will perceive that the greatest force, and no small probability, is present in my order of the

**CHAPTER VII.**
*Still concerning the origin of the 10 heavens, and concerning divine ideas; Afterwards, concerning the particular Sephiroth or numerations of Man, and how they relate to the mundane ones?*

**A**braham the Cabalist says in the book Ietzira; *There are ten numerations or Sephiroth belimai, besides why ten and not nine, ten and not eleven; understand with wisdom, be wise with intellect:* Where, taking the name Sephiroth generally for that which extends into the Macrocosm and Microcosm, it denotes that the parts of the quaternary number aggregated together produce 10 and not 9, and again 10 and not 11. For

from darkness and deceptions to light and truth; this is what the Sages said, "*make the hidden manifest, and the manifest hidden*," that is, reduce darkness and light, each of them, namely, into its own proper nature. But these Sephirotic Ideas are pure, formal, and most abstruse things; and yet, because they are said to be created, therefore they are as if composite; since their being and existence differ in this, that their being is as it were their matter and origin, which is the purest created Spirit; but their essence is like a form drawn out from the potentiality of matter. But God alone is, in whom being and essence are the same: But the third person is that one which unites form with matter by a wonderful bond and glue; And this is that person who composes and makes the union, according to that saying of the Sage; "*By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and by the Spirit from His mouth all their power*." From these things therefore it is possible to see that these 10 ideal Sephiroth are in respect to their influences both in Man and in the World, and that especially in the book Ietzirah they are understood concerning man. Whence it says; "*Ten are the enumerations of the Sephiroth of Belimai, etc. Be wise with understanding, and understand with wisdom*." For to be wise is to conceive things by any argument of the senses: Whence it is clear that sense is an inferior Sephiroth of man, and that intellect, to which Binah, that is, intelligence, or the third Sephiroth, is attributed, is one of the highest Sephiroth of man, and that Wisdom, which is referred to Hochma, is the second Sephiroth, inasmuch as it is the mind itself or e-

      From these things, therefore, it is quite clearly established how superior things act spiritually upon inferior things, both in man and in the world: For El acts from the Chesed of Reason through the order of Dominations into the sphere of Jupiter, that is, into the nature of human life, which is in the middle region of the Microcosm: just as Ehieh, the first Mind, or the obscure Aleph, or the Father, acts through Seraphim, that is, by divine love into the will, which is the first mover of the Microcosm, from Keter, that is, from the seat of His unity: Similarly, YHVH, the second Mind, infuses its power into Hochmah through Cherubim, that is, the multitude of wisdom and knowledge, into the sphere of life and its Zodiacal circle, which is therefore called Zodiac from *zoon*, that is, Animal; inasmuch as it is the origin of life, constantly infusing its rays and influences into the Planets: Hence it is said that in Wisdom or the Word there is life: And this sphere is the source of natural action, just as the Mind is the source of supernatural action; hence it is called Action: Therefore, the mind of man, which is compared to the Word and Wisdom, carries with it the virtue of this; which, inasmuch as it is that breath of life infused into man by the first Mind or inspirer, therefore Yah, which is also a divine name of clemency and mercy, is adapted to it.
      Furthermore, the influx of Intellect, or the third Sephiroth, is also into the sphere of Saturn: Hence, melancholics are said to be more intelligent and prudent than others; and from this, the soul has its receptive power. But, to descend now to the fifth Sephiroth, which is Memory, this is like a storehouse and as it were a center of the other Sephiroth, in which all forms of impressions, both those ascending from Malchut or the will through the senses, and those descending from God and the Mind, are retained as in a sanctuary: For it is the image of the law, which must be held and observed, lest punishment follow: Hence to this is attributed Geburah, which denotes power, force, punishment. The name of God presiding over this is Elohim, by which all things were created and preserved in the world, just as all things produced by intellect and sense are preserved and continued in Memory and, as it were, imprinted like a seal on wax: Thus also the Mind impressed form not only on men, but also on all creatures of the world with its seal Emeth, that is, Truth. Its influxes occur through the order of Powers into the spheres of Saturn and Mars, which have retentive power: But, because cold is the occasion of oblivion, therefore its influxes fall into the sphere of Mars, which also denotes severity towards violators and contemptors of laws.
      The cogitative or estimative faculty possesses the sixth branch, in which are beauty and loveliness and the delights of thinking about those things in the middle, which are presented to the eyes of thought in the human heaven and its earth: Hence the origin of rapture and ecstasy; hence pleasant meditations and bodily delights, if we consider the external things of man or the pleasures of the flesh; hence the beauty of the mind and the pleasantness of its diverse aspects are contemplated, if thought adheres to it: Therefore, thought reigns in the middle of this Sephirothic tree, like the Sun in the world, which looks upon both superior and inferior things with the same eye, and rises upon the good and the bad: For thus thought also occupies itself with both good and evil; and yet both seem beautiful to it, unless there is violence and passion in the thinking soul: Hence this cogitative faculty is the plant Tiphereth in this human tree, over which presides the name Tetragrammaton, and it is as it were the trunk of the whole tree, because it extends from the mind to the ultimate plant of the will: Its flow, however, passes through the order of virtues, that is, through the four Cardinal virtues, although sometimes, led by false reason, it is accustomed to hold or esteem vices as virtues. Indeed, with the natures, influxes, and properties of these Sephiroth well considered, along with the condition of the spheres into which they flow, it will not be so difficult, as it seems to me, to discourse about the source of souls, that is, the kingdom and seat which souls originally possess, and from which, as from their own homeland, they descend into bodies. Various authors have written in various ways concerning the true origin or source of souls. For the Hebrews, from their most recondite secrets, assert that the soul proceeds from the great four-letter name of God, יהוה Jehovah: Which opinion we indeed supported with the strongest arguments in the preceding Section; where we demonstrated that the virtue of the Tetragrammaton is the soul and life of the universal world and of every creature. Furthermore, we also say that the soul of man proceeds from the virtue of the name presiding over the second Sephirah, namely Jehovah and יהוה, inasmuch as, according to St. John, *in the Word was life, and that life was the light of men:* And this Word in Genesis is called *the breath of life.* Others think that the human soul flowed from the Trinity, and especially from the Holy Spirit, as to its essence, and that it then migrated downwards into Geburah.

...will participate; Finally, if it migrates through the seventh orb or region of Virtues, it will embrace reason, and the virtue of Ehieh will illuminate it with enlightenment and miracles: For, just as we see that the power of vision of the eye usually takes on the property or color of the transparent medium, whether it be uniform and red, or saffron-colored and yellow water, or blue, like the sky and sapphire, to which it is exposed, so also in the same way, influences or created sparks of souls emanating from the source of uncreated light take on the nature of the medium through which they pass: For from the orders of Angels, souls take on the condition of intellectual reason; And the Mind is always the supreme portion of the human soul, which in its descent puts on many garments with their qualities, as is more broadly explained in Tract 1, Section 1, Book 4, Chapters 3 & 4 of the Physical History of the Microcosm, both by reasons and demonstrations: In the middle heaven, it seizes for itself the necessary disposition for life. Hence, the soul flowing from Cheter through the Seraphim into the primum mobile, renders the native (person) of strong will and constant opinion in its Seraphic condition; through the Dominations into Jupiter, it makes natural virtue good; and will give exaltation to its body, and likewise will bestow powers of acting and practicing; If it glides through the Virtues into Venus, it strengthens the concupiscible power, gives the motion of desire, makes the well-disposed soul cheerful, delighting in society and music.

Furthermore, if the soul is infused from the property of the second person, namely יה in Hochmah, through ב, that is, the Cherubic intelligences; it will acquire for itself the splendor of knowledge, and its intention (even if enclosed in an opaque body) will for the most part be exalted into that region; wisdom, therefore, will rejoice through immediate passage into this medium: If through ג, that is, through the Principalities, it will be powerful in reason, and will surpass and excel others in morals and reverence for superiors. As for the portion of life, it will be varied according to the variety of temperaments of the real houses of Mars or Mercury, through whose sieves this soul flows: For passing through the order of Cherubim into the eighth sphere, it will render the vital soul agile and active; through the order of Principalities into Mars, it will have increased irascible power, and denotes ardor of animosity in war: But if through the order of Archangels (from which the supreme soul seizes strong imagination for itself) it glides downwards into the sphere of Mercury, it will enjoy a sound imaginative power, and will be adorned with sharpness of intellect and love of sciences, and at the same time will find there the vigor of interpreting, pronouncing, and penetrating. And here it must be noted that the Son or Wisdom acts by the ordination of the Father through the Spirit. Finally, the Holy Spirit Elohim emits from Binah its own human sparks either through the order of Thrones (which indeed there put on the spirit of justice and judgment, and descend from it into the ethereal region into the sphere of Saturn, in which they acquire gravity, constancy, and prudence as regards morality, and receptive and retentive power as regards physical disposition) or through the Powers, where they also seize a portion of its condition; namely, fortitude for overcoming malignant spirits in spiritual combat; and then they pass into the royal tabernacle of the Sun, in which they obtain fullness of life, the imagination of knowing, and the nature of opining, as well as animosity, inasmuch as its angel Michael obtained victory against the Prince of darkness, and Apollo against Python; and consequently also renders the soul strong and spirited in bodily combat, just as the nature of Mars makes its soul audacious: Finally, passing through the choir of angels, they find obedience and good sense there; with these endowments, they descend into the sphere of the Moon, where they acquire generative and vegetative power, and thus the faculty of both decreasing and increasing: And finally, with these natures, they tend downwards into the aerial nature, as into their ultimate course; and thus they penetrate into the body with its aerial covering, or rather into the sperm, which is almost nothing other than the ultimate diaphanous garment of the descending soul.

From these things, therefore, it seems quite clear that souls are observed to differ and diverge explicitly from each other, both by supernatural endowments, and by those which they had in the ideal series of the Sephiroth, and by these which they received in their descent from the orders of intelligences, as well as by the enjoyment of the celestial and natural world itself, by which the necessary aids of vital nature are bestowed upon them; and this according to the will of the Creator, according to that saying of the Apostle, "He, who remains the same, divides to each as He wills." Similarly, the fixed stars unite their powers with those of the Planets according to their triplicities; and continually pour their influences into the lower regions with the Planets: Hence, every sign of the Zodiac, whether by place of house, detriment, exaltation, triplicity, sex, or a part thereof, and likewise degrees, faces, terms, and such other things, are more proper to this Planet than to that, as has been clearly explained in our section on Astrology.

Furthermore, from these things, it can be understood that the visible Zodiac, or the gilded circle of the eighth sphere, everywhere interwoven with various stars, has its ideal and invisible Zodiac, passing through the center of the Sephirah Hochmah, whose king, governor, and prince is יה Jah, or the virtue of the Tetragrammaton, or the Word, or the Messiah, or the soul of the world, both ideal and real; ideal inasmuch as it gives a splendid soul to the invisible Zodiac; hence the Zodiac is named from life: This same sphere also pours secondary life into the visible Zodiac in the eighth heaven through the orders of Cherubim: Hence we find 12 animals, of the visible signs, formed here on earth by influences, which in nature and quality correspond with those...

are perceived to correspond, just as the celestial Aries with the terrestrial ram, Taurus with the bull, Gemini with the twins, Cancer with the crab, etc. And indeed, both Astrologers, and also some Philosophers and Christian Theologians have written wonderful things about the comparison of the superior or ideal Zodiac with the inferior one, and about the miraculous events which usually occur from their variation: This indeed must happen, inasmuch as the motion of that supercelestial one is slower than that of the celestial one. They say therefore that various effects are produced in the world due to the diverse operations of the parts of one Zodiac upon others, namely the invisible Zodiac upon the visible one; this indeed could not happen unless the motion of the superior differed from the motion of the inferior: For in the beginning of the world, the first degree of Aries in the invisible Zodiac surpassed that first degree of the visible Aries; and therefore, because of the harmony of influences, they said that that age was golden, inasmuch as in it the same element did not invade its like with contrary actions: And this is the reason why that age had its origin with Paradise: They assign this reason for that matter, that they observed the invisible Zodiac to have moved one degree and 28 minutes every 200 years, and consequently its revolution to be completed in 49,000 years. This period they called the Platonic year, as they said that when it was completed, all things would return to their original state. But leaving these things aside, we conclude that, just as Hochma flows from its invisible Zodiac into the visible Zodiac, so too the seven lower Sephiroth correspond to the seven Planets, and contain within themselves ideal and invisible Planetary spheres; each of which infuses its property into the real sphere and its visible star. And, just as vital virtue first flowed into the Planets from the Zodiac, before they themselves had any vital virtue; so also souls received their essential and intellectual being from the invisible Zodiac before they were clothed with the nature of the visible Zodiac. And, just as the influxes of vital virtue occur from the visible Zodiac into the Planets; so also souls are poured forth from Hochma into the lower Sephiroth through the orbs of intelligences, before they penetrate to the starry sphere; Hence it is said by the Cabalists that God infuses the soul, which passes through the superior Sun Tiphereth, and imbibes its influx, and clothes itself with that property of the Sun Tiphereth. Therefore, according to them, the superior Sun is the middle Sephiroth or dimension: And consequently, there are also invisible and ideal Planets, which are the seven lower ones from Hochma: For Malchut is attributed to the region of the lower world, as some wish. We conclude therefore that it is most certain that God, triune and one, is the infuser of souls first into His Sephiroth, and then through the orders of intelligences into the ethereal region, so that by means of visible stars they may be transported into lower things for the generation of humans: For God is the first agent, and consequently the first giver of forms; And therefore, inasmuch as He is the first act, it is necessary that He proceeds immediately from the first actor: From Him, therefore, flows all life, form, and order. Although, therefore, all souls emanate from a single source, which the Cabalists call the northern fountain of Geburah, we nevertheless derive the luminous fountain from the supernatural essence of the Lords of the three superior Sephiroth: They pass nevertheless through other dimensions or Sephirotic intermediaries before they glide down into the spheres, and from these into bodies or the spermatic mass; from which they receive various properties; Hence it happens that each soul receives that portion of light whose nature is the medium to which it is exposed, or with which it is accustomed to be joined, as is more clearly explained in the preceding [sections]. How, moreover, the human soul or Mind, which is a ray or spark of divinity itself, in its descent carries with it the natures of every sphere, both supercelestial, celestial, and animal, we have openly demonstrated, first in Tract 1, Sect. 1, Book 4, Chapters 3 & 4, "On the Physics of the Microcosm's History." And in Book 12 of the same, Chapter 4. And also in Tract 1, Sect. 2, Book 3, Chapters 1 & 7, "Of Microcosmic History." But now finally in the following chapter we will show that the trunk of the whole tree is that ineffable name Tetragrammaton, without which no soul can descend or exist.

CHAPTER IX.

That the ineffable name Tetragrammaton is the trunk of the Sephirotic tree, both of the Macrocosm and the Microcosm.

The Hebrews, as has been said above, from their most hidden mysteries, assertively say that the soul emanates from the great four-letter name of God, יהוה Jehovah, like infinite branches and leaves from the trunk of a tree; from which all other names of God presiding over all the Sephiroth arise, like branches from the trunk of any tree: And since י Jod signifies the same as Jehovah, or all four letters, inasmuch as it denotes the number ten, and 1, 2, 3, 4 joined together make 10, therefore י Jod is rightly called the root of the tree, from which the virtues of the trunk and branches arise: Wherefore י Jod is attributed to Ehieh, or Kether: But ה governs the third Sephiroth, to which the Holy Spirit is referred, inasmuch as ה denotes respiration:

--- Page 653 ---
**ON THE PRIMARY PRINCIPLES OF THE MICROCOSM.** 155

The third letter of the Tetragrammaton, ו Vau, corresponds to the sixth Sephirah, over which Eloah presides, inasmuch as its seal is Emeth Adonai; and the Word or Unity in He, that is, God placing His tabernacle in the sun. Therefore, ו Vau properly refers to the center of the entire Sephirotic tree; and for this reason, it is likened to the presiding (spirit) of the superior Sun, Tephireth. But the last ה He is joined to Malchut, which sends its influences into the elemental region. Such a disposition of letters in the ideal trunk (after whose image the world received its proportion and measure) the Cabalists also seem to acknowledge, and among recent authors, Reuchlin also seems to approve of it. This name, therefore, is the Archetypal and eternal idea, comprehending the essence of divine Majesty; according to whose exemplar the dimensions of both the Macrocosm and Microcosm were really delineated and most skillfully constructed, and indeed, both as regards their internal Being and their external (Being): For their internal essence is imprinted in the dimensions of the Sephiroth; but in the external existence of both, י Jod looks forth from darkness, from the denary (ten) into the centenary (hundred) and millenary (thousand); And its first aspect is in ה He, or the first or Empyrean Spirit in the Macrocosm, and the intellectual (spirit) in the Microcosm: This element ה indeed measures the denary dimension; And therefore, just as the number ten is the simplest of all parts, so also the Empyrean Spirit in the world and the intellectual (spirit) in man is the simplest, most subtle, and purest. Afterwards, ו Vau, which in numeration denotes unity above ה He, which is the figure of the number five, designates ו or the ethereal heaven, or the middle, whose Spirit is hidden by the light of Unity: For Unity placed its tabernacle in the sun, which (sun) light or Unity concealed with its light and beauty; so that not ה, but Unity in ה making ו Vau, appears in the solar body in the Macrocosm, and also in the arterial blood of the Microcosm, which redness usually conceals. Furthermore, the last or lowest ה He denotes the lower waters, which ו Vau separated from the upper (waters): Whence it is said that He separated the waters from the waters, and in the Microcosm, the animal heaven from the natural, or the divine from the earthly. And this ה denotes the number a thousand, just as ו signifies the second place, that is, the square of the number ten. But indeed, because by the Hebrews the number a thousand is denoted by a large Aleph, just as Unity (is denoted) by a small Aleph, whose image is Jod in the first composition, therefore it is denoted that יהוה Jehovah is truly Alpha and Omega, that is, the beginning in creation and generation, and the end or ultimate in corruption and death: Which indeed is manifested by such a demonstration.

[Diagram showing Hebrew letters Aleph, He, Vav, He, Aleph connected by a dotted line with labels A, B, C, D, A below them. Under label B is the word "Generatio".]

Where A is the principle of generation; B is the fetus's growth to life; C is vigor, perfection, and the middle of human age; D is the decline to death, which is the ultimate line of things, by which both the Being and the essence of the composite, through resolution, returns to that which was in the beginning. Hence, in this way, that ineffable name will stand, with that line reduced into a circle; which indeed is most suitable to the name Tetragrammaton, inasmuch as it consists of spherical Elements.

Here A, or י Jod, denotes the dark Aleph, inasmuch as it is the ultimate process of privation or resolution, and the bright א inasmuch as it is the origin of generation: For night is as clear to God as day. By the flow from A to B, let there be the origin of life or generation; And from B to C is increase or vegetation: In B is the vigor of life or the sun at the meridian of life; from C to D is the decline of life; and at point D is death, and from D to A is dissolution into that which was in the beginning. Thus, therefore, it appears that Jod is the Alpha and Omega of the circle, inasmuch as it is that which begins and ends the motion of every created or generated thing:

CHAP. I.

Concerning the Mysteries of the elements of Adam's name, and of other names
proper to Man.

[Large decorative initial Q containing a landscape scene with a building and trees] Just as we declared in the Treatise on the secondary or Physical principles of the Macrocosm; that the three mothers of the world were origins, namely א Aleph or the hidden light of the void earth or darkness; that is, Being in potential, מ Mem of the Waters or of the thing actually created, and ש Shin connecting both mothers with a bond of unity in a threefold disposition (for Shin is the Hieroglyphic image of the Holy Spirit) so also we say that the physical principles of the Microcosm shine forth from the hieroglyphic words of its name. As for its name, we find that it is described by three letters of immense profundity, namely א Aleph, ד Daleth, and מ Mem. Nor indeed should it seem absurd to the scientists of this world, what I have said, that a great mystery is contained in the names of creatures, since it is read that God brought all the animals of the earth and all the birds of the sky to Adam, so that he might see what he would call them: and Adam himself called all the animals, and all the birds of the sky, and all the beasts of the earth by their names: Whence it is certain that he, with divine demonstration preceding, gave names proper to the nature and condition of each living creature; and consequently, since all things received their Being and essence by the Word and divine fiery characters, and uttered from the mouth of Elohim, it is necessary that the power of each creature obtained its name and Being in the holy letters of its name: For thus it is handed down by David in the Psalm, that the Lord attributed names to each star; which indeed corresponded with their distinct natures; indeed, the ideal and spiritual characters, which are true impressions of the life and existence of creatures, are mystically imprinted in them. Therefore, the first name imposed on man, as found in Genesis, is אדם (Adam), because, as some wish, he was created from dust and earth. For אדמה (Adamah) is properly cultivated earth of a red and clayey color. By this description, it is denoted that man is not empty or uncultivated earth, but filled with the tincture of divine light and the clarity of the Holy Spirit: For his mass was sanguine flesh imbued with fiery and celestial spirit: For this earth was so prepared by the creator that it would receive all the virtues and icons of all the Sephiroth within itself through that divine breath of life; and consequently, it was not earth properly, but heaven, or heaven in earth, or a celestial, super-celestial, and Deiform earth; whose splendor was indeed so exalted before the fall and transgression, that all darkness was dispelled by the power of light, and Adam's body shone like a Ruby: which indeed we also deduce from the characters of his name, as we will show more fully below: Wherefore אדם (Adam) is also the same as Ruby, or pyrope, a precious stone endowed with transparency. Therefore, the name אדם (Adam) Man comes from the root אדם (adam) to be red: Whence אדם (adam) is red, reddish; Therefore, he received his material substance from the universal earth created, prepared in the clouds; but his tincture of life from heaven, and the fifth essence of reason from the Spirit and breath of God or Wisdom from the second Hochma

CHAP. II.
Concerning the first principle of Man, which was earth, or darkness.

Three supercelestial fathers, both of man himself and of the world, are found and consist in the dimension of the great name Tetragrammaton, as has been said above; whom we have affirmed to be the primary and supercelestial principles of all things: But the Mothers were revealed in the first physical disposition of both the greater and the lesser world, at whose nod Darkness, and from them light and water, were brought forth into the world for its metaphysical and physical perfection. These mothers are indeed as it were passive, inasmuch as they received the actions or impressions of the fathers, namely א (Aleph) and י (Yod), by which they became pregnant, each of the three, namely, in its own species: Wherefore we have called these mothers, namely אמש (EMeSh), whose matrices are Darkness, Water, and Light, secondary principles. But in place of the dark Aleph in the world, we find ד (Daleth) in man; which is also a hieroglyph of eternal wisdom in a dark house; And Aleph denotes wisdom revealed and outwardly apparent; hence it is placed before the word for face: And Mem at the end signifies water or the moist and passive principle. Therefore, we will first discuss the nature of the dark earth, which is signified by ד (Daleth), which is the first physical principle of man: For God formed Adam from the dust of the earth, before He breathed into his face the breath of life. Therefore, we will begin with his earth extracted from the dust of the earth, and then afterwards concerning the medium through which the breath passed, and finally concerning the Deiform breath itself floating in that moist medium, I will, I hope, make remarks highly pertinent to the purpose, though succinctly. That species of darkness, therefore, which was last in the Macrocosm, is the first and principal of the Microcosm; and thus it is, as it were, the basis and foundation of the entire human structure; for it is into this that God, after He had duly and according to His pleasure prepared it, breathed His breath of life; and in this way, the supercelestial and immortal God willed to forge man, a terrestrial God imbued with mortality, from these two naturally diverse principles, so that he, clothed in corporeal clay, might sagaciously observe, and, endowed with the breath of life, might wisely love divine things. Concerning the reason for this matter, namely the conjunction of celestial nature with terrestrial for the composition of the Microcosmic machine, and especially why the divine Mind is enclosed in an opaque body, we have spoken clearly in Tract. 1. Sect. 1. book 7. chap. 3. On the history of the Microcosm; Similarly, in book 5 of the same Tractate and Section, On the nature of the human body, and what its earth was like, and on other not to be despised matters, we have said many words: Indeed, I would like you to read that entire book, as it pertains solely to this subject, namely the description of the external Microcosm. Concerning this conjunction of the soul with the body, Synesius thus sang in his Hymns, speaking of the soul or man's heaven; "A part also, by a heavy bond, obtained an earthly form, and separated from its parents, drank dark oblivion, admiring the unpleasant earth with blind anxieties:" For, as Mercurius Trismegistus says, the body is like a wall enclosing the soul; And it is also like a matrix, receiving and nourishing all the influences of the ideal Sephiroth of its heaven, no differently than that great earth of the Macrocosm, which is therefore called the mother of all things, and because of the multitude of the portion of heaven which it receives into itself, it is most rightly called by Job 4:9 "the house of clay" of the inner man, who has an earthly foundation; And because of the divinity which it retains within itself, it is called the temple of God and of the Holy Spirit: just as Christ himself, speaking enigmatically, used the word temple for the body in John 2:21. Concerning this human principle or basis, Job 16:18 speaks to this effect; "O earth, cover not my blood, and let my cry have no resting place:" Similarly, the Wise Man in Wisdom 9:11 speaks of it thus; "For a perishable body weighs down the soul, and this earthly tent burdens the mind with many cares etc." Hence it is clear that the body is like a dark prison of the Microcosmic heaven itself, no differently than we see the heaven of the Macrocosm everywhere surrounded by the darkness of matter (hyle); for beyond the convexity of the heavens, nothing but darkness is found, which extends infinitely beyond the edges of heaven: and in this same way, earthly darknesses cover the heaven or human soul floating in the supercelestial spirit in the celestial (realm): These, therefore, are the darknesses that blind the soul and impress upon it the marks of self-oblivion: Hence Job 27:19 says, "Man cannot, because of his darkness, arrange his words with God:" And the Wise Man in Ecclesiastes 5:16 says that man eats in darkness all the days of his life and that for this reason there is much wrath and infirmity for him. Hence, therefore, the unhappiness of man, as will be said below in its proper place.

**CHAPTER III.**

That there is a twofold adjunct of man, namely either from his external part, by which he is called mortal and most vile, or at least from his internal portion, by which he is named immortal, divine, and the image of the creator himself.

What earth is, from which the external part of man was fashioned, we have declared quite openly in Book 7, Treatise 1, Section 1 of the Microcosmic History, namely, that it is the more dreggy and darker part of the entire mass of waters, from which mass, indeed, as Saint Peter testifies, both earth and heaven came forth. And since the composition of man is partly from that dead head, or that dreggy substance left in the center of the Alembic, after the subtle was separated from the dense by the power of the universal fire emitted by the creator (which portion, indeed, with divine preparation preceding, was his external part) and partly from a threefold exalted spirit, one of which excels the other by many degrees in purity and simplicity (which threefold spirit is known to serve him in place of a triple heaven, namely, the Empyrean, Ethereal, and Elemental); it follows (I say) from this, that man sometimes has an appellation from his earthly and external part, and sometimes claims his name for himself with respect to his heaven or internal part. CAP. VI.
Concerning the second Principle of Man, which is signified by the Mother, or the character Mem; namely, concerning the Spirit or human heaven.

Having explained that principle of Man, which corresponds to the earth of the world no differently than that [earth] to Darkness, and Darkness to the potential character of the small Aleph (א); which bears the same proportion to Yod, which is found in the first place of the number ten (whose image it is, and which it denotes), as Aleph in the beginning of the digits, which is the Father of numbers (and this principle of man is indeed signified by the character of its name Daleth (ד), which denotes a house or a door, inasmuch as the body is the dwelling of the divine soul), it now follows that we speak of the second principle of man, namely concerning the humid nature, which is signified by the character Mem (מ) in the name of Adam: Indeed, this Mem relates to the sphere of humidity, or rather to the entire humid nature, otherwise called by the name of Water (to which Mem (מ) is attributed from the three Mothers of the world), just as He (ה) of the Tetragrammaton's name has a relation to it, as Father to Mother. And indeed, the character of the element Mem is rightly attributed to the heaven of both the Microcosm and the Macrocosm, inasmuch as the heaven of the Microcosm contains within itself a portion of every Macrocosmic heaven: For its intellectual and rational spirit corresponds to the proportion of the Empyrean heaven, the vital [spirit] is referred to the ethereal heaven, and the natural [spirit], which regards the sublunar sphere of humidity, is seen by its nature to equate to the elemental spirit; And consequently, the same Cabalistic Mother, namely Mem (מ), is attributed to the spiritual composition of the Microcosm: For, as we have fully demonstrated elsewhere, every spirit is of the nature of water; indeed, the sacred scriptures indicate to us that the uncreated spirit predominated over the waters, saying that the spirit of Elohim was carried over the waters, or acted upon the waters, no differently than a male upon a female: To this active spirit, the character He (ה) of the Tetragrammaton is assigned: For it is necessary that the father act upon the mother to procreate things in the world, both great and small.

This portion of man, therefore, is his heaven, or internal portion; by virtue of whose act man is called immortal and a divine animal, just as by reason of his internal part, sordid and defiled by darkness, he has acquired the marks of disturbances and diseases and the name of mortality. And yet, through the conjunction and proximity of the lowest portion of the human heaven with the mass of darkness, the entire lower mass of humid nature is disturbed, infested by darkness, subject to changes, and sometimes affects the entire Microcosmic spirit, as it is founded upon it as a base, with restlessness: Indeed, just as the Cacodaemon himself has power over the lowest region of the world by divine permission, sometimes malevolently agitating winds, air, clouds, storms, and visible waters, so also the Devil sometimes enters the lowest region of the human heaven, and is accustomed to disturb the entire machine of the Microcosm, as not only the sacred scriptures teach us, but also the authorities of other trustworthy persons and even daily experience itself give certain credence to this matter. But indeed, just as evil demons do not have power over the matter of the ethereal heaven, inasmuch as it is too pure and perfectly purged from all defilement of darkness, so also they cannot have force and power over the humid spirit corresponding to life, so that, although their rage in the lower heaven of man may be impetuous, it cannot nevertheless harm life: Hence God said to Satan: *Behold, in your hand it is, nevertheless preserve his soul;* that is, in your hand is the body and that aerial spirit by which the body and material composite are nourished, so that indeed that is in your power; but the ethereal spirit, which is the receptacle of life, will not be permitted to you, that you touch it.

Thus also we read that the evil spirit of God vexed Saul; yet it could not destroy his life; inasmuch as its power in no way extended to the ethereal region: Nor was the unclean spirit able to affect the soul of the Demoniac, that is, the vital spirit, even though its name was Legion, arguing the strength or union of many Demons; But nevertheless, it so infinitely vexed the spirit of that man, and agitated the body nourished by that spirit in such a furious manner, that no one could bind him with chains, as we can read in *Mark 5:2*. CHAPTER IX.
*Concerning the element of Fire, which arises from this principle of the Microcosm, namely concerning yellow Bile.*

Just as we asserted in the Macrocosm that the element of fire is that sphere of the world's elemental region which surrounds and rises above the sphere of humidity, which nevertheless we said was nothing else than an excessive kindling of a part of the sphere of humidity from the reverberation and reflection of supercelestial rays; so also in the Microcosm we have a fiery nature leaping upwards from the chylous substance, and lurking in the lighter fluid of the sphere of humidity, and converting all its liquid into a fiery color and nature: Which region indeed has its seat in the concavity of the liver above the convexity of the stomach, in which watery meteors are generated, that is, in the uppermost region of the air. And although the substance of this element is visible, and behaves contrary to the nature of the element of fire, inasmuch as it is itself humid and fluid, the disposition of fire, however,

the Devil acts, with humor departing from temperament, and disturbing health itself; And this happens especially in diseases arising from cholera, etc. This also undoubtedly usually happens in melancholic diseases and malignant fevers, because this hot nature, joining itself with the fiery nature of the Cacodemon, and penetrating into smoke or vapor or wind, violently moves it, and in it is carried not only to invade the camps of the vital spirits, and to beat the capsules of the heart in a formidable manner, whence follow syncope, exanimations, and tremor and palpitation of the heart, but also against other proud and ambitious defenses of the animal spirits it rises up, and does not cease to invade the palace of Phantasy, indeed even the divine temple of reason itself; Whence, both in fevers and in melancholics, follow phrenitis, deliria, manias, lycanthropies, and other similar kinds of alienations, such as Despair, the appearance of vain visions, etc. likewise love of solitude, cares and anxieties, fears and suspicions without any given occasion, sighs, and infinite other symptoms follow.

Therefore, we conclude that, just as this humor with its evil soul brings little utility to the body, so indeed it provides a great argument for harm and mischief to it: Wherefore there is need of the industry of the best Physician, and of the medicines of a scientific Artist, by which this humor with its soul or agent may be constrained as if by secure chains or bonds into its proper seat; for it, when outside its place, either in its own substance, or by the mere spirit and breath of the formal soul, not only renders other humors, otherwise quite mild in their natures, wandering through the body, fierce and makes them authors of infirmities, but also it itself is present to them as a certain leader of all evil, giving motion to its power to do harm, no differently than fire gives flame and life to a lamp, or to turpentine, which was previously quiet and innocent, and only in potential to burn or to affect badly. And indeed, if we have well examined the nature of the Macrocosmic element of fire, we will finally perceive that it itself is the author and origin of any motion towards corruption and alteration in this lower world; just as, conversely, solar or celestial fire is the evident cause of generation and health and conservation, and as it were the father of the life of lower creatures, as will appear more clearly in the experiment described in the following chapter.

CHAP. I.

*On the principles of the Gentile Philosophers & Physicians, & that they were ignorant of uncreated principles. On tertiary principles, or imperfectly mixed bodies closest to composition, which are called meteors. A clear demonstration indicating the nature of an imperfectly mixed body.*

[Large decorative initial D] EGARDING primary or Metaphysical and uncreated Principles: Likewise regarding those secondary or Physical and created ones; from which two primary qualities, namely heat and cold, arise, and again by their mutual action, two other more passive qualities, namely humidity and dryness, are produced, by whose action and passion towards each other those four substances are created in the world, which are commonly called Elements; we have indeed given a sufficiently open and clear account in the preceding sections. The Gentiles were never, or at least very sparingly, engaged in the primary and uncreated principles of things, whence it also happened that they used to speak of secondary Principles as blind men speak of colors, some (I say) with only a very few exceptions, to whom, on account of their divine insight into abstruse and mystical principles, the title of divinity was attributed. Aristotle therefore spoke of his Principles in an obscure manner, regarding the true and primary Physical foundations, namely Darkness, Waters, and Light, under a veil and a quasi-obscure mantle, and treating of them under the names of Privation, Matter, and Form: but he was ignorant of those primary and uncreated principles, inasmuch as he considered the world uncreated and eternal. Galen and Hippocrates made their primary principles four supreme qualities, namely supreme heat, cold, humidity, and dryness, which qualities, if they are inherent in matter, they assertively say constitute the four elements. So that these also (as appears from their writings) did not know those supreme and uncreated principles, from which all things were primordially made, nor indeed did they regard Darkness, Light, and Water (from which the aforesaid four qualities were produced). And this was the reason for such great uncertainty and inconstancy in the sciences, and also in both Philosophy and Medicine, because, namely, with the Principles or uncreated or Archetypal causes unknown, it is indeed impossible to judge rightly concerning the Principled or caused things. But we, by the revelation of prior principles emanating from one source, are taught that there are still other principles closer to complete composition or to a perfectly mixed body, than either Darkness or Light or Water, or Earth or fire or the sphere of humidity, which are the three elements of composition. For as we see that in the first creation, the otherness or composition of the angel, nay certainly even the consistency of the whole world, namely Light & Water

Water (which make duality) were procreated from unity, so also we say that in the simplicity of e-

tion. Just as therefore from the essence of the monad to duality, namely Light & Water, there was a
progression to the perfect creation of the world in the likeness of the trinity: so also from light and water,
both dark and clear, heaven and earth were made, from which three elements (which others make four)
are derived. Similarly, from one of these elements no mixture is made, much less composition,
which exists more perfect than incomplete mixture. But from two, and sometimes from three, that

to the simplicity of elements than the exactly composed, and consequently it follows that it is a princi-

and the most exact composition made from unities. Thus indeed an element is, as it were, a unity by whose
doubling an imperfect mixture is usually procreated: and yet nevertheless from that mixture, by the labor
and industry of Nature, complete composition and perfect generation usually occur: But when that com-
position fails, there is immediately a reduction into its nearer principle or imperfect mixture,
which indeed is found to happen constantly in the corruption of things. Hence therefore it is clearly estab-
lished that both the generation and corruption of composition move from that imperfect medium and
return to it again: Hence this axiom so often proclaimed by Philosophers: *There is no true dissolution of a composite thing, unless it is first reduced to its primary matter, that is, its proximate and more immediate origin.*
There is therefore in every generation a progression from a starting point through a medium to an end point in this manner.

Therefore, among bodies of this kind, imperfectly mixed, those principles of compound things seem to be enumerated which are contained between the elements themselves and completely elemental bodies, and are properly those bodies, whether visible or invisible, which by the addition of parts or by perfection—that is, by complete motion, namely from the starting point to the destination—constitute and generate perfectly mixed bodies, both animal and vegetable and mineral. For what else was the remote matter or proximate principle of metal or any other mineral than smoke or water rarefied and mixed with fire? What the proximate? Is it not sulfur and quicksilver, that is, vapor mixed with exhalation? What is the primary animal nature besides water and light? How, moreover, these meteors, both hidden and manifest, are carried in the Microcosmic spirit will be explained below in its proper place, where also, concerning those mundane things, although we will say very few words, we will nevertheless make them clear and distinct.

C A P. III.

*That everything created and generated, or corrupted, has received its motion towards its*
*perfection from its principles through a meteorological medium,*
*that is, an imperfectly mixed one.*

Therefore, there was never any motion in the world, either for perfect creation, or for generation, or for corruption, which was not made through a meteorological medium, that is, an imperfectly mixed one. For just as for the completion of a melody, a middle, internal, and less perfect consonance is usually required, so also for creation we see the binary number interposed between the creator and the created thing, by which that creature is led to the perfection of creation. For example, by progression from the uncreated unity we arrive at duality, denoting matter and form, water and light, by whose union, through the bond of the spirit of the ternary order, a complete creature was begotten from those primary elements on the first day of creation, which is endowed with an angelic form. In a similar manner, between duality and its square (4), 3 intervenes, which is as it were an imperfectly mixed or medium between 2 and 4. Such, therefore, is the substance of the middle heaven, whose substance (3) is matter, while its form is the supercelestial binary (2): therefore, 2 united to 3 gives this heaven the name of the fifth essence. The perfect creature from these is the Sun, and the other stars, which fulfill the role of the square. Similarly, the Sun and the Stars behave as imperfectly mixed bodies or fiery meteors themselves with respect to bodies of the lowest order of perfect elementary composition, in which the number eight is found in a cubic series. For although in itself the mixture between light and the spirit of the Empyrean heaven is most perfect, nevertheless, with respect to angelic composition, it is called an imperfect mixture, inasmuch as it is the midpoint of motion between the creating monad and the created angel, since such a mixture is on the way to perfection.

**CHAPTER VI.**
*How the reason of varied mundane mixture can be most excellently deduced from the consi-*
*deration of my double mundane pyramid: And concerning the true theory of Physical Pyramids.*

**N**or certainly is this progression of nature to be sought only in the great and immense world, but
also in the motion of any creature from its starting point to its ending point: that is, from the point of extreme
rawness to that of complete maturation. For such was the breadth of motion towards perfection in the greater
world, which we have openly explained in our previous works by the varied adaptation of two different pyramids,
namely the formal and the material. For example, we will take an apple in its state of extreme
rawness and immaturity, in which state we find its matter, consisting of the primary waters of the world,
almost entirely devoid of actual light or essential form, or at least endowed with almost no trace or
act of perfection: and in this state of it, we place the beginning of the cone of the formal pyramid in this crude mass,
from which it gradually approaches the base or summit the more that fruit proceeds to the degree
of perfection or maturity: in which motion it will be right to understand and perceive that
the more the perfection of the formal pyramid in the apple (which is observed in the degrees of maturity)
abounds and increases, the more it also converts the material nature of the apple into its likeness,
and thus at the end of its maturity, the formal act of the apple is equally mixed with its passive material
or suffering female nature, from whose mutual coition a complete seed apt for the procreation of its like will be produced. This,
I say, is the intention and mixture of my pyramids, both in every individual subject of the world
and in its whole, namely the variety and continuity of action and motion, and the diversity of degrees of change
of matter undergoing such continuous action from the starting point to the ending point.

This motion is indeed usually observed to be even more perfect in minerals themselves, for in quicksilver (in which the formal heat is very weak)
the beginning of the formal pyramid's motion can be perceived as in a subject of gross water,
whose next degree of progression is discerned to be in lead, in which it begins to hasten towards the perfection of gold:
then through tin to silver and from that into Gold, in which the fiery rays of formal light are manifested even to the eyes of fools,
which before, due to the inequality of matter not yet entirely subjected to the actions of form,
were repressed and hidden: which indeed was a sign that the assaults of matter were not completely overcome
and subjected to the intense appetite of fiery form. Hence it is clear that just as the principle of motion towards the perfect
composition of metals was in quicksilver, so also we say that its completion is in gold,
inasmuch as nature does not tend beyond this goal of perfection but rests in it, unless further excited by the artifice of the most sagacious philosopher:
This same progression also exists in the animal subject, whose starting point is the seed, in which that spark of the form,
completing the place of the pyramid's cone, exists, by the multiplication of which, motion occurs from the fluid seed or crude animal water
to the completion of the fetus and to its perfect maturity, which in man we call youth.

The intermediate degrees of these progressions can most rightly be called meteors or imperfect mixtures,
inasmuch as they are on the way to perfect composition, that is, they have not yet reached nature's goal.
In which motion, if any impediment occurs to them by which they are hindered in their way,
they can most aptly be called diseases or morbid and preternatural meteors, and sometimes they retrogress
and return to those principles from which they emerged, and produce the death of the composite or the destruction
of the thing to be composed. But if such meteors proceed without any impediment to the end destined for them by nature,
they are called natural and bring generation, life, and health to the creature both to be generated and already generated.
And this is the intention of our pyramids, both in every generable and corrupt

of light, ch. 2. that all things possessing life tend upwards by their own instinct, and all things influencing life incline downwards. They were nothing before the instant of creation, and divinity itself is said to lie hidden, or with respect to the divine act; and in this state, all things are truly considered after the mystery of creation, in which God is said to be manifest and not hidden: Therefore, the prior state of formless matter is explained by the subterranean hemisphere of the mirror, in which a dark Aleph (א) is expressed in the center of the hyle, which is a hieroglyph of the hidden God. And this hyle is called 'Earth without form and void' because it lacks every act of light, and divine grace is not perceived to act within it; by the lack of which (since without it nothing can be fulfilled), potential matter is called void, and indeed it is called divine potential, since God lies hidden within it, and yet is potentially ready, as far as we are concerned, to act within it, its rays of beauty at last revealed, though still contracted within itself; and indeed the creator reduced this potential to act at the very instant he began to create the world: And just as here on earth, when the Sun is absent, night immediately invades everything, so also for the absence of the Sun or divine act (which we call wisdom, older than the Sun and the world itself), we have placed the lowest hemisphere of the mirror, on whose left side we have exposed the twilight of Day, splendor, and the act of divine wisdom, just as on its right or opposite side, the evening time after the setting of the divine Sun or the end of the world is denoted. In the diurnal hemisphere, the outer orb indicates the degrees of perfection and imperfection of every creature, both in the progress of creation and in the series of generation. Thus indeed, the movement of wisdom in creation was made from the point of the East to the meridian of vigor, between which extremes of perfection is the meteorological medium tending both to generation and nutrition, which is called increment, just as between the point of perfection or meridian vigor and that of corruption and death or the setting of the Sun, is that meteorological medium called Decrement, which from disease and putrefaction, from the exaltation of life, tends towards its opposite until it reaches the twilight of death: Hence it is said that the generation of one is the corruption of another; indeed, many mysteries lie hidden here, which it would be too long to recount in this place. The second sphere, however, denotes the order of degrees of progression in creation and generation, from nothing and the dark or small Aleph (א), denoting unity, to the specific formation of the world to be created, whose Sun rises in Jod (י): which is the character of divine emanation from darkness and the sign of the number ten, whose end is the great Aleph (א), which is signified by the number one thousand

But Elohim Gibbor from the Sephirah Geburah (which denotes punishment) flows through the Powers (led by the malevolent angel Samuel, such influxes are opposite to life) into the sphere of Mars; this planet is indeed called malevolent and a lesser misfortune, just as Saturn is called a greater one because of its congealing dryness. Therefore, the influxes of Mars act inclemently, and pour down into the lower regions an impulsive force full of the violence of fire, which its Olympic Daemon has established downwards into the element of fire. Whence in both worlds, preternaturally hot exhalations, carrying unhealthiness with them, are excited, from which fiery meteors are ignited, both visible ones like comets, beams, perpendicular fires, and invisible ones, from which follow plagues, wasting of land and body, emaciation and dryness, which famines accompany, and fevers in the Microcosm, Erysipelas, etc. And thus one must proceed with the rest.

Finally, the last wheel of the mirror explains the meteors of any body, whether animal, vegetable, or finally mineral, from which they are composed according to the laws of nature. Such are Mercury, whose author is water produced by Ehieh; Sulfur, whose principle was light or created fire, which received its power from Jah flowing from its throne Hochma; and Salt, which is the union of both, namely Mercury and Sulfur, influenced by Elohim. And salt is the simplest earth and, as it were, the center of all bodies, for thus philosophers write that the center of the macrocosm's earth is most pure and secure from defilement. But the other meteors of the same orb are partly salubrious and partly insalubrious, according to the property of the Sephirah from which they are poured. And this last sphere is the ultimate meteor, or proximate matter, or the immediate cause of perfect composition, both animal, vegetable, and mineral. Wherefore, although meteors of this kind are imperfectly mixed in themselves, yet because they approach more closely to perfect composition, they are therefore called more composite meteors, that is, proximate causes of perfect mixture or composition. And in composites, Mercury is called that radical moisture by which the agent or innate heat, which is Sulfur, is nourished; and Sulfur is that agent which operates as a form in matter adapted to it for the essential being of the composite; and Salt, which participates in these two, is that central earth which attracts parts necessary for composition and augmentation from the four elements. Whence every composite has, as meteors proximate to its generation, Mercury itself, from the part of subtle water; and Sulfur, from the part of subtle fire, from which mixed an anima (soul) is made; and Salt, more fixed, from the part of subtle earth, from which, as from a secret boundary, the aggregation of the body and the tabernacle of the aforesaid soul derive their origin.

From which it is indeed clear that for the composition of any creature, the most remote cause is God, between whom and those proximate causes many other intermediate causes intervene, as is clearly explained in the mirror itself.
