First Experiment, On the discovery and revelation of the hidden sense or mystery of every Hebrew word, and this solely through the contemplation of the fathers י Jod ה He ו Vau & mothers א Aleph מ Mem & ש Shin, whether present or absent.

Indeed, a wonderful light is brought to Hebrew words by the presence as well as the absence of these truly holy and formal characters, since by these signs their secret sense, or essential arcana, is most excellently elucidated for those who diligently observe them: For as regards primarily the fathers, or merely formal letters (which are also called round for reasons alleged by us above), it must be understood that insofar as they are the principles of all principles, in which the unique uncreated essence consists, to that extent, without doubt, their presence conceals some divine mystery in the hidden part of the word where they are found; and where more of these characters are found, there, without doubt, a greater presence of divinity exists, although it is not so openly explained by common Hebrew signification. For example, in this word יה Jah, nothing but divine essence is found: And also יהוה Jehova, which characters are indeed considered solely in the divine essence without any consideration of created or material characters, whence they denote divine essence alone. Next to these in excellence come the mothers א Aleph מ Mem & ש Shin, since they are, as it were, the closest and primary garments or vehicles of divinity in nature: As the soul א Aleph of light is י Jod, life ש Shin is ו Vau, and the creating internal spirit מ Mem, is ה He. Hence, where these two kinds of characters are mixed together, there, without doubt, is the most exalted intention or mystical meaning of that word; and the more the fathers abound in the word, the nobler the word will be esteemed: For example, אהיה Ehieh, in which the essence and property of God the father is contemplated; אלהים Elohim, God the Holy Spirit, or God of Waters. Where the final מ Mem, denoting water, is united with י & א, it forms אלוה Eloah, and so in other cases: Hence, the round characters with the mothers denote Divine action in nature. By a similar reasoning, if only mothers are found in words, they denote a thing sublimated in the mysteries of nature all the more, the more characters of that nature the word denoting it contains within itself: Thus, in the word שמים (heavens), we see an open מ Mem and a closed ם Mem, which are hieroglyphs of subtle and dense waters. Likewise, ש Shin is a sign of light, by which the heavens are adorned, and ה is a hieroglyph of the spiritual world, the head of the heavens, and the life of the world. Thus, שמש (Sun) contains within itself two mothers and again a luminous mother twice. Hence, it denotes that just as יה Jah, or יהוה Jehova, is the more excellent essence of the archetypal or uncreated kingdom, so also is שמש Sun in the typical and created or natural kingdom. For the Sun is the visible prince and emperor of all visible creatures of the world. Finally, where all these letters are perceived to be absent, there indeed little good or at least external light is to be expected: We could indeed produce an entire volume on the presence or absence of these formal characters. But truly, it is by no means our intention to dwell solely on them.

Second Experiment, On the admirable explanation of the Sephirotic number, in which equal portions corresponding to each Sephirotic property are found.

There is no number to be found in the world divisible into so many equal parts as is one thousand eighty, which we have found to be divided into ten portions, each corresponding to a Sephira. Thus, indeed, its half is 540. But its third part is 360. According to which number the days of the year are divided. Its fourth part is 270. Its fifth part is 216. Its sixth part is 180. Its eighth part is 135. Its ninth part is 120, which space of time God indeed assigned for human age. Its tenth part is 108. But its fifteenth part is 72. For so many do the 22 letters joined with the 50 Gates of Wisdom make; likewise, the strong angels of the whole earth were 72, according to the opinion of the Cabalists. For according to the Cabalists, from the number of the Tetragrammaton arises 72, from which 72 angels are produced, as if from the seal of the creator, by a certain divine emanation. Finally, its twentieth part is 54. In these ten portions of that number, without doubt, the mysteries of the ten Sephiroth are comprehended, representing archetypal natures and divine properties in this world, which indeed some ancient Rabbis have tried to proclaim more clearly and explicitly.

**On many other mysteries of divination which by a true and formal in-**
**spection of this mirror can be elucidated.**

Many other questions or doubts can also be resolved by the knowledge of this most true Astrology, provided that the artist is skilled in it, not in the common way of one whose habit is to grasp the external but omit the internal, or like Aesop's dog, to choose the shadow and neglect the essential substance: For example. How is the nature of the predominant Angel for any native, and of the demon, both Olympic and elemental, subject to him, to be found? Which is the stronger vital act of the soul in the native? Which will be a man's most fortunate or unfortunate day? For this question, the Sephiroth of that man's Lord of the Horoscope and the predominant Lord of the requested day must be considered. Which of two men making war or a dispute between themselves will prevail over the other in some contention, on a fixed day? Where the Sephiroth of the nativity of each, along with the Lord of the heavens on the given day, their strength and weakness must be considered. And many other questions of importance can be resolved by the power of this mirror, which in this place, as well as other things related by us, to explain to the common (and indeed vain) populace would be ridiculous (I know), wherefore I will not endeavor to say more about this universal mirror.

**How this universal mirror is included in the four characters of the great**
**Tetragrammaton name with the four mothers corresponding to them.**

Let the first sphere of the following mirror denote the three primary or archetypal principles which the Mosaic fathers called, where one character or principle is repeated twice, namely ה He, after the pattern of which the superior waters were divided from the inferior waters, and to each uncreated character its own mother is subjected, from which the remaining subordinate principles, comprehended between mere simplicity and composition, are posited in their place, each indeed according to the reason of its own property under each: Where, with the initiating illumination of Mem, it begins from א Aleph, the luminous. For the world begins in luminous Aleph, through מ Mem initiating, and ends through ם Mem final and closed in dark Aleph, for when the supreme Sun sets, it is necessary that the light of the world be again reduced to darkness, whence, as small Aleph is the beginning of number (namely, unity), so also great Aleph is the end, which denotes the millennial number beyond which there is no progression. Thus the world was born, and thus will be its destruction, if only luminous Aleph removes its luminous spirit from the world by hiding itself in darkness.

In the preceding Macrocosmic speculum (diagram) it appears that the world began from a luminous Aleph, for the initiating Mem is illuminated by a luminous Aleph: but the form of the world ends in the final Mem ם where light returns again into darkness, for the luminous Aleph, by hiding itself, is changed into a dark Aleph. Aleph therefore is the beginning of things, and is their ultimate end: It is Alpha & it is Omega, it is unity & it is the myriad number beyond which there is no dimension in Arithmetic. Thus the world was born and no differently will be its destruction, namely by the luminous Aleph removing its face from the mundane spirit & hiding itself in darkness, that is, by migrating from its divine act into divine potency; And from this it is that Aleph is said to partake of the nature of both sexes, in the manner of a Hermaphrodite, namely of the male insofar as it is act & form, and of the female with respect to potency & matter: Hence said Mercurius Trismegistus in Pimander 1: "The Mind, most full of the fecundity of both sexes, etc."
